16232.title: Applied Economic Analysis
16232.description: This subject introduces the application of economic principles and frameworks in the formulation and interpretation of urban policy. The importance of rigorous analysis in the context of policy formulation and interpretation is emphasised. The subject begins with an introduction to the microeconomic principles for guiding policy options. It then explores in detail specific applications from housing, infrastructure provision, and environmental valuation. The subject takes a case study approach and students apply their learning through discussions, hands-on exercises, quizzes, and a final examination.
learningOutcomes: Comprehend and explain economic concepts in an urban policy context
Apply and interpret different economic theories in a way that is meaningful and useful in developing and assessing urban policies over a range of subject areas
Evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of economic approaches on policy solutions, while presenting convincing and reasoned arguments to a variety of audiences
Apply the knowledge and skills developed to real world problems in conditions under which property economists work
Analyse the main ways in which ethical issues are manifested in economic policy

16233.title: Urban Planning & Development Process
16233.description: In this subject, you'll learn to use economic principles for shaping and understanding urban policy, with an emphasis on detailed analysis. Beginning with microeconomics for policy decisions, you'll explore housing, infrastructure, and environmental valuation. Engage with case studies and interactive learning methods, including discussions and exercises, reinforced by quizzes and a final exam. This approach will develop your analytical abilities to effectively engage with and impact urban policy.
learningOutcomes: Understand how and why plans are made; how regulatory instruments and design standards are formulated and implemented; and how such instruments are used to influence and encourage good design and management of the urban environment.

Acquire an ability to recognise and apply the principles of sound environmentally sustainable development in an urban planning context and understand the values which are typically associated with 'good' and 'poor' urban planning and development practice.

16234.title: Property Valuation
16234.description:
This subject equips you with an understanding of the valuation profession, including roles, functions, and the purposes of valuations. You'll explore various value types, property interests, valuation principles, and case law. Learn valuation methods such as the Market, Cost, and Income Approaches, and understand partial interests, financial theory, and the time value of money's impact on these methods. You'll also learn to identify and account for risk, and gain insight into valuation reporting standards. Proficiency in a spreadsheet program like Microsoft Excel is expected.

Assessments ensure you grasp key concepts, theories, and methods, with class exercises, group property valuations, and a final exam that tests your knowledge of a valuer's responsibilities and the intricacies of valuation methods and associated risks. This foundational subject is vital for applying valuation theory and practice in the property industry.
learningOutcomes: Understand the principles and applications of property valuation.through active participation during the in-class discussions and applied learning activities.
Define and explain the valuation of partial interests in real estate.
Select and apply appropriate valuation methods for different property types based on analysis of market evidence during the in-class discussions and applied learning activities.
Prepare a market overview and draft valuation instructions and reports in accordance with industry standards.
Determine the highest and best use of land and identify changing uses of land through active participation during the in-class discussions and applied learning activities.

16235.title: Urban Economics
16235.description: This is a core subject that engages with the economics of cities and urban regions. Through a series of lectures, tutorials and discussions, we will understand and critically apply economic concepts, theories and tools to urban growth, urban development and urban policy-making. Urban Economics explores the nature of cities and how economic forces shape urban change. While acknowledging the interconnections between urban, rural and peri-urban spaces, we will delve into the causes of urban problems such as poverty, disadvantage and urban sustainability. The 'economic' in urban economics is understood as enmeshed in complex social and environmental experiences. The themes covered include the drivers of the urban economy, including agglomeration economies, the urban and spatial structure of economic growth and change, urban land rent and the economics of urban sustainability.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate a good theoretical understanding of urban problems and prospects, including the place of 'property' in the process of urban economic growth and change within ecological limits.
Apply key urban economic concepts in real world situations.
Probe the role of various institutions in urban and regional development processes.
Undertake research and provide a compelling presentation of its results in a professional manner.

Through this, you'll gain insights into how various taxes influence property holdings and investment decisions.

Identify assessable income and allowable deductions with regards to income producing property.
Prepare and analyse schedules for the decline in value of assets and capital works.

16259.title: Honours Research 2
16259.description: In this second subject of the six-part Honours sequence for the Bachelor of Property Economics, you'll work with a supervisor to design and plan a research project, which can vary in approach, including quantitative, qualitative, traditional academic format, or primarily online presentation. The focus is on developing a robust research methodology, preparing you to commence fieldwork. You'll deepen your understanding of research methodologies, assess their suitability for your research questions, and acquire specific research skills such as survey design, interview techniques, or statistical analysis, as agreed with your supervisor. This subject involves one-on-one meetings with your supervisor to craft a research design and author the methodology chapter of your thesis.

Apply problem solving strategies and use empirical analysis in built environment research.

16262.title: Honours Research 1
16262.description:
In this first subject of the Bachelor of Property Economics (Honours) six-part series, you'll embark on a research project under the guidance of a supervisor, learning to conduct a literature review and develop research methodology through a blend of online and face-to-face interactions. Your research can adopt various forms, from qualitative to quantitative analysis, with the structure tailored to your research goals.

You'll engage in one-on-one meetings with your supervisor to select a research topic, formulate specific questions, and conduct a comprehensive literature review, laying the foundation for your project. You'll establish the rationale for your research, set aims and objectives, and demonstrate adeptness in library searches and literature review structuring, including managing an endnote library of sources. This subject hones essential academic research skills, such as defining research questions and critically analysing existing literature, which are also invaluable in private and government research roles.
learningOutcomes: Select an appropriate research topic for specific and emerging problems in the built environment
Understand how to pose and frame research questions, aims and objectives
Search for relevant literature and sources of information
Write a critical review of the selected literature

16263.title: Design Team Management
16263.description: This subject equips you with the skills to effectively manage design teams in complex construction projects, blending theoretical models with practical design management strategies. You'll develop expertise in areas such as team coordination, communication, contractual obligations, and the use of digital technologies for enhanced collaboration. Learning is interactive, featuring case studies and insights from industry experts, ensuring you understand the roles within architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) disciplines. You'll critically engage with the digital transformation of the construction industry and its impact on your career. Through individual and group work, you'll tackle real-world challenges, requiring self-study and field research to contribute meaningfully to discussions and solutions. The content remains current, reflecting the evolving nature of industry practices.
learningOutcomes: Comprehend and evaluate design processes and methodologies.
Recognise and apply effective communication and collaboration strategies in team-based projects.
Apply information and knowledge management within design teams.
Demonstrate knowledge of alternative contractual relationships within teams.

16264.description: This subject introduces you to accounting and business management with an emphasis on the financial dynamics of construction and property businesses. You'll grasp the core financial drivers of a company and the ethical considerations in financial reporting. The course equips you to interpret and analyse key financial documents—profit or loss statements, financial positions, budgets, and cash flows—to evaluate a company's financial health.

Prepare Statement of Profit or Loss, Balance Sheet, and apply ration analysis as a tool for strategic planning.

Provide an analysis of cost-volume-profit relationships for both construction firms and service industries.
Apply quantitative and qualitative issues for investment decisions.

16266.description: This subject explores the environmental impact of building construction and urban development, highlighting the responsibility of built environment professionals in mitigating these effects. You'll examine global environmental issues, the contribution of the construction sector, and the application of sustainability practices in both residential and commercial projects, including sustainability ratings. The course delves into life cycle assessment, sustainable urban planning, and design principles. You'll gain insights into the historical and contemporary factors influencing city development and understand the environmental, social, and economic implications of urban design. Additionally, the role of technology in addressing environmental challenges within the built environment is addressed, providing a foundation for shaping sustainable cities.
learningOutcomes: Understand the environmental and ethical impacts of urban development and design.
Discuss historical and contemporary urban development trends and evaluate current sustainable planning initiatives.
Explain the main principles of sustainable urban development and relevant environmental considerations.
Identify quality urban design principles and environmentally sympathetic design and assess their application in planned and completed development projects.

16298.title: Property Management
16298.description:
This is a core subject in the first year of the Bachelor of Property Economics. The subject is an in-depth study of management of commercial property, and the relationship between owner, managing agent and tenant. It encompasses various lease structures, the role of the property manager, and their statutory obligations and requirements, including the enforcement of lease conditions, budgeting and forecasting.

Among the facets of property management covered are facilities management, which underpin the operations of commercial, industrial and retail property. The increasing importance of workplace health and safety are addressed within statutory and operational frameworks. An introduction to the theories of mediation for property managers in settling property disputes will be covered.

Students are exposed to financial budgeting, forecasting, planning for operating and capital expenditure and strategic investment and asset planning using practical examples which demonstrate the application of these facets of the property management process. The theory underpinning each topic aligns with practical real-life examples in providing context for the concepts and theories addressed in this subject
learningOutcomes: Define and apply commercial property management functions and responsibilities
Engage with Workplace Health and Safety WHS environment and sustainability standards
Read and negotiate commercial & retail leases & commercial and FM management agreements and mediate disputes
Calculate net, gross & face rents, undertake rent reviews & participate in the resolution of rent disputes
Define, apply and collect property outgoings and prepare income & expense budgets

16307.title: Project Management Integration
16307.description: This capstone project subject allows you to integrate and showcase your professional knowledge and skills by working in groups to manage a project from inception to completion, including commissioning. You will adhere to strict milestones, demonstrating thorough preparation, planning, execution, testing, and documentation. Proactive problem-solving is key. The course aligns with the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK), covering project initiation, planning, execution, control, and closing, integrating scope, time, cost, quality, risk, and procurement. Effective teamwork and communication are emphasized throughout the project lifecycle.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate comprehensive project management skills and knowledge.
Identify the main strategies and processes for effective client and project stakeholder management.
Demonstrate an understanding of typical construction processes including site assembly, workplace safety and traffic management.
Interpret and use project documentation.

16313.title: Construction Industry Economics
16313.description: In this foundational subject for the Bachelor of Construction Project Management, you'll learn about the Australian economy's structure and performance, focusing on economic aspects pertinent to the building, construction, property development, and management sectors. You'll be introduced to economic theory and macroeconomic concepts, including the business cycle, fiscal and monetary policies, and their impact on the property and construction industries. The subject also addresses the influence of technology on economic growth and the dynamics of financial crises.
learningOutcomes: Understand the basic principles of economics and their relevance to the property and construction industries
Apply economic theory to measurement of the economy and its management through macroeconomic policies
Explain the role and economic significance of the Australian Built Environment Sector
Place the economy in a global context

Describe conventional construction methods, materials, terminology and details for industrial buildings

16317.title: Risk and Safety Management
16317.description: In your third year of the Bachelor of Construction Project Management, this core subject equips you with a framework for managing Work, Health & Safety (WHS) and risk on construction sites. You'll explore the stringent legal obligations under WHS legislation, including workers' compensation and insurance. The course covers management practices for maintaining site safety and addresses the challenges in doing so. It integrates effective risk management practices with safety management, providing an overview of project risk management, theories of risk causation, and techniques for risk identification, evaluation, and response. You'll learn to develop project risk management systems and methods for monitoring and controlling risks, focusing on the typical risks faced by project stakeholders.
learningOutcomes: Understand the principles and processes of risk and safety management in construction projects.
Understand the main safety legislation requirements for construction projects
Understand how to prepare a project Risk Management Plan and Safety Management Plan for construction projects
Recognise and understand the main factors affecting risk and safety on construction projects and how they can be best addressed
Discuss the main issues, perspectives and challenges for risk management and safety management on construction projects.

You'll explore special purpose valuations, including those for strata and community title properties, stratum subdivisions, heritage properties, hypothetical developments, financial reporting, and prestige properties.

Research and report on a class of specialised property.
Calculate and apply valuation knowledge and methodology to industry-standard special purpose property valuation.
Communicate effectively through professional research-based written reports in specialised property valuation.

16333.title: Statutory Valuation and Compensation
16333.description: This subject trains you to assess, prepare, and defend statutory valuations for purposes such as land acquisition, urban renewal, and taxation, which are significant for tax revenue in Australia. You'll learn the importance of valuations in legal contexts, including litigation, family law, and equity cases involving property. The course covers drafting valuation instructions, preparing statements of evidence, and presenting expert testimony in court. You'll also learn to determine fees, accept and comply with instructions, and conduct valuations according to statutory requirements.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the responsibilities of valuers and property professionals.
Assess rating and taxing assessments and prepare to defend them in a court case through statements of evidence and preparation for cross examination.
Define the causes of liability against property professionals and the possibilities of policy reform relating to compulsory acquisition and rating of land.
Navigate the statutory processes and methods of determining compensation for land acquisition.
Conduct valuations and prepare reports and relevant calculations in compliance with industry and statutory standards.

16338.title: International Property Investment
16338.description: This subject focuses on the theory and practice of direct and indirect international property investment, including both inbound investment into Australia and outbound investment into global markets. You'll engage with lectures, case studies, and exercises that highlight the connection between investment and valuation, underscoring the importance of risk management and informed decision-making. The course examines the reasons behind international property investment, the compilation of a global real estate portfolio, the macro and micro factors affecting investment performance, and the various investment formats appropriate for different international contexts.
learningOutcomes: Construct and communicate investment strategies based on major sources of financial market information.
Evaluate the role of risk and return in the asset allocation decision.
Explain the relationship between investment theory and practical portfolio management in light of economic policies.
Identify the attributes of different asset types and their role in a diversified portfolio.
Construct a diversified portfolio and prepare economic and financial reports to explain the investment strategy.

16412.title: Cost Management 4: Advanced Cost Management
16412.description: This subject explores advanced estimating and cost management techniques used by contractors, including tendering, cost monitoring, and cost control. It examines the practical challenges of cost estimation, project procurement, and strategies for achieving competitive advantage. The subject also covers key decision-making tools such as investment appraisal, feasibility studies, and cost–benefit analysis. Students will use contemporary industry software to undertake measurement and estimating tasks, and integrate estimating processes with Building Information Modelling (BIM) systems.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of PMBOK Competency Units/Knowledge Areas in Project Cost Management through active participation in in-class discussions and applied learning activities.
Demonstrate an understanding of advanced digital technology in design, estimating and cost management
Understand the concept of bidding and tendering, early contractor involvement (ECI), procurement methods and infrastructure cost management
Understand the concept of investment appraisal and techniques
Use computer software for design, measurement, estimating, and construction programming

16422.title: Construction Technology 4
16422.description: This subject explores construction technology for multi-storey commercial buildings, starting with an overview of high-rise construction methods, materials handling, and typical elements such as concrete frames, pre-stressed and pre-fabricated construction, slip-form, jump-form, and curtain walling. It extends to internal fit-outs and covers structural principles and building services technology, including hydraulics, electrical, mechanical, security, communication, fire protection, and vertical transportation. You'll also learn about relevant building regulations and codes, and the challenges of ensuring compliance in high-rise construction.
learningOutcomes: Understand and describe the interrelationship, behaviour and function of components in multi-storey buildings.
Understand and describe conventional construction methods, materials, terminology and details for multi-storey buildings.
Understand the function and detail of typical construction interfaces between different building elements.
Relate their academic studies to practical applications.

16423.title: Procurement and Contract Management
16423.description: This subject investigates the procurement systems and contract management practices in the construction industry. You'll study various project procurement methods and common construction contracts, focusing on contractual responsibilities, liabilities, and related issues. Exercises will enhance your understanding of contract conditions and risk allocation. The course also covers effective claims management, including variations, progress claims, and delay cost claims, extending to subcontract and supply agreement management. You'll learn about cost, time, quality monitoring, cash flow forecasting, and earned value analysis. Additionally, the subject addresses conflict management and dispute resolution, incorporating contemporary software and practices like web-based contract administration and integration with Building Information Modelling (BIM) systems.
learningOutcomes: Identify and explain key aspects of project procurement and contract administration.
Interpret the obligations and responsibilities imposed by the various general conditions of contract in common use.
Prepare and record contractual claims based on good claims management practice.
Explain the benefits of web-based contract administration.
Explain the mechanisms for conflict management and dispute resolution in construction.

16466.description: This subject equips you with the skills to apply economic theory and methods to evaluate economic conditions and policies. It aims to deepen your understanding of macroeconomic theory and policy within a modern, open economy context. You'll explore key economic concepts, the interplay of demand, supply, and pricing, as well as the impact of fiscal and monetary policy on the property and construction sectors. The curriculum includes discussions on technology's role in economic growth and insights into the 2007 financial crisis. Learning is facilitated through weekly lectures complemented by online resources from Cengage Learning, offering a blend of classroom engagement and online activities.
learningOutcomes: Understand the basic principles of economics and their relevance to the property and construction industries
Apply economic theory to measurement of the economy and its management through macroeconomic policies
Explain the role and economic significance of the Australian Built Environment Sector
Apply research from behavioural economics to issues in macroeconomics and industry

Additionally, you'll understand legal sources, receive a primer on legal citation, and learn how to locate legal information.

Differentiate between legal and ethical considerations in the construction and property industry.

16470.title: Digital Design and Construction 2
16470.description: This subject equips you with advanced skills in model-based construction scheduling, focusing on the transformative impact of building information modelling (BIM) for 4D planning, scheduling, and simulation. You'll learn how 4D simulations enhance work plan accuracy, optimise temporary structure scheduling, and manage site logistics. The course covers both traditional scheduling and modern lean construction techniques, such as the last planner system, location-based management, and flowline concepts. You'll apply this knowledge to create competitive construction schedules and ensure a seamless flow of construction activities. Practical learning is delivered through workshops and computing labs, using real-world projects as a basis.

Apply knowledge of construction scheduling methodologies within a 4D modelling environment to detail and refine the construction schedule relative to workflow, site logistics, materials handling, and resource management.
Demonstrate knowledge of 4D modelling software applications relative to when and how they are used for construction and site planning.

The course guides you in identifying design requirements set by regulatory bodies, such as the National Construction Code and Australian Standards. You'll also understand how the integration of pipes, ducts, and cabling affects design, construction, and maintenance practices.

Students will know about and be able to apply professional best practices of building services in terms of design requirements, materials, terminology and technology used

Students will be able to assess the purpose (attributes and intent of application) of standard building services elements and make informed decisions about the appropriateness of alternate solutions (e.g. renewable energy, green building solutions, sustainable fire safety, etc.)

16632.description: This subject explores the foundational concepts and applications of NSW planning and environmental law. You'll learn about the NSW planning system's structure, including legislation for planning, development, pollution control, contaminated land, heritage, and biodiversity. 16634.description: In this Year 2 core subject for the Bachelor of Property Economics, you'll master the use of a financial calculator for valuing leasehold and investment properties. The subject emphasises financial theory and its practical application in property cashflow analysis and valuation. Key topics include the time value of money (TVM), capitalisation rates, interest rates, leasehold valuation, and discounted cash flow analysis. You'll learn to calculate the present value of future cash flows using various techniques. Engagement with the lecturer before class is through emails and an online quiz on the financial calculator's functions. Lectures involve practice questions and self-assessment against provided solutions to prepare for tests and exams.

16642.title: Property Investment and Valuation
16642.description:
In this second-year core subject for the Bachelor of Property Economics, you'll focus on property investment and valuation, focusing on office and retail income-producing properties. The cap rate and discounted cash flow analysis are primarily for making investment and valuation decisions. The learning experience will also include using Excel to build DCF models and conduct sensitivity and scenario analyses. Learning methods include class discussions, tutorials, learning software and independent reading.

The subject equips you with practical skills for real-life investment projects, covering investment theory, financial mathematics, capitalisation rate, net present value, internal rate of return, and factors influencing investment decisions.

Assessment ensures your proficiency in the subject's learning objectives. You'll apply class knowledge to a real-life investment project for an individual assignment and collaborate on a group assignment for a real estate case. A final exam tests your understanding of investment principles, decision-making and problem-solving skills.
learningOutcomes: Apply key investment theories and techniques to make informed property investment decisions.
Develop critical thinking and analytical skills to assess investment risks and opportunities.
Develop analyse and report results of discounted cash flow (DCF) modelling based on relevant data.
Collaborate effectively in a professional context.

16655.title: Property Finance
16655.description: In this Year 3 core subject for the Bachelor of Property Economics, you'll delve into property finance and investment theories, examining capital structure, leverage, financial analysis, funding sources, cost of capital, and financial risk management. You'll explore the practical application of finance theory, focusing on how Australian real estate companies and developers secure funding. The course provides insight into decision-making processes regarding gearing, choice of financing sources, and the financial markets commonly engaged by the real estate industry.
learningOutcomes: Analyse and apply financial theories and models in property investment and corporate finance.
Calculate key financial metrics in corporate real estate lending.
Conduct spreadsheet-based financial analyses to assess leverage impacts in property finance.
Collaborate effectively within a team to meet outcomes.

16656.title: Sustainable Construction and Development Management
16656.description:
In this subject, you'll learn about new technologies to enhance building performance, including building and site services, facilities management, and green retrofits. It addresses building pathology, from identifying defects to implementing repairs, with a focus on project and building scales, and highlights the latest innovations.

You'll receive individual feedback through in-class group reviews, with formative feedback during group projects. The teaching is designed to develop the knowledge and skills needed for assessments, enriched by guest speakers and site visits when possible.

The subject introduces sustainable construction and development management, exploring climate risk and sustainable property development, sustainability concepts, explains scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions, precinct-scale master planning, and sustainable construction practices, including cost planning, procurement and social considerations. It also covers designing for sustainability and building services to reduce environmental impact.

The subject covers managing sustainable building adaptation and reuse throughout the building lifecycle. It includes diagnosing building defects, sustainability in leasehold properties, Sydney's conversion adaptation market, international best practices, the role of 'eco-concierge', building certification, circular economy and sustainability in building services, focusing on retrofitting and adaptation.
learningOutcomes: Communicate, collaborate and apply technologies effectively in a professional context.
Demonstrate advanced understanding of sustainable construction and management technologies, practices, and applications.
Critically evaluate existing practices in construction using appropriate evidence.

16657.title: Property Investment and Portfolio Management
16657.description:
This subject equips you with a theoretical and practical understanding of the portfolio approach to investments, focusing on investment theory and strategic application. You'll learn the investment process and develop tools for informed investment and portfolio decisions.

Upon completion, you'll be able to apply modern portfolio theory, analyse risks and returns of different asset types and investment portfolios, and understand the attributes of various asset classes. You'll also explore how monetary and fiscal policies affect investment performance, measure risk and return, construct efficient portfolios, price risk, and examine investor behaviour.
learningOutcomes: Construct and communicate investment strategies based on major sources of financial market information.
Evaluate the role of risk and return in the asset allocation decision.
Explain the relationship between investment theory and practical portfolio management in light of economic policies.
Identify the attributes of different asset types and their role in a diversified portfolio.
Construct a diversified portfolio and prepare economic and financial reports to explain the investment strategy.

16658.title: Capstone Project: Property Development Analysis
16658.description: In the Capstone subject, you'll demonstrate your Property Economics expertise by crafting and presenting an Investment Development Proposal for a potential investor client. This comprehensive assessment includes site selection, planning, market research, risk and investment analysis, due diligence, and sustainable development strategies, with a focus on financial feasibility and sustainability, such as affordable housing. You'll work in teams of up to four to ensure a holistic approach, culminating in a presentation and report to the client. Emphasis is placed on professional communication, including language, tone, and infographics, to prepare you for real-world client interactions.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate team management, communication and collaboration skills.
Demonstrate written, oral and visual communication skills to present research data, analysis, judgement and proposal of solution(s) using professional presentation standards.

Complete to a professional standard a Development Property Proposal Report and be able to interpret the impact that all relevant headings in the report may have on the subject site and its potential for development/redevelopment.

Demonstrate an understanding and ability to analyse the development process from an idea inception through to the site completion, planning, market and feasibility analysis. This will include investment, equity and financing considerations, and sustainability. Additionally, consideration of possible alternative uses such as mixed use, design and construction implications should be included.
16658.requisiteText: (1 AND 2 AND 3 AND (4 OR 4a) AND 5 AND 6 AND (7 OR 7a))

16680.title: Special Topics in Property
16680.description: In this elective, you'll enhance your skills in property valuation and financial analysis, applying them to commercial property investment scenarios. The subject prepares you for the National University Real Estate Case Competition. Working in groups, you'll present acquisition recommendations using capitalisation and discounted cash flow (DCF) methods. You'll refine your financial modelling skills and learn to apply decision-making criteria like internal rate of return (IRR) and net present value (NPV), supported by suitable financing strategies. Your presentations will be critiqued by peers and expert panels, providing valuable feedback.
learningOutcomes: Apply real estate investment and finance theories and valuation techniques in real-life scenarios.
Construct financial models to assess real estate investment opportunities using IRR / NPV decision criteria.
Analyse, structure, and report the findings from research and financial modelling.
Work effectively with team members and communicate verbally and in writing professionally.

16900.title: Construction for Developing Communities
16900.description: This subject immerses you in the design and construction of residential or small-scale developments in disadvantaged communities, both domestically and internationally. It's project-based, blending cultural understanding with construction techniques pertinent to the local context. The core experience is an on-site residential workshop, where you'll join construction teams to contribute to tangible community projects, gaining hands-on experience and cross-cultural insights.
learningOutcomes: Prepare project and risk management plans for construction in developing communities.
Demonstrate an understanding of complexities and logistical issues in delivering a construction project in a developing communities.
Demonstrate an appreciation of teamwork and the delivery of a construction project in a developing community context
Recognise the economic and social challenges facing the world in housing the disadvantaged.

16913.title: Time Management
16913.description:
This subject explores time management in construction projects with a focus on key techniques such as developing work breakdown structures (WBS), estimating task duration, allocating resources, scheduling and sequencing activities, and applying critical path programming. Students will also learn to use industry-standard software tools to create construction programs.

You will tackle real-world planning and construction time management challenges by developing a project program both manually and using digital tools. To demonstrate your understanding of best practices, you will construct a WBS, allocate resources, assess productivity at task level, and program work packages, culminating in a digital presentation of your program to a project sponsor.

Mastery of construction programming is essential for effective project planning, execution, and control. This subject develops that mastery through a combination of theoretical foundations and practical application of both manual and digital time management methods.
learningOutcomes: Discuss the essential managerial attitudes and knowledge for effective construction project scheduling.
Prepare construction project programs using both manual and digital methods.
Apply knowledge of time management practices to sequence a construction project based on the clients' requirement.
Interpret and maintain construction project programs and manage delays

16914.description: This subject investigates the construction industry's effects on its workforce and the communities it serves, fostering critical debate on corporate social responsibility and human resource management. You'll aim to become a leader who guides the industry towards a more positive societal impact. Your learning stems from lectures, dialogues with industry leaders, a major team assignment, group and individual presentations of your recommendations, and independent research. The subject synthesises cutting-edge global research and best practices within a practical case study context.
learningOutcomes: Understand how your actions as managers affects the people you manage and the communities you build in.
Understand the importance of managing people and stakeholders effectively.
Engage in ethical, critical and reflective thinking when managing people and stakeholders.
Effectively engage critical and independent thinking in the interpretation of theory and its practical application in corporate social responsibility and human resource management.

17106.title: Contractual Documentation
17106.description: This subject thoroughly analyses the importance of documenting property transactions (standard contracts and Options), including the repercussions of not doing so, and the applicable laws which may be the cause of, or the remedy to, the particular issue. Students will also be taught how to draft and interpret documentation in the property development sector, and be given hands-on experience with real life transactional documentation. Students will also look at laws which may apply where there is no contractual documentation at all. While focus will be given to the laws of NSW, there will be inter-state comparative law analysis in this subject.
learningOutcomes: Understand contract law, deposits, liquidated damages, and Heads of Agreement
Understand relevant legislative requirements including "off the plan" contracts
Understand options, the steps involved in the conveyancing process and equitable doctrines
Appreciate the difference in both conveyancing law and practice as between NSW, QLD and Vic.

17107.title: Construction Law
17107.description: This subject thoroughly analyses the importance of documenting property transactions (standard construction contracts), including the repercussions of not doing so, and the applicable laws which may be the cause of, or the remedy to, the particular issue. Students will also be taught how to draft and interpret documentation in the property development sector, and be given hands-on experience with real life transactional documentation. Students will also look at laws which may apply where there is no contractual documentation at all. While focus will be given to the laws of NSW, there will be inter-state comparative law analysis in this subject.
learningOutcomes: Identify and interpret the key documents usually found in a construction document in relation to a construction contract.
Identify and describe the relevant statutes in construction law, with regards to roles and obligations for key participants in the construction industry.
Understand what the course of a construction project, and forms of security would look like from a contract law and programming perspective.
Interpret construction contracts in calculating delay claims.
Apply general contract law principles of damages to the specific area of defects in construction law. (edited)

17108.title: Construction Costing and Estimating
17108.description:
This subject examines construction cost estimating and cost planning and the procedures used by building contractors, sub-contractors and consultants when completing this work. The approach includes a mixture of theory and application, to examine techniques used by contractors when estimating the construction cost of a given design as well the techniques used by cost planners when estimating anticipated construction costs through the building design process.

The subject provides an overview of relevant industry terminology, the tendering process, progress payments, preliminaries, overheads, preparing order lists, life cycle costing, cost control and the use of historical cost data for forward planning. Additionally, the subject investigates property depreciation and the important points to consider to ensure all eligible allowances are claimed.

On completion students should know the difference between cost estimating and cost planning, be able to complete a basic cost estimate and cost plan and be in a position to critically review an estimator or cost planner’s work.
learningOutcomes: Apply estimating terminology and process.
Apply cost planning terminology and process.
Estimate and control construction costs.
Understand the complexities of property depreciation.
Understand the basic skills of a construction cost team so you can critically review their work.

17125.title: Development Feasibility and Modelling
17125.description: This subject equips you with the knowledge of residential property valuation methods, focusing on development site analysis and financial assessment. You'll gain a solid foundation in conducting feasibility studies and making critical property development decisions. The course also delves into the financial factors influencing property projects and teaches you relevant financial analysis techniques.
learningOutcomes: Use time value of money theory for financially related assessments
Assess the value of residential development sites using the direct comparison, hypothetical development, and discounted cash flow valuation approach
Demonstrate a critical perspective of valuations methodologies commonly used in undertaking the assessment of residential development sites

17126.title: Property Transactions
17126.description: This subject provides an overview of the New South Wales (NSW) legal framework regarding personal and intellectual property ownership, real estate—including title concepts, leases, mortgages, and conveyancing processes—as well as options to purchase. You'll focus on contract law, particularly in construction and joint ventures, and explore negligence, including liability for faulty advice or certification, within the context of the statute of limitations. Additionally, you'll learn about local government procedures for building, planning, and subdivision approvals in NSW, and the appeal mechanisms to the Land and Environment Court.
learningOutcomes: Appropriately apply the relevant legal framework to a range of tenure interests held in both real and personal property.
Demonstrate an understanding of the law of contract, both common and statute.
Research and demonstrate an understanding of legal source material and tenure titling and plan instruments.
Demonstrate knowledge of the Australian legal system (including the courts hierarchy and sources of law).
Critically reflect on how relevant laws will impact on daily practice in your chosen discipline.

17127.title: Valuation Methodology
17127.description: This subject delves into the valuation profession, detailing roles, functions, and the reasons behind conducting valuations. You'll explore various value types, property interests, valuation principles, and relevant case law. The course teaches valuation methods such as the Market Approach, Cost Approach, and Income Approach, equipping you to apply these to various properties and consider risk factors. You'll also review valuation reporting standards. Familiarity with a spreadsheet program like Microsoft Excel is expected.
learningOutcomes: Understand the various types of valuation reports and their purpose.
Identify the valuers role and the valuation standards.
Assess the value of property using various valuation approaches.
Prepare a valuation report incorporating the appropriate standards and analysis.

args.text: Admission into C04445 Master of Property Development

17128.title: Property Development Finance
17128.description: This subject enhances your problem-solving skills, understanding of finance theories, and their application in property development, alongside communication and client presentation abilities. You'll learn about finance sources for property developments, debt versus equity, specialised financing such as hybrids, and offshore options. The course covers project finance, evaluation techniques, and risk management. You'll develop financing strategies, build discounted cash flow (DCF) models for decision-making, and analyse risk through sensitivity and scenario analysis.
learningOutcomes: Explain financial management and finance sources for major categories of property development projects.
Critically assess the relationship between theory and practical application of financing strategies.
Apply discounted cash flow models to assist with financial design of property development projects.
Analyse and evaluate development risks.

17129.title: Property Market Risk and Analysis
17129.description:
This capstone subject aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of and related skills to determine and assess critical factors involved in achieving successful outcomes for property development projects. In this subject students are expected to synthesise their understanding gained from the previous subjects within the program. Building on a student's prior course learning in feasibility studies, planning and property development processes, this subject involves analysis of the underpinning economic factors and other dynamics when analysing specific property markets.

Using demographic, statistical and other published data, students are taught a range of skills including the application of demand and supply analysis to forecast likely demand for a project and potential price points. Property development risk analysis techniques are used to identify critical development inputs, management issues and economic variables that may create significant risks in specific projects. Risk measurement techniques including sensitivity, scenario analysis and Monte Carlo simulation, using software applications to identify, measure and manage specific project risks.
learningOutcomes: Identify and understand risk in property development.
Understand the implications of property market cycles for property development.
Identify and understand the application of risk management techniques in property development.
Demonstrate an understanding of the application of risk to potential property development scenarios and prepare a project risk assessment report.

17131.title: Construction Technology and Regulation
17131.description: This subject introduces students to the building construction industry's technology and construction management processes with particular focus on regulation and build quality. The subject is divided broadly into two component parts. The first component acquaints the student with construction technology for residential buildings. The second component deals with construction technologies for multi-storey, multi-occupancy residential construction and high-rise construction. Build quality and regulation is discussed in relation to the topic areas throughout the subject.
learningOutcomes: Understand the use of the National Construction Code, Building Code of Australia, Australian Standards and the general mechanisms that oversee building regulation and build quality.
Understand the influence of planning regulations and constructions contracts.
Understand the principles and process of residential construction methods:
Understand the principles and process of a Multi-Storey Construction Overview.

17132.title: Land Acquisition Statutory Valuation and Litigation
17132.description: This subject immerses you in the statutory valuation processes for land compensation, rating, taxing, and the implications of developer charges. You'll examine compulsory land acquisition by the government, developer impacts, and develop negotiation skills for expediting development decisions. The course prepares you to shape policy, streamline acquisition, and reform property taxes. You'll learn to assess, prepare, and defend statutory valuations for acquisitions and taxation, and to effectively present expert evidence in these matters.
learningOutcomes: Understand the principles and practice of land acquisition, statutory valuation and valuation litigation in NSW.
Understand the basis and assessment of different forms of compensation for land acquisition in NSW.
Understand the basis and assessment of land value for statutory valuation in NSW.
Understand the role of the valuer in litigation and specialist valuations.

Have an understanding of discounted cash flow valuation methodology
Have an understanding of investment analysis techniques and approaches
Develop an understanding of investment property performance measurement and reporting

17135.title: Property Development Process
17135.description: This subject offers an insight into the property development journey, from land acquisition to obtaining development approvals. You'll explore the roles of architects, surveyors, builders, and project managers within the development cycle. The course includes market analysis and pre-sales strategies. You'll examine projects from multiple perspectives, including those of developers, the community, investors, and end-users.
learningOutcomes: Understand the distinct steps of the Property Development Process and the purpose of each step.
Understand the role of various stakeholders and contributors in the Development Process – particularly the Developer/Development Manager.
Understand the concept of Development Risk and how it materialises in the Development Process and how this is managed and mitigated.

17518.title: Real Estate Asset Class Analysis
17518.description: This subject equips you with the skills to analyse real estate investments across various asset types, including residential, commercial, and specialised sectors like student accommodation. You'll learn to appreciate the nuances between property funds and going concerns, understand the value drivers, and assess risk and return for different property classes. The course examines the real asset lifecycle, due diligence in real asset decisions, and the environmental, social, and governance (ESG) implications for each asset type. You'll also explore the role of green finance in property investment, enhancing your financial analysis skills within the real estate market.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the types and main characteristics of various real estate assets.
Develop critical thinking skills by identifying and assessing the drivers and cycles of different real estate types, as well as levels of risk and return of property classes.

Make rational decisions on the type of real estate assets to invest, given a range of property alternatives by conducting due diligence around investment purpose, KPIs, risk and financial environment.
Demonstrate an understanding of ESG that impact investment decision in the asset class.

In this core subject of the Master of Property Development with a valuation sub-major, you'll explore the valuation profession's role, functions, and obligations, as well as the purposes of valuations. 17775.description: This subject delves into the statutory valuation processes for land compensation, rating, taxing, and the impact of developer charges. 17778.description: This subject equips you with the skills to create a comprehensive IPO document for real estate, suitable for listed or unlisted offerings. You'll study managed investment scheme legislation, real estate IPO research methods, and explore equity and debt as capital funding sources. You'll learn to determine suitable debt levels based on earnings risks of the asset(s) and examine different debt-to-equity scenarios and their impact on returns. This subject focuses on the principles of building a diverse asset portfolio, exploring diversification, risk, and return in the context of property asset allocation. The course will help you comprehend how external factors influence property investments and the asset allocation decision-making process. By the end of the subject, you'll be equipped to design a portfolio within a specific asset allocation strategy.

17914.title: Urban Project - Part A
17914.description:
Description

Urban Project: Part A and Urban Project: Part B offers the opportunity to urban planning and urban design students to develop an individual final research project focused on a contemporary topic within the field. Urban Project is divided across two sessions, in the first session (Part A) students complete 50% of the research and in the next session, students complete the rest 50% (Part B).

For Master of Urban Planning Students

For urban planning, this subject develops core skills that give students the ability to successfully complete rigorous and original planning problem-solving exercises. These skills enable students to design, conduct, and oversee original applied research. Students work with an academic supervisor to develop a research project of their own, including the project identification and framing, research questions, literature review, methodology design, data collection, results discussion and a completed research report on their chosen topic.

For Master of Urban Design Students

For urban design, this subject builds on the core skills gained through the previous urban design studios and further develops students’ abilities in integrating morphology analysis, urban analytics, understanding of place, and the planning environment. Students work with an academic supervisor to develop their project. After completing their project, students will have a grasp of the urban design process and how design can generate urban change whilst considering the importance of urban greening and ecology, addressing climate change challenges, and applying place-making approaches to deliver healthier and safer places.
learningOutcomes: Reflect critically on personal and diverse perspectives in analysing urban issues.
Apply a range of methods to evaluate site-specific and contextual strengths and challenges.
Develop integrated solutions addressing environmental, economic, and socio-cultural needs.
Communicate urban insights effectively through verbal, written, and visual media.
Justify proposed solutions with a clear rationale aligned with research findings and analysis.

Illustrate the process of new venture creation, social entrepreneurship and entrepreneurship within existing organisations and its value in the development of a healthy economy
Identify the fundamental determinants of competitive advantage in entrepreneurial endeavours
Conduct feasibility assessment of a new business concept

20106.title: Management Capstone
20106.description: This capstone subject synthesises and applies the knowledge gained throughout your major, integrating core disciplines comprehensively. It offers opportunities to employ your skills in research, presentation, and teamwork, culminating in submissions to relevant authorities and academic communities. You'll engage with ethical and sustainability issues while gaining practical management experience, demonstrating how various business disciplines enhance your professional expertise.
learningOutcomes: Apply theoretical approaches to work practice
Engage in critical theoretical and professional discourse
Synthesize existing theories and expertise in creative and innovative ways
Reflect on personal, social, emotional and practical issues of working in the context of a team
Develop logical, consistent plans to solve a research-in-action problem, evaluate the consequences of the solution and articulate reasons for choosing the solution in an interdisciplinary context

args.text: Admission into C10226 Bachelor of Business

20108.title: Introduction to International Business
20108.description: Explore the complexities of the international business landscape, focusing on political, economic, socio-cultural, and legal contexts, and how firms navigate these challenges. You'll learn to identify global opportunities, manage cross-border operations, and implement sustainable and ethical practices. Engage with theories and real-world case studies to understand international tensions and strategies. Learning combines lectures with practical tutorials, where you'll collaborate on cases and receive feedback to refine your understanding. Prepare by reviewing materials to maximize class benefits and performance. Regular feedback will guide your progress, complementing the Transnational Management subject to equip you with a comprehensive global business acumen.
learningOutcomes: Discuss how different macro-environmental forces influence approaches to managing international business
Examine the impact of the activities of international firms in light of sustainability and social responsibility
Apply skills in critical thinking to analyse, and proffer practical solutions to, the challenges of operating Internationally

requisite.text: Admission into C10226 Bachelor of Business

20109.title: Introduction to Strategy
20109.description: This subject is designed to give students a broad overview of the complexity of developing and implementing strategy in a local, national, and international business environment. They are encouraged to explore the context of wicked problems, contemporary challenges, ethical dilemmas and sustainability issues in different business and organisational environments. Students gain an understanding of how changes in the business and organisational environment, business modelling, competitive intelligence and scenario analysis inform and affect strategic decision-making and managerial processes.
learningOutcomes: Analyse the connections between and impacts on an organization’s strategy and innovation processes of social, technological, economic, and environmental changes
Plan for major business uncertainties using scenarios and scenario planning to design flexible strategic plans
Apply strategic management principles, analytical tools, and concepts in the construction and/or critique of a strategic plan
Justify strategic recommendations and actions in a challenging business context
Demonstrate ability to work independently and with others as a member of a team to achieve an agreed goal

requisite.text: Admission into C10226 Bachelor of Business

20110.title: Transnational Management
20110.description:
This subject introduces concepts and capabilities that are critical to navigating the complexities of managing in transnational contexts. It integrates frameworks and practices from diverse disciplinary areas, such as cross-cultural psychology, social psychology, organisational behaviour, and international human resource management, to help students address the major challenges (and opportunities) of global management.

An important learning outcome of this subject is how culture influences students' (and others’) assumptions, perceptions, attributions and behaviours, and therefore how it shapes managerial practices. The content and activities in this subject are designed to help students develop awareness and competencies to more effectively communicate, collaborate, manage and lead in culturally-diverse transnational settings.
learningOutcomes: Examine the impact of culture on themselves and others, and the cross-cultural capabilities needed to bridge cultural differences
Apply a range of management approaches to suit different transnational settings and functions, including communicating, collaborating, managing and leading
Discuss the impact on global careers of the challenges and opportunities which exist in transnational contexts

requisite.text: Admission into C10226 Bachelor of Business

20111.title: Understanding Organisations: Theory and Practice
20111.description: In this subject students consider what is theory and what is theorising in the specific context of organisations and organisation theory. They learn about both mainstream classical business theorising and some alternatives. This examination should lead to an understanding that theory and organisational reality interact, influencing and shaping each other. It then follows that the practising manager is informed by theory when defining issues, sense making and choosing practical action.
learningOutcomes: Explain the nature and roles of organisations in business and management, using different theoretical perspectives
Apply different theoretical frameworks in addressing managerial issues that confront contemporary organisations
Evaluate the uses and limitations of organisational theories and their implications in managerial and business practices
Communicate individually and in a team, sound recommendations informed by relevant literature on organisational theories that address organisational and managerial issues

requisite.text: Admission into C10226 Bachelor of Business

20112.title: Business Ethics and Sustainability
20112.description: In this subject, students explore the breadth and depth of ethical issues confronting contemporary organisations as they relate to general business practice and social and ecological sustainability. They examine major philosophical conceptualisations of ethics and apply these to critically analyse both theory and practice. The subject places particular emphasis on developing ethical vocabulary and ethical argumentation so that they are better equipped to successfully carry an ethically informed subjectivity into their organisational practice. This subject provides students with various frameworks for incorporating and critically evaluating sustainability in organisational practices and decision-making.
learningOutcomes: Critically appraise organisational and individual responses to ethical issues, conflicts and dilemmas, using relevant ethical theories and philosophies
Develop, and clearly articulate, an informed ethical position on business issues
Articulate the global sustainability landscape of principles, legal and regulatory frameworks and the social and environmental drivers of the sustainable enterprise logic
Explain the relationships between sustainability and innovation, entrepreneurship, value creation and corporate governance

requisite.text: Admission into C10226 Bachelor of Business

20115.title: International Business Capstone
20115.description:
The capstone subject engages students with the overall internationalisation process of companies. The content and assessment items help them to consolidate the knowledge and skills they have learnt in the International Business Major by integrating and applying these in a holistic manner.

Students analyse contemporary business cases and foreign market entry decisions of international firms. In doing so, they are challenged to critically analyse the practical aspects of managing in a global environment, and so gain skills that will be transferable to future work in international contexts.
learningOutcomes: Apply a range of international business theories and models to work practices and decisions relevant to global business environments
Engage with critical theoretical and professional discourse relevant to managing in global settings
Synthesise international business theories and knowledge in creative and innovative ways
Propose and justify a market entry assessment of a company’s international expansion

requisite.text: Admission into C10226 Bachelor of Business

20400.title: International Marketing
20400.description: This subject equips you with modern theoretical knowledge of international marketing and practical skills for effective global marketing management. It covers the concepts and environmental factors of international marketing before delving into the development of practical strategies tailored to diverse global markets.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate an awareness and understanding of international marketing concepts
Apply the theoretical concepts of marketing to the differing realities of the international marketplace
Demonstrate the relevance of the need for business to market internationally
Prepare an international marketing plan for a company

20505.title: The Financial System
20505.description: This subject aims to deepen your understanding of a modern financial system's operations, encompassing payment, financing, and market-risk management. You'll focus on financial institutions, markets including stocks, bonds, and foreign exchange, and derivatives like futures and options.
learningOutcomes: Discuss how the Australian financial system performs its core financial functions; the settlement of transactions, the flow of funds and risk transfer
Explain the roles and principal operations of deposit-taking financial institutions, fund management institutions and the major financial markets including the markets for derivative contracts
Describe the structure of the main financial instruments (including the plain vanilla derivative contracts) and demonstrate their use in the flow of funds and risk-transfer functions.

20507.title: Corporate Finance
20507.description: Building on the corporate finance concepts from the core subject in finance, this subject examines capital budgeting and capital structure decisions. You'll explore the cost of capital estimation and dividend decisions through both empirical and theoretical lenses, enhancing your analytical skills in finance.
learningOutcomes: Analyse and evaluate investment projects; identify and mitigate the underlying risks; and determine the appropriate funding structures
Explain how firms can use market prices in their investment decisions and how their decisions are reflected in market prices; how incentives interfere with the process of value creation
Identify the relevant parameters affecting a project; estimate their values using different approaches; and understand the implications of each approach

20508.title: Ethics in Finance
20508.description: Ethical practices instil a public trust in the fairness of markets, allowing them to function efficiently. Additionally, ethical practices by finance and investment professionals benefit all market participants and stakeholders and lead to increased investor confidence in global capital markets. The perspectives acquired in this subject are useful to students in their place of work. A framework for ethical conduct in the investment profession is presented by focusing on the CFA Institute Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct. Citing examples of the scandals that have shaken public confidence in the ethics of Wall Street, this subject explains the importance of ethics in the operation of financial institutions and in the personal conduct of finance professionals.
learningOutcomes: Explain the major intellectual theories of ethics as a basis for the analysis and resolution of ethical dilemmas in finance

Critically examine ethical standards and issues of questionable professional conduct in finance by addressing topical issues related to ethics in investment decisions, financial markets, and financial services

Relate ethical principles to the financial theory of the firm including issues related to stakeholder theory, takeovers, corporate social responsibility and accountability, and international businesses

Analyse, interpret and apply the CFA Institute Standards of Professional Conduct and recommend practices and procedures designed to prevent violations of ethical and professional practices related to financial analysis, investment management, and financial market trading.

20509.title: Applied Portfolio Management
20509.description: This subject offers practical experience in modern portfolio management, introducing Python to design and test strategies across various financial assets. You'll explore the economic underpinnings of asset price predictability and algorithmic strategy development, along with the impact of machine learning and artificial intelligence on the field. Weekly coding workshops focus on building and testing strategies using real market data, with no prior coding knowledge necessary.
learningOutcomes: Understand the effect of technological innovation on the portfolio management industry
Apply knowledge of the development process of a quantitative portfolio strategy
Analyse risk and return opportunities of a portfolio strategy using quantitative tools

20510.description: This subject introduces the portfolio approach to investments, applying mean-variance diversification to portfolio construction and management. You'll review asset pricing models and their application to investment strategies, covering bond management, active and passive strategies, and investment performance measurement.
learningOutcomes: Discuss the role of risk and return in the investment management process;
Appraise theories relating to asset pricing and portfolio choice;
Evaluate risky asset classes and associated risk management techniques;
Identify problems and issues in investment management

20511.title: Financial Metrics for Decision Making
20511.description: This subject serves as an introduction to financial decision-making and the role of (big) data in financial decisions. It enables students to make smart decisions, such as management finance decisions, personal savings decisions and investment decisions. The starting point is the traditional paradigm, which assumes that individuals have rational beliefs (with Bayesian updating when new information arrives) and the objective of maximising their expected utilities. This view is enriched, using models of decision-making based on research in psychology, which allow for beliefs that are not fully rational, as well as for alternative preferences and limits to cognition. Using real data, students calculate the metrics used to make financial decisions, they learn how to apply decision-making rules to those metrics, and they discover the systematic pitfalls and biases that plague decision-making, as well as techniques for overcoming them.
learningOutcomes: Describe various decision-making techniques and explain the roles of financial metrics, utility theory, prospect theory and systematic biases in financial decision-making
Recommend a financial decision based on data, using appropriate financial and statistical concepts and techniques
Identify cognitive biases and analyse their impact on corporate behaviour and asset prices

20512.title: Derivative Securities
20512.description: This subject enhances your understanding of key derivative securities—forwards, futures, swaps, and options—in global markets. You'll learn derivatives pricing, arbitrage principles, and their application in hedging and trading. Through practical problems, you'll hone technical skills in risk management and strategy evaluation for various derivative contracts, essential for a finance career.
learningOutcomes: Explain derivatives pricing and use standard pricing formulae
Discuss financial risks and how to manage them
Illustrate the use of derivatives in the management of financial risks and in exploring financial arbitrage
Analyse and formulate derivative trading positions and strategies for financial trading purposes

20513.title: Applied Financial Decision Making (Capstone)
20513.description: As the final subject in the Finance Major, Applied Financial Decision Making integrates theory and practice, enhancing decision-making skills across various financial contexts. Through case studies and real-world data, you'll navigate the complexities of personal wealth, investment and risk management, corporate finance, capital structure, executive pay, venture capital, and ethics. This hands-on approach prepares you for practical financial decision-making.
learningOutcomes: Apply financial analysis tools to financial valuation and capital budgeting using business data and other relevant information.
Make financial decisions based on the analysis of real-life business problems.
Demonstrate technical and professional skills through application of financial instruments, and analysis of the institutions and markets in which finance is practiced.
Present results and findings of financial analyses and their implications to inform stakeholder actions.

20705.description: This subject provides students with the tools necessary to describe and analyse financial data. Analyse financial data and produce forecasts using appropriate statistical and analytical methods

20721.description: This subject is designed to provide an understanding of the investment process and to develop a set of tools for making investment and portfolio decisions. 20741.description: This subject examines the structure and behaviour of Australia's financial system and its main components. Its principal topics are the instruments and processes through which financing is arranged, the pricing of instruments and the associated risks and their management with derivatives. The subject forms part of the finance specialisation in the MBA and Master of Business degree programs where it provides a preparation for more specialised subjects in investment management, international finance and the various subjects that deal with financial institutions and risk management.

20747.title: Accounting for Managerial Decisions
20747.description:
This subject aims to expose students to the nature and use of accounting information as used by managers to plan and control business operations as well as for decision support. The subject is intended to prepare students to understand and use accounting information for decision support, analysing historical operations and planning future business activity. It provides a sound grounding in the application of accounting concepts and techniques used to gain intelligence about all aspects of business operations.

The topics comprise a mix of financial and management accounting. The financial accounting topics concern the basic financial statements, their analysis and the concepts and procedures that underpin their preparation. The management accounting topics relate to cost and profit planning, and the use and application of financial information to support management decision activity for both routine and non-routine business situations.
learningOutcomes: Explain the purpose, content and format of financial statements and the methods used by accountants to prepare these statements
Apply skills in analysing, recording and reporting accounting information including through the use of computerised accounting systems
Explain the role of management accounting information in managerial decision-making and apply basic management accounting techniques

By using current material from the Chartered Alternative Investments Association (CAIA), students study material deemed relevant by the industry. As preparation for employment, the course assessments are designed to improve critical thinking, report writing and quantitative abilities. Class discussion and involvement are encouraged.

evaluate the strategies and risks involved with a range of alternative investments including, real estate, commodities, private equity, equity hedge funds and global macro hedge funds

articulate lessons from the alternative investments industry via cases and the state of regulation globally

It investigates environmental, social and governance (ESG) issues and the ways in which these can be addressed using financial instruments, a sustainable financial system and investment decisions that focus on sustainability. Current industry practice is analysed and incorporated into the underlying theories. The subject draws on the experience and expertise of senior academics and industry practitioners.

apply critical analytical decision-making tools and techniques to the valuation of green finance instruments
evaluate the techniques applied to sustainability in financial decisions

Effectively communicate the results of quantitative and qualitative analysis to investors and corporate executives
