20865.title: Digital and Decentralised Markets
20865.description: This subject introduces you to financial markets and their transformation through technologies such as automation, blockchain, and smart contracts. You will develop an understanding of how financial markets operate, their role in the economy, and their impact on businesses and investment decisions, as well as the tools and frameworks used to assess market quality and efficiency. The subject examines developments in traditional markets, including algorithmic trading and regulatory change, alongside emerging areas such as Financial Technology (FinTech) and Decentralised Finance (DeFi). You will explore topics such as blockchain, tokenisation, decentralised exchanges, and non-fungible tokens, and consider the associated risks, challenges, and future directions of these innovations.
learningOutcomes: Analyse the impact of market architectures and market design features on trading and market efficiency
Explain the key roles of financial markets, and their interactions with asset pricing and companies
Critically evaluate technology-driven innovations in financial markets
Evaluate and assess financial market quality using empirical techniques

20883.title: AI-Driven Compliance, Anomaly and Fraud Detection
20883.description: This subject examines the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to support compliance and fraud detection in financial systems. You will develop a conceptual understanding of key AI techniques, including data integration, feature engineering, ensemble methods, and text mining, and learn how these approaches can be used to identify patterns, detect anomalies, and generate actionable insights from financial data. Through real-world examples, you will explore the application of AI in analysing complex datasets and supporting evidence-based decision-making. The subject also considers the ethical and regulatory challenges associated with AI, including algorithmic bias, data privacy, and the need for transparency and accountability. By the end of the subject, you will be equipped to apply AI tools to identify financial risks, support compliance processes, and make informed decisions in professional finance contexts.
learningOutcomes: Critically evaluate AI technologies for compliance, anomaly detection, and fraud prevention in finance
Critically evaluate and mitigate ethical risks of AI in financial contexts
Analyse and solve finance problems using AI-driven approaches
Communicate AI insights effectively to diverse stakeholders

Diagnose employee underperformance issues and critically evaluate strategies for improving performance through fair and proper procedures.

21440.title: Management Skills
21440.description: This subject prepares you with the theoretical and practical tools needed for a successful career in management. We draw on theories such as positive psychology and positive organisational scholarship to create thriving, sustainable organisations that place a premium on employee wellbeing, optimal functioning and cultural inclusion. The subject has been designed around three themes (i) foundations of self-knowledge and understanding, (ii) managing the self at work, and (iii) managing thriving workplaces. 21698.title: Managing for Social Impact (Capstone)
21698.description:
In today's world, businesses face complex social and environmental challenges. Success now depends on balancing economic goals with positive social outcomes. This subject explores how organisations can create sustainable value for society and the environment, and how managers can analyse, communicate and lead effective social impact.

In this subject, you will undertake empirical research with a team, and interact with industry and community leaders, to understand the impact of businesses on social and environmental issues. As a result, you will develop strategies to solve an organisation's pressing challenges, in turn facilitating their sustainable operations and objectives for broader social impact. By the subject’s conclusion, your managerial capabilities and technical skills will be enhanced through professional career development workshops supporting your entrance to professional practice in a specialised industry sector.
learningOutcomes: Critically analyse complex issues and problems in managing social impact
Apply current knowledge of disciplinary and inter-disciplinary theory on managing social impact to public, private and not-for-profit organisations to develop appropriate and well justified solutions
Communicate complex solutions and information in high quality, multimedia formats for the intended audience and social impact purpose
Reflect upon personal management styles, knowledge and practices to achieve effective social impact outcomes within a diverse range of contexts and situations
Apply knowledge of Indigenous Australian contexts to inform professional capabilities to work with and for Indigenous Australians across management professions

21699.title: Diversity Management
21699.description:
Understanding diversity and inclusion is not just a matter of political correctness; it is about fostering environments where every individual feels valued and respected. With workplaces becoming increasingly diverse, it is crucial to equip yourself with the knowledge and skills necessary to navigate this landscape effectively.

In this subject, you will delve deep into the theories and practices underpinning diversity management, unravelling how they translate into real-world contexts. Immersive case studies, in areas such as disability, gender, sexuality, and race, and a micro-placement with a diversity-focused organisation, will prepare you to address complex diversity and inclusion challenges in future professional endeavours. By the subject's conclusion, you will emerge with a comprehensive grasp of diversity and inclusion dynamics within organisational settings and be well-prepared to confront discrimination and unconscious bias, championing inclusivity as a cornerstone of your professional journey.
learningOutcomes: Analyse the interrelations between identity, organisations, and systems of power
Critique mainstream theories and practices of diversity management
Apply theories of diversity and inclusion to analyse organisations and society
Integrate theory with workplace integrated learning (WIL) to improve diversity and inclusion practices

21720.title: Human Resource Management
21720.description:
This subject presents an introduction to the field of human resource management (HRM). Topics covered include the role and importance of strategic HRM; ethical considerations in HRM, managing knowledge, the importance of effective HR talent attraction and retention; the contribution of various HR functions such as recruitment, selection, motivation, rewards and incentives, performance management and appraisal, as well as training and development; and the role of key stakeholders.

The subject investigates frameworks that assist with crafting an effective HRM, identifying challenges (including ethical issues) and devising solutions. The subject also examines employee engagement and leading edge HRM analytics. A key component of the subject is gaining skills in the ability to think critically about crafting a HRM system for global and Indigenous cultures, as well as the ability to use HRM tools that enhance organisational outcomes.

The principal focus of the lectures and tutorials is to develop an understanding of the key issues and to understand current issues and debates. The material will be presented through lectures, class discussion, case studies (short videos and/or readings) and active learning. Our emphasis on active application is reflected in a major focus on experiential learning via storytelling, roleplay and narrative, video etc. This includes extensive collaboration among peers. Students will receive formative feedback during class and through assessments. This includes formative feedback from their teachers and peers provided prior to census date through online materials and in-class practice presentations.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate the various HRM roles and processes and their contribution to enhancing organisational success and social impact
Apply the insights from relevant research to analyse and improve HRM practices
Design HRM practices in global contexts
Communicate information to persuade and motivate diverse stakeholders
Work effectively in teams to achieve a collective purpose

21877.description:
Strategic and sustainable procurement, a critical part of effective supply chain management, sets strategic priorities and direction for procurement to aligns with an enterprise's business goals. It is a data-driven, enterprise-wide process which minimizes supply risk and emphasizes on acquiring goods or services of the right quality, at the right price, and in time to ensure enterprise's sustainable growth.

This subject address strategic procurement management, covering its role as a strategic function and key issues like outsourcing, sourcing strategies, total cost of ownership, procurement social responsibility, category management and negotiations. You'll explore various procurement applications, including international sourcing, capital procurement, and e-procurement, with a focus on corporate social responsibility. The course aims to equip you with concepts and strategies to optimise procurement practices, enhancing your organisation's competitive edge.
learningOutcomes: Appraise the strategic nature of the procurement function in organizations
Design efficient and effective procurement strategies and systems to solve complex strategic procurement problems
Communicate procurement plan, strategies and systems clearly to a diverse range of stakeholders
Work effectively with procurement and supply chain stakeholders to deliver negotiated project outcomes
Critically reflect on ethical practice to influence professional capabilities to work with and for Indigenous peoples in procurement

21889.title: Future of Work
21889.description: Future of Work considers the HR and management issues arising from new technologies and examines how these emerging technologies are driving rapid changes in where and how people work. You will consider the impact of artificial intelligence and automation on productivity and job security and how new modes of work, such as 'gig work', hybrid and remote work are disrupting traditional approaches to management. You will examine how mega trends such as globalization and climate change accelerate economic and social change and consider the human dimension of rapid change such as job loss or 'job obsolescence', job satisfaction and psychosocial risks such as loneliness and burnout. You will then evaluate the many different ways we may mitigate human and societal risk arising from rapid change. The subject considers likely areas of future job loss, the sociology of human-technology interaction and emerging inter and intra personal issues such as work family conflict, skills loss and social isolation. Future of work competencies are considered as are the legal and ethical issues arising from new technologies such as surveillance and privacy. Tutorials entail experiential learning, group work and case-based learning.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate the importance of current developments in technology, culture and society for the practice of human resource management
Integrate theory, technology, and data insights to inform ethical HRM decision making
Critically analyse emerging human resource management issues with consideration of contextual factors
Develop plans for future of work trends grounded in critical reflections of past and emerging practices

21946.description:

Technological advances, new products with shorter life cycles, intense global competition, and rising customer expectations have spurred new procurement and supply chain management strategies. Data driven decision making assists procurement and supply chain manager to design right strategies and manage performance in a competitive and dynamic business environment. Supply chain management analytics is pivotal to data driven decision making which enables organizations to optimize processes, reduce lead times, minimize stockouts and streamline operations.

This subject focuses on the supply chain management analytics for an effective and efficient design of supply chain networks to minimize supply chain cost while managing service quality and performance. You'll explore strategic sourcing, procurement strategies, sales and operations plan, demand-side logistics, distribution strategies, and market behaviour's impact on supply chain design. Tactically, you'll learn cost patterns, efficient sourcing, forecasting, layout design, supply chain network optimization, data analysis, distribution, and warehousing and supply chain performance management. These insights will help you strategise and align logistics and supply chain networks dynamically, enabling you to implement practices that enhance cost and service performance for global competitiveness.
learningOutcomes: Formulate and implement appropriate SCM strategies and managing supply chain performance using SCM analytics tools and techniques
Analyse supply chain strategies and performance parameters to improve customer satisfaction through cost and service optimisation
Design and re-design global supply chains to cope with increased volatility so as to align sourcing segments, procurement strategies, logistics strategies and market segments

Appraise how to govern the intersection of procurement management and supply chain networks and the intersection of logistics strategies and market segments for managing costs and service level tradeoffs
Evaluate the operational dynamics in global logistics and distribution e.g. practical tactics to storage, transportation, order picking, packing, material movement and physical control

21947.title: Supply Chain Risk Management
21947.description:
This subject addresses the challenges of risk and complexity in supply chains within volatile environments, drawing on Yossi Sheffi's concept of the resilient enterprise. You'll explore how organisational resilience is essential for managing the uncertainties of interconnected societies and economies, focusing on developing an organic capability to respond to disruptions. The subject delves into managing risk and complexity in global supply chains, equipping you with skills to devise strategies for uncertain conditions.

You'll learn about resilience in supply chains, identify risk sources, understand the role of procurement strategies and insurance in risk management, make informed decisions, and lead in mitigating risks. These skills are vital for stakeholders managing operations, designing supply chains, managing customer expectations, and delivering service experiences to enhance resilience, competitiveness, and profitability. Additionally, you'll discuss the ethical and social responsibilities associated with supply chain risks.
learningOutcomes: Engage and collaborate with stakeholders to design resilient supply chains
Apply tools and techniques to solve supply chain risk problems and communicate them to supply chain stakeholders to improve project outcomes
Work in a team to critically evaluate managerial decisions to analyse supply chain risk factors and their mitigation strategies for improving business, environmental and societal outcomes
Reflect on the impact of supply chain risk management practices on organisational resilience

22320.description:
This subject equips you with the skills necessary to apply accounting treatments for business combinations within the Australian context. Learning unfolds through weekly pre-recorded lecture materials that introduce technical and theoretical concepts, supplemented by practical examples. This is followed by face-to-face interactive workshops where you will engage in class discussions of demonstration questions and case studies. It is essential that you read the lecture materials before attending the workshops. Tutorials are designed to reinforce lecture content and develop hands-on accounting skills.

You are encouraged to come prepared to discuss and solve assigned problems. As part of the assessments, you will also participate in a group project to analyse a recent M&A case to bring more real-world relevance into your learning. You will receive timely feedback through Canvas, class interactions, assessments, and forum responses.

Prepare financial statements for economic entities that accounts for subsidiaries, associates and joint ventures, and provides segment information
Implement accounting and reporting techniques to non-routine circumstances and new events
Discuss, in written form, the appropriate accounting treatment applicable in the given circumstances.

22705.title: Management Planning and Control
22705.description:
This subject develops your understanding of how management accounting and control practices can be used to achieve organisational objectives. You will learn about the role and impact of budgets, performance metrics, and managerial incentives, in guiding employee behaviours. You will also explore how these practices differ across firms and the influence of technology on accounting processes.

Your learning involves weekly three-hour seminars, blending lectures with group and individual activities that mirror professional scenarios. Prior to sessions, you will engage with materials and tasks that contribute to your learning portfolio, which forms part of your subject assessment. Case studies throughout the course illustrate real-world applications, enhancing your grasp of the content. Demonstrate how information and communications technology influences management decision-making and control

This subject equips you with the knowledge and technical expertise needed to conduct external audits that provide assurance over the financial statement of publicly listed companies. You'll engage in active learning through a blend of workshops and practical tutorial activities, where you'll apply your knowledge to tackle case studies that analyse real corporate failures. You will be assessed on your ability to make critical judgements, identify audit risks, communicate effectively, and provide strategic audit recommendations. 22789.title: Financial Analytics
22789.description:
In Financial Analytics, you will learn to utilise data to solve real-world financial challenges and drive business decisions. Through hands-on experience with industry-standard tools and techniques, you will develop the essential skills needed in today's data-driven financial world.

You will learn to ask the right questions when approaching financial problems and identify which data can help answer them. Central to your learning will be mastering the IMPACT analytics framework, giving you a structured approach to tackle any financial analytics project. This framework will guide you in developing practical skills in cleaning and preparing both financial and non-financial datasets for analysis.

Throughout the subject, you will create data visualisations that tell clear stories about financial trends and patterns, while applying statistical techniques to uncover meaningful relationships in financial data. You will build your ability to translate complex analytical findings into clear recommendations for business stakeholders, ensuring your insights drive real business value.

By the end of the subject, you will be able to approach financial problems systematically, choose appropriate analytical techniques, and communicate your insights effectively. These skills will position you to make meaningful contributions to financial decision-making in any organisation.

Collaborate with colleagues and a range of stakeholders to deliver negotiated business outcomes
Critically evaluate data practices to improve analytical processes to drive positive and equitable outcomes
Design and implement analytical approaches using appropriate software tools to extract insights from financial data for decision-making

22805.title: Data Governance and Regulation
22805.description:
In this subject, you will explore the principles and practices of data governance and regulation essential for modern business analytics. You will develop a comprehensive understanding of the legal, ethical, and regulatory frameworks that govern how organisations collect, use, and manage data. You will learn about critical areas including data privacy, security, quality, and ownership.

You will discover how to implement robust data governance policies and procedures to ensure compliance with key regulations such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the Australian Privacy Principles (APPs). You will also examine the ethical dimensions of data practices, developing frameworks to address issues of fairness and accountability in data-driven decision-making. Upon completion, you will be equipped to navigate the complex landscape of data governance and lead the implementation of responsible data practices within organisations.
learningOutcomes: Critically evaluate data governance and ethical frameworks and practices to ensure they drive positive and equitable outcomes in organisations
Analyse and apply ethical principles and regulatory requirements in the context of data collection, management, and use
Assess the implications of national and international data protection regulations on organisational data practices
Reflect on the rights to consent, privacy, data sovereignty and self determination to work ethically with and for Indigenous Australians as business analytics professionals

23002.title: Market Design
23002.description:
This subject equips you with the knowledge and ability to analyse strategic decision-making, a new area of economic science. You will see how this changes our understanding of the way markets work and then you’ll use this understanding to explore the rules that govern markets and how they can be designed to produce better social outcomes. The markets you study will include online auctions, government auctioning of natural resources, matching markets (for example, where students must be matched to classes or schools, medical patients to hospitals, or kidneys to recipients), health care markets and electricity markets.

Your learning will combine lectures with tutorials, fostering an interactive environment in which theory meets practice, preparing you for the challenges of working in real markets and helping to improve their operation and performance.
learningOutcomes: understand the field of market design, its applications and the associated engineering concerns
develop reasonable solutions to real work market design problems and evaluated their theoretical performance
use economic theory, experiments and empirical analysis to assess market rules and institutions

Design experiments to compare the performance of alternative trading mechanisms and solutions to social dilemmas

23021.title: Labour Economics
23021.description:
This subject equips you with the analytical tools to understand and evaluate the functioning of labour markets, particularly in Australia. You'll learn to apply economic theories to explain employer and employee behaviour, and analyse labour market outcomes such as wages and employment. You will critically assess the impact of labour market policies and shocks - such as minimum wage laws, anti-discrimination regulations, family-friendly policies, education subsidies and technological changes- on labour markets.

Your learning journey will comprise interactive lectures and tutorials, where you'll engage with real-world scenarios and policy debates. Online resources, including lecture materials and discussion forums, support your studies, allowing you to download content, complete assessments, and collaborate with peers and lecturers. Expect prompt feedback on weekly tasks and comprehensive reviews of major assignments to enhance your understanding of labour markets.
learningOutcomes: describe institutions and historical trends relevant to Australian labour markets as well as sources of individual differences in wages and employment
apply formal microeconomic frameworks to analyse a range of labour market phenomena
critically evaluate government policies with respect to their effects on wages and employment.

23115.title: Economics for Business
23115.description:
This subject equips you with an understanding of foundational economic principles and the ability to analyse consumer and business behaviour. You’ll also explore the interaction of these parties in various market contexts, you’ll examine different types of government policy, and you’ll learn how these policies can affect the economic environment. Economic relations between countries is also something that you’ll be able to explain after you’ve completed this subject. Your skills in analysing economic forces will be developed as will your ability to articulate the results of your analysis in written form.

Learning combines lectures on key concepts and their practical application, with tutorials focused on problem-solving and case studies. You're expected to engage with pre-class readings and problems so that you can contribute effectively to classroom discussion. Additionally, online exercises provide feedback on your grasp of key ideas, while a moderated discussion board facilitates peer and instructor interaction.
learningOutcomes: Explain the core principles of market competition and market failures, the characteristics of a variety of market structures and the main factors shaping the macroeconomic environment in which consumers and businesses operate

Analyse and predict the effects of government policies and other economic forces on consumer and business behaviour, market outcomes, and the macroeconomic environment, while considering the impacts of these economic decisions on social welfare, equity, and the environment
Interpret and critically evaluate economic commentary in the media
Communicate economic analysis clearly in written form, tailoring the content to be appropriate and accessible for the intended audience
Critically reflect on how Indigenous experiences intersect with sustainable policies to inform employment decisions that support Indigenous communities

23505.title: Economics of Monetary Policy and Central Banking
23505.description:
This subject will enable you to develop a comprehensive understanding of monetary policy, central banking and financial regulation. It uses models developed in Intermediate Macroeconomics to explore the challenges faced by central banks in the twenty-first century, especially the conduct of monetary policy, responses to and prevention of financial crises, and management of the new tools of macro-prudential regulation.

Learning is facilitated by class preparation, interactive problem-based discussion and writing tasks that apply frameworks from monetary economics to either a policy issue of current significance or a conceptual issue with important policy implications. Your written communication skills will be honed as you apply theoretical frameworks to current policy problems or important controversies in monetary economics.
learningOutcomes: Articulate the role of central banks within the macroeconomy and analyse the challenges of implementing monetary policy using appropriate formal models
Explain the nature and causes of financial crises, and critique various policies that have been advocated to limit the occurrence and effects of such crises

Critically reflect on the changing nature of central banking in recent years and assess complications that have emerged between the operation of monetary policy and other forms of financial regulation
Effectively communicate their explanations and analysis of monetary phenomena in written form

23510.title: Economic Inequality
23510.description:
This subject will help you develop an understanding of the nature and causes of inequalities in wealth and income that characterise the world. You’ll learn about global as well as local dimensions of inequality, and you’ll explore the nature of disparities between various population sub-groups including indigenous peoples, and how these disparities change over time.

You'll learn to measure inequality, to differentiate between outcome and opportunity disparities, and to use economic theories in explaining these phenomena. Factors such as capital, labour, technological change, globalisation, education, financialisation and institutional structures will all become concepts at your disposal to analyse the drivers of inequality. Additionally, you'll assess government policies aimed at reducing inequality. Your learning combines online lectures, self-study and interactive tutorials, where you'll engage with case studies and group discussions to reinforce your knowledge.
learningOutcomes: Discuss the relationships between equity, equality of outcomes and opportunities, and poverty
Compare and contrast the ways in which inequality can be measured
Describe how inequality has evolved over time within and between countries and sub-populations and its consequences for those countries and sub-populations
Discuss the determinants of various types of inequality
Analyse how various government policies may be used to mitigate against the various types of inequality and their consequences
Critically evaluate the claim that rising inequality is inevitable

23569.title: Economic Growth, Development and Sustainability
23569.description: This subject will help you explore the nature of economic growth, the various explanations economists have offered for the process of growth, and the relationship between growth and economic development, particularly in poorer countries. You will consider how economic growth has played such an important role in raising living standards in a number of countries around the world since the industrial revolution and analyse why the effects of that growth have been so unevenly distributed. You will also acquire the conceptual tools to assess recent calls for a re-think of the emphasis placed on economic growth given the link between growth and climate change. You will examine the potential limits on growth and consider what a sustainable and globally just approach to growth might look like by paying careful attention to the development needs of poorer nations.
learningOutcomes: Explain the impacts of unequal material prosperity
Analyse the determinants of economic growth and its relationship to development and sustainability

23571.description:
This subject will enable you to develop a good working knowledge of regression analysis and model-building techniques, essential for empirical work in business and other ework environments. You'll learn the skill of using regression models to quantify the causal effect of one economic factor on another, and being able to make predictions about the future course of economic variables depending on the behaviour of their drivers. This will significantly extend your analytical abilities.

Teaching combines lectures on core concepts with applications, and tutorials with the opportunity for hands-on experience with statistical software. You'll be expected to engage with pre-uploaded materials, to actively participate in problem-solving during tutorials, and to utilise additional practice problems in your own study time that will reinforce your learning. Consultation hours are available for personalised support, ensuring that you gain a robust grasp of econometrics for professional use.
learningOutcomes: derive least squares estimators and their properties
build multiple regression models using real-world data
interpret multiple regression coefficients and conduct inference
explain the properties of regression models with different functional forms.

23580.title: Contemporary Economic Perspectives (Capstone)
23580.description: This capstone subject will enable you to draw together, extend and apply many of the key ideas and frameworks that you have previously encountered in your economics major in both microeconomics and macroeconomics subjects. You’ll extend your knowledge by building various explanations for why nations trade with each other, and you’ll look at modern trade patterns and differences in economic circumstances around the world. You’ll also develop the complementary skills of looking at economic reasoning through a critical lens and applying economic reasoning in novel ways. You’ll explore current issues such as global inequality, economic nationalism and policy responses to trade imbalances. Your learning unfolds through interactive lectures and tutorials, completing tasks that will enhance your public speaking and presentation skills, and solving numerical problems.
learningOutcomes: Analyse global economic issues and key international organizations using macro- and microeconomic models and theories to propose analytically-sound solutions
Communicate complex economic analysis to diverse audiences
Evaluate implications of mainstream economic policies in order to improve social and ethical outcomes
Collaborate with peers to conduct research and develop policy proposals which address contemporary economic challenges
Critically reflect on how Indigenous experiences intersect with economic policies to address income inequality and promote equitable outcomes for Indigenous communities

23600.title: Economic Policy and Analysis (Capstone)
23600.description: This capstone subject for the Bachelor of Economics equips you with the ability to bring together, reflect on and apply to real-world problems many of the economic principles that you have learned across your degree. There is an emphasis on the logic and impact of economic policies in areas such as poverty, sustainability and public health. You'll learn to assess how rules and incentives influence economic outcomes, and you’ll develop competencies in applied research and policy evaluation. Learning involves lectures, group discussions, and self-directed research, culminating in presentations and a policy report to refine your policy analysis skills. Pre-class activities require you to engage with readings and contribute to online discussions, fostering critical thinking and collaboration. You'll undertake individual and team projects, presenting your research and writing a policy paper, with ongoing feedback to guide your progress. Additionally, the subject strengthens your academic and professional language capabilities, vital for career success, and includes an assessment of your English language proficiency.

Develop an appropriate empirical strategy to analyse the policy-relevant research problem, that can include the effects of economic decisions on social welfare, equity, or the environment

23706.title: Economics for Management
23706.description:
This subject equips you with a thorough understanding of the core principles of both microeconomics and macroeconomics, essential for effective business management. You'll develop the ability to recognise the forces of supply and demand, to predict basic aspects of consumer behaviour, to account for production costs, and to identify the price-setting options available to firms in a range of market contexts. You’ll also learn to interpret larger-scale economic phenomenon relevant for the performance of firms such as the determinants of gross domestic product and growth, the likely course of consumer price inflation, movements in unemployment, and the forces that affect interest rates.

You'll be expected to engage actively, completing pre-class multiple-choice and short-answer questions, and participating in discussions on articles about current issues affecting the Australian economy. In-class exercises, including interactive media, enhance your understanding, while peer-assisted study sessions offer additional support. Attendance is crucial, and for those needing language support, completion of an online language screening task and subsequent tutorials is mandatory to pass.
learningOutcomes: Explain the key principles of macro/microeconomic analysis and the forces that determine key economic indicators that impact on the local and global economy
Select, manipulate and interpret economic data to analyse economic conditions and developments
Apply economic models and frameworks to the analysis of complex business issues
Report the findings of economic analyses to inform business decision-making

25300.title: Fundamentals of Business Finance
25300.description: The subject introduces and develops the core technical and theoretical concepts of Finance and illustrates their application to practical financial decision-making problems. Two crucial concepts are introduced: (1) the time-value of money (TVM); and (2) financial risk. TVM techniques are applied to the valuation and management of financial instruments, such as annuities, perpetuities and amortising loans, and to financial securities, such as stocks and bonds. Different ways of measuring financial risk are considered and the fundamental relationship between risk and return is demonstrated empirically and explained. TVM and risk analysis techniques are applied to investment and financing decision problems in a Corporate Finance context. In particular, students learn how firms decide which projects to invest in and how they choose to raise the capital to fund those investments.

25881.title: AI-integrated Sustainable Finance
25881.description: With the advent of climate change, health crises, and global pollution there is a global trend and need for responsible investing and sustainable finance practices. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has tremendous potential to accelerate and industrialise evidence-based, data-driven sustainable finance, ESG-related decision making, and climate risk management. Natural language processing (NLP) and spatial AI have become leading technologies in this area, as have simulations, digital twins, virtual worlds, and omniverse. Asset managers, asset owners, banks, insurance companies, regulators, and central banks are increasingly applying ESG criteria as part of their analysis process to identify material risks and growth opportunities. Developments in AI and machine learning have led to the creation of a new type of ESG data that do not necessarily rely on information provided by companies. In this subject we review the use of AI in the ESG field: textual analysis to measure firms’ incidents or verify the credibility of companies’ concrete commitments, satellite and sensor data to analyse companies’ environmental impact or estimate physical risk exposures, machine learning to fill missing corporate data (e.g., greenhouse gas emissions). We discuss potential challenges, in terms of transparency, manipulation risks and costs associated with these new data and tools.
learningOutcomes: Examine AI technologies that facilitate ESG compliance, enhance sustainable finance practices, and support effective climate risk management in the finance industry
Evaluate and mitigate ethical risks associated with AI implementation in financial contexts
Analyse and solve complex finance-related problems using AI-driven approaches
Communicate AI-driven insights effectively to diverse stakeholders
Critically reflect on ethical considerations and social responsibility in AI applications for finance

25882.title: AI-powered Investment and Risk Management
25882.description: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has revolutionised the investment profession, enabling investment managers to process vast amounts of data, identify patterns, and make informed decisions with unprecedented speed and accuracy. The subject provides practical skills in leveraging AI techniques for investment decision-making and risk management in the modern financial markets. Students will explore the intersection of AI and investment management, highlighting the transformative role of AI in enhancing investment strategies, risk analysis, and portfolio optimisation. For instance, robo-advisors have gained popularity as automated investment platforms that utilise AI algorithms to provide personalised investment advice and portfolio management services to individual investors. In quantitative trading, AI models analyse historical data to identify market inefficiencies and execute trades automatically, capitalising on short-term price discrepancies. In this subject, students learn the principles, methodologies, and practical applications of AI in investment and risk management. Through hands-on exercises and projects, students will apply these techniques to analyse financial market data, evaluate investment strategies, construct optimised portfolios, and quantify and manage various financial risks. The course will also address the ethical considerations associated with the use of AI in investment and risk management, such as bias and fairness, interpretability of AI models, and the impact of algorithmic decision-making on market dynamics.
learningOutcomes: Examine AI technologies that enhance investment strategies, optimise portfolios, and improve risk management practices in the financial industry
Evaluate and mitigate ethical risks associated with AI implementation in financial contexts, focusing on bias, fairness, and the interpretability of AI models
Analyse and solve complex finance-related problems using AI-driven approaches
Communicate AI-driven insights effectively to diverse stakeholders
Critically reflect on the impact of AI on market dynamics and the overall investment landscape, considering both opportunities and potential challenges

It is therefore crucial that a future workforce develop a deep understanding of the healthcare system and the way health care is financed, purchased and provided. As such, there is a high need to develop workforce skills to evaluate and optimise the utilisation of technologies in healthcare systems. This subject provides students with an understanding of the economics of health and health care, and enables them to apply analytical economics skills to problems of resource allocation in the health system. Furthermore, it provides students with a critical understanding of the principles, techniques and real-world application of health technology assessment, clinical evidence synthesis, patient outcomes and economic modelling.

26899.title: Postgraduate Business Internship
26899.description:
In this subject, you’ll enhance your professional and business skills while gaining valuable hands-on experience in the workplace. This is your opportunity to explore your career path in a meaningful way.
You will participate in work-integrated learning (WIL), allowing you to connect your university studies with real-world professional experiences.

This subject is available to graduate students in the UTS Business School with an elective. To enrol, you’ll need to secure an internship of 100-180 hours and follow the steps on the UTS Business School’s Internship website. You must have your internship officially approved before enrolling in this subject.

You’ll work with your host organisation to agree on the internship details and ensure your work experience aligns with learning objectives designed to help you succeed.

For more information, go to Postgraduate internship subjects.

Students may not enrol business internship subject in the last session of study to ensure that completion of required hours of work will not impact on graduation and/or international students' visa conditions.

Any protections, safeguards, and access to insurance cover referred to in the UTS Internships Management Policy and related procedures do not apply to you who choose to source and undertake an internship without formal UTS approval (even though an internship may be required by your course).
learningOutcomes: Communicate complex ideas and concepts to influence business outcomes
Critically reflect on personal and professional development, identifying strategies for future improvement
Evaluate the importance of cultural awareness, ethical decision-making, and social responsibility in your future professional practice
Apply prior learning and knowledge to professional experience

The thesis should advance knowledge in the area of business research and be of a standard publishable in an international refereed journal.

Convey research clearly and fluently, in high-quality form appropriate for academic and/or professional audiences

31005.title: Machine Learning
31005.description: This subject equips you with the skills to apply machine learning, a key driver of innovation across various industries, by teaching you to program and analyse intelligent systems that learn from data. You will develop a clear understanding of both foundational and advanced algorithms through practical exercises and theoretical study. Your learning experience will blend active engagement with real-world applications, particularly in artificial intelligence, preparing you for immediate professional application and further exploration in the field.
learningOutcomes: Describe the scope, limitations and application of several advanced machine learning methods. (D.1)
Use or program a machine learning method. (D.1)
Design an approach to machine learning problems in specialised domains. (C.1)
Demonstrate an understanding of the issues underlying machine learning to successfully outline an approach to solving a machine learning problem. (D.1)

31030.title: Project
31030.description: This subject is intended to give you experience in working independently on a small research or development project. The project may be drawn from any area of information technology, engineering or may be part of a multidisciplinary project such as those managed by UTS Shopfront. You will work on the project independently under the supervision of an academic staff member.
learningOutcomes: Apply skills and knowledge gained throughout the course to a specific project. (C.1)
Conduct critical self-review and reflection on the outcomes and the competencies developed while undertaking the project. (F.1)
Apply basic project management techniques to ensure completion of deliverables in a timely manner. (D.1)
Communicate appropriately with the relevant stakeholder(s). (E.1)
31030.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have previously completed subjects relevant to the project topic.

31061.title: Database Principles
31061.description: This subject provides a foundational understanding of database design and implementation, focusing on relational design principles and Entity Relationship Diagrams. You will learn to interpret and develop these diagrams and access databases using Structured Query Language (SQL) for data retrieval. Additionally, the subject covers the coding skills necessary to construct a database. Preparation is essential ahead of lectures, while labs offer practical exercises for your learning, ensuring you can effectively design and query databases.
learningOutcomes: Design an Entity-Relationship (E-R) model from specifications and transform a conceptual model into corresponding logical data structures. (D.1)
Construct Structured Query Language (SQL) statements and maintain a simple database. (D.1)
Critically evaluate database designs and the role databases play in effective software applications. (C.1)
Effectively communicate database design. (E.1)
31061.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject are familiar with basic system analysis concepts and have basic software skills.

31080.title: Interactive Media
31080.description: This subject introduces you to the fundamentals of interactive media, preparing you to design and develop systems that integrate digital audio, images, animation, and video for immersive user experiences. You will gain proficiency in creative coding tools and techniques, applying them to create compelling content for various domains such as gaming, arts, and data visualisation. The emphasis is on practical application, ensuring that you can craft interactive media that captivate users in real-world scenarios.
learningOutcomes: Apply knowledge of digital sampling, storage and mapping techniques for still images, video, sound and sensor data to make appropriate design choices for interactive media applications. (D.1)
Use digital sound, image and video processing algorithms to alter digital media. (D.1)
Design and develop interactive media applications which incorporate a range of different interactive components to create effective and engaging user experiences. (C.1)
Reflect on the nature of digital media components to devise novel and effective applications and descriptions of interactive media systems. (F.1)
Provide creative and critical feedback and ask thoughtful questions of peers in a supportive and constructive manner (E.1)

31097.title: IT Operations Management
31097.description: In this subject, you will develop the skills necessary for managing resources in an information systems organisation, including hardware, software, and personnel. You will learn about resource acquisition, software development, workplace management, recruitment, training, security practices, operations management, and service level agreements. The subject also covers industry frameworks and standards such as ITIL, alongside contemporary topics like cloud computing, equipping you with a comprehensive skill set for effective IT resource management.
learningOutcomes: Identify with the scope and challenges of the role of an IT Manager. (B.1)
Analyse the responsibilities, structures and functional areas of the IT Department. (D.1)
Produce competency portfolios and service level agreements in an IT department. (C.1)
Suggest commercially viable solutions to typical challenges in an IT department. (D.1)

31102.title: Game Design Studio 1
31102.description: In this subject, you will learn the practical aspects of game design and development by creating games that meet client specifications. You'll explore game mechanics from indie and experimental games to inform your own creations, adopting a player-centric design philosophy with constant user testing. Collaborative teamwork mirrors industry practices, with you taking on specific roles and working independently yet guided, culminating in responsibility for delivering and presenting the final project.
learningOutcomes: Iteratively design and develop an innovative game incorporating feedback from user testing. (C.1)
Apply Agile project management principles and relevant frameworks to games development and software engineering. (D.1)
Collaboratively work in a team to deliver project outcomes. (E.1)
Critically reflect on individual contributions to inform future practice in teamwork contexts. (F.1)

31103.title: Game Design Studio 2
31103.description: This subject hones your practical skills in game design and development through multidisciplinary team collaboration, following Agile Project Management Principles. You will work closely with students from other Faculties, and you'll specialise in areas like 3D modeling, scripting, level design, or music composition, contributing to the creation of commercial-quality video games. Your team, which retains the intellectual property rights, is encouraged to market your game post-completion, aligning with the dynamic nature of the games industry and offering real-world application potential.
learningOutcomes: Iteratively design and develop a complex game incorporating multidisciplinary design and feedback from user testing. (C.1)
Apply Agile project management principles and relevant frameworks to games development and software engineering. (D.1)
Collaboratively work in an interdisciplinary team to manage project outcomes. (E.1)
Critically reflect on individual contributions to inform future practice in teamwork contexts. (F.1)

31241.title: Interactive 3D Animation
31241.description:
This subject delves into 3D animation for interactive applications like games or short animated productions, covering the entire production pipeline from storyboarding to animation, camera positioning, interactive control, code integration, lighting, advanced real-time rendering, and VFX.

You will actively engage in pre-production planning, practical realisation, and post-production with a game engine and a project-based approach emphasising learning by doing. This hands-on experience equips you with the skills to manage, enhance, and integrate animated components into games or to execute a complete animation project.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the theory of the design and production of 3D digital animation. (D.1)
Develop animation skills and the ability to look at motion analytically. (D.1)
Design and rig a basic character for 3D animation using appropriate processes and workflows. (C.1)
Create a character-based 3D Animation from planning stage (storyboard) to final 3D rendered short. (C.1)
31241.recommended: basic knowledge of drawing and 2D digital image processing (basic Photoshop) is useful

31243.title: AI/Analytics Capstone Project B
31243.description:
In this subject, you'll engage with a project around data analytics or artificial intelligence. You'll initiate this project in a learning contract, guided by a mentor, to either address a research issue through guided semi-independent research or solve a complex real-world problem by applying practical steps -- data preparation, data preprocessing, pattern discovery/model training, evaluation, and application/deployment, culminating in a detailed report of your findings/solution.

This subject equips you with expertise in data analytics/AI techniques and professional communication of results.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate competency in conceptualising, designing, planning and implementing research studies in data analytics. (C.1)
Select and apply an appropriate research method for solving a real-world analytics problem. (C.1)
Explain and justify an application of problem solving, reported in the required format and style. (E.1)

31245.title: Business Process and IT Strategy
31245.description:
This subject introduces you to the strategic use of information technology (IT) to enhance business processes and strategies. A major concern for businesses is finding a competitive advantage and effectively leveraging IT resources to align with business goals. For IT managers, this involves understanding and managing complex issues related to the roles of IT and IT strategy in enabling business processes and generating business benefits and competitive advantage. In this subject, we will explore theories and methods related to the value of IT. You will learn about and discuss business and strategy processes that lead to learning organisations capable of achieving sustainable competitive advantage.

Business processes and IT strategy are crucial concerns for both business and IT managers. Managing information is a critical skill for success in today's business environment. Managers need to understand their organisation's capabilities and the use of information resources. This subject aims to provide a foundation to help general business managers become knowledgeable participants in decision-making processes related to information systems (IS). By critically reviewing the contributions of IS resources in businesses and organisational settings, you will gain a contextual understanding of how IS permeates many aspects of business.

Through case studies, this subject reinforces material provided in lectures and tutorials, along with additional research and prior knowledge. It gives you the opportunity to enhance your problem-solving, critical thinking, and organisational skills as part of a group, as well as to engage in peer learning. The subject emphasises the development and assessment of real-world experience through applied and innovative tasks and team effort. You will develop the knowledge and skills required for using and managing information within an organisation, as well as essential management and communication skills.
learningOutcomes: Theorise on the impact of information systems technology in business process transformation (BPT) and strategic information systems planning (SISP) and why businesses undertake BPT or SISP to achieve sustainable competitive advantage. (B.1)
Explain the role of non-IT enablers that affect successful BPT. (B.1)
Describe the complex network of organisational issues that arise during BPT or SISP and their impact on IS and business alignment. (B.1)
Explain the need for collaboration between IS personnel and their customers to achieve satisfactory solving of complex problems. (B.1)
Present, discuss and support their analyses of issues involving business and strategy processes in learning organisations. (E.1)

31247.title: Collaborative Business Processes
31247.description: This subject provides you with a comprehensive problem-solving framework, essential for agile teams to foster creativity, critical thinking, and innovation. Starting with problem scoping, you'll gain a data-supported understanding of issues, utilising collaborative tools for knowledge sharing. You'll apply techniques like process modelling and systems thinking to generate solutions, while focusing on addressing current and emergent societal or business challenges. The subject encourages knowledge exchange and the development of practical solutions.
learningOutcomes: Analyse the roles of collaborative processes in problem solving, in the context of contemporary challenges. (B.1)
Collaboratively synthesise multiple viewpoints, and evaluate ideas to formulate “wicked problems”. (C.1)
Apply appropriate collaborative process toolsets to solve the selected problem(s). (D.1)
Evaluate formulations and solutions of peers to inform optimal outcomes. (E.1)
Use reflection strategies to enhance students’ personal contributions to the workplace. (F.1)

31248.title: Serious Games and Gamification Studio
31248.description: This subject focuses on creating serious games and gamified experiences, designed for purposes beyond entertainment such as education or training. You'll learn cutting-edge design frameworks and techniques for tailoring games to specific audiences and objectives. Working with end-users, you'll engage in co-design workshops, prototype development, playtesting, and evaluation to ensure impactful outcomes. Additionally, you'll consider the ethical implications inherent in game design.
learningOutcomes: Apply professional standards relating to Indigenous Australian contexts when designing games and serious games. (A.1)
Evaluate ethical, cultural, and societal considerations when designing a bespoke serious game or gamified experience. (B.1)
Design a game-like prototype that serves a specific purpose for a specific audience. (C.1)
Critically reflect on one’s own designs and iteratively propose alternate game-like solutions that fit a purpose and benefit an audience. (F.1)

31250.title: Introduction to Data Analytics
31250.description: This subject covers the fundamentals of data analytics, blending art and science to transform large, complex datasets into actionable insights. You will learn data preprocessing, exploration, visualization, and predictive modeling using various data analytics techniques. By connecting cutting-edge research with practical applications, this subject prepares you to undertake data mining projects, collaborate with analytics professionals, and effectively communicate your findings.
learningOutcomes: Explain the value proposition of data analytics in a business context to immediate stakeholders. (B.1)
Use data analytics techniques to derive meaningful insights from data in a business context. (C.1)
Apply data analytics techniques to explore and predict trends based on data set. (D.1)
Identify the limitations and possibilities of different data analytics methods. (D.1)
Communicate data analytics findings to immediate stakeholders. (E.1)

31251.title: Data Structures and Algorithms
31251.description: This subject equips you with the skills to design, evaluate, and implement data structures and algorithms using C++, ensuring they meet criteria for functionality and usability. You'll learn the underlying concepts, theories, and technologies essential for creating software solutions that are suitable, understandable, easy to learn, and compliant.
learningOutcomes: Apply principles of program design to the C++ language in an integrated development environment. (C.1)
Analyse data structures and algorithms principles to unstructured data and complicated problem. (D.1)
Apply data structures and algorithms principles using C++ to complicated problems. (D.1)
31251.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have prior programming experience in some language, including understanding of basic programming concepts such as variables, conditional statements, and control flow.

31257.title: Information System Development Methodologies
31257.description: This subject arms you with the techniques to navigate the complexities of information system design and development, acknowledging there's no one-size-fits-all solution. You'll learn to assess various methodologies, pinpointing their strengths and weaknesses, a critical skill for effective software project management.
learningOutcomes: Analyse key aspects of a number of Information System development methodologies to develop business Systems. (B.1)
Explain that different methodologies target different aspects of Information System development, such as requirements gathering, project management or cross-organisational development. (C.1)
Evaluate development methodologies and articulate their underlying philosophies to solve organisational Information System problems. (D.1)
Illustrate a methodology, or aspects of different methodologies to substantiate the suitability of particular circumstances. (D.1)
31257.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge of the software development life cycle and systems modelling techniques

31258.title: Innovations for Global Relationship Management
31258.description: This subject explores the evolving role of the Australian computing industry, emphasising its shift towards leveraging computers for relationship maintenance, knowledge management, and innovation to gain competitive advantage. You'll examine the industry's global context, the value of IT in business, and the implications of e-commerce, customer relationship management, user modelling, outsourcing, offshoring, and legal issues in the digital economy. The subject also addresses organising business information, focusing on informal flows within organisations, and examines various work relationships, team formation, and management processes. Practical skills include using portals and other tools for customer loyalty and outsourcing collaborations.
learningOutcomes: Explain the impact and opportunities of IT within the Australian and global economic context by using computer tools such as portals, etc to maintain relationships and grow these opportunities. (B.1)

Discuss how IT adds value to business in e-commerce, relationship and knowledge management, user modelling for customer satisfaction, outsourcing, off shoring and software development by using computers for innovation that leads to competitive advantage. (B.1)
Recognise how Intellectual Property, Service Level Agreements, patents and other legal tools are involved in the formalization of relationships in IT. (D.1)
Demonstrate the attributes employers look for when hiring and comprehend how to develop these skills in the context of organisational culture and fit of the employee. (F.1)

31260.title: Fundamentals of Interaction Design
31260.description: This subject develops your ability to design, evaluate, and implement interactive systems with a human-centered approach. You'll understand human-computer interaction (HCI) and interaction design principles, learning key concepts, tools, and techniques. You'll also consider how designers' metaphors for human activity affect system usability and how human-centered design and evaluation can enhance interactive systems.
learningOutcomes: Apply a range of approaches, techniques, tools, and methods available when designing useful and usable technology. (D.1)
Design digital mockup of prototype to achieve success for usability. (C.1)
Assist people through design of interconnected solutions going beyond isolated technologies. (B.1)
31260.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge of interactive technologies, design and programming skills.

31262.title: Game Design Methodologies
31262.description: This games subject trains you to be an engineer of entertainment, teaching you the essential theoretical concepts and practical methodologies for game design. You will learn to structure, document, target, and scope your game designs with further refinement through weekly iteration via playtest feedback. As part of a group, you will first learn to apply these creative theories and methods to develop a physical board game prototype before moving on to crafting a digital game using a popular game engine. While this subject is not focused on game development skills such as coding or art creation, you are encouraged to self-learn what's necessary to realise your group’s vision. Regular playtesting with peers will help refine your designs. By the subject's end, you'll have created both board and digital games, showcasing your interaction design expertise for future employment portfolios. You will be better prepared for the iterative development cycle common in later game studio subjects and the wider game industry.
learningOutcomes: Design and critique games as dynamic systems of formal and dramatic elements. (C.1)
Collaborate effectively within a group to incorporate diverse perspectives and skill sets in the design. (E.1)
Rapidly develop digital game prototypes to gather early player feedback. (D.1)
Critically reflect and act on playtest feedback during iterative designs cycles. (C.1)
31262.recommended: familiarity with computer graphics and experience with designing interactive systems

31263.title: Introduction to Computer Game Development
31263.description: This subject introduces you to game development using a commercial-grade game engine, focusing on building a strong foundation in generalisable virtual interaction simulation theory and intermediate programming problem solving skills in the Unity Game Engine. You'll become familiar with industry terminology, engine interface tools, vector and matrix maths for object transformation, and programming involving the engine API. You will be assessed on your practical skills development through weekly lab content to ensure consistent skill development over the session. You will create a classic video game over the semester, beginning with the asset creation and import into the engine, and then programming the game logic akin to the original game experience. You will also craft a level with a unique twist to allow for you to develop your creative problem-solving skills, a crucial skill for any aspiring game developer. The skills developed in this subject will prepare you to contribute effectively to group projects in future game-related subjects and subject outcomes can be utilised in an employment portfolio.
learningOutcomes: Understand foundational language and theory of game development technology. (D.1)
Apply mathematical and game programming knowledge to solve development tasks. (D.1)
Navigate the interface and codebase of an industry standard game development engine. (D.1)
Proactively identify their own knowledge gaps and establish skills in life-long learning through sourcing new knowledge to solve previously unseen intermediate problems. (F.1)
Design and implement minor variations to existing game designs. (C.1)

31264.title: Computer Graphics
31264.description: This subject equips you with problem-solving and communication skills specific to computer graphics, focusing on shape representation, manipulation, and visualisation. You will learn to design and implement 3D interactive graphics for applications such as virtual reality (VR), data visualisation, and gaming. Balancing theory and practice, you'll delve into graphical pipelines and representations and apply this knowledge using WebGL and the ThreeJS framework. You'll emerge with an understanding of the systems driving game engines and 3D animation software and the ability to create interactive 3D web applications, valuable for various studies and careers.
learningOutcomes: Implement an interactive application using ThreeJS and WebGL. (C.1)
Integrate principles of linear algebra into computer graphics applications (D.1)
Implement data structures and algorithms for 3D shape representation and real-time rendering (D.1)
Communicate design ideas, models, implementations and outcomes to a technical audience. (E.1)
Reflect on one’s own work to identify changes in practice for future projects. (F.1)
31264.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have some experience with an integrated development environment such as Visual Studio would be an advantage, but is not essential; knowledge of linear algebra (e.g. vectors, matrices and their manipulation), data structures (e.g. multi-dimensional arrays, stack) is strongly recommended; good programming skills in at least one programming language is required to successfully complete the subject.

31265.title: Communication for IT Professionals
31265.description: This core subject will highlight new ways of working, provide insights into the scope of technology, and look at considerations within the Australian context. You will learn to make decisions that impact people, community, and the environment. Through authentic experiences, you will develop skills and knowledge, providing a solid base for your continuous professional development as an IT professional. In the subject, you will complete the Engineers Without Borders Challenge, working in a team to develop solutions to real-world challenges for an Australian Aboriginal or Torres Strait Island community. You will form a team with peers, working in and outside class throughout the session on the project that you select. Your team will research the project background, refine scope and identify technological considerations. You will then ideate and prototype potential solutions that work in the community context. Finally, you will propose a fully developed design idea that benefits the partner community. In completing the challenge, you will develop multidisciplinary and professional skills including: researching skills to inform the development of design solutions; applying the design process to solve genuine humanitarian challenges; considering socio-technical issues including working with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities; developing professional communications skill; and participating and leading team processes.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate an awareness of Indigenous Australian cultural, historic, and contemporary contexts in order to inform work in a complex project. (A.1)
Identify stakeholder needs and ethical considerations through the empathise design stage. (B.1)
Apply a design thinking approach to meet stakeholder needs. (C.1)
Communicate an evidence-based design solution for an IT or engineering project. (E.1)
Explain the collaboration and contributions of team planning, communication and problem-solving in developing a design solution. (E.1)

31266.title: Introduction to Information Systems
31266.description: This subject examines the integration and application of IT technology within society, business, government, and community systems, highlighting trends like increased mobility, complexity, globalisation, and networking in a data-centric world. It explores how IT technology enhances service delivery and competitiveness in a global, networked economy. You'll learn the role of information systems in business management and network formation, using real-world case studies to grasp how IS contributes to competitive advantage. The subject covers IS development, implementation, and maintenance, while also fostering team collaboration and relationship skills. Ethical, privacy, and security considerations are also addressed. You'll apply theoretical knowledge to practical scenarios, innovate, and cultivate teamwork skills.
learningOutcomes: Identify business, organizational and society environment to propose types of IS for obtaining and maintaining competitive advantage. (B.1)
Demonstrate data management approaches for implementing knowledge management systems in organisations. (D.1)
Discuss key concepts relating to telecommunication and networking. (D.1)
Describe the process of acquiring information systems and applications. (D.1)
Identify ethical issues in the IS context to propose recommendations. (B.1)

31268.title: Web Systems
31268.description: This subject is an introduction to information technology, using the web as a core case study. You will learn about the underlying hardware, software, networks and operating systems behind websites, and set up a functional website using this knowledge.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate understanding of the basic concepts of hardware, software, cybersecurity, processes and the components of an Operating System including how to work on the command line and create simple scripts. (D.1)
Identify and explain the role and function of the Internet, the World Wide Web, and their components. Describe and make use of distributed applications on the Internet. (D.1)
Design and implement a simple web site to a given specification. (C.1)
31268.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have prior use of an operating system; the availity to browse and search the internet.

31269.title: Business Requirements Modelling
31269.description:
This subject focuses on modelling business requirements, emphasising the importance of understanding different perspectives of the users to enhances system quality in resolving real-world business problems. 

You'll explore contemporary requirements modelling approaches, both agile and non-agile software engineering principles, methods, tools, and techniques, to analyse business processes and model requirements via the business process models and data models as well as capture functional and non-functional requirements via agile artifacts and object-oriented models.

You'll participate in interactive and hands-on lectures, tutorials as well as team projects with real-world business problems, which will develop key skills for critical roles like Business Analyst in designing and developing innovative software systems in professional settings
learningOutcomes: Identify stakeholders, define their needs, and determine the methods to effectively capture and model business requirements in the system development process. (B.1)
Apply diverse systems analysis and design techniques to model system and user requirements and document them effectively using an Agile Software Requirements Specification (Agile SRS). (C.1)
Apply modelling and systems analysis techniques to effectively describe the operations and functionality of a business system using business process models and data models. (D.1)
Communicate the impact of individual contributions by analysing personal decisions and articulating their influence on team outcomes. (E.1)

31271.title: Database Fundamentals
31271.description:
This subject lays the foundation for effective database systems, teaching you how data is structured and managed within organizations, ensuring its usability for applications and users. You will also learn SQL for effective data retrieval and modification, enhancing your ability to work with databases in various contexts.

During the subject, you'll explore the significance and challenges of good database design and management, which underpin a strong basis for developing functional software applications. You'll enhance your skills through hands-on practicals and case study analyses, applying theoretical concepts to real-world situations.

This subject is particularly beneficial for students pursuing majors in computer science, information systems, or related fields. It prepares you for roles in database administration, software development, and data analysis.
learningOutcomes: Construct conceptual data models using appropriate database design, and data modelling principles. (C.1)
Identify data redundancy levels and their impact on database integrity and maintainability using data normalisation principles. (D.1)
Construct efficient SQL queries to retrieve and manipulate data as required. (D.1)
31271.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject are familiar with basic system analysis concepts and have basic software skills.

31272.title: Project Management and the Professional
31272.description: This subject equips you with project management skills, focusing on information systems and professional project management. You will learn about ethical standards and the organisational context of projects. You will also learn about the roles of project team members, managing time, risk, cost and communications and the value of quality. These skills are vital for university success and for success in your future career. Learning involves being part of a small project team. You will collaborate to create project documents, receiving constructive feedback to foster improvement. These activities culminate in a significant group assessment followed by a reflection on what you have learnt. You will also write a report stating the possible ethical dilemmas in a given case study and describing how industry codes may be used to suggest solutions to these dilemmas. Academic and professional language and communication skills are measured through a milestone assessment task that gauges both your subject knowledge and communication proficiency.This subject also supports the development of the Indigenous Graduate Attribute (IGA). You will engage with IGA learning modules and industry perspectives to strengthen your understanding of the ethical engagement with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and communities. These resources introduce principles such as Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC), Indigenous self‑determination, Indigenous Data Sovereignty, and reciprocity, and highlight their relevance to professional project practice.
learningOutcomes: Critically reflect on ethical principles of stakeholder engagement to work effectively with and for Indigenous Australians within project contexts. (A.1)
Explain the social impact of information technology and responsibility of IT professionals and importance of ethical codes of conduct within projects. (B.1)
Divide a project into components to explain what value that project will provide if implemented. (D.1)
Use team building skills and generic tools to plan a project. (E.1)
Collaborate in teams to create the project outcome. (E.1)
Reflect on what has been learnt and how this can feed into better outcomes for future projects. (F.1)
