31275.title: Mobile Networking
31275.description: Wireless networks, including cellular, WiFi, Bluetooth, satellite, and near-field communication networks, establish pervasive connections to devices and end-users, serving as foundational technologies across virtually all industries today. This subject explores the principles and applications of wireless telecommunications and their integration with the internet. It emphasizes key concepts, infrastructure, and protocols critical to these networks, particularly their ability to support a diverse array of devices and mobility needs. The subject includes guest lectures from leading Australian telecommunications companies, offering firsthand insights into the latest cellular technologies. You will gain extensive hands-on experience by addressing real-world industry challenges and developing either emulated sensing/communication systems or working prototypes in group projects. This approach not only imparts fundamental knowledge but also equips you with practical skills applicable across numerous engineering fields. By the end of this subject, you'll have a comprehensive understanding of wireless networks, equipped to engage with advanced technologies and innovations.
learningOutcomes: Explain the concepts, techniques and protocols employed in various wireless networks to perform consulting tasks involving support roles for wireless technologies. (D.1)
Analyze the network infrastructure requirements to support mobile devices and users. (B.1)
Develop and roadshow innovative solutions for practical applications of wireless technologies. (C.1)
Evaluate and solve integrated problems in mobile networking by applying theoretical concepts, protocol standards, and case-based reasoning. (D.1)

args.text: Admission into MAJ03539 54cp Telecommunications and Electronics (MPE)

31277.title: Routing and Switching Essentials
31277.description: Building on prior knowledge, this subject offers a deeper dive into networking. You'll develop expertise for specialisation and understand networks' influence on applications. Key skills include learning IP addressing, routing protocols and switched networks. You will be designing and implementing small to medium-sized intranets, and managing network security. You'll also evaluate the role of TCP/IP, ICMP, and other IP network protocols, with practical work involving CISCO routers and switches.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate proficiency in designing a hierarchical IPv4 addressing scheme. (D.1)
Design small to medium sized networks with switches and routers given design criteria. (C.1)
Build and operate network infrastructure services for small to medium sized networks. (D.1)
Demonstrate teamwork capability and communication skills. (E.1)
31277.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge in open system interconnection (OSI); transmission control protocol/internet protocol (TCP/IP) and data network models; knowledge of networking terminology, data transmission media, data networking components and devices; internet protocol addressing.

31282.title: Systems Testing and Quality Management
31282.description: This subject equips you with practical knowledge and skills for measuring and controlling software quality. You'll learn about software quality assurance, management principles, and testing approaches for systems and software.
learningOutcomes: Design specific processes, types and phases of testing to assure quality in software products (C.1)
Identify principles and approaches to testing and quality management to projects and business outcomes (D.1)
Apply a variety of testing techniques to evaluate system operations and functions (D.1)
Apply quality assurance and management principles in testing environment (D.1)
Collaboratively plan, develop, apply and document test quality systems (E.1)

31482.title: Honours Project B
31482.description: In this advanced stage of your honours programme, you'll complete a research project, building on prior work and guided by an academic supervisor. You'll develop and showcase your ability to conduct independent research, solve complex problems, and present your findings with scholarly rigour. Your learning will be self-directed, culminating in a project that either delivers a system, creative work or contributes to academic research, reflecting the depth of knowledge and skills acquired throughout your studies. Progress will be monitored through regular discussions with your supervisor, ensuring you meet the high expectations and timelines necessary for graduation readiness
learningOutcomes: Conceptualise, design, plan and implement advanced research studies in their field of study and practice. (C.1)
Ability to reflect on previous studies and knowledge and apply them to their fields of research/innovation. (C.1)
Pitch the research background, design, implementation, results and conclusions to an audience of peers and staff with effective and clear communication skills. (E.1)
Apply critical, descriptive, persuasive and analytical skills to a research report or paper to demonstrate innovative research in ways appropriate to the discipline audience and purpose. (C.1)

31748.title: Programming on the Internet
31748.description: This subject equips you with an in-depth understanding of internet-based programming and the World Wide Web's intricacies, from its evolution to its technical core. You'll learn essential data presentation techniques and delve into the client/server model, focusing on website creation with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, JSON, MySQL/MongoDB, and modern JavaScript libraries for building user interfaces (e.g., React). The subject offers a solid foundation for grasping the WWW's workings, constructing websites, and mastering web software development through scripting.
learningOutcomes: Identify concepts pertaining to the Internet and World Wide web such as TCP/IP, protocols, domain names, IP addresses and n-tier architecture. (D.1)
Apply principles of internet security to websites. (D.1)
Apply principles of website design to improve efficiency using industry used web development languages. (D.1)
Apply client-side and server-side scripting to manage a range of simple web server interactions. (D.1)
Relate web development frameworks to effectively manage websites. (D.1)

31777.title: Advanced Interaction Design
31777.description: This subject focuses on user experience (UX) in interaction design, crucial for technology adoption and competitive edge. You'll learn conceptual tools to discuss, analyse, and critique UX with digital technologies. The subject covers a range of interactions like mobile, social, pervasive computing, and IoT, helping you understand how to design for specific user experiences in context. You'll also learn design methods like user research, sketching, prototyping, and evaluation to create technology solutions that are not only effective but engaging. By building on fundamental design concepts, you'll be equipped to design technologies that optimise user experience.
learningOutcomes: Use appropriate conceptual tools to accurately describe, critique, analyse and evaluate user experiences that arise through-and-during interactions with information technology. (D.1)
Identify the types of user experiences that are most appropriate for different types of human-computer interactions. (C.1)
Apply appropriate methods, concepts, and techniques to successfully design interactive technologies that can support engaging user experiences during use. (C.1)
Describe the range of social/technical and experiential concepts that are important to consider when designing technologies that can be experienced positively by users. (B.1)
Demonstrate awareness on how to design in a positive and respectful manner when working with, and for, Indigenous Australians. (A.1)
31777.recommended: It is recommended that students complete 48cp (2 years of full-time study) prior to commencing this subject.

31927.title: Application Development with .NET
31927.description: This subject introduces you to C# programming using Visual Studio and the .NET development framework. You will explore the .NET framework and its core concepts, applying this knowledge to develop applications in C#.
learningOutcomes: Understand the .NET framework architecture. (D.1)
Understand how the .NET framework implements OO concepts and the implications this has for new language design. (D.1)
Understand the mechanisms and techniques for the deployment and configuration of .NET applications. (D.1)
Be able to utilize the .NET libraries. (D.1)
Design and develop a C# program in the .NET environment. (C.1)
31927.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have a good understanding of programming constructs, O-O concepts and programming practices.

32009.title: Advanced Routing Principles
32009.description: This subject focuses on routing technology and provides a comprehensive explanation of routing. It extends your skills and knowledge in scalable interior and exterior routing protocols, policy-based routing, route optimisation and redistribution. Content is primarily drawn from CCNP Enterprise: Core Networking (ENCOR) with additional insights from CCNP Enterprise: Advanced Routing. The subject is run in the UTS Cisco Systems Network Academy.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate physical network infrastructure to recommend and operationalise appropriate for stakeholder needs. (B.1)
Compare and optimise interior and exterior scalable routing protocols in a multi-protocol scenario for internal connectivity and access to an Internet Service Provider (ISP). (D.1)
Explain the advantages and limitations of scalable routing protocols and their suitability for the small, medium and large enterprise. (D.1)

32011.title: Multilayer Switched Networks
32011.description: This subject advances your understanding and practical skills in designing and implementing switched campus networks, using VLANs to enhance performance, reliability, management, and security. You'll explore various approaches to plan, configure, and verify complex enterprise switching solutions, with hands-on experience on Cisco Systems layer 2 and layer 3 switches. The curriculum aligns with CCNP Enterprise: Core Networking (ENCOR) and is conducted at the UTS Cisco Systems Network Academy.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate the design benefits and limitations of switched campus networks by applying knowledge of the theoretical characteristics of different high-speed switched network technologies. (C.1)
Apply appropriate switched network technologies to meet needs of switched networks. (C.1)
Apply troubleshooting steps to solve problems encountered in switched LANs. (D.1)
Explain to technically informed people the merits of different modes of network configurations. (D.1)

32027.title: Interactive Media
32027.description: This subject introduces you to the core principles and tools of interactive media, widely used across games, the arts, data visualisation, and business. You'll learn to use creative coding to design and develop systems that integrate digital audio, images, animations, and video, aiming to craft rich, engaging user experiences for real-world applications.
learningOutcomes: Apply knowledge of digital sampling, storage and mapping techniques for still images, video, sound and sensor data to make appropriate design choices for interactive media applications. (D.1)
Use digital sound, image and video processing algorithms to alter digital media. (D.1)
Design and develop interactive media applications which incorporate a range of different interactive components to create effective and engaging user experiences. (C.1)
Reflect on the nature of digital media components to devise novel and effective applications and descriptions of interactive media systems. (F.1)
Provide creative and critical feedback and ask thoughtful questions of peers in a supportive and constructive manner (E.1)

32040.title: Industry Project
32040.description: This subject equips you to manage with strategic analysis and design issues for corporate information systems environment, utilising a major case study to apply and reinforce prior knowledge. You'll learn to evaluate different system strategies and enhance your senior management and communication abilities. Learning is interactive, emphasising practical judgement and teamwork while working in an industry-like environment.
learningOutcomes: Identify the requirements for an industry based information system in a medium to large and complex organisation. (B.1)
Design an appropriate information systems solution, assess its impact on the organisation and make management recommendations. (C.1)
Design and implement a strategy for introducing change to a complex corporate information system. (C.1)
Engage in decision making in areas of uncertainty in a complex project. (D.1)
Clearly communicate contributions of practical situations and changes to a range of audiences. (E.1)
32040.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge in systems design; requirements gathering; project planning; networking; report writing; presentations; working in teams.

32113.title: Advanced Database
32113.description: Software systems require trustworthy data management systems. This subject covers advanced database concepts, requirements, architecture, design and systems. Current trends and challenges in the practice of data management are explored to develop the robust data solutions. In small teams, students apply these contemporary data management practices to their advanced database project work. Students learn to integrate and manage data from different sources to support the data-intensive software systems.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate data design and management and its value in relation to supporting corporate stakeholder data resource. (B.1)
Design data models to support complex corporate stakeholder requirements. (C.1)
Create database systems and solutions to support a range of data types and structures to support complex queries and results. (D.1)
Collaborate effectively in a group to address a practical business problem. (E.1)

32118.title: Wireless Communications
32118.description: This subject provides a foundational understanding of wireless communication systems, focusing on the technology, infrastructure, and protocols essential for devices and mobility. It first looks at underlying technologies and then reviews major wireless systems and networks. Practical learning through Matlab-based simulations complements theoretical study. You will also work as a group to develop a solution to practical wireless communications problems, by applying technologies learned in the subject.
learningOutcomes: Explain the fundamental technologies used in wireless communications, for supporting mobility, multiple access, and high data rate connections. (D.1)
Describe and analyse the network infrastructure requirements to support mobile devices and users. (B.1)

Illustrate the concepts, techniques, protocols and architecture employed in wireless personal area networks, wireless local area networks, cellular networks, and satellite networks, and perform basic requirements analysis. (D.1)

Select and apply proper wireless techniques, and current systems and network technologies to the consideration of next generation technologies and how they fit into intended IoT networks from the edge through to cloud and why they will be important demonstrating and explaining their advantages in selected applications in practical applications. Simulate and analyze the performance of the design to provide decision support. (C.1)

32130.title: Fundamentals of Data Analytics
32130.description: This subject equips you with both theoretical and hands-on experience of data analytics, the process of extracting meaningful insights from large data sets. You'll learn statistical methods and data visualisation techniques to explore and process vast volumes of data, and unsupervised as well as supervised techniques to discover patterns and insights for knowledge discovery. The subject synthesises cutting-edge research and practice, preparing you to lead data analytics projects that transform data into commercially valuable information.
learningOutcomes: Scope framed data informed business problems using contextual, ethical, and stakeholder awareness. (B.1)
Design data analytics approaches to business objectives and data constraints. (C.1)
Use appropriate data analytics methods to describe and implement descriptive and predictive analytics solutions. (D.1)
Communicate data analytics methods and insights effectively in oral and written forms, demonstrating responsible and critical collaboration with AI tools. (E.1)

32144.title: Technology Research Preparation
32144.description: This subject equips you with vital communication skills for your engineering and IT career. It focusses on you understanding key research principles, activities and outcomes, which include but are not restricted to crafting literature reviews, completing ethics applications and more. You will be guided and assessed on how to propose a research project as part of the foundational research activities for your degree. By enhancing your academic and professional language proficiency which is crucial for both university and workplace success you will engage with a series of interactive lectures and tutorials, where you will apply concepts in practical exercises and weekly written assignments as provided via the Canvas site.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate critical analysis of technology research and the codes of conduct/ethical practices when working with and for Indigenous peoples. (A.1)
Integrate academic integrity and critical evaluation of sources and perspectives into a research report. (B.1)
Synthesize review of the literature by critically evaluating textual sources of information to inform research argument. (C.1)
Communicate research argument to a range of audiences. (E.1)

32146.title: Data Visualisation and Visual Analytics
32146.description: This subject focuses on the vital technologies of data visualisation and visual interaction that underpin visual analytics and decision-making. You'll engage with recent data visualisation literature and practice using advanced software. The subject outlines the visual data analytics process and methodology, including the critical role of human interaction with interactive visual interfaces. Upon completion, you'll be adept at designing and evaluating sophisticated visualisation interfaces, positioning you for roles as a data visualisation designer and visual data analyst.
learningOutcomes: Recognise, compare and apply a range of static data visualisation techniques. (D.1)
Apply interactive data visualisation techniques. (D.1)
Design and create data visualisations for particular social contexts that are appropriate for specific users. (C.1)
Design and create data visualisations that facilitate the discovery and presentation of data-driven stories. (C.1)

32309.title: Digital Forensics
32309.description: In this practice-based subject, you will engage in laboratory-based learning to determine if a crime has been committed through the acquisition, analysis, and reporting of digital evidence. Your studies will focus on forensic analysis of network data, including the recovery of website visitation evidence relevant for court cases, alongside scrutinising digital storage devices to identify and retrieve critical data. You will also delve into the examination of operating systems to unearth hidden data, perform detailed analysis of metadata to gain deeper insights, and apply rigorous forensic principles to produce sound and defensible reports. Through these hands-on activities, you will develop a comprehensive understanding of digital forensics and its applications in real-world scenarios.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate theories of digital forensics. (D.1)
Understand the structure of forensic evidence. (D.1)
Implement forensically sound digital security practices in industry. (B.1, C.1)
Demonstrate competence in applying industry-standard forensic analysis techniques. (D.1)

32310.title: Network Security Appliances
32310.description: This practical subject draws from the Network Security course provided by the Cisco Academy, with a focus on hands-on laboratory work centred around network security appliances. You'll delve into security technologies, products, and solutions, learning to design, install, configure, and maintain firewalls and secure routers. Key skills include implementing AAA (Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting) and VPNs (Virtual Private Networks) using routers and firewalls. You'll also understand how encryption, hashes, and digital signatures collaborate to ensure confidentiality, integrity, and authentication.
learningOutcomes: Describe the theoretical aspects of computer security with an in-depth focus on modern network security threats. (B.1)
Design, configure, test, manage, monitor and support network security infrastructure devices. (C.1)
Apply network security theory into practice using industry based techniques, processes and standards. (D.1)
Demonstrate practical skills on real-world commercial networking equipment. (D.1)
32310.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have an understanding of the principles and objectives of network security and of the fundamentals of network security technologies; CCNA-level networking concepts and skills, in particular CCNA-level routing and switching skills.

32405.title: Human-Centred Design Research Methods
32405.description: This subject focuses on making people the core of the interaction design process through human-centred design methods, with particular attention to the interviewing and probes methods. Interviewing gathers direct information and adapts flexibly across the design process, while probes, using tailored props, require more setup but aim to inspire creative insights and prepare participants for a follow-up interview. You'll learn both methods, applying them step-by-step to real participants, guided by a brief and with readings and examples to tailor your approach. You must recruit at least three strangers (people you do not know and who are not familiar with the subject) for interviews and one stranger for the probe study.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of human-centred design methods. (B.1)
Demonstrate an ability to plan, design and carry out small user research projects. (C.1)
Develop an analysis of the findings from user research suitable for use in professional projects. (B.1)
Explain results and outcomes to others in their cohort and to broader audiences through paper writing, poster and video presentations. (E.1)
Apply positive and respectful ethical practices, such as the AIATSIS Code and NHMRC’s ethical code for researchers. (A.1, B.1)

32509.title: Advanced Interaction Design
32509.description: This subject delves into user experience (UX) in interaction design, crucial for technology adoption and competitive differentiation. UX reflects a user's interaction with digital products and varies widely in definition across academia and industry. You'll acquire conceptual tools to discuss UX effectively, identifying and critiquing digital technology experiences. Practical skills are developed by examining human-computer interactions, including mobile and pervasive computing, IoT, and more, focusing on user experiences in specific contexts and goals. You'll learn design methods like user research, sketching, and prototyping, applying these to create technology solutions that are not only functional but also enhance user engagement. By building on fundamental design principles, you'll be equipped to craft technologies that optimize user experience.
learningOutcomes: Use appropriate conceptual tools to accurately describe, critique, analyse and evaluate user experiences that arise through, and during, interactions with information technology. (D.1)
Identify the types of user experiences that are most appropriate for different types of human-computer interactions. (C.1)
Apply appropriate methods, concepts, and techniques to successfully design interactive technologies that can support engaging user experiences during use. (C.1)
Describe the range of social/technical and experiential concepts that are important to consider when designing technologies that can be experienced positively by users. (B.1)
Demonstrate awareness on how to design in a positive and respectful manner when working with, and for, Indigenous Australians. (A.1)

32513.title: Advanced Data Analytics Algorithms
32513.description: This subject advances your understanding of data analytics through a machine learning lens, exploring how intelligent agents learn and adapt. Applied across various sectors, machine learning is central to discovering new knowledge. You'll delve into knowledge discovery algorithms, building on prior data analytics knowledge to comprehend both elementary and complex algorithms. The subject blends hands-on practice with foundational theories, enabling you to master key techniques through implementation and analysis. Additionally, you'll explore machine learning's practical applications, particularly in artificial intelligence, equipping you with the skills to apply this knowledge in real-world scenarios.
learningOutcomes: Describe the scope, limitations and application of several advanced machine learning methods. (D.1)
Use or program a machine learning method. (C.1)
Design an approach to machine learning problems in specialised domains. (C.1)
Demonstrate an understanding of the issues underlying machine learning to successfully outline an approach to solving a machine learning problem. (D.1)

32516.title: Internet Programming
32516.description: This subject equips you with an in-depth understanding of internet-based programming and the World Wide Web's intricacies, from its evolution to its technical core. You'll learn essential data presentation techniques and delve into the client/server model, focusing on website creation with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, JSON, MySQL/MongoDB, and modern JavaScript libraries for building user interfaces (e.g., React). The subject offers a solid foundation for grasping the WWW's workings, constructing websites, and mastering web software development through scripting.
learningOutcomes: Identify concepts pertaining to the Internet and World Wide web such as TCP/IP, protocols, domain names, IP addresses and n-tier architecture. (D.1)
Apply principles of internet security to websites. (D.1)
Apply principles of website design to improve efficiency using industry used web development languages. (D.1)
Apply client-side and server-side scripting to manage a range of simple web server interactions. (D.1)
Relate web development frameworks to effectively manage websites. (D.1)

32524.title: LANS and Routing
32524.description: This subject will provide you with a foundational understanding of how computer networks operate, particularly in the creation, operation, and maintenance of local area networks (LANs). You will develop a working knowledge of IP addressing schemes and essential routing and switching techniques within autonomous systems, using specialised networking devices to build small-to-medium networks. Utilising Cisco Networking Academy's online resources, you will engage in regular hands-on practice and gain real-world problem-solving skills by performing basic configuration and troubleshooting tasks with Cisco routers and switches.
learningOutcomes: Design small to medium-sized routed and switched networks, including hierarchical IP addressing schemes, to meet specified requirements. (C.1)
Apply computer network concepts and technologies to analyse and solve network problems. (D.1)
Utilise appropriate networking equipment and media to implement, troubleshoot and verify connectivity of small to medium-sized networks using Cisco hardware and software. (D.1)
Demonstrate teamwork skills in labs and projects to achieve specified requirements. (E.1)

32531.title: Global Information Systems
32531.description: This subject explores how globalisation has redefined information systems to support international business operations, including alliances and joint ventures. You'll examine the global IT industry's trajectory and structure, the strategic value of IT in business, and the impact of e-commerce, customer relationship management, knowledge management, outsourcing, and offshoring. Legal considerations in the digital economy for formalising business relationships are also addressed. Emphasis is placed on organising business information, with particular attention to informal flows within organisations. You'll learn about varying work types, team formation, and management processes, alongside practical skills in using portals and other tools to build relationships, maintain customer loyalty, and manage outsourcing partnerships.
learningOutcomes: Analyse the legal and cultural issues and implications related to implementation of global information systems to a range of products and services. (B.1)
Evaluate the effect and relationship of disruption and sustainability of technologies people and businesses within the global environment. (B.1)
Analyse information processes and management structures arising out of conducting business within the global environment. (D.1)
Explain the characteristics of global information systems and their role in business to a diverse range of people. (E.1)
Collaboratively work in defined roles to produce design solution to complex problem. (E.1)

32548.title: Cybersecurity
32548.description: This subject deepens your understanding of cybersecurity from both technical and management viewpoints. You'll explore and discuss cyber-attack methods and defense strategies using industry-standard tools. Key topics include cyber-attacks and defenses, web security, firewalls, intrusion detection systems, and security services like confidentiality, integrity, and authentication (CIA). You'll also learn about technologies including IPSec, SSL, PGP, and S/MIME. You will perform research on recent cyber-attacks and their mitigation methods to master the skills applied in industry context.
learningOutcomes: Recognise and compare major theories and principles that are used in the implementation of a secure network. (D.1)
Apply the underlying algorithms used to construct Security Protocols. (D.1)

32557.title: Enabling Enterprise Information Systems
32557.description: This postgraduate subject explores how information systems generate business value, focusing on various enterprise information needs and the application of systems to address business challenges. By taking this subject, you will gain a deep understanding of the strategic organisational use of information systems, mobile, cloud, and social computing. This knowledge will be invaluable in advancing your career in business or technology management, as you will be able to leverage cutting-edge technologies to solve real-world business problems. You'll develop essential skills in analysing market trends, designing effective information systems, and aligning them with business strategies. These skills are critical for roles in IT management, consulting, and strategic planning. Furthermore, engaging in design activities and collaborating in teams will enhance your practical and interpersonal skills, making you more effective in professional settings. Learning in this subject is interactive and hands-on. You'll participate in lectures, tutorials with case studies, and team projects, which will help you apply theoretical knowledge to practical scenarios. This approach ensures that you not only understand the concepts but also can implement them in a business context.

Propose effective, human-centered information systems that align with business strategies and positively impact lives through social innovation. (C.1)

Apply a deep understanding of the strategic use of information systems, identifying business processes and utilising mobile, cloud, and social computing technologies to address business challenges. (D.1)

Engage in design activities and team projects to enhance practical, interpersonal, and communication skills, applying theoretical knowledge to practical scenarios and justifying effective teamwork in solving innovation-driven problems. (E.1)
Reflect on the individual impact of participation and collaboration activities that influenced decisions for improved business solutions. (F.1)

33116.title: Design, Data, and Decisions
33116.description: This subject focuses on data analysis. You will learn how to collect and analyse data, and how to draw valid conclusions from the data. You'll begin by examining how to sample from a population, and how to describe the data collected. You will then explore how to form and test hypotheses about the population using the data collected from the sample.

distinguish between observational and experimental studies, and draw conclusions appropriate to each type of study

33130.title: Mathematics 1
33130.description: This subject helps you develop the knowledge and skills necessary for problem-solving and mathematical modelling at an introductory level. You will apply differential calculus to model situations in science and engineering that involve oscillations. Integral calculus is used to solve selected problems involving first- and second-order differential equations, and to calculate areas, volumes, lengths and other physical quantities. You will be introduced to vectors, matrix multiplication and determinants, and apply them to problem-solving and modelling. You'll also review sequences and series and be introduced to power series to approximate more functions.
learningOutcomes: Describe the relevance of mathematics to engineering and science and the role which engineering and science play in the development and evolution of mathematical ideas and methods.
Apply mathematical tools and resources to model real world problems in engineering and science.
Demonstrate correct use of mathematical terminology and concepts, and show understanding of those concepts by describing them in both formal and informal language.
Achieve a high level of skill in the mathematical techniques covered in the subject content.
Communicate mathematical knowledge clearly, logically and critically.

35005.description: This subject teaches Fourier Analysis, the decomposition of functions or signals into sines and cosines, essential in fields where periodicity is key, such as Engineering, Finance, and Biology. 35007.description: This subject develops advanced methods in vector calculus, partial differential equations, and complex analysis. It covers vector fields and differential operators, including the Laplacian, and introduces techniques such as Fourier series and Green’s functions for solving differential equations. The subject also studies analytic functions, contour integration, and residue calculus. Applications are drawn from differential equations, signal analysis, and mathematical modelling.

Analyse and solve partial differential equations using methods such as separation of variables and Fourier series.
Demonstrate understanding of complex functions, including differentiation, integration, and series expansions in the complex plane.
Apply contour integration and residue theory to evaluate integrals and solve applied problems.
Communicate mathematical reasoning and solutions clearly, and interpret results in the context of mathematical modelling applications.

35010.description: Quantitative knowledge and skills are fundamental to many disciplines and many professions. apply mathematical knowledge and skills in a variety of situations, in both familiar and new contexts

36100.title: Data Science for Innovation
36100.description:
This subject introduces students to the cutting-edge initiatives that organisations and professionals are embarking on to extract and communicate value from data. The subject contextualises professional data science practices for innovation by drawing together skills and knowledge regarding data, communication, and ethics.

Students examine contemporary cases illustrating how novel data sources can act as catalysts to drive innovation and transform industries and professions globally in health, finance, insurance, management, marketing, journalism, librarianship, education, science, transportation, aviation and the environment. First-hand exploratory interaction with data enables students to engage in inquiry-based research to seek informative correlations, patterns and trends leading to discoveries, and identify data discovery studies of interest to them. Through hands-on data discovery experiments, students explore data as complex and heterogeneous, with new techniques and technologies raising implications for approaches to the ethical and legal collection of personal data.
learningOutcomes: Apply data summarization and preprocessing techniques to clean, transform, and prepare data for analysis, ensuring data quality and integrity.
Formulate and test hypotheses, interpret p-values, and make informed conclusions based on statistical evidence.
Utilize clustering and association rule analysis to extract insights from transdisciplinary data through innovative methods.

Conduct classification and regression tasks with innovative approaches, creating models capable of categorizing both structured and unstructured data into predefined classes or predicting continuous numerical outcomes.

Effectively communicate transdisciplinary data discovery projects tailored to the specific discipline, audience, and purpose, and critically evaluate the privacy, ethical, and legal implications of collecting and publishing personal data.

36101.title: Leading Data Science Initiatives
36101.description: This subject equips you with leadership skills specifically for data-driven projects by combining project management techniques with data lifecycle principles. You’ll learn to plan, execute, and deliver data initiatives while effectively managing scope, time, and cost. Essential skills covered include team building, leadership, stakeholder engagement, and project management. You’ll delve into various project management methodologies and create comprehensive data management plans. Key topics include data infrastructure, data policies, privacy, security, ethics.
learningOutcomes: Apply project management best practices to data-driven projects.
Integrate data management with project delivery frameworks across different industries and projects.
Design and construct project initiation and planning artefacts for data projects.
Develop and manage project team and stakeholder communication.
Evaluate the risks for data projects and the impact of external contexts on project governance and delivery.

36103.title: Statistical Thinking for Data Science
36103.description: This subject instills the statistical thinking central to data science, teaching you to apply statistical methods to extract insights from data. You'll start with fundamental principles and modern inference methods, gaining hands-on experience with real-world data. Progressing to statistical models and estimation techniques, you'll complete a data science research cycle, formulating questions, analyzing data, and communicating results effectively. The subject begins with workshops and lectures, transitioning to self-directed learning, fostering your growth as a data scientist. By the end, you'll have a solid foundation in the technical, conceptual, and practical realms of data science.
learningOutcomes: Manage data science project complexities.
Formulate precise data science inquiries and justify the use of appropriate statistical concepts and tools to respond to those questions.
Find, clean, and merge datasets from a range of sources to answer real world data science problems.
Apply appropriate statistical methods for datasets and interpret and communicate the results in ways that suit the needs of diverse stakeholders.
Engage with the local and global data science professional community to build ethical practices and responsibilities when working with Indigenous data and communities.

36106.title: Machine Learning Algorithms and Applications
36106.description: This subject introduces students to key machine learning algorithms and their application in real-world settings. Participants are guided in developing an intuitive understanding of how the algorithms work, as well as their strengths and weaknesses. In addition to gaining practical experience with the algorithms, students develop an understanding of the basic principles of machine learning and the connections between different algorithms. Additionally, they are exposed to industry standard methodologies for data mining and analytics via readings and assessments. Since data science problems are infused with assumptions, often with ethical and legal implications, due attention is given to questioning the assumptions behind data and approaches used to analyse it.
learningOutcomes: Apply an industry standard analytics life cycle methodology for data mining and pattern discovery
Interpret, synthesise and communicate insights extracted from machine learning algorithms in a context-appropriate manner.
Articulate the strengths, weaknesses and assumptions of a selection of machine learning algorithms in relation to structured and unstructured data
Execute and interpret machine learning approaches available for extracting value from data
Demonstrate an appreciation, with examples, of a critical, ethical perspective on decisions made throughout the analytics lifecycle

36121.title: Artificial Intelligence Principles and Applications
36121.description:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is one of the hottest topics in computer science and engineering in the modern era. It is at the heart of current technology and the applications and understanding of AI helps to solve many contemporary and future real world problems. Artificial intelligence is a research domain and the knowledge of AI helps us to understand the intelligent human behaviors on a computer.

The key objectives of AI are to make a computer in such a way that it can plan, learn, and resolve problems autonomously. Through this subject students get the idea of current research topics in artificial intelligence include reasoning, general problem solving approaches, planning, learning and so on. They learn advanced search techniques in AI for introducing innovative Artificial Intelligence solutions.

This advanced AI subject helps students to learn and strengthen their technical skills and build their careers in AI based industries. Furthermore, this subject helps students to solve real world complex problems based on AI techniques.
learningOutcomes: Understand general problem-solving approaches in AI.
Apply knowledge of logic and structural knowledge representation.
Utilise Bayesian Networks and probabilistic reasoning.
Work with deep neural networks, multilayer networks, and decision trees.
Explore real-world applications of AI considering AI Ethics and Responsible AI Design.

36122.title: Python Programming
36122.description:
Programming is the process of designing, writing, testing, and maintaining computer programs, which are sets of instructions that a computer can execute to perform specific tasks.

This subject provides students with a basic understanding of the fundamental programming concepts that are inherent in all computer programs. In addition, an introduction is given to the principals involved in designing, developing, testing and debugging software applications. Students obtain knowledge and skills with procedural and object-oriented programming.

Specific concepts include defining data types, control flow, iteration, functions and recursion. Advanced object-oriented programming topics including encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism and abstraction will also be introduced. Students are able to reinterpret a general problem into a computer problem and apply the object-oriented analysis and design fundamentals to develop source code.
learningOutcomes: Apply programming style conventions to consistently write readable code.
Create entire procedural programs based on descriptive problem specifications.

Demonstrate a profound understanding of programming principles, encompassing data types, variables, operators, and control-flow structures such as simple statements, sequences, if-then-else constructs, while loops, and functions
Construct and evaluate code for recursively-defined numerical functions and array manipulations
Apply fundamental concepts of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) including encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism to design and implement modular, reusable, and extensible software solutions.
Apply effective testing methods and assess programs through debugging, showcasing the ability to create a set of tests for a small program or function.
Proficiently use standard library functions to enhance program functionality.
Design and implement Graphical User Interfaces (GUIs) for applications, integrating user-friendly interactive elements to enhance the user experience and functionality.

36127.title: Innovation Lab: Capstone Project
36127.description: This innovation lab (iLab) - capstone subject focuses students towards designing and investigating a data-driven prototype in using contemporary techniques and multi-structure data sets. This subject is unique compared to those in other data science courses in that it allows students to work on real world problems using experimental approaches from conceptualisation, design to data search and analytics to proposing solutions.This simulates a ‘virtual’ work environment type scenario making it highly applicable in a real working environment whilst still allowing both disciplinary and transdisciplinary approaches to be pushed to its boundaries towards innovative ideas. Student teams work on diverse data-driven solutions for complex real-world challenges. Using a range of open data sets and suitable case studies, students hone their skills in framing questions useful for embarking upon discoveries, addressing gaps in knowledge or tackling problems in the lab environment, suitable for adaption in a work context. Students communicate the outcomes of their innovative lab investigations to relevant audiences.
learningOutcomes: Research and apply critically and creatively the knowledge and skills gained to complex challenges by engaging with a variety of data and different analytic techniques, building upon transdisciplinary skills to be an ‘agent of change’ in the data science profession.

Investigate, analyze and evaluate open data sources ethically using problem finding and problem-solving techniques, including human centered approaches to enrich data sense making, inform trends and propose new ideas, products or services.

37234.title: Mathematical Analysis
37234.description:
This subject develops the rigorous foundations of calculus. It introduces the structure of the real numbers and the least upper bound property, and builds a precise understanding of limits, continuity and differentiation. You will study Taylor series, Riemann integration and the fundamental theorem of calculus, as well as sequences and series of functions, including uniform convergence.

Emphasis is placed on logical reasoning and the construction of clear and rigorous mathematical proofs. The subject develops your ability to analyse mathematical statements, justify arguments and communicate solutions with precision.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate understanding of the theoretical foundations of calculus, including real numbers, limits, continuity, differentiation and integration.
Analyse sequences, series and functions, including concepts of convergence and uniform convergence.
Construct clear and rigorous mathematical proofs using appropriate definitions, theorems and logical arguments.
Communicate mathematical reasoning and solutions precisely using appropriate notation and structure.

37242.title: Introduction to Optimisation
37242.description: This subject introduces the optimization methods and quantitative management concepts that are essential for decision-making in the fields such as supply chain management, financial analysis, transportation, production planning, and scheduling. learningOutcomes: Apply fundamental principles and concepts of mathematical programming to analyse tractable simplifications of real-world problems in quantitative management and engineering, and demonstrate the understanding of the limitations of the simplified problem formulations;
Choose and implement the most appropriate mathematical programming method to solve a particular optimisation problem
Present the results of modelling task in a written report providing concise mathematical programming-based analysis and explanation of the methodology used.

37495.description: This subject explores evaluation study methods, advancing from regression models to include basic randomised control trials (RCTs), survey design and estimation, time series analysis for interventions like the Sydney 'Lock-Out Laws', propensity score adjustment, and two-stage regression. 38003.title: Time Series and Stochastic Calculus
38003.description: This subject introduces fundamental concepts and methods in time series modelling, stochastic calculus, and probability theory in preparation for further studies in mathematics, particularly in quantitative finance. Following a discussion of essential concepts in probability theory and stochastic process, this subject examines classical time series models such as the autoregressive moving average (ARMA) and generalized autoregressive conditionally heteroskedastic (GARCH) models. The subject then covers the essential theory and techniques in stochastic calculus for continuous-time stochastic processes, culminating in the study of stochastic integration, Ito’s formula, martingales, and change of measure techniques. Applications of the models and methods are illustrated using real financial data and computational software.
learningOutcomes: Define the main probability-theoretic and statistical concepts required in the analysis of discrete-time and continuous-time stochastic processes
Model the evolution of random phenomena using standard techniques in time series modelling and stochastic calculus

Formulate regression models for analysis of a complicated data set
Apply appropriate models and perform analyses and diagnostics using the computer packages R, BUGS and/or Stan
Derive expressions used for fitting and inference in generalised linear and mixed models
Write independent code in the R language

38006.title: Machine Learning: Mathematical Theory and Applications
38006.description: This subject offers a comprehensive introduction to machine learning, covering fundamental techniques and their applications across engineering, statistics, and economics. You will gain a deep understanding of supervised, semi-supervised, and unsupervised learning, regularisation, decision trees, ensemble methods, Gaussian processes, and deep learning. Practical experience is emphasised through hands-on implementation and use of machine learning algorithms and popular software packages.
learningOutcomes: Understand the balance between bias and variance in machine learning models and evaluate a model based on its predictive performance
Formulate an appropriate model for a given dataset and determine an estimation approach
Implement and evaluate machine learning algorithms using programming skills
Demonstrate effective collaboration and communication skills to solve machine learning problems and compare possible solutions

38007.title: Financial Market Instruments
38007.description: This subject provides a rigorous introduction to the main financial instruments and markets that comprise the financial system and to the pricing of financial instruments using no-arbitrage arguments. Examples of financial instruments covered in the subject include equities and foreign exchange, bills and bonds, forward rate agreements (FRAs), and interest rate swaps. This subject also closely covers the basics of options contracts, including definitions, strategies, and valuation.
learningOutcomes: Understand the mechanics of the common financial market instruments and their applications in markets. In particular, students should have an in-depth knowledge of basic fixed income securities, forward and futures on equity, FX and interest rate, interest rate swaps and options
Apply the pricing formulae for these instruments under various scenarios
Compute the risks associated with these instruments and apply techniques to manage these risks
Construct various types yield curves from traded instruments
Understand option contracts and devise option trading strategies

38008.title: Interest Rates and Credit Risk Models
38008.description: This subject focuses on topics of interest rate theory and credit risk modelling and emphasises their analogies. In this subject, you will obtain a thorough working knowledge of models for interest rate and credit risk, their practical implementation and calibration to market data, and their underlying assumptions and limitations. In the process, you will also master the mathematical techniques underpinning the models. The subject covers the following major topics: products of fixed-income markets, short-rate models, forward-rate and LIBOR market models, financial instruments in credit risk management. In the framework of models of default, discussions will cover the pros and cons of synthetic credit-linked instruments, the dependence structure of default events, and default contagion and its role in the global financial crisis.
learningOutcomes: Apply and calibrate to market data standard stochastic models of interest rate and credit risk
Derive closed-form and near closed-form solutions to derivative pricing problems involving interest rate and credit risk
Understand the ethical issues and potential conflicts of interest that can arise in the design, valuation and issuance of structured financial products

38009.title: Master Research Capstone (Quantitative Finance)
38009.description: Given the increasing complexity of financial markets, numerical and computational methods for solving quantitative finance problems have become essential to derive concrete insights from sophisticated financial models. This capstone project subject concentrates on developing practical skills for solving quantitative finance problems using numerical and computational approaches. You will conceptualise and articulate a quantitative finance problem based on current industry examples and emerging industry trends and devise and execute a suitable theoretical and computational framework for solving the problem. You will then implement the theoretical and computational framework you have devised to address the quantitative finance problem you have identified. Informed by your analysis, you will communicate your findings through a detailed report and present your key findings and insights to a specialist audience.
learningOutcomes: Report, in both written and oral forms, the chosen quantitative finance problem, the proposed methodological framework, the implementation of the framework, and the results and insights from the analysis using professional language
Formulate a sound computational/numerical framework to solve the quantitative finance problem and implement the framework in Python
Identify and apply mathematical, statistical, and quantitative techniques required to address and solve the chosen quantitative finance problem
Identify and articulate a quantitative finance problem, including its context, motivation, and implications on academic literature and/or quantitative finance practice

38010.title: Quantitative Methods for Risk Analysis
38010.description: This subject offers a comprehensive and rigorous exposition to the theory and practice of financial risk measurement and management. The subject covers the value-at-risk (VaR) and expected shortfall (ES) risk measures, which are pertinent to current financial regulatory frameworks. Parametric and non-parametric techniques, including historical and Monte Carlo simulation, to calculate or approximate risk measures are covered. Furthermore, in view of emerging evidence of the intricate interplay of risk factors, you will also study general notions of dependence beyond linear correlation. To more accurately model the dependence structure between risk factors, copulas are discussed in depth and applied to the calculation of risk measures. You will then apply these risk modelling and management concepts to the analysis of market risk and operational risk, among others.
learningOutcomes: Explain the regulatory environment for financial risk management as specified, for example, by the Basel Accords (Basel II and Basel III) and Solvency II
Identify and model key risk events and risk factors facing financial institutions, especially with respect to complex portfolios of financial instruments, and the financial industry at large
State and interpret the properties of risk measures (including value-at-risk and expected shortfall) and compare and contrast different risk measures in terms of these properties
Quantify and analyse the market risk exposure of complex portfolios using various risk measures and calculation methods
Characterise and analyse the dependence structure between and among risk factors and effectively utilise copulas to model these dependence structures

38011.title: Fundamentals of Derivative Security Pricing
38011.description: This subject provides an intuitive grasp of derivative securities pricing. You'll explore the theory of arbitrage pricing in discrete and continuous time, various interpretations of arbitrage pricing conditions, and their resolution via partial differential equations, martingale, and integral evaluation perspectives. The subject also examines exotic options, American options, and option pricing under stochastic volatility and jump-diffusion models.
learningOutcomes: Understand the assumptions and the mathematical background of derivative pricing theory in continuous time

Implement the theoretical models of continuous time finance and to develop intuition for the underlying financial issues and aspects such as arbitrage-free derivative pricing, martingales, stochastic volatility and jump-diffusion models
Understand available literature on derivative securities pricing
Price derivative securities from both the partial differential equation and the martingale viewpoints

40005.title: Advanced iOS Development
40005.description: This subject offers an advanced insight into iOS application development with Swift and SwiftUI, where you'll master complex concepts, frameworks, and tools to create robust, innovative iOS apps. It emphasises hands-on experience with industry-standard practices, pushing you to devise solutions that address real-world software needs.
learningOutcomes: Design well-structured solution blueprints that satisfy given software requirements within the iOS development environment. (C.1)
Develop skills and competencies in implementing a solution using Swift programming language with the iOS development environment. (D.1)
Work with teams when designing and developing iOS applications and communicate the developed solution to a wider audience. (E.1)

40006.title: iOS industry Studio
40006.description: This studio is designed to enhance your practical iOS application development skills to become professionally competent. You will participate in reflective design practices, collaborate in teams, receive mentorship and learn advanced techniques. This hands-on learning experience will provide you with a comprehensive understanding of the iOS development environment and its frameworks to deliver real-world applications.
learningOutcomes: Identify the social impacts of iOS applications. (B.1)
Design a solution to demonstrate software skills with SwiftUI. (C.1)
Demonstrate technical capability in software development techniques and tools with SwiftUI. (D.1)
Demonstrate communication and collaboration skills in a team to develop iOS applications. (E.1)
Critically self-review their performance to improve themselves and their teams. (F.1)

40007.title: iOS Innovation Studio
40007.description: This Foundational studio subject offers you a challenge-based learning environment where you will develop fundamental skills in solving real-world problems, collaborating in diverse teams, and designing and developing apps within the Apple iOS ecosystem. The subject empowers you with a skill set at the intersection of technology, creativity, and entrepreneurship. Through the studio experience, you will work in multidisciplinary cohorts mixing with peers from a range of backgrounds and experiences to work through the design thinking process to develop a semi-functional iOS prototype app.
learningOutcomes: Identify and engage with a range of project stakeholders to obtain domain-specific knowledge. (B.1)
Apply Design Thinking approaches to design user-friendly digital solutions to meet stakeholder requirements. (C.1)
Produce a semi-functional prototype using Swift and Xcode to implement an iOS app. (D.1)
Collaboratively articulate project milestones based on feedback and teamwork that address a real-world problem. (E.1)
Reflect throughout design and development process with feedback to justify areas of, and potential for, professional growth as IOS technologist. (F.1)

40008.title: Career Management
40008.description: This subject equips you with the skills and knowledge to excel in initial workplace roles, enhancing your employability and professional conduct. You'll learn to craft compelling job applications, excel in interviews, and navigate Australian workplace culture, including effective time management and wellbeing. Active learning is central, with a flipped classroom approach requiring pre-class preparation, enabling in-class discussions and practical exercises on job-seeking and workplace integration. Group projects from Week 4 foster teamwork and project management skills. Additionally, you'll refine your academic and professional language, with milestone tasks gauging your progress in these areas and subject-specific objectives.
learningOutcomes: Identify and reflect on project management strategies in industry. (D.1)
Reflect on the effectiveness of and apply interpersonal skills in team work. (F.1)
Apply self-marketing strategies for job applications and interviews. (F.1)
Reflect on personal capabilities, professional behaviours and skills required to be successful in your career. (F.1)

41001.title: Cloud Computing and Software as a Service
41001.description: This subject introduces you to cloud computing, covering cloud architecture, IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, virtualisation, and multi-tenancy. You'll engage in group work to produce a research report critically analysing a cloud computing aspect, followed by developing cloud-based software engineering skills on an existing platform. The second assignment involves group collaboration to create a cloud-based software application.
learningOutcomes: Articulate the need for cloud computing, elements of cloud computing for e-business, e-government, e-banking, e-health and e-learning. (B.1)
Describe the architecture of different types of Cloud Services (IaaS, PaaS and SaaS), different types of Virtualization and their industrial use. (D.1)
Critically understand the current issues in Cloud Computing for informed business decision making. (D.1)
Create a Cloud Computing prototye that will be on a Cloud platform for areas such as e-government, e-banking, e-health and e-learning. (C.1)

41012.title: Programming for Mechatronic Systems
41012.description: This subject lays out the theoretical foundations of object-oriented programming using C++, honing your skills in designing, implementing and managing code for moderately complex mechatronics systems. You'll learn to create modular, reusable, reliable, and maintainable code. Through an individual project, you'll apply these concepts to design and implement components of a mechatronic system, tackling real-life challenges. The curriculum covers objects, classes, abstraction, inheritance, polymorphism, threading, event handling, and the use of C++ standard features like the STL, APIs, middleware, as well as documentation and testing strategies.
learningOutcomes: Design classes that are reusable, reliable and maintainable. (C.1)
Apply theoretical knowledge of sensors and control to practical programming problems. (D.1)
Select appropriate class structures and data handling methods for task at hand. (D.1)
Implement and test object-oriented applications of moderate complexity. (D.1)
Communicate programming design decisions, dependencies, interconnections, use cases and testing procedures in a written document. (E.1)

41012.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge of the C language and digital systems

41013.title: Industrial Robotics
41013.description: This introductory subject on industrial robotics arms you with an understanding of robot manipulator representation, kinematics, and control. You'll explore the diverse tasks that robots can undertake and, in teams, construct a simulated industrial robot, developing both the model and the necessary control and planning software. Safety is a core component, with a focus on integrating safe design and operating procedures to mitigate risks. Additionally, the subject prompts critical thinking on the ethical implications of the growing presence of robots in industry and daily life, including the socioeconomic impacts on the human workforce.
learningOutcomes: Describe mathematically and programmatically the relative position/ orientation of robots and objects. (D.1)
Describe which safety systems can be used in robotics and reflect on safety engineering in relation to robotics. (B.1)
Reflect on your learning of what robots are, their advantages/disadvantages, their future role, and ethical implications of robots on humans in the global community. (B.1)
Model robots in a workspace to enable collision detection and avoidance. (C.1)
Describe, implement and apply straightforward path planning techniques used for industrial robots. (D.1)
41013.requisiteText: (1 AND 2 AND (3 OR 3a OR 3b OR 3c OR 3d))

41014.title: Sensors and Control for Mechatronic Systems
41014.description: This subject aims to enhance your theoretical knowledge and practical skills in sensing, estimation, as well as feedback control techniques for mechatronic and robotic systems. You'll learn to select and evaluate sensors, process sensor data, and implement computer-aided tools for designing estimation and control systems that leverage sensory information. Key topics include visual and depth sensing, time-of-flight measurements, detection, tracking, state-space modelling, estimation (Kalman filter) and advanced control strategies like linear quadratic control. Real-world engineering case studies will contextualise and examine these concepts.
learningOutcomes: Explain the fundamental working principles of sensors and demonstrate data acquisition from these sensors for use in mechatronic system applications. (D.1)
Apply knowledge of image processing and active sensor processing for using the data to guide mechatronic systems. (D.1)
Apply knowledge of advanced control techniques to control mechatronic systems. (D.1)
Design sensor, signal processing and control solutions to solve practical problems. (C.1)
41014.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have basic knowledge of classical control techniques.

41019.title: Prototyping Physical Interaction
41019.description: This subject hones your ability to design, assess, and implement interactive physical devices with a human-centred approach. You'll learn to prototype using sensors, actuators, and diverse display methods to enhance user interaction and experience. By processing sensor data and designing multimodal feedback, you'll refine your prototypes through iterative user assessments, progressively perfecting the design.
learningOutcomes: Use a human-centred design process to design and develop an interactive system. (C.1)
Model a physical interactive system for a project. (C.1)
Embed sensors and process sensor data to support the user experience of a physical interactive system. (D.1)
Assess the usability and appropriateness of an interactive system through studying use in context. (C.1)
Communicate design and implementation strategies effectively to a range of disciplinary and non-disciplinary stakeholders. (E.1)
41019.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have some basic programming knowledge, but no particular language knowledge is assumed.

41020.title: Human-centred Design Methods
41020.description: This subject focuses on making people the core of the interaction design process through human-centred design methods, with particular attention to the interviewing and probes methods. Interviewing gathers direct information and adapts flexibly across the design process, while probes, using tailored props, require more setup but aim to inspire creative insights and prepare participants for a follow-up interview. You'll learn both methods, applying them step-by-step to real participants, guided by a brief and with readings and examples to tailor your approach. You must recruit at least three strangers (people you do not know and who are not familiar with the subject) for interviews and one stranger for the probe study.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of human-centred design methods. (D.1)
Demonstrate an ability to plan, design and carry out small user research projects. (C.1)
Develop an analysis of the findings from user research suitable for use in professional projects. (B.1)
Explain results and outcomes to others in their cohort and to broader audiences through paper writing, poster and video presentations. (E.1)
Apply positive and respectful ethical practices, such as the AIATSIS Code and NHMRC’s ethical code for researchers. (A.1, B.1)
41020.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject be familiar with the basics of human-computer interaction, human-centred design and evaluation methods; the principles and use of iterative design cycles of reflection, prototype (re)design and evaluation; and issues relating to data gathering and analysis.

41024.title: Advanced Games Programming
41024.description: This developing level subject dives into the advanced games topics of artificial intelligence, procedural content generation, and networked multiplayer. You will learn these topics by utilising the industry-standard game engine, Unreal Engine 5, and the C++ programming language. You will learn skills and concepts through assessed weekly lab modules that will teach you skills and algorithms that are transferable between game development environments and that can generalise across many aspects of games development. You will further develop your understanding of these topics and combine them in a session-long group project that will culminate in a novel game or tool prototype that enhances your portfolio and prepares you for significant contributions to third-year capstone projects. The subject's development was supported by the 2019 Epic MegaGrants scheme.
learningOutcomes: Understand advanced concepts in games programming and conduct self-directed learning to explore such topics in-depth. (D.1)
Iteratively design and develop technical demonstrations that combine numerous forms of fundamental and advanced game development techniques. (C.1)
Collaborate with group members to share knowledge of advanced game development topics, resulting in the design of unified user experience. (E.1)
Abstract and communicate the intent, benefits, and complexities of an advanced game or tool design to a wider audience of peers. (E.1)
Critically analyse the prototypes of others and provide professional and constructive feedback. (E.1)

41025.title: Introduction to Software Development
41025.description: This subject introduces the fundamentals of modern software development, more specifically, website development. You will learn traditional and agile software development principles, methods, tools, and techniques, and explore current trends and challenges in software development. You will also learn how to design, develop, and evaluate software that implements commercially realistic but manageably small requirements. Teaching is delivered through pre-recorded lectures and hands-on workshops. In your weekly workshops and assessment tasks, you will be given assignments to modify or extend existing software features or functions and, at times, to create new ones. You will be encouraged to practice peer learning and collaboration, but ultimately, you must complete your tasks independently. By successfully completing this subject, you will experience, understand the importance of, and be able to apply sound professional practices in software development.
learningOutcomes: Investigate and solve software development problems with minimal supervision. (C.1)
Determine and balance the competing goals of software development activities within their constraints. (C.1)
Plan and manage a software development task to create, modify or extend a software feature or function to completion within the task constraints. (C.1)
Apply sound software engineering practices to successfully create, modify or extend a software feature or function. (C.1)
Communicate clearly software and task information to interested stakeholders. (E.1)

41026.title: Advanced Software Development
41026.description: This subject advances your understanding of software development, such as the design, development, and evaluation of a complex software system that fulfills specific functional and non-functional requirements. You will work in highly autonomous teams that, while supervised and directed, take full responsibility for the project and delivery of the expected outcomes. The subject focuses on professional practices including team management, project planning, and all key software development processes. You will also make and justify informed design decisions, enhancing your capability to deliver sound software solutions.
learningOutcomes: Elicit and manage customer requirements throughout the project. (B.1)
Design, construct and evaluate software to meet customer requirements. (C.1)
Implement a complex software development project using optimal methods and designs. (D.1)
Collaborate with team in a range of roles to manage the software development project to completion. (E.1)
Communicate relevant and timely project, software and team information to all stakeholders. (E.1)
41026.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have competence in programming and software development methods and tools

41028.description: This subject is for your engineering internship, You'll develop real-world skills and apply classroom learning in a professional setting, enhancing your employability. learningOutcomes: Communicate what has been learnt in the workplace and how it was learnt. (E.1)
Participate in the creation of workplace learning communities. (F.1)

41029.title: Engineering Capstone A
41029.description: This subject equips you with the skills to apply engineering knowledge and problem-solving in a capstone project, essential for your final year. You'll tackle complex engineering challenges relevant to industry, academia, or personal interests, developing expertise in research design, project management, and critical communication. Learning involves creating a theoretical framework and project plan, preparing you for the subsequent implementation phase. You'll engage in interactive workshops, focusing on topics like the social perspectives of engineering, research questions, literature reviews, methodologies, ethics. Resources on Canvas and the Reading List support your preparation, while regular meetings with your Capstone Supervisor and peer review seminars enhance your project's development and your ability to critique and improve work collaboratively. This subject hones your application of knowledge and research skills, aligning with Engineers Australia competencies and Australian Qualifications Framework standards for bachelor's and honours degrees.
learningOutcomes: Develop a research question that is related to their field of practice. (B.1)
Review the relevant research literature to identify an opportunity to contribute to an existing field of knowledge (B.1)
Design an ethical and sustainable research project with an appropriate methodology (C.1)

Seek and respond to feedback from supervisor and peers to inform reflection upon performance (E.1)

41033.title: Integrated Electronic Systems Design
41033.description: This subject provides an introduction to the fundamentals of electronics engineering and the electronics industry through practical lab and project work. You will learn the principles of basic analogue circuits, including signal processing and acquisition. The projects, both individual and team-based, involve constructing circuits based on the knowledge gained in class. You will also become proficient in using circuit simulation and layout software such as Advanced Design System (ADS), and MATLAB for circuit modelling and analysis.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate basic electronics circuitry knowledge and skills including software tools and hardware components. (D.1)
Solve electronics engineering problems using computer aided software solutions. (D.1)
Demonstrate familiarity with emerging cutting-edge electronics engineering technologies. (D.1)

41035.title: Professional Practice Preparation 1
41035.description: This subject teaches you how to apply for professional engineering or IT internships and how to learn on the job. You'll develop your commercial awareness and document your professional growth, while developing your awareness of professional ethics, safety, and how to communicate with employers. Through a blend of workshops and tutorials, you'll engage in active learning, preparing in advance with provided resources. In four key workshops, you'll gain essential knowledge and collaborate with peers. Additionally, four intensive tutorials offer a platform to review your peers’ work and exchange perspectives on how to effectively obtain a professional position and meet the learning outcomes.
learningOutcomes: Communicate professional attributes and job seeking strategies to secure an engineering or IT position. (E.1)
Reflect on professional responsibilities and attributes to communicate value to potential employers, and for lifelong learning. (F.1)
Identify ethical dimensions of professional situations to inform decision making. (B.1)
