41036.title: Professional Experience 1
41036.description: This subject serves as a practical foundation during your first industry internship. You will develop real-world skills and apply classroom learning in a professional setting, enhancing your employability. The learning experience is hands-on, with direct industry or community engagement, fostering a deeper understanding of engineering and IT practices in the workplace.
learningOutcomes: Learn, through practice, the fundamental workplace skills required of a professional engineer.

41038.title: Professional Practice Review 1
41038.description: This subject equips you with critical reflection and presentation skills, enhancing your professional development. You will analyse your performance in your first internship and determine how this will influence your second internship and your subsequent career. You will also deliver a concise online presentation describing your experiences as an intern. Your learning journey combines recorded lectures, interactive tutorials, and seminars, fostering both independent study and collaborative engagement. Prior to sessions, you'll engage with online resources and submit reflective entries, which serve as a foundation for peer feedback in tutorials. This process not only refines your skills but also aids in articulating your professional identity. You'll summarise peer feedback for assessment and later, present a three-slide narrative of your internship experience, encapsulating your growth and lessons learned.
learningOutcomes: Reflect on professional experience, and conduct critical self and peer review in order to plan for their own professional development. (F.1)
Articulate, in both written and verbal formats, the development of their professional identity to date. (E.1)

41039.title: Programming 1
41039.description: This subject provides a foundation in core programming concepts, vital for careers in computer science and software development. It emphasises project-based learning, independent research, and effective communication. You'll also be introduced to real-world programming practices, preparing you to tackle complex industry-level projects. This approach ensures you develop the multifaceted skill set required for solving sophisticated programming challenges.
learningOutcomes: Apply basic programming concepts of state, iteration, and decision. (D.1)
Solve computational problems by using abstract modelling and conceptualisation. (D.1)
Design and create simple functioning programs to achieve objectives. (C.1)
Interpret, describe, and document programs using clear communication. (E.1)
Reflect on programming decisions and formulate alternatives. (C.1)

41040.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
41040.description: This subject enhances your grasp of Artificial Intelligence (AI), covering learning, natural language processing, computer vision, search, knowledge representation, and reasoning. With lectures and practical labs focused on specific AI techniques, you'll learn to select appropriate models and algorithms for tasks and apply AI methods in simple applications. You will be assessed by a knowledge test, a set of mini-AI application examples and a group project addressing a real-world problem using AI technique, reflecting your ability for exemplifying AI applications and designing AI solutions in practical scenarios.
learningOutcomes: Explain key concepts and applications of AI techniques. (D.1)
Design solutions to implement AI techniques to solve simple real world problems. (C.1)
Communicate the application of AI techniques in collaboration with team members. (E.1)
41040.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have completed 33230 Mathematics 2 and 37181 Discrete Mathematics. It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have epxerience with linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete logic

41045.title: Professional Practice Preparation 2
41045.description: This subject prepares you for an engineering career by aligning with Engineers Australia Stage 2 Competency Standards. Through participation in five workshops, you'll gain insights into employment processes, ethics, social responsibility, and leadership, while honing creativity and understanding workplace culture. You'll develop communication skills and readiness for senior internships by engaging in collaborative tasks and reflective practices. Pre-workshop readings enable you to contribute effectively to discussions, equipping you for professional hurdles and continuous learning.
learningOutcomes: Articulate preparedness for participating in an engineering workplace as appropriate for a senior internship. (F.1)
Document and communicate capabilities to contribute to a workplace and engage in workplace learning. (E.1)

args.scope: spk(s): C09067 - Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) Diploma Professional Engineering Practice
spk(s): C09071 - Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) Bachelor of Business Diploma Professional Engineering Practice
spk(s): C09073 - Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) Bachelor of Science Diploma Professional Engineering Practice
spk(s): C09075 - Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) Bachelor of Medical Science Diploma Professional Engineering Practice
spk(s): C09124 - Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) Bachelor of International Studies Diploma Professional Engineering Practice

41046.title: Professional Experience 2
41046.description: This subject is essentially a 'placeholder' for while you are working in industry or the community for the purpose of the second of your two industry internships.
learningOutcomes: Participate in an engineering or IT workplace

41048.title: Professional Practice Review 2
41048.description: This subject allows you to reflect on and articulate your workplace learning, preparing you for chartered engineer status, a graduate engineering or IT role, or to contribute to the field. Through four interactive workshops and a Professional Practice & Leadership Forum, you'll present your work to industry experts. You'll also form a Peer Review Group for collaborative learning. Attendance at the forum is mandatory, though special consideration may be available if you're unable to present.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate personal commitment to, and capability to fulfill, their obligations to the engineering and IT communities. (F.1)
Reflect upon their professional capabilities and attributes and communicate these succinctly to potential employers and the wider professional engineering and IT communities. (F.1)
Communicate their professional capabilities and attributes to potential employers and the wider professional community. (E.1)

41052.title: Advanced Algorithms
41052.description: Algorithms are the heart of computer science and information technology. This subject dives deeply into more advanced data structures and algorithmic techniques for solving problems, particularly graph and optimisation problems. You will practice implementing these ideas to solve new problems, gain experience testing and evaluating the performance of algorithms, and learn to communicate algorithmic strategies effectively.
learningOutcomes: Understand computational problems and consider possible solutions in the context of their application areas. (D.1)
Apply advanced data structures, programming techniques and algorithmic paradigms to create efficient algorithms for computational problems. (C.1)
Evaluate the computational complexity of a problem or algorithm. (D.1)
Communicate the functioning of complex algorithms in collaboration with peers. (E.1)

41053.title: Materials and Manufacturing Engineering A
41053.description: This subject introduces you to engineering materials, their physical properties, and their integration into the design process. You will learn the principles of various manufacturing processes, i.e. casting, forming, machining, joining, powder metallurgy, heat treatment, surface treatment, and their influence on design. You will also learn the concept of additive manufacturing. By the end, you will possess fundamental knowledge for selecting suitable materials and manufacturing processes for specific components and applications.
learningOutcomes: Identify and select materials based on suitability of physical properties and environmental conditions. (D.1)
Recommend manufacturing processes that are best suited to producing simple artefacts and machine elements. (D.1)
Select and apply materials and manufacturing processes that are suitable for the design of a particular component. (C.1)

41054.title: Applied Mechanics and Design A
41054.description: In this foundational subject, you'll learn how to analyse and design load-bearing mechanical components to meet strength and stiffness requirements. You'll use the methods of engineering mechanics including free-body-diagrams and equations of equilibrium to determine external and internal forces and moments. You’ll use mechanics of materials methods to determine stress, strain and deflection. You'll also conduct laboratory experiments to determine mechanical properties of materials and component behaviour and compare your experimental results with theoretical calculations and published data.
learningOutcomes: Design simple machine structural components for strength and stiffness. (D.1)
Analyse relatively simple machine structural components by applying fundamental engineering mechanics and mechanics of materials concepts. (D.1)
Apply experimental and computational techniques to analyse simple mechanical components. (D.1)

41055.title: Professional Experience Review
41055.description: This subject equips you with the skills to articulate your professional identity and engage in effective verbal and written communication, essential for engineers. You'll develop a professional practice portfolio to showcase your capabilities and reflect on your experiences, meeting Engineers Australia's requirement of 12 weeks of professional practice. An interview assessing your professional experience and portfolio content is also part of the subject, which combines online and face-to-face learning, including an online lecture, tutorials, and a seminar. You'll engage with online resources to prepare for classes and assessments. The initial online lecture outlines the subject requirements, focusing on writing critical incidents and mastering constructive critique. Subsequent tutorials provide feedback opportunities for refining your portfolio, CV, and reflective writing, requiring you to review peers' work and summarise received feedback. The final seminar involves an assessed online interview, culminating your learning experience.
learningOutcomes: Reflect on professional experience, and conduct critical self and peer review in order to plan for their own professional development. (F.1)
Articulate, in both written and verbal formats, the development of their professional identity to date. (E.1)

41056.title: Machines and Mechanisms A
41056.description: The subject provides insights into the behaviour of solid bodies in motion, making it essential for fields including mechanical engineering, manufacturing engineering, aerospace engineering, biomedical engineering, etc. It equips you with the ability to solve the movement of interconnected bodies under the influence of external forces. You'll delve into the kinematics and kinetics of rigid bodies in planar motion, including displacements, velocities, accelerations, forces, energy, impulse and momentum, and learn the energy method, in contrast to direct applications of Newton's second law of motion. By studying the dynamics of real mechanical systems, you will appreciate the relevance of dynamics in engineering machines and structures.
learningOutcomes: Apply principles of kinematics and kinetics to the analysis of mechanical systems for determination of physical behaviour. (D.1)
Apply velocity and acceleration equations of a rigid body in planar motion to calculate forces, momentum and energy and simulate behaviour using suitable software tools. (D.1)
Design a simple mechanism, taking into account the dynamic forces associated with the mechanism. (C.1)

41057.title: Thermofluids A
41057.description: This subject imparts an understanding of fluids and heat transfer, which are integral to machine design and operation. You'll grasp key concepts and principles, enabling practical analysis and design of engineering systems. The curriculum fosters an interest in fluid and thermal phenomena, covering applications from basic to complex.
learningOutcomes: Assess the impact of efficiency and energy conservation in the engineering design process, including lifecycle costing. (B.1)
Apply fundamental principles of fluid mechanics and heat transfer to analyse engineering applications. (D.1)
Design simple fluid flow and heat transfer systems, in the context of Australian Standards. (C.1)

41058.title: Dynamic Systems and Control A
41058.description: This subject focuses on the critical role of vibration and noise control in the design, performance, and longevity of mechanical and structural systems. You'll learn to model simplified linear dynamic systems common in mechanical and mechatronic engineering and analyse their vibration behaviours subject to various inputs. You’ll also learn classical control engineering techniques to manipulate the dynamics of mechanical and mechatronic systems for desired outcomes. The concepts and tools covered are applicable across various engineering disciplines.
learningOutcomes: Model, measure, and analyse simple dynamic physical systems to determine their performance characteristics. (D.1)
Design closed-loop feedback control systems to meet specific performance, stability, robustness criteria, and standards. (C.1, D.1)
Interrogate results from theory, simulation and experimental to verify their accuracy and application to problems in vibration and control. (D.1)

41059.title: Mechanical Design Fundamentals Studio 1
41059.description: This first studio subject for Mechanical and Mechatronics Engineering students focuses on applying theoretical knowledge to a practical engineering challenge. You will engage in a design-and-build project, honing fundamental design skills by addressing a defined problem. The project involves going through the engineering design process to design and build a system for the Warman Design and Build Challenge. Success relies on effective teamwork, clear communication, and thorough documentation of the design process, including ideas, decisions, and justifications. Through the subject, you will enhance project management abilities, engineering documentation skills, and technical proficiency,  while showcasing creativity and collaboration.
learningOutcomes: Integrate relevant guidelines from the Engineers Australia Code of Ethics to guide project decisions and professional conduct. (B.1)
Demonstrate the ability to follow the engineering design process, from ideation to testing and validation, in the development of components of a larger system. (C.1)
Use CAD modelling and design documentation to communicate engineering designs. (D.1)
Demonstrate effective collaboration, proficient communication, and project management techniques to achieve team objectives. (E.1)
Reflect on feedback from mentors, self, peers, and team members to document evidence of critical analyses of improving performance. (F.1)
41059.requisiteText: (1 AND (2 OR 2a) AND (3 OR 3a OR 3b OR 3c))

41060.title: Mechanical Design Fundamentals Studio 2
41060.description: This studio subject expands on design methods from previous studies, introducing a systems thinking approach to complex thermo-fluidic system design, integrating both fluid and mechanical elements. You'll tackle a technical problem, applying systems thinking to devise a unique solution mindful of environmental and socio-economic impacts. This experience will enhance your ability to manage and innovate within the realm of heat and power transfer applications in engineering.
learningOutcomes: Establish priorities, uncertainties and risks (social, cultural, legislative, environmental, economics, etc.) by engaging with stakeholders to identify and scope a problem . (B.1)
Apply design/systems thinking to respond to a well-defined problem. (C.1)
Apply technical skills to develop, model and/or evaluate thermofluid designs. (D.1)
Demonstrate effective collaboration and communication skills as an effective team member or team leader. (E.1)
Conduct critical self, peer, and team reflection for performance improvement. (F.1)

41066.title: Mechanical Systems Design Studio 1
41066.description: This studio subject enhances your ability to critically interpret engineering designs and make informed decisions. You'll dissect the fit, form, and function of designs, applying reverse engineering to deconstruct and understand underlying concepts. Your analysis will critique the design's suitability, leading to the creation of an improved second-generation design, backed by sound reasoning and thorough justification. This process will sharpen your evaluative skills and decision-making in modern engineering design.
learningOutcomes: Conduct a design problem analysis and scoping, including justification of socio-technical requirements, uncertainties and risks. (B.1)
Reverse-engineer components that contribute to the solution of a system-level Mechanical Design problem. (C.1)
Evaluate design solutions using Mechanical Design skills and strategies. (D.1)
Evidence contribution on delivering the team’s project plan, re-design elements and project deliverables. (E.1)
Reflect on leadership, influence and impact relating to progress on individual capabilities. (F.1)
41066.requisiteText: ((1 OR 1a OR 1b) AND (2 OR 2a OR 2b OR 2c OR 2d OR 2e OR 2f))

41067.title: Mechanical Systems Design Studio 2
41067.description: This studio consolidates earlier concepts from foundational subjects and technical knowledge. You will learn and apply an established engineering systems design process that enables you to develop and design technical systems in a flexible yet systematic manner. Based on this, you'll tackle a broadly defined engineering problem, working in industry-style teams to deliver unique solutions. The project will expose you to key needs, requirements, and challenges of an industry-like project. The subject bridges engineering science and practice, concentrating on the methodical facets of engineering design, such as conducting relevant analyses and making informed technical decisions and recommendations.
learningOutcomes: Apply and justify a flexible engineering systems design process and methods to structure and solve a complex engineering design problem and react to changes (e.g. market, supplier, legislative, company-internal, etc.). (C.1)

Conduct a design problem analysis and scoping, including justification of socio-technical requirements, uncertainties and risks (e.g. social, cultural, legislative, and environmental, economics etc.) by engaging different stakeholders. (B.1)
Apply technical skills to develop, model, evaluate and/or justify alternative engineering designs. (D.1)
Evidence ownership of continuous delivering on project team plan, intermediate milestones, and project deliverables. (E.1)
Demonstrate the ability to learn from design reviews and improve engineering designs accordingly. (F.1)
Reflect personally on project original components, new idea components and impact of the application of the reflections. (F.1)
41067.requisiteText: ((1 OR 1a OR 1b) AND (2 OR 2a OR 2b OR 2c OR 2d OR 2e OR 2f))

41068.title: Robotics Studio 1
41068.description: This studio develops your skills in critiquing and designing modern estimation methods for robotics and mechatronic systems. You will dissect a mechatronics problem, discerning the requirements for an estimation solution and applying suitable techniques. Your analysis will assess the design's suitability and justify the choices made, deepening your understanding of the capabilities and limitations of these engineering tools in system design.
learningOutcomes: Establish priorities, uncertainties and risks to identify and scope a problem. (B.1)
Apply design/systems thinking to the analysis of a mobile robot problem. (C.1)
Apply technical skills to develop, model and/or evaluate an estimation solution. (D.1)
Demonstrate effective collaboration and communication skills as an effective member or team leader of team/s.  (E.1)
Conduct critical self, peer and team reflection for performance evaluation. (F.1)

41069.title: Robotics Studio 2
41069.description: Building upon previous studios and technical subjects, this studio engages you in interpreting a broadly defined robotics challenge, to be addressed with robot path-planning or control techniques. You will work in teams to devise a unique design solution using systems engineering principles, bridging engineering and professional practice. This subject blends technical design work with elements from systems engineering, requiring you to scope out a project, do the technical developments, plan and execute tests, and integrate multiple subsystems together as a team.
learningOutcomes: Apply design/systems thinking to the analysis of a robotics problem.  (C.1)
Apply technical skills to develop, model and/or evaluate a robotics path planning or control solution. (D.1)
Demonstrate effective collaboration and communication skills as an effective member or team leader of team/s. (E.1)
Conduct critical self, peer and team reflection for performance evaluation. (F.1)

41070.title: Embedded Mechatronics Studio
41070.description: In this studio, you'll advance your engineering design skills by creating an analog printed circuit board (PCB) that interfaces with an embedded system, sensors, and actuators to implement a sophisticated and intelligent device. You'll integrate knowledge from earlier studies, applying it to electronics and embedded system programming, gaining practical experience in electronic system design. The focus is on analog circuit design with elements from mechanical design and embedded programming, that is, the studio covers the three main pillars of any mechatronic system. By employing modern Electrical Computer-Aided Design (ECAD), you will learn about sensor signal conditioning, amplification, filtering, analog switching, generating haptic and visual inputs/outputs, and analog-to-digital conversion. Working in groups, you'll address a defined problem with a mechatronic solution and as such, success hinges on effective teamwork, clear communication, and thorough documentation of your design process and rationale.
learningOutcomes: Identify environmental and economic impacts of embedded mechatronic solutions in a given context. (B.1)
Apply systematic electronic and mechanical computer aided engineering synthesis and design processes in combination with embedded software to develop a mechatronic system. (C.1)
Use technical skills to develop, model, simulate, prototype, and evaluate electronic circuit designs and embedded software. (D.1)
Demonstrate effective collaboration, communication, and documentation skills as a member or team leader. (E.1)
Use feedback to reflect for performance evaluation and iterate on a given problem. (F.1)

41076.title: Methods in Quantum Computing
41076.description: This subject offers a structured introduction to quantum computing, a revolutionary technology poised to surpass traditional computing capabilities. You'll learn the fundamental principles, discover quantum algorithms, and acquire programming skills to develop software that leverages the extraordinary potential of quantum computers, preparing you for advancements expected in the near future.
learningOutcomes: Explain the advantages of quantum computing over classical computing. (D.1)
Evaluate the application of quantum computing technologies to known and unknown contexts. (D.1)
Analyse efficiency and complexity of quantum technologies. (D.1)

41078.title: Computing Science Studio 1
41078.description: This subject immerses you in the world of computer science research, examining its purpose and methodologies. You will develop academic writing skills for literature reviews and reports, explore research collaboration, leadership, and ethics, and under mentor guidance, investigate chosen topics. There's encouragement to consult with leading computer scientists and a focus on honing communication, ethical, and analytical skills vital for a career in computing science.
learningOutcomes: Identify the social and ethical impacts of computer science research in a given context. (B.1)
Design a methodological solution to systematically review a research field/topic. (C.1)
Implement a set of analytical methods, tools, and strategies to analyse and evaluate academic resources. (D.1)
Construct written, spoken, and visual communication with teamwork. (E.1)
Reflect self-development, learning experience, and collaborative interactions. (F.1)

requisite.scope: spk(s): C09119 - Bachelor of Computing Science (Honours)

41078.recommended: It is recommended that students complete all 1st-year Bachelor of Computing Science (Honours) subjects prior to commencing this subject.

41079.title: Computing Science Studio 2
41079.description: In this studio-based subject, you will apply your prior knowledge and cutting-edge research advances to solve real-world problems, often requiring cross-disciplinary solutions. From conceptualisation to execution, you will work in a team to develop and deliver a small project, guided by UTS's leading researchers. This experience will enhance your problem-solving skills, refine your communication skills, strengthen your grasp of professional ethics, and enhance your analytical abilities for critical literature evaluation, as a stepping stone for the research component in your computing science course. This subject builds upon the groundwork laid in Computing Science Studio 1.
learningOutcomes: Scope stakeholder needs and/or pain points of a problem using social, ethical, and economic awareness. (B.1)
Apply critical thinking, problem-solving and decision-making methodologies to design practical computing science solutions. (C.1)
Apply discipline fundamentals, software tools and state-of-the-art to develop and validate solutions for computing design problems. (D.1)
Communicate effectively in a collaborative environment to formulate computing science problems and contribute to deliver solutions. (E.1)
Self-review personal performance in terms of problem-solving, professional skills, and teamwork for continuous improvement. (F.1)
41079.recommended: It is recommended that students complete all 2nd-year Bachelor of Computing Science (Honours) subjects prior to commencing this subject.

41080.title: Theory of Computing Science
41080.description: This subject explores the theory of computation, covering automata, decidability, and computational complexity. These topics provide key tools for you to perform rewriting and parsing, and to determine the complexity of various problems. Understanding computational complexity is crucial for creating cost-effective and practical solutions, such as optimising large-scale problems in online services. Additionally, a firm grasp of computational theory underpins the creation of user-friendly, secure systems and the identification of performance issues in programming, leading to more efficient algorithm design.
learningOutcomes: Build models for real-world applications and plan computations realisable on computers. (C.1)
Formulate the Turing machine computation model using formal definition and higher-level operation description. (D.1)
Distinguish some decidable/non-decidable problems by proof in the Turing machine computation framework. (D.1)
Analyse algorithm efficiency and improve when possible. (D.1)

41082.title: Introduction to Data Engineering
41082.description: This subject lays the groundwork for understanding data engineering and its role in today's data-driven world. You'll actively engage in designing data collection experiments, processing and analysing data, and visualising it effectively for informed decision-making. You'll gather your own datasets or work with existing datasets for class activities and a culminating project. Proficiency in MATLAB, essential for modelling and analysis, is a key outcome. The subject is a core component for Data Science Engineering majors but is also open to students from other disciplines seeking to enhance their data engineering skills.
learningOutcomes: Use practical skills to model and simulate complex and complicated systems. (D.1)
Understand, collect and store data. (D.1)
Validate, visualise and authenticate data. (D.1)
Characterise the role of data engineering in data science projects. (B.1)
Design, perform and evaluate a data gathering activity using the Matlab environment. (C.1)

41084.title: Fundamentals Studio A
41084.description: This studio, the first in the fundamentals stage for Data and Electronic Engineering majors, moves beyond traditional curricula to foster an environment where you can apply and expand your knowledge through practical experience. It's centred on product development, requiring collaborative work in the studio with peers, academics, and industry mentors. You'll undertake a mix of self-directed study and team-based project work, progressing through stages of assessment, design, and implementation, mirroring the classic engineering process. Guided by a learning contract set at the start, you'll focus on acquiring fundamental skills and knowledge to realise basic product functionality, with an emphasis on creativity, technical expertise, teamwork, communication, and project management. Utilise this opportunity to delve into new topics that complement your coursework and personal interests.
learningOutcomes: Identify needs of a product owner and formulate product requirements to address those needs. (B.1)
Model, prototype and/or build a product to meet requirements. (C.1)
Demonstrate advancement of fundamental knowledge and skills appropriate to the student's discipline. (D.1)
Collaboratively work in defined roles to solve complex problems (E.1)
Demonstrate personal reflection on learning through engineering record keeping and knowledge sharing with peers (F.1)

41085.title: Fundamentals Studio B
41085.description: In this second studio of the Data and Electronic Engineering fundamentals stage, you're not confined to a standard curriculum but given the freedom to apply and enhance your knowledge through doing. The studio is a dynamic workspace where you'll collaborate with peers, academics, and industry mentors on product-based projects, blending individual study with team effort. Through the engineering process—assess, design, implement—you learn to apply knowledge to practical achievements. A learning contract directs your individual tasks from the outset. Here, you'll build on fundamental knowledge and skills to create a functioning product, emphasising creativity, diverse methods, technical growth, teamwork, communication, and project management. This studio is your chance to broaden your understanding by integrating new, personally interesting topics with previous coursework.
learningOutcomes: Identify needs of a product owner and formulate product requirements to address those needs. (B.1)
Model, prototype and/or build a product to meet requirements. (C.1)
Demonstrate advancement of fundamental knowledge and skills appropriate to the student's discipline. (D.1)
Collaboratively work in defined roles to solve complex problems (E.1)
Demonstrate personal reflection on learning through engineering record keeping and knowledge sharing with peers (F.1).

41086.title: Applications Studio A
41086.description: In this studio, the first in the applications stage for Data and Electronic Engineering majors, you'll transform knowledge into action within a non-traditional, hands-on learning environment. Engage in product-based projects inside the studio, working alongside fellow students, academics, and industry mentors, mixing self-study with collaborative teamwork. Following the engineering cycle—assess, design, implement—you'll apply your knowledge to achieve tangible outcomes, guided by a learning contract set early on. The Applications Studio hones your specialist theoretical understanding and practical skills, focusing on analysis, modelling, benchmarking, and simulation in product development. This studio expects a higher level of proficiency, with students ready to tackle more complex product development tasks, leveraging their advanced knowledge and skills.
learningOutcomes: Identify needs of a product owner and formulate product requirements to address those needs. (B.1)
Model, prototype and/or build a product to meet requirements. (C.1)
Demonstrate sophisticated analysis, modelling, benchmarking and theoretical understanding of concepts appropriate to the student's discipline. (D.1)
Apply a systematic approach to teamwork and project management in solving complex problems. (E.1)
Demonstrate personal reflection and next steps through systematic engineering record keeping and knowledge sharing with peers. (F.1)

41088.title: Professional Studio A
41088.description: In this first professional studio, you'll bridge theory and practice within a studio setting, translating knowledge into tangible capabilities. You'll collaborate with others, including industry and research product owners, to undertake project work that embodies the full engineering process: assess, design, and implement, all aligned with a learning contract. The Professional Studio emphasises your evolution into a professional engineer, reflected in product development choices that may range from industry-aligned to research-driven or entrepreneurial ventures. You'll incorporate industry standards and best practices, encompassing the entire product lifecycle from stakeholder analysis to validation and pitching. Beyond technical specifications, you're encouraged to consider commercialisation, intellectual property, ethics, equity, privacy and security aspects relevant to your product, preparing you for the multifaceted role of a professional engineer.
learningOutcomes: Identify needs of a product owner and formulate product requirements to address those needs. (B.1)
Model, prototype and/or build a product to meet requirements. (C.1)
Select and apply best practice in professional knowledge and skills appropriate to the product being developed and the student's discipline. (D.1)
Demonstrate superior capability and personal leadership in working as a team on complex product development. (E.1)
Demonstrate a professional approach to engineering record-keeping and personal reflection. (F.1)

41089.title: Professional Studio B
41089.description: In this second professional studio, you'll further develop the ability to turn knowledge into action in a studio environment. Collaborative and individual work, guided by a learning contract, will see you progress through the engineering phases of assessment, design, and implementation. This studio sharpens your focus on the professional engineering role within product development, allowing for industry, research, or entrepreneurial projects. You'll be expected to adhere to industry standards and best practices, managing the full product lifecycle from needs analysis to final validation and pitching. Critical thinking extends beyond technical achievements, encompassing commercial, ethical, and legal considerations, ensuring a comprehensive approach to your engineering practice.
learningOutcomes: Identify needs of a product owner and formulate product requirements to address those needs. (B.1)
Model, prototype and/or build a product to meet requirements. (C.1)
Select and apply best practice in professional knowledge and skills appropriate to the product being developed and the student's discipline. (D.1)
Demonstrate superior capability and personal leadership in working as a team on complex product development. (E.1)
Demonstrate a professional approach to engineering record-keeping and personal reflection. (F.1)

41091.title: Data Systems
41091.description: This subject delves into systems engineering for complex, data-centric systems, covering their lifecycle from design to management. You'll learn to build data pipelines through Extract, Transform, Load processes, apply Python for data engineering and reporting, and explore the Hadoop ecosystem and cloud data system providers. The learning experience is project-based, combining workshops on data engineering with collaborative project work, equipping you with practical, in-demand skills.
learningOutcomes: Define requirements and specifications of data system. (B.1)
Demonstrate a systematic design and thinking process for data system development. (C.1)
Prototype or implement data system according to system specifications. (D.1)
Communicate effectively to data system project stakeholders. (E.1)
Work effectively in a team to develop a data system, demonstrating continuous improvement and independence. (E.1, F.1)

41092.title: Network Fundamentals
41092.description:
This subject introduces the principles and practice of modern computer networking through a top-down exploration of the Internet and the TCP/IP protocol suite. Using Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach as the core text, students examine how networked applications communicate, how data is transported reliably and efficiently, how packets are routed across networks, and how link-layer technologies support end-to-end communication.

The subject combines conceptual understanding with practical experience. Students will analyse live network traffic, develop client-server applications using socket programming, and configure Cisco networking equipment to design and build functional networks. Through these activities, students will strengthen their ability to troubleshoot network behaviour, evaluate network services, and design efficient, reliable applications and network solutions.

By the end of the subject, students will have a solid foundation in Internet architecture, network protocols, and practical networking skills relevant to IT, software, data engineering, and cloud-connected systems.
learningOutcomes: Understand the key architectural principles of the Internet, namely protocol layering and service models. (D.1)
Analyse various components of the Internet, including Applications, Transport, Network, Addressing, and Data Link, to select the most appropriate network services. (C.1)
Examine and explain end-to-end packet delivery throughout the network system to gain insight into the behaviour of the Internet. (D.1)
Design and implement network applications to provide a service, such as web and email. (C.1)
41092.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have basic programming skills, such as Python, in order to complete the programming projects

41099.title: Introduction to Mechatronics Engineering
41099.description: This subject equips you with the foundational knowledge and skills to design mechatronic systems, offering an early introduction to electronic components and coding within a mechanical engineering context. You'll engage in a studio-like project that encourages creative and critical thinking, setting the stage for the studio approach you'll encounter more frequently in advanced studies. This practical foundation is directly relevant to both your academic journey and future work experiences.
learningOutcomes: Write programs/code for microcontrollers. (D.1)
Create schematics and wiring diagrams for electronic circuits. (D.1)
Design mechatronic devices incorporating microcontrollers, sensors, actuators and other electronic devices. (C.1)
Build mechatronic devices incorporating microcontrollers, sensors, actuators and other electronic devices. (D.1)

41108.title: Integrated Product Development for Industry 4.0
41108.description: Product development creates a new technical product/system to fulfil specific needs and requirements. The resulting product design directly affects the entire product life cycle, such as manufacturing, maintenance and recycling. Thus, product development cannot happen in isolation but has to be part of an integrated product life cycle spanning approach. In this respect, Advanced Manufacturing creates new challenges but also offers new opportunities for such an integrated approach. You will learn to apply an integrated product development methodology, which will enable you to systematically develop new technical products. A key focus is on identifying relevant socio-technical needs and requirements across the entire product life cycle. You will develop a product to deepen your learning experience.

41113.title: Software Development Studio
41113.description: This studio subject focuses on the practical aspects of software development, fostering a rich and engaging practice-based environment to enhance your professional competence. It emphasises reflective design, teamwork, mentoring, and learning through tackling challenging problems. You will form teams with your peers to simulate a real software development team, interacting with industry or academic clients to understand their requirements and deliver software solutions. Teaching is delivered through mini-lectures in studio sessions, covering topics such as version control and agile project management. In the assessments, you will demonstrate your software design and development skills, as well as your skill in reflective practice. By completing this subject, you will be equipped with knowledge and experience that is in high demand in industry.
learningOutcomes: Develop communication and collaboration skills in a team. (E.1)
Build capability in reflective practice. (F.1)
Build capability in software design skills. (C.1)
Build technical capability in software development techniques and tools. (D.1)

41117.title: Introduction to Chemical Process Engineering
41117.description: This subject equips you with the theory and practice of chemical process engineering, focusing on the industrial-scale transformation of raw materials into valuable products. You'll explore foundational theoretical concepts including mass and energy balances, thermodynamics, and transport phenomena including hands on practical lab classes. The subject also covers industrial unit operations like mass, and heat transfer, as well as chemical polymer reaction, hydrogen energy and chemical pollutant. Additionally, you'll delve into process design, control, chemical risk assessment, and plant operation, preparing you for the practical challenges of the field.
learningOutcomes: Describe professional responsibilities for sustainable distribution of resources and energy in engineering projects. (B.1)
Design sustainable process flow diagrams to meet client needs. (C.1)
Apply data analysis to inform design optimisation solution for client needs. (D.1)
Reflect on ways collaboration with colleagues influences personal and professional shifts in understanding and behaviour in the context of Ali engineering project. (F.1)

41118.title: Artificial Intelligence in Robotics
41118.description: This subject delves into Artificial Intelligence (AI) concepts, theory, and algorithms relevant to robotics and mechatronic systems, covering data-driven perception, and various machine learning paradigms applied to intelligent robots including traditional, reinforcement and deep learning. Through workshops and tutorials, you will grasp the technical and ethical complexities of intelligent systems, learning to identify and apply cutting-edge algorithms and tools for autonomous decision-making. This knowledge is essential as intelligent robots increasingly reshape industries and society.
learningOutcomes: Design an intelligent robot solution for a real-world problem. (C.1)
Demonstrate Artificial Intelligence techniques in robotics. (D.1)
Demonstrate effective communication to present and document a robotic system solution. (E.1)
Critically review self and peer performance to ensure improvement of oneself and a team. (F.1)

41124.title: Electrification and Renewables Studio
41124.description: This is a Developing studio subject in renewable energy engineering where you synthesise your disciplinary knowledge and practice to a unstructured problem or project. Electrification is widely employed in modern transportation, homes, buildings, industry, and agriculture sectors. It offers enhanced energy efficiency, lower maintenance costs, longer lifetimes, and advanced features that significantly improve work performance. The combination of electrification and renewables provides a sustainable solution for reducing carbon footprints and paving the way towards a cleaner energy future. In this subject, you will apply a broad range of technologies and knowledge related to energy system electrification, with a focus on fostering a cleaner energy future. It covers power electronics, electric machines, energy storage systems, renewable energy, and smart grid technologies. By participating in team projects, you will address fundamental issues like analysing power distribution systems, designing efficient power converters, developing innovative energy storage solutions, modelling renewable energy generation and optimising complex electrical systems by using computer simulations. This subject broadens your understanding of electrification technologies but also provides exposure to industry scenarios and aims to enhance your professional skills while contributing to advancements in electrification and renewable energy, ultimately shaping a sustainable future.
learningOutcomes: Analyse modern electrical energy systems across various industries to identify impact on social, economic, and environmental factors. (B.1)
Design electrical energy systems to solve problems according to customised requirements, specifications and industry standards. (C.1)
Use appropriate mathematical models, software and tools to model electrical energy systems. (D.1)
Communicate effectively to operate successfully within cross-disciplinary and cross-cultural contexts. (E.1)
Analyse own progress through systematic engineering record-keeping and by sharing knowledge with peers. (F.1)

41127.title: Software Design Studio
41127.description: This subject equips you with the experience and understanding of software engineering practices necessary for developing large, fail-safe systems. You'll learn the importance of balancing initial design with solution implementation, and through hands-on experience, appreciate the need for discipline in maintaining robust practices. The subject emphasises understanding the long-term impact of chosen development methods, tools, and resources, and fosters the ability to critically evaluate and enhance these processes.
learningOutcomes: Define business requirements within an organisational context. (B.1)
Demonstrate design strategies for a software system. (C.1)
Apply design tools and techniques such as agile, requirement analysis, to improve software quality. (D.1)
Work efficiently as a team using systematic project management processes. (E.1)
Reflect on one’s own practice as part of an overall career plan. (F.1)

41128.title: Software Analysis Studio
41128.description: This subject introduces you to automated software analysis to detect software bugs and enhance system reliability and security. You will apply system programming skills based on open-source frameworks to design and develop source code analysis tools for identifying coding errors. You will engage with real-world software development practices in this subject. Assessment will be based on your technical capabilities, comprehension of software analysis and communication abilities.
learningOutcomes: Discuss the role of software analysis in delivering safe and reliable software systems to satisfy social needs. (B.1)
Design and develop software analysis tools. (C.1)
Demonstrate a range of software analysis techniques. (D.1)
Demonstrate effective communication and collaboration skills within a software team. (E.1)
Reflect on performance to demonstrate continual improvement. (F.1)

41129.title: Software Innovation Studio
41129.description: The Software Innovation Studio subject blends field research and user observation with cutting-edge algorithm application to drive innovation in software design and service enhancement. It cultivates skills in idea generation, logical reasoning, systematic execution, and agile project management. You'll experience the full software engineering cycle in a practice- and project-based setting, with the goal of developing valuable software solutions, enhancing existing platforms, or resolving complex issues.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate stakeholder requirements and translate into software project (B.1)
Develop and improve innovative software that fits users’ needs. (C.1)
Apply systematic and logical data analytics for software engineering. (D.1)
Apply agile and systematic approaches to manage software engineering projects, as an efficient team. (E.1)
Reflect on skills learned as the final step in the development of one’s career plan. (F.1)

41130.title: Professional Practice Studio
41130.description: The Professional Practice Studio is an interdisciplinary space where students from engineering and IT collaborate on complex, real-world problems alongside industry and community partners. This subject challenges your perceptions of your studies, career, and professional identity. You'll apply engineering and IT skills to unconventional problems, demonstrating the versatility of these disciplines. The studio enhances research, design thinking, and systems thinking skills, while offering networking opportunities with professionals and academics. You'll gain a portfolio-worthy project, learn to articulate your practice to employers, and understand the application of academic learning in professional settings. The studio combines workshops and independent work, transitioning from staff-led to student-directed as you progress. For more details and to prepare for enrolment, visit the UTS Professional Practice Studio website.
learningOutcomes: Apply engineering processes to define a problem, generate possible solutions, select and justify suitable options, and prototype and verify solutions, in a complex interdisciplinary context. (C.1)
Collaborate effectively in interdisciplinary teams and apply team processes, including self and peer evaluation. (E.1)
Articulate and present project work to clients and stakeholders to elicit feedback. (E.1)
Reflect on own developing capabilities to articulate strengths and areas for professional growth. (F.1)

41160.title: Introduction to Biomedical Engineering
41160.description: Biomedical engineering merges engineering principles with medical sciences to improve healthcare, covering diagnosis, treatment, and rehabilitation. It involves a spectrum of technologies, from pacemakers to cutting-edge developments like stem cell engineering and 3D organ printing. In this subject you will explore key areas such as tissue engineering, imaging, and nanotechnology, equipping you with the knowledge to innovate solutions for medical challenges through lectures, labs, and collaborative projects.
learningOutcomes: Identify the scope of biomedical engineering and its applications to healthcare. (D.1)
Design a biomedical engineering solution to real-life medical and clinical problems. (C.1)
Communicate ideas and findings in biomedical engineering in verbal and written forms. (E.1)
Collaboratively generate a biomedical engineering solution to a complex biomedical problem. (E.1)

41161.title: Biomedical Industry Frameworks
41161.description: This subject will provide you with an understanding of the regulatory frameworks and procedures in the biotech and medical device industry. You will learn to navigate quality systems, management systems, regulatory affairs, design processes, ethics, IP and risk analysis such as FMEAs, applying relevant tools in medical device regulation. You will also become familiar with regulatory environments in Australia and other international markets such as the US and EU. This knowledge will lay the groundwork for a career within the medical device regulatory area.
learningOutcomes: Analyse the biomedical industry regulations to understand the various aspects of health-related systems and products. (B.1)
Identify standard mechanisms associated with quality systems. (D.1)
Evaluate regulatory affairs, design processes and risk analysis. (B.1)
Analyse regulatory environments both within Australia and overseas. (C.1)
Present findings to a variety of audiences including stakeholders. (E.1)

41162.title: Fundamentals of Biomedical Engineering Studio A
41162.description: This subject introduces you to biomedical engineering, focusing on medical device signal processing and the technology used in molecular diagnostics for disease. You'll engage in studio-based learning, tackling real-life medical challenges to improve patient health outcomes. The subject covers processing and modelling physiological signals for medical devices, and teaches the basic steps of genome sequencing while giving insights the application of such biomedical areas. Furthermore, it will provide views on career opportunities using the skills obtained in the studio.
learningOutcomes: Communicate and collaborate in teams to manage biomedical projects. (E.1)
Acquire, process, analyse and model basic biomedical signals. (D.1)
Use design skills (in software) to generate solutions in medical and assistive technologies. (C.1)
Apply technical techniques and tools to develop models for RNA sequencing technologies. (D.1)
Present project findings to a variety of audiences. (E.1)

41163.title: Fundamentals of Biomedical Engineering Studio B
41163.description: This studio-based subject immerses you in the applications of biomaterials in regenerative medicine, and nanobiotechnology in cancer diagnosis, focusing on 3D printing technique for biomedical implants, and nanotechnology for cancer cell imaging. You'll gain practical skills in 3D modelling, printing and testing bone implants, as well as in designing and constructing optical nanoprobes for cancer cells labelling with nanoparticles and biological molecules. Collaborative projects will guide you from concept to prototype, using SOLIDWORKS for design and 3D printing for realisation. Additionally, you'll learn techniques of cell culture, cell staining, nanoparticles modification, antibody conjugations for cancer cells labelling and imaging, culminating in a solid grasp of the modelling and manufacturing processes in biomedical engineering as well as design, modification and imaging in nanobiotechnology.
learningOutcomes: Use design skills to simulate the problems using models and then generate solutions in biomaterials and nanobiotechnology. Apply specific techniques and tools to develop models in biomaterials and nanobiotechnology. (C.1)
Apply specific techniques and tools to develop models in biomaterials and nanobiotechnology. (D.1)
Analyse models, systems and materials to solve problems in health systems. (D.1)
Collaborate in teams to manage projects and communicate findings to diverse stakeholders. (E.1)

41168.title: Biomedical Engineering Design
41168.description:
Biomedical engineering design and optimisation is a critical stage in the development of medical devices, contributing to advancements in biomedical engineering by enhancing functionality, safety, and performance. Medical devices must be carefully designed to ensure optimal and safe functionality in real-world conditions. This requires consideration of various factors including mechanical properties and relevant biocompatibility requirements.

In this developing subject, you will explore the principles of engineering design, develop advanced computer-aided design (CAD) skills using industry-standard software (e.g., SolidWorks), gain knowledge of various national and international standards relevant to the design and evaluation of medical devices, learn patient-specific design techniques and the necessary software, and apply finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate the biomechanical behaviour of medical devices. Through this process, you will design medical devices, evaluate their biomechanical properties, and optimize their performance to ensure safety and reliability.

The subject includes two project streams, with students selecting one stream for their final assessment. While each project focuses on a different medical challenge, both provide equivalent opportunities for you to engage with the technical content and achieve the intended learning outcomes of the subject.
learningOutcomes: Apply engineering design principles to develop complex solutions for biomedical engineering challenges (C.1)
Apply finite element analysis (FEA) to characterise and optimise biomechanical properties of medical devices. (D.1)
Apply relevant national and international standards to the analysis and evaluation of medical devices. (D.1)
Collaboratively manage biomedical engineering projects to professionally communicate findings. (E.1)

41171.title: Quantum Computer Architectures
41171.description: This subject delves into quantum computing, where quantum processors confer exponential advantages over classical counterparts. Quantum architecture design is an interdisciplinary field, combining physics, information theory, computer science, and control theory. You'll learn the workings of quantum processors, explore varied construction approaches, and master control and characterization techniques, gaining a comprehensive understanding of quantum computing architectures.
learningOutcomes: Communicate effectively across a wide class of physical quantum technology platforms with hardware and software engineers of disparate backgrounds. (E.1)
Design control methods and circuit structures across all major quantum platforms to perform computation and communication tasks. (D.1)
Design quantum computing architectures taking into account the constraints of different physical systems. (C.1)

41173.title: Quantum Software and Programming
41173.description: This subject introduces you to the quantum technology ecosystem through hands-on use of emerging quantum software tools. You'll solidify your understanding of quantum computing by learning to analyse quantum circuits, investigating how they can be used to solve problems, and creating simulations of those quantum circuits.
learningOutcomes: Implement quantum algorithms using programming languages, such as Q#/Qiskit/Cirq, for undertaking research and development. (C.1)
Analyse quantum circuits and algorithms. (D.1)
Communicate effectively individually and as a team to meet stated project outcomes. (E.1)

41174.title: Quantum Algorithms
41174.description: You'll gain proficiency in fundamental quantum algorithms, such as Shor's algorithm for integer factorisation and Grover's search algorithm. From there, you’ll learn about quantum walks, simulation of quantum systems, and algorithms for solving linear equations.
learningOutcomes: Write algorithms in the quantum circuit model. (D.1)
Apply the quantum algorithms learned to new problems and describe solutions. (C.1)
Demonstrate and communicate limitations of quantum algorithms. (E.1)

41175.title: Emerging Topics in Quantum Information Science

41180.title: Data Analytics in Cybersecurity
41180.description: Data Analytics for Cybersecurity equips you with the skills to leverage big data and threat intelligence in combating both insider and external cyber threats. You will learn to apply statistical methods to discern patterns and use intelligent technologies to identify security issues from data. The subject introduces machine learning applications in cybersecurity and standard data analytics processes. Through hands-on exercises, you will develop practical skills in analysing corporate computer and network vulnerabilities, thereby enhancing your ability to identify and mitigate security risks. This subject bridges the gap between data analytics and cybersecurity, providing you with the tools to effectively protect modern digital infrastructures.
learningOutcomes: Apply data analytics to investigate cybersecurity datasets. (D.1)
Detect and analyse cyber‐attacks using data analytics. (D.1)
Synthesise data analytics with other techniques to appropriately set rules for intrusion detection. (D.1)
Clearly communicate process of data analysis and security recommendations to a broad audience. (E.1)

41181.title: Information Security and Management
41181.description: This subject focuses on training you in IT security policy development and human security management while addressing critical legal and ethical considerations. You will lay the groundwork for applying cyber safety and security measures at a corporate level. By conducting security assessments within business constraints, you will learn to employ professional methodologies effectively. The subject also covers the systematic evaluation of business and security operations, equipping you with skills in contingency planning, risk assessment, risk management, and compliance across diverse business environments. You'll be prepared to develop comprehensive security policies and manage human factors in cybersecurity, ensuring robust protection and ethical governance within organisations.
learningOutcomes: Investigate security management issues in organisations by analysing requirements, plans and IT security policies. (B.1)
Propose appropriate information security protection mechanisms by assessing security risks, threats and vulnerabilities. (B.1)
Identify security training and education needs and associated legal and ethical awareness for organisational personnel. (B.1)
Apply organisational planning and project management principles to IT security planning individually and collaboratively. (E.1)
Demonstrate awareness on how to assess and identify cyber security issues when working with, and for, Indigenous Australians. (A.1)
41181.requisiteText: ((1 OR 1a OR 1b OR 1c OR 1d OR 1e OR 1f) AND (2 OR 2a OR 2b OR 2c))

41182.title: System Security
41182.description: This subject provides a comprehensive understanding of contemporary system security concepts, strategies, and practical techniques essential for securing operating systems, databases, and servers. You will learn to implement security measures throughout the design and configuration phases, ensuring robust system security and privacy. The subject places a strong emphasis on system hardening mechanisms and prominent security techniques, which you will apply in hands-on practical sessions. By testing the resilience of hardened systems against various attack vectors, you will gain critical skills in defending against real-world cybersecurity threats. This subject fosters both theoretical knowledge and practical expertise, preparing you to effectively safeguard corporate computing environments.
learningOutcomes: Identify and explain the difference between particular types of security systems. (D.1)
Identify and analyse security vulnerabilities and issues in computer systems. (D.1)
Propose and justify technical solutions and potential remedy actions to increase security. (D.1)
Communicate with peers effectively concerning ethical hacking practice. (E.1)
41182.requisiteText: ((1 OR 1a OR 1b OR 1c OR 1d OR 1e OR 1f OR 1g OR 1h OR 1i))

41183.title: Privacy Preserving
41183.description: In this subject you'll master techniques for safeguarding data privacy, enabling organisations to handle personal or confidential data responsibly. The subject explores privacy models to build defenses against privacy breaches, delving into data anonymisation, statistical privacy approaches, and differential privacy, ensuring you can protect and manage sensitive information effectively.
learningOutcomes: Identify and explain the most common privacy models that are used in various communities and organisations. (B.1)
Evaluate the effectiveness of existing privacy measures. (D.1)
Apply privacy preserving techniques appropriate to a variety of security configurations and scenarios. (D.1)
Work as a team to investigate a real‐world privacy breach in a corporate environment. (E.1)

41184.title: Secure Programming and Penetration Testing
41184.description: This subject will equip you with the knowledge and skills necessary to develop secure software and assess the security of systems through source code analysis and penetration testing techniques. There will be coverage of the principles and practices of secure coding, the identification and mitigation of vulnerabilities, software verification, and the methodologies used in penetration testing. You will learn how to approach and develop automatic auditing systems, identifying vulnerabilities and developing security analysis and testing methods to protect systems against cyber-attacks. Additionally, you'll have the chance to engage in national and international security challenges, with assessments on secure programming, software analysis, and your communication skills in speaking and writing.
learningOutcomes: Classify software security vulnerabilities in the source code of systems, applications, and services. (D.1)
Automate the analysis of a software project using source code analysis on top of compilers to defend against real‐world attacks from malicious entities. (D.1)
Communicate effectively individually and as a team to describe plans for countering changing security threats. (E.1)
41184.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge experience with C/C++; Code Analysis; Compilers.

41185.title: Emerging Topics in Cybersecurity and Privacy
41185.description: This subject delves into contemporary IT security theories and practical skills in the cybersecurity profession, enhanced by guest lectures and workshops. You will develop a professional understanding of cybersecurity by examining emerging threats to web applications and systems, along with cutting-edge privacy and ethical issues. You'll explore current trends and challenges through professional practice and literature review. Working in small teams, you'll apply modern techniques for requirements elicitation, analysis, modelling, specification, and validation to real-world projects.
learningOutcomes: Examine various aspects of security systems according to new research outcomes and evolving understandings of security threats. (D.1)
Evaluate the design, implementation, configuration and application of existing security systems based on the latest IT security research outcomes. (C.1)
Synthesize literature and practically apply new research outcomes and approaches to real problems. (C.1)
Collaborate to communicate research synthesis alongside practical results. (E.1)

41191.title: Business Intelligence
41191.description: This undergraduate subject equips you with an understanding of business intelligence applications in organisational contexts, focusing on knowledge management, business process management, and decision-making. By taking this subject, you will gain valuable skills in generating, sharing, retaining, and applying information and knowledge within corporations, which are crucial for enhancing business efficiency and decision-making processes. You will develop essential skills in system development approaches and design strategies for business intelligence systems, preparing you for roles in business analysis and system design. These skills will not only help you become proficient in managing business processes but also make you an asset in any organisational setting that relies on data-driven decision-making. Your learning experience will be interactive and practical. Through engaging in case studies, project-based tasks, and group activities, you will apply theoretical knowledge to real-world business issues using different analytical tools. As you handle data sets, you'll improve your skills in analysing and implementing solutions. This practical approach ensures that you not only grasp the theoretical concepts but also become proficient in using these tools to effectively address and resolve business challenges.
learningOutcomes: Analyse Indigenous knowledge systems and practices as examples of cultural information systems. (A.1)
Assess ethical considerations in decision-making processes and practices for a business intelligence system in a real organisation. (B.1)
Design business intelligence applications to add value and competitive advantage in an organisation. (C.1)
Apply business intelligence and analytics tools to solve real-world problems and interpret results. (D.1)
Actively engage in and lead collaborative efforts within the business intelligence domain (E.1)

41193.title: IS Data Visualisation Studio
41193.description:
Taking the Information Systems (IS) perspective, rather than the more common Data Science or IT perspectives, this subject focuses on the latest developments and professional practices in data visualisation and visual analytics for non-technical decision-makers. Recognising the importance of data visualisation literacy in various disciplines, including IS, this subject stands out by emphasising (i) understanding the reasons behind using data visualisation in addition to learning how to create them, (ii) identifying business and organisational cases along with their requirements, stakeholders, and problem space, (iii) visual ethics and the responsible use of visual data, and (iv) utilising commercial data visualisation software instead of elaborate coding.

In short, the subject aims for visual problem exploration “through data” rather than the creation of static visual outputs. To achieve this, you will be taught through a combination of lectures and studios with a focus on design thinking exercises and ethical visual analytics. You will develop the necessary skills and mindset for problem finding and solving through visual data exploration that goes beyond creating static visual outputs. These skills include identifying different stakeholders and analysing their decision-making needs and environments, problem formulation, finding and ethically harvesting relevant data, ensuring data quality, data integration, multidimensional modelling, and developing a data exploration prototype using commercial data visualisation software.

Focusing on value creation and the decision-making needs of different stakeholders, you will also learn how to use data-driven visual storytelling and other contemporary techniques to explore the problem space, inform, influence, and inspire various types of stakeholders, including those in business and IT.
learningOutcomes: Determine the value proposition of data visualisation and visual data exploration for different decision-makers in an enterprise context. (B.1)
Integrate relevant data sources in an ethical manner following contemporary data quality and data integration principles and practice in an enterprise context. (D.1)
Design a prototype of a data exploration environment as an information system. (C.1)
Work collaboratively to design a data exploration prototype for a real-world problem. (E.1)
Reflect on the experience of becoming a competent, ethical and holistic data visualisation professional in an enterprise context. (F.1)

41200.title: Engineering Project Appraisal
41200.description: This foundational subject introduces you to key professional engineering frameworks, focusing on ethics, project management, sustainability, and economics. Through this subject, you'll evaluate real-world projects, scrutinising their sustainability and community impact. Building on skills from 'Introduction to Engineering Projects', you'll deepen your understanding of professional practice before tackling more complex projects in subsequent subjects. The subject applies case studies to link theory to practice. Tutorial sessions foster your collaboration in practicing case study analysis techniques, understanding frameworks, and appraising engineering projects. With peer feedback, you will critique peers' work, honing diverse appraisal approaches.
learningOutcomes: Identify professional ethical obligations relevant to an engineering project. (B.1)
Identify how sustainability approaches and principles have been applied to an engineering project. (B.1)
Identify economic perspectives relevant to engineering projects. (B.1)
Identify the effective use of project management approaches in engineering projects. (D.1)
Apply established frameworks to engineering decisions using critical thinking skills. (C.1)

41201.title: Designing Sustainable Engineering Projects
41201.description: In this subject, you'll advance from foundational design principles to completing a full design cycle, from problem identification to presenting solutions to a client, incorporating systems thinking. Sustainability is central, encompassing environmental, economic, and social aspects, and you'll apply relevant tools and techniques within a group project themed by the coordinator, such as food or energy security. You'll work in teams, rotating roles to explore different sustainability perspectives, integrating feedback to refine your approach. Researching individually and in team, you'll converge to select appropriate sustainability frameworks and design a solution mindful of various factors, culminating in a professionally framed report.
learningOutcomes: Identify social, environmental, and economic needs and constraints for a project using sustainability frameworks, methods and tools. (B.1)
Apply systems thinking approaches to design solutions in complex projects. (C.1)
Apply relational teamwork skills to successfully complete a group project. (E.1)
Reflect on experiences to inform lifelong learning. (F.1)

41202.title: Professional Engineering Communication
41202.description:
This subject is focused on developing your professional communication and critical thinking skills, deepening your understanding of the professional responsibilities of engineers (for example risk in projects) and how these apply to planning and managing engineering projects. I You'll engage with diverse communication mediums and documents essential for negotiating project facets with various audiences and stakeholders, focusing on the tendering process. You'll interpret, analyse, and present information to different audiences, enhancing your ability to evaluate engineering proposals through business, ethical, and project management lenses.

You will build on your experiences of engineering projects in Introduction to Engineering Projects and Designing Sustainable Engineering Projects, and expand on this to better understand the complexities of contemporary engineering practice. You will expands the scope of project evaluation introduced in Engineering Project Appraisal by highlighting the importance of communication with real people and their different interests, motivations, assumptions, and values in a business context. This also foreshadows the broader cross-cultural complexity which are explored further in Collaboration in Complex Projects with its Indigenous engineering theme.
learningOutcomes: Communicate to a professional standard to different stakeholders with regard to context and purpose. (E.1)
Relate the Engineers Australia Code of Ethics and other dimensions of professional obligations to engineering projects. (B.1)
Interpret financial documents to appraise viability of engineering proposals. (D.1)
Apply critical thinking skills to propose and justify engineering decisions in a complex project. (C.1)
Applying theory of project management to engineering projects. (D.1)

41203.title: Collaboration in Complex Projects
41203.description:
This subject immerses you in the sustainable practices of Australia's Indigenous peoples, reflecting their sophisticated engineering principles. You'll undertake a group design project, integrating Indigenous approaches to sustainability and environmental stewardship, thereby deepening your understanding of the Indigenous Graduate Attribute.

As a culmination of core subjects, you're expected to employ and exhibit advanced teamwork and sustainability skills, as well as your growing Indigenous Professional Capability. Building on previous teamwork experiences, you'll apply collaborative skills to a complex project, working respectfully in diverse teams. Your sustainability comprehension will also be elevated beyond earlier coursework.

Learning occurs through weekly tutorials, where you'll work in groups to create design solutions, including prototypes, for a complex engineering project with Indigenous stakeholder considerations. The subject adopts a studio format, starting with structured activities and research to ensure clarity on project objectives. Subsequently, you'll independently manage and execute the project, providing weekly progress updates. Assessments will evaluate your application of respectful communication in both verbal and written forms, demonstrating your engagement with the subject's core values.
learningOutcomes: Incorporate considerations of Indigenous Australian culture into a design process and solution. (A.1)
Demonstrate an understanding of respectful communication with the diversity of Indigenous stakeholders. (A.1)
Report on sustainability to a professional standard in complex engineering projects. (B.1)
Collaborate in diverse interdisciplinary teams and with stakeholders to achieve problem solutions. (E.1)

41240.description: In this Pre-Professional studio subject, you will engage with cutting-edge biomedical engineering research through one of two project streams: Single Cell Sequencing in Cancer or Lateral Flow Assay. The first project equips you with bioinformatics skills to analyse cancer datasets using single-cell sequencing technology. The second offers hands-on experience in creating rapid diagnostic tests, similar to COVID-19 RATs, involving nanoparticle technology, assay fabrication, and modelling with SolidWorks and MATLAB. By the end, you'll have honed project design and problem-solving abilities, alongside technical expertise in emerging biomedical engineering fields.

41241.title: Advanced Biomedical Engineering Studio B
41241.description: In this Pre-Professional studio you will engage in an in-depth exploration into the innovative field of medical device development. You will engage in creating physical instruments and developing sophisticated software solutions. These biomedical devices are crucial in diagnosing diseases and are indispensable in hospitals and pathology labs globally. You will work on medical device prototypes, involving the assembly and prototyping of diagnostic tools like Point of Care PCR devices for pathogen detection. You will also create rudimentary or draw on existing AI technologies for medical imaging, utilising deep convolutional neural networks to solve imaging challenges. Through 3D CAD design, additive manufacturing, parts integration, and testing, you will build these devices. By completing this subject, you will develop professional skills in project design and prototyping, problem-solving, stakeholder analysis, and technical expertise, preparing you for the medical device industry.
