41277.title: Control Design
41277.description: This electrical and electronic engineering common core subject provides a comprehensive introduction to principles and techniques used in the analysis and design of control systems. You will explore topics such as mathematical modelling, stability analysis, and feedback control. You will gain practical experience through demonstrations and simulations, while preparing you for more advanced project work in control systems. By the end of the subject, you will be able to transform a manual plant into an autonomous system by designing stable control strategies with guaranteed closed-loop dynamic performance. After completing this subject, you will be able to apply this knowledge to engineering challenges in areas such as Industry 4.0, robotics, automation, renewable energy integration, electric vehicles, and all kinds of electromechanical systems.
learningOutcomes: Design an autonomous control system that conforms to given specifications. (C.1)
Identify model uncertainties and/or disturbances that affect control system performance to enhance robustness. (D.1)
Collaborate for optimal project proficiency as part of networking with stakeholders. (E.1)
Reflect on individual progress through question formulation at different stages of a project. (F.1)

41278.title: Power Electronics
41278.description: This subject offers a comprehensive foundation in power electronics, which is a key technology driving the latest advancement in electrical engineering. The curriculum covers a range of important topics, including the study of semiconductor devices, passive components, converter topologies, and power conversion methods. By enrolling in this subject, you will develop a solid understanding of the principles and control strategies that govern the operation of power electronic converters. These converters play a crucial role in facilitating voltage, current, and frequency conversions that are essential for modern electrical systems. Through a combination of theory, laboratory work, and projects, you will acquire the skills necessary for analysing, designing, and implementing power electronic converters. Furthermore, you will gain essential knowledge in advanced topics such as thermal management, soft-switching techniques, and electromagnetic interference. With this knowledge, you will be well-prepared to design efficient power electronic systems and apply your expertise in practical, real-world scenarios. This includes electric power systems, renewable energy generation and storage, the Internet of Energy, and the electrification of transportation.
learningOutcomes: Analyse the impact of power electronics on utility supply and the environment. (B.1)
Design solutions to implement and test power electronic circuits according to customised specifications and industry standards. (C.1)
Use appropriate mathematical models, simulation and design tools and datasheets to analyse and design power electronic devices, circuits, and systems. (D.1)
Demonstrate effective communication and teamwork skills through laboratory experiments and project work. (E.1)

41301.title: Industrial Engineering
41301.description: This subject addresses the imperative for operational excellence in dynamic organisational environments, grounding you in Industrial Engineering principles that tackle the challenges of planning and optimising production systems. Lean Management, a pivotal approach for enhancing productivity and reducing waste, is central to this subject and extends its relevance beyond manufacturing. You will acquire the methods and tools necessary to structure and standardise workflows, devise assembly concepts, manage material supply, and conduct feasibility studies, all with the goal of creating efficient and productive work systems.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate basic understanding of the elements of production and working systems in the context of social, environmental and economic needs. (B.1)
Analyse and improve production and working systems using basic industrial engineering concepts and methods. (C.1)
Apply the basic principles of communication in professional engineering contexts to concisely present insights to a technical and non-technical audience. (E.1)

41302.title: Additive Manufacturing 1
41302.description: This subject offers a foundational understanding of additive manufacturing, also known as 3D printing, equipping you with the knowledge and skills to transform raw materials into products through this thriving manufacturing method. You will learn about the standardised additive manufacturing processes, develop skills in design and fabrication, and practise the typical workflow required for successful production to prepare you for the evolving 3D printing industry.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate skills in material processing, additive manufacturing methods, and related production skills. (D.1)
Apply basic concepts in design for additive manufacturing to clearly defined problems. (C.1)
Demonstrate basic evaluation of additive manufacturing in the context of stakeholders, organisations, economic, social, and environmental impacts and opportunities. (B.1)

This includes developing knowledge of automation principles, programmable logic controllers (PLCs), feedback control including proportional-integral-differential (PID), sequential control, robot kinematics and trajectory planning.

41380.title: Heat and Mass Transfer
41380.description: This foundational subject delves into the fundamentals of heat and mass transfer, teaching you to develop transport models from first principles. You will study how temperature and concentration gradients form within and across boundary layers. The subject applies the principles of heat and mass transfer to various contexts, including multi-stage processes and natural and forced convection, as well as phase transitions. By the end, you'll be adept at solving heat and mass transfer system problems and recommending solutions relevant to the chemical process industries.
learningOutcomes: Analyse flow of heat and mass transfer using diagrammatic analysis and understand the safety and environmental considerations associated with heat and mass transfer processes in chemical process engineering projects. (C.1)
Apply heat and mass transfer concepts and processes to chemical reactions. (D.1)
Apply heat and mass transfer principles to innovate chemical engineering systems and other technologies. (D.1)

41381.title: Advanced Fluid and Particle Mechanics
41381.description:
In this Developing subject, you will be asked to engage in the analysis of complex fluids, which are widely used in modern technologies and industries, particularly in foods, water, printing and coating materials, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, and mineral processing. Understanding the fundamental principles of non-Newtonian fluids and particle mechanics in a fluid is crucial in these engineering practices. The subject will equip you with practical knowledge of fluid and particle mechanics in the context of chemical process engineering, where fluid (liquid or gas) interacts with particulate solids.

The subject has three parts: it begins by covering rheological concepts of non-Newtonian fluids, such as viscoelasticity, physical properties, and quantities, with an emphasis on the design calculation of the flow. Basic principles of viscometry and analysis of rheological measurements are also introduced. Then, you are invited to investigate how complex fluids are understood within the context of microscopic aspects of surface and interface sciences. This includes surface and interfacial tension, surface chemistry, and their correlation to colloidal stability. The final section will provide coverage of single and multi-particles in fluid, solid-fluid transport, particle aggregation and agglomeration, and particle transport, slurries and fluid flow through a packed bed of particles are discussed in association with relevant case studies and numerical problem-solving methods using computational calculation.

Completion of this subject will enable you to describe and model the physical behaviour of fluid-particle systems and perform design calculations and analyses of typical chemical engineering processes involving non-Newtonian fluids or complex fluid-particle systems.
learningOutcomes: Identify safety issues and hazards of non-Newtonian fluids and fluid-particle systems in viscous solutions. (B.1)
Design industrial processes for non-Newtonian fluids and complex particle operations. (C.1)
Analyse complex fluids and particulate systems in chemical engineering research and industrial processes. (D.1)
Communicate the design rationale for a solution to a complex fluids and particulate system. (E.1)

41382.title: Unit Operations
41382.description:
In this Developing subject, you will exercise your knowledge and skills to design and operate unit operations and equipment for chemical process engineering applications, e.g., oil & gas refining, pharmaceuticals, food & beverage, and water purification, safely and economically. You will learn the principles of membrane separation, distillation, liquid-liquid extraction, ion exchange, absorption, adsorption, and drying in industrial processes, as well as learning to incorporate economics, safety, and environmental sustainability in all stages of the design.

By the end of this subject, you will be able to analyse the transport phenomena of the fluids as well as various separation processes. Furthermore, you will develop skills to design and formulate the piping and instrumentation diagram (P&ID) of an integrated system of multiple unit operations, and provide justification/assessment of the P&ID based on hazard and operability study, safety life cycle and techno-economic analysis. You will also gain the ability to critically evaluate process designs using hazard identification techniques, assess operability for safe and efficient operation, and perform techno-economic analyses to ensure project feasibility, equipping you to make informed decisions about the process design lifecycle, safety, operability, and economic viability.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate design configurations for hazard identification, safety and economic viability. (B.1)
Design piping and instrumentation diagrams to meet the needs of an integrated system of multiple unit operations for the construction of a chemical engineering process. (C.1)
Analyse transport phenomena of fluids as well as various separation processes. (D.1)
Communicate design decisions and rationale to a range of audiences. (E.1)

41383.title: Process Simulation
41383.description:
In this Developing subject you will further your understanding of process modelling concepts covered in previous subjects such as Introduction to Chemical Process Engineering. This subject enables you to visualise how the equipment operates in terms of mass and energy balances and will cover topics such as familiarisation with simulation tools and building a unit operations process flow diagram. You will learn how to apply the principles of process simulation tool to model and analyse various industrial operation units, including pumps, distillation columns, mixers/splitters, heat exchangers, reactors, and separators. Additionally, you will set up and solve material and energy balances using simulation tools to develop a simple process model and run an analysis of basic process data. By the end of the semester, you will have a thorough understanding of chemical process simulation, including the application of process simulation tool to model and analyse complete industrial operation units.
You will engage in peer learning and work on a group project based around a real-world problem which will build your collaboration skills and enhance your engagement and understanding of the practical applications of process simulation.
learningOutcomes: Assess impacts of industrial operation units on both chemical process industries and the environment by applying simulation tools. (B.1)
Design and optimise chemical engineering processes using modelling and simulation tools. (C.1)
Apply simulation tools for process modelling and analysis in real-world engineering applications. (D.1)
Collaborate during design process to achieve team chemical processing product goals. (E.1)

41384.title: Chemical Thermodynamics and Reactor Design
41384.description: In this Pre-Professional subject, you will learn practical knowledge to select and design reactors for a range of chemical transformations, including plug flow, packed-bed, batch, and continuously stirred tank reactors. You will integrate reaction kinetics and equilibrium with thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and heat and mass transfer to analyse and model chemical processes for each reactor type. Starting with single-reaction design equations, you will then generalise to multiple reactions to address real-world reactor design involving chemical, biochemical, and catalytic systems. To deepen your understanding, you will also conduct a numerical lab experiment, where you will apply numerical simulations to estimate reaction rate laws and synthesise theory with practical reactor design.
learningOutcomes: Critically evaluate reactor design principles that enable green chemistry and renewable energy innovations, demonstrating their role in fostering socially responsible and climate-resilient industrial and societal outcomes. (B.1)
Design appropriate reactors for diverse real-world applications, such as water treatment, energy production, and carbon abatement. (C.1)
Apply analytical tools to determine the relationship among heat, work and physical changes of state for identifying chemical reaction mechanisms and calculating reaction rate and equilibrium. (D.1)
Integrate chemical engineering principles and team-based role responsibilities to collaboratively design a chemical reactor that meets specified engineering constraints. (E.1)

41385.title: Process Dynamics and Control
41385.description: In this Pre-Professional subject, you will be introduced to mathematical tools for analysing the transient behaviour of open and closed-loop process systems. You will learn to apply methods to design and implement an automated process such as feedback control, feedforward control, cascade control, multi-loop control and model-based control. Instrumentation and control devices for automatic control and applications of emerging digital tools such as telemetry, virtual reality, and digital twins will also be covered. Upon the completion of this subject, you will have experience analysing the operation of modern process plants.
learningOutcomes: Create a simulation-based design of a control system for a chemical process. (C.1)
Apply computational techniques and process simulation software to optimise chemical process control strategies (D.1)
Demonstrate knowledge of basic concepts of process dynamics and control. (D.1)
Collaborate in teams to communicate chemical engineering decisions with emphasis on clarity to other engineers. (E.1)

41386.title: Process Design and Safety Studio
41386.description: This pre-professional studio subject will develop your skills to design and manage complex engineering systems. You will work collaboratively on an authentic design project using the application of data analytics and data visualisation for the whole system performance monitoring and optimisation. You will produce design documentation by presenting your design to stakeholders as well as undertaking a Hazard and Operability analysis, and conducting an economic, and environmental sustainability evaluation. Upon the completion of this subject, you will be ready to work in an industrial plant environment adhering to the safety requirements in designing and operating complex engineering systems.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate a process design solution by considering its environmental and economic impacts. (B.1)
Design a process solution to meet client expectations and safety standard through application of established engineering models including use of software to simulate system performances. (C.1)
Apply simulation tools for process modelling and conduct safety analysis in real-world engineering applications. (D.1)
Collaborate and communicate during design process to achieve team goals. (E.1)
Reflect on feedback to improve professional practice to achieve project goals. (F.1)

41759.title: Capstone
41759.description:
The Capstone Project is a culminating subject undertaken by final-year students, designed to integrate and apply the knowledge, skills, and methodologies acquired throughout their degree program. Students work to deliver a substantial, research-informed, or industry-based project that addresses a complex real-world problem, opportunity, or area of interest within their discipline.

The project involves stages of problem identification, research, solution design, development, and evaluation. Many projects are delivered in collaboration with industry partners, research groups, or community organisations. It provides students with the opportunity to demonstrate independent thinking, technical competence, project management, and professional communication skills while producing a tangible outcome such as a prototype, software application, research report, or strategic proposal documented in a comprehensive final report.

It focuses on developing work-ready graduates with strong capabilities in independent research, creative problem-solving, innovation, and effective professional communication within the technology sector.
learningOutcomes: Integrate socially responsible professional judgement by identifying, evaluating, and responding to the ethical, environmental, social, and economic consequences of IT decisions, consistent with sustainable and accountable practice. (B.1)

Design solutions to complex computing problems by applying systematic design processes, creativity, and established discipline specific methods within broader technical, organisational, and societal contexts. (C.1)
Apply discipline‑specific knowledge, tools, and analytical methods to complex technical problems and evaluate sound professional decision‑making across IT contexts. (D.1)
Communicate project intent, design decisions, and outcomes clearly and professionally to a range of stakeholders and contribute constructively to team‑based work. (E.1)
Critically reflect on the development of discipline relevant professional skills and knowledge. (F.1)

41890.title: Applying Network Security
41890.description: In this subject, you will delve into the theory behind computer security and apply it practically, drawing on content from the Network Security course provided by the Cisco Academy. You'll focus on network security appliances and infrastructure, including firewalls, access control, secure network design, Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), and data encryption, to build a robust understanding of protecting digital networks.

Design, configure, test, manage, monitor and support network security infrastructure devices. (C.1)
Apply network security theory into practice using industry based techniques, processes and standards. (D.1)
Apply practical skills learnt in the labs to real-world commercial equipment and to prepare themselves for a industry based certification exam. (D.1)

41900.title: Cryptography
41900.description: In this subject, you will delve into the critical role of cryptographic techniques in maintaining data confidentiality and ensuring data integrity. These techniques are foundational in cybersecurity, securing a variety of systems such as wireless networks, online payment systems, and cryptocurrencies. You will explore key principles of cryptography, including both symmetric and asymmetric ciphers, cryptographic hash functions, message authentication codes, and digital signatures. Additionally, this subject introduces you to the popular applications of cryptography, such as the cryptographic designs in blockchain. Through hands-on exercises, you will analyse various cryptographic techniques, use popular cryptographic tools, and practise simulated attacks on cryptographic systems.
learningOutcomes: Explain the architectural principles, mathematical theories and key designs of underlying cryptographic algorithms. (D.1)
Implement cryptographic techniques and tools to prevent data interception and modification. (D.1)
Demonstrate system design principles and programmatic practices that lead to secure software systems. (C.1)
Work as an effective member of development teams. (E.1)
41900.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have completed 35010 Foundation Mathematics or equivalent.

41905.title: Software Defined Networks
41905.description: This subject addresses the demand for skilled network engineers in Software Defined Networking (SDN), a framework poised to meet the scalability and extensibility challenges of modern telecommunication networks. You will learn key SDN concepts and Network Function Virtualisation (NFV), and through hands-on labs, you will develop applications over an SDN controller. The subject equips you with the skills to enhance performance in data centres and enterprise networks, preparing you for industry needs.
learningOutcomes: Design, program, simulate and implement Software Defined Networking applications. (C.1)
Differentiate and evaluate Software Defined Networking Architectures, Controller Environments, Application Programming Interfaces and Platforms. (D.1)
Use tools for modelling Software Defined Networks. (D.1)
Use case scenarios to explain Network Function Virtualisation technologies, applications and benefits. (D.1)
Present project investigation, design and implementation to technical and lay audience. (E.1)

42027.title: Software Defined Networks
42027.description: This subject introduces Software Defined Networking (SDN), a response to the need for scalable, extensible network technologies amid increasing internet traffic. You will learn the core concepts in SDN and Network Function Virtualisation (NFV), and develop SDN applications over an SDN controller through practical labs. With SDN's rising influence in data centres and enterprise networks, the industry seeks engineers skilled in this transformative technology, positioning you at the forefront of networking innovation.
learningOutcomes: Design, program, simulate and implement Software Defined Networking applications. (C.1)
Differentiate and evaluate Software Defined Networking Architectures, Controller Environments, Application Programming Interfaces and Platforms. (D.1)
Use tools for modelling Software Defined Networks. (D.1)
Use case scenarios to explain Network Function Virtualisation technologies, applications and benefits. (D.1)
Present project investigation, design and implementation to technical and lay audience. (E.1)

42028.title: Deep Learning and Convolutional Neural Network
42028.description: This subject delves into deep learning and convolutional neural networks (CNNs), highlighting their practical applications in data analytics, image recognition, and object detection. You'll study deep learning architectures, focusing on end-to-end model training for tasks like image classification. Practical sessions include setting up deep learning libraries, fine-tuning networks, and training your own CNNs on GPUs. You'll also learn model deployment to build an AI system. The coursework involves individual comprehension of cutting-edge research and collaborative projects to implement image classification and object detection systems.
learningOutcomes: Compare and contrast latest trends in Deep Learning strategies with traditional machine learning techniques. (D.1)
Build, train and test basic Convolutional Neural Networks for real image classification projects. (D.1)
Use Deep Learning software tools to explore state-of-the-art techniques and applications. (D.1)
Build, train and test customised object detection systems using Deep CNN-based techniques. (D.1)
Collaboratively develop the analysis, design and implementation of solutions to real-world computer vision problems. (C.1, E.1)

42035.title: Cloud Security
42035.description: This subject explores the fundamentals of security, privacy, and trust in cloud computing, a paradigm that underpins most digital applications/services. Through the subject, you'll learn and apply these principles, designing secure, trustworthy cloud-based solutions on real-life platforms like AWS or Azure. Through project-based learning and industry-standard security risk analysis, you'll acquire the skills to assess, design, and implement security solutions for trustworthy cloud-based applications, gaining a deep understanding of the critical aspects of cloud system security.
learningOutcomes: Analyse security risks and threats in cloud and cloud applications with reference to government regulations and industry best practice. (B.1)
Design secure defence mechanisms for cloud applications encompassing the security domains of infrastructure, platform, application, data and privacy. (C.1)
Implement security mechanisms for securing cloud applications to minimise risk and threats in a cloud system/service. (D.1)

42036.title: Cybersecurity for Mobile Platforms
42036.description: This subject delves into the security risks and emerging threats associated with modern mobile devices and their operating systems. You'll explore platform security models, beginning with an introduction to the Android Studio simulation environment. The subject covers mobile platform security, encryption and decryption of messages, and mobile hardware security. You'll examine enterprise security extensions and conduct SQL mobile data injection, enhancing your understanding of data vulnerabilities. The subject also includes a comprehensive study of iOS security, covering hardware, system, application, service, and network security. Through practice-based learning, including secure data handling using AES and digital signatures, you will gain hands-on experience. The subject concludes with a review and recap of cybersecurity for mobile platforms, ensuring a well-rounded understanding of the field.
learningOutcomes: Analyse the current cybersecurity issues and challenges for the development of security solutions in mobile platforms. (B.1)
Apply practical security tools and technologies to design appropriate solutions for specific mobile platforms. (C.1)
Examine security risks to prevent fraud from mobile systems, services and applications. (D.1)

42037.title: IoT Security
42037.description: This subject introduces you to the Internet of Things (IoT), focusing on the security challenges and solutions associated with IoT devices and networks. You'll start with an introduction to IoT security and the Contiki software environment. The subject covers a range of critical topics, including implementing IPv6 on IoT devices, authentication methods, and ReST CoAP communications, all through hands-on labs using Contiki. You will explore IoT forensic techniques, hardware security, and data security and privacy concerns, learning practical skills like security port scanning, packet crafting, and Bluetooth sniffing. The subject delves into IoT malware, smart home security, and web application vulnerabilities, providing a comprehensive view of the threats and defenses in the IoT ecosystem. Through industry-relevant projects, you will build secure IoT systems, addressing real-world security challenges and enhancing your ability to protect IoT devices and networks. The subject concludes with a review and recap of IoT security principles, ensuring you have a solid foundation to create a secure and reliable digital ecosystem.
learningOutcomes: Understand the current cybersecurity issues and challenges for the development security solutions in IoT networks. (B.1)
Design IoT applications that incorporate practical security tools and technologies. (C.1)
Develop and implement secured solutions using a simulated environment such as Contiki in a team environment. (D.1)

42043.title: Robotics Studio 1
42043.description: This studio subject, the first in the Robotics major, immerses you in the practical and theoretical aspects of robotics engineering through product-based learning. Unlike traditional subjects, it is centred around a studio environment where you'll collaborate with peers, academic staff, and industry mentors to translate knowledge directly into a robotics system. You'll engage in both self-directed study and project work, focusing on hardware/software and sensing/perception tracks. Your progress will be shaped by a learning contract, ensuring skill development in areas relevant to real-world applications. Successful completion equips you with the foundational skills and knowledge for more complex projects in subsequent studios.
learningOutcomes: Apply stakeholder analysis to inform engagement with stakeholders to scope robotics problem. (B.1)
Apply design thinking approach to develop solution to a robotics problem. (C.1)

Collaborate in teams to demonstrate application of the programming, sensing and control competencies of a robotic system. (E.1)

42048.description: In the Innovation Studio, you'll work in multidisciplinary teams on a self-directed industry project, identifying business problems and designing solutions to meet stakeholder needs. 42050.title: SAS Predictive Business Analytics
42050.description: Predictive business analytics is used to predict unknown future events by analysing historical business data and plays a critical function in data-driven business. This subject will equip you with the theoretical and practical foundations of predictive business analytics. You will comprehend analytical methods for business problem solving encompassing the entire predictive analytics lifecycle, from understanding business problems to deploying predictive models in the real-time business environment via case studies. This understanding will be further enhanced via demonstrations and hands-on exercises. You will use Model Studio in SAS Viya to develop and compare advanced analytics models, learning to create supervised machine learning models for informed decision-making with big data. The subject uses no code technology while setting you up to potentially achieve SAS Certified Specialist: Machine Learning Using SAS Viya certification.
learningOutcomes: Explore and transform business data into analytic-ready features for predictive modelling. (D.1)
Design and implement predictive models for predicting unknown future events in business environment. (C.1)
Evaluate and deploy predictive models in business production environment. (D.1)
Communicate effectively in a collaborative environment to explain and justify a design solution. (E.1)

42056.title: Serious Games Research
42056.description: This studio subject focuses on the creation and impact assessment of serious games and gamified experiences, which are designed for objectives beyond entertainment, such as education and rehabilitation. You'll learn cutting-edge frameworks for tailoring games to specific audiences and purposes, working closely with end-users through co-design workshops, prototype development, playtesting, and evaluation to ensure effectiveness. Additionally, you'll explore ethical and design considerations integral to serious game development.
learningOutcomes: Apply professional standards relating to Indigenous Australian contexts when designing games and serious games. (A.1)
Evaluate ethical, cultural, and societal considerations when designing a bespoke serious game or gamified experience. (B.1)
Design a game-like prototype that serves a specific purpose for a specific audience. (C.1)
Critically reflect on one’s own designs and iteratively propose alternate game-like solutions that fit a purpose and benefit an audience. (F.1)

42058.description: This studio equips you with practical skills in telecommunications and electronics, transforming theoretical knowledge into actionable expertise. 42069.title: Research Methods
42069.description: As the second subject in the research series for higher degree research students, this subject completes the formal research training by introducing the concept of what it means to be a holistic researcher. To be a proficient researcher, skills must include knowledge of varying ontologies, epistemologies, paradigms and methodologies. Knowing tools and techniques that are available for use outside one's immediate discipline only enhances a researcher. To do this, the subject takes your understanding of the purpose of research and helps you to justify the importance of your research and how using a specific methodology to conduct the research will support your argument. The subject aims to place you, as a researcher in the wider context of the research ecosystem by introducing different research methods to support the discipline-based research questions. The subject also helps you to build an understanding of how research is conducted differently beyond the academy and introduces students to the writing and presentation expectations of HDR processes at UTS.
learningOutcomes: Present a rationale (Impact/significance) for the research study based on context, discipline, topic, and population. (B.1)
Customise research methods based on research objectives stated in research projects. (C.1)
Justify disciplinary research methods to assure reliability and validity of research study. (D.1)
Draw on the community of researchers to aid in the enhancement of one's own research abilities (E.1)
Reflect on implications of research knowledge, design and impacts on research to wider disciplinary community. (F.1)

Learning to process sensor data and design multi-sensory feedback, you'll enhance your prototype through iterative user assessment, honing your design to completion.

Embed sensors and process sensor data to support the user experience of a physical interactive system. (D.1)
Assess the usability and appropriateness of an interactive system through studying use in context. (C.1)
Communicate design and implementation strategies effectively to a range of disciplinary and non-disciplinary stakeholders. (E.1)

42090.title: Introduction to Sustainable Microgrids
42090.description: This subject aims to equip you with an understanding of the design and control of sustainable microgrids, small-scale power systems that can function independently or in conjunction with larger grids. You'll learn about the essentials of microgrids, including their architecture, distributed generation, energy storage technologies like batteries and fuel cells, converter functions, power management, and hierarchical controls. The curriculum also covers microgrid modeling, stability, and protection, as well as detailed insights into storage and battery technologies. Through real-world case studies, you'll gain practical knowledge, equipping you to contribute to the development of efficient and reliable energy systems essential for global transformation.
learningOutcomes: Describe sustainable microgrids and the challenges of implementing them in communities. (B.1)
Design and evaluate new microgrids considering consumer behaviours and technical requirements to improve the resilience of power supply. (C.1)
Analyse cost and benefits of microrgid technology to support low-carbon power system operation and energy efficient operation. (D.1)
Evaluate the design of a current microgrid to determine its reliability, sustainability and possible improvements. (C.1)

42093.title: Electrical Power and Energy Systems Studio A
42093.description: This studio provides practice-based learning environment tailored for electrical engineering students to deeply grasp and develop professional skills in modeling and designing electrical power and energy systems. Recognising the dynamic shifts in the industry driven by environmental, technical, and economic factors, this studio prioritises reflective design approaches, collaboration, mentorship, and thorough learning by engaging with intricate problems. Through this experience, you will progress towards senior team roles, refine your reflective skills, and utilise modeling proficiency to create and verify simulations and real-world solutions. This comprehensive preparation equips you to tackle current and future challenges in energy systems, with a focus on achieving a future net-zero energy system.
learningOutcomes: Justify the role of cost-effective energy conversion systems for sustainable energy systems and future smart grids. (B.1)
Validate models and sustainable engineering solutions to electrical power and/or energy systems problems. (C.1)
Demonstrate application methods, tools and resources to achieve system objectives. (D.1)
Communicate with peers about solutions and possible research findings to solve difficult problems. (E.1)
Reflect on team’s progress and feedback to improve personal performance and team’s achievement. (F.1)

42094.title: Electrical Power and Energy Systems Studio B

42095.title: Introduction to Building Information Modelling
42095.description: This subject equips you with essential knowledge and practical skills in Building Information Modelling (BIM), a transformative approach in the construction industry. You'll learn about BIM's core concepts, including Open Data Exchange, Integrated Project Delivery, and Lean Construction, and understand the significance of model-based data in collaborative, quality-focused construction settings. You'll also develop technical proficiency in vendor-neutral data exchange, model checking, and review processes. The subject explores the impact of data quality on BIM applications such as 3D simulation, sustainability, digital twins, scheduling (4D), and cost estimation (5D). Delivered in block mode, the subject combines brief lectures with workshops, where you'll engage with industry projects and datasets to master BIM workflows and multidisciplinary design reviews. Preparation through online materials is required for active participation in discussions, case study analysis, and hands-on industry model activities. Progress is tracked through milestones, tutorial exercises, and an in-class quiz.
learningOutcomes: Apply key technologies, processes and protocols supporting BIM-enabled design and construction. (D.1)
Manage model-based information for design, construction and operations. (C.1)
Communicate capabilities and benefits of BIM, Open Data Exchange, Integrated Project Delivery, and Lean Construction to project stakeholders. (E.1)
Evaluate an organisation’s BIM capability maturity. (B.1)

42096.title: Data Visualisation Foundations
42096.description: This subject provides an understanding of data visualisation and visual analytics, equipping you with the skills to select and apply various visualisation techniques in diverse contexts. You will learn to manage and prepare data for visualisation, and critically assess the effectiveness of different visualisation methods.
learningOutcomes: Recognise and compare a range of standard data visualisation techniques. (D.1)
Be able to apply a range of standard data visualisation techniques. (D.1)

42097.title: Advanced Data Visualisation
42097.description: This subject advances your ability to visualise complex data sets, including time-series, textual, and spatio-temporal data, crafting clear and user-specific visualisations. You'll focus on creating interactive visualisations and understand the implications of interactivity for design through hands-on practice.
learningOutcomes: Design interactive data visualisation techniques. (C.1)
Apply interactive data visualisation techniques. (D.1)

42098.title: Applied Data Visualisation
42098.description: This subject hones your skills in crafting data visualisations that enhance data-driven storytelling. You'll explore narrative development and how interactive techniques allow users to engage with data within a story arc. Additionally, you'll examine cutting-edge technologies, like real-time 3D game engines and novel audio-visual hardware, for their potential in creating collaborative and immersive visualisations.
learningOutcomes: Design and create data visualisations for particular social contexts that are appropriate for specific users. (C.1)
Design and create data visualisations that facilitate the discovery and presentation of data-driven stories. (C.1)

42127.title: Digital Engineering for Infrastructure and Facilities
42127.description: Digital Engineering for Infrastructure and Facilities addresses an industry-recognised need for contemporary civil infrastructure projects. It will equip you with a theoretical foundation and practical skills through engagement with industry best practices, workflows, and real-world datasets. Key areas covered include Common Data Environments, Survey and Existing Conditions Modelling, Design Coordination, and Quantity Take-Off for Planning, Cost and Carbon Estimation. On successful completion you will be well prepared to take a leading role in the digital delivery of infrastructure and building projects, making them more efficient, effective, and adaptable to the evolving needs of modern methods of construction.
learningOutcomes: Establish and manage infrastructure projects by effectively incorporating digital engineering principles, tools, and techniques. (D.1)
Consider best practice approaches for effectively communicating and collaborating with project teams and stakeholders throughout infrastructure projects. (E.1)
Apply information management strategies and tools to design and establish a common data environment for infrastructure and building projects. (C.1)
Interpret and manage multiple data sources to create comprehensive digital representations of infrastructure sites, ensuring accuracy and relevance. (D.1)
Implement and evaluate effective design coordination strategies using digital tools and methodologies to resolve discrepancies and ensure data integrity. (D.1)
Accurately extract model-based take-offs facilitating detailed project planning, costings and carbon measurement for data-driven decision-making. (B.1)

requisite.text: Admission into C50100 Digital Engineering for Infrastructure and Facilities

42127.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have a background in engineering or construction related disciplines, or one year of relevant work experience on infrastructure construction projects, and basic familiarity with general CAD or BIM concepts is recommended for participants in this course.

42135.title: Design for Automation: Product and Equipment Manufacturing
42135.description: This subject explores how design enhances automation in manufacturing, focusing on the optimisation of assembly, transportation, storage, and handling processes. As production demands grow, companies are increasingly relying on automation; understanding how design influences these processes is crucial for streamlining production and boosting efficiency. You'll learn to create designs that complement and improve automated manufacturing systems.
learningOutcomes: Identify automation opportunities for improving product and equipment manufacturing, encompassing product consistency, design, productivity, efficiency, workplace safety, and sustainability. (B.1)
Evaluate product and/or production processes to identify parts suitable for automation and those requiring redesign prior to automation. (D.1)
Develop a strategic automation proposal that encompasses manufacturing technologies, addresses product and equipment manufacturing concerns and anticipates potential issues. (C.1)
42135.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge of Industrial Engineering; Design of Production Systems; Design of Mechanical and Mechatronic Systems; Industrial Automation.

42136.title: Design for Automation: Food and Beverage Production
42136.description: This subject addresses how automation and digitisation can transform the food and beverage manufacturing industry, enhancing traceability, quality control, consistency, productivity, efficiency, and safety. You'll learn to design systems that minimise double handling, refine quality control to reduce variation, optimise pallet loading, and implement suitable pick and place technologies and inline robotics. These skills are key to advancing manufacturing processes within the sector.
learningOutcomes: Identify automation opportunities for improving food and beverage manufacturing, encompassing traceability, quality control, productivity, efficiency, workplace safety and sustainability. (B.1)
Evaluate product and/or production processes to identify parts suitable for automation and those requiring redesign prior to automation. (D.1)
Develop a strategic automation proposal that encompasses manufacturing technologies, addresses food and beverage handling concerns and anticipates potential issues. (C.1)
42136.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge of Industrial Engineering; Design of Production Systems; Design of Mechanical and Mechatronic Systems; Industrial Automation.

42137.title: Managing Modern Industrial Automation
42137.description: This subject, in collaboration with UTS and Siemens, imparts a broad understanding of how industrial automation can revolutionize manufacturing. You'll study how modern automation solutions can enhance competitiveness and sustainability in industrial operations. Engaging with diverse case studies, you'll witness the impact of automation and explore Industry 4.0 technologies, equipping you with insights into the future of manufacturing.
learningOutcomes: Understand main elements of factory physics, performance, and quality indicators associated with production systems. (D.1)
Apply methods and techniques to redesign production systems considering modern industrial automation and industry 4.0 technologies. (C.1)
Assess the impact of adopting a set of industry 4.0 technologies within production systems. (B.1)
42137.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge of Industrial Engineering; Design of Production Systems; Industrial Automation.

42138.title: Design for Automation: Prefab Construction Manufacturing
42138.description: This subject examines how advanced manufacturing techniques, such as prefabrication, automated fastening, and welding technologies, can be leveraged to meet rising production demands in the construction industry. By focusing on the design aspect, you'll learn how to streamline the production process through automation, enhancing the efficiency and speed of constructing products.
learningOutcomes: Identify automation opportunities for improving prefabricated construction manufacturing, encompassing productivity, efficiency, technologies, workplace safety and sustainability (B.1)
Evaluate product and/or production processes to identify parts suitable for automation and those requiring redesign prior to automation. (D.1)
Develop a strategic automation proposal that encompasses manufacturing technologies, addresses prefabricated constructions concerns and anticipates potential issues. (C.1)
42138.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge of Industrial Engineering; Design of Production Systems; Design of Mechanical and Mechatronic Systems; Industrial Automation.

42143.title: Statistical Process Control
42143.description: This subject equips you with a comprehensive understanding of statistical process control (SPC), a fundamental component of quality management and continuous improvement in industrial settings, with insights from Thales. You'll learn to master the key features and tools of SPC, including the correct selection of control charts, sampling size, and process capability assessment. Practical industry examples, case studies, and project activities enhance your learning, ensuring you can apply SPC effectively within any enterprise.
learningOutcomes: Interpret and appropriately apply common Statistical Process Control (SPC) tools. (D.1)
Demonstrate applicable data collection, analyse and interpretation. (D.1)
Develop targeted SPC investigation and response strategies. (C.1)
42143.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge of Industrial Engineering; Design of Production Systems; Industrial Automation.

42144.title: Advanced Programming and Use of Collaborative Robots
42144.description: This subject is designed to extend students' knowledge of cobots, focusing on applying cobots to industry relevant tasks. Through this subject, students gain experience programming cobots to perform industry-relevant complex tasks and troubleshoot emergent challenges related to cobots. Students are able to integrate a cobot with peripheral equipment to form part of a larger system, and utilise end-of-arm-tooling to perform physical operations such as materials handing and palletising.
learningOutcomes: Program cobots to perform industry-relevant complex tasks and troubleshoot associated challenges. (D.1)
Utilise end-of-arm-tooling to perform physical operations such as materials handing. (D.1)
Integrate a cobot with peripheral equipment to form part of a larger system. (D.1)

42145.title: 3D Scanning Methods for Reverse Engineering
42145.description: This subject is designed to build on the knowledge and proficiency in the principles and techniques of reverse engineering learnt in the Introduction to Reverse Engineering subject, whilst using 3D scanning methods. Through this subject, students gain experience in using 3D scanning technology to capture a component’s complete geometry and using mesh clean-up tools to prepare faceted bodies for downstream modelling and/or manufacturing. They also learn how to identify logical facet shapes and group triangles for use in the creation of faces, use reverse engineering software to create native surfaces on top of imported data, and use deviation analysis to ensure accuracy between the re-engineered part and its original. This subject equips students with the skills necessary to apply reverse engineering techniques using 3D scanning methods for manufacturing, quality assurance, or other purposes.
learningOutcomes: Use 3D scanning technology to capture a component’s complete geometry. (D.1)
Demonstrate knowledge in using point cloud and mesh clean-up tools to remove errors and prepare faceted bodies for downstream modelling and/or manufacturing. (D.1)
Create surfaces on top of imported data to enable use in CAD software. (D.1)

42146.title: Manual Methods for Reverse Engineering
42146.description:
This micro-credential provides an introduction to the principles and practices of manual reverse engineering. The subject is structured to equip learners with the necessary skills and knowledge for accurately measuring physical objects using advanced tools such as computer metrology, vernier calipers, and micrometers.

Students engage in detailed analysis and interpretation of measurement data, a critical step in constructing precise digital representations of physical entities. The subject also encompasses the application of manual reverse engineering techniques, essential for the reproduction of components in fields like manufacturing and quality assurance. This subject is designed to foster a thorough understanding of these processes, preparing students for professional applications in various technical domains.
learningOutcomes: Reflect on the principles and techniques of manual reverse engineering methods for engineering applications in your own work context. (F.1)
Analyse measurement data to validate the accuracy of a 3D scanned component. (D.1)
Apply manual techniques to reverse engineer components for engineering professionals engaged with manufacturing and quality assurance. (D.1)

42172.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
42172.description: This subject provides a grounding in Artificial Intelligence (AI), covering core areas such as learning, natural language processing, computer vision, search, knowledge representation, and reasoning. Through lectures/workshops and labs, you'll gain conceptual understanding of basic AI techniques and practical experience of using AI techniques and tools. You will be assessed in a knowledge test, a set of simple AI applications, and a group project designing an AI solution for a real-world problem, developing sound judgement and competence in this cutting-edge field.
learningOutcomes: Describe key ideas and applications of common AI techniques to people in the same discipline. (D.1)
Apply common AI algorithms to solve simple real-world problems. (D.1)
Design and justify AI solutions for medium to large problems. (C.1)
Collaborate effectively on a project team. (E.1)

42173.title: Advanced Natural Language Processing
42173.description: This subject introduces advanced topics and technologies in natural language processing, and their applications to real-world problems. You'll build on prior NLP knowledge to understand powerful algorithms and explore deep learning approaches that drive cutting-edge NLP technologies, applying them to real-world challenges.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the advantages and limitations of several advanced natural language processing methods. (D.1)
Review technologies used in advanced natural language processing literature, and perform self-reflection. (F.1)
Develop an advanced natural language processing project for a real-world problem. (C.1)
Communicate project results in both oral and written forms. (E.1)

42174.title: Artificial Intelligence Studio
42174.description:
In this subject, you'll undertake a comprehensive project that needs substantial research effort, applying your full range of AI skills. Your task is to conduct research and project development in a team that hones your ability to articulate a research question or a problem statement, relate it to existing work, select appropriate methods or models, iteratively develop the solution, and effectively present your findings and demonstrate your ability to work as part of a team.

You will tackle a real-world problem and develop a complete solution in the project that encompasses stages from background research, through data handling, to solution development and deployment. You'll receive guidance from an academic mentor and produce an individual portfolio that outlines your learning journey and your achievements in this subject, including a reflective journal and contribution to project artifacts (e.g., project proposal, project plan, proof of concept of solution idea, interim solution and final solution). You will be assessed on your portfolio and an oral presentation, reflecting professional academic and industry standards.
learningOutcomes: Identify environmental and social impacts of the AI solution in a given context. (B.1)
Design an AI solution to address a real-world problem. (C.1)
Choose appropriate AI methods to develop a complete solution in a real-world setting. (D.1)
Communicate the results of the AI investigation appropriate for a business audience. (E.1)
Reflect on interactions with project teams that influence adjustments to own practice. (F.1)

42177.title: Image Processing and Pattern Recognition
42177.description: This subject imparts the ability to extract information from images and videos using image processing and pattern recognition techniques, underpinning innovative applications like video surveillance and medical diagnostics. You will learn the principles of image processing and pattern recognition, create software for automatic image and video analysis, and explore recent advancements in the field. The goal is to cultivate skills necessary to develop image processing and computer vision applications. You will apply your knowledge in a team-based project, tackling real-world problems such as detecting individuals and objects in surveillance footage, automating medical image diagnosis, and recognising faces in images, while also delving into current research to enhance your understanding of this fast-paced domain.
learningOutcomes: Use foundational techniques of image processing and analysis such as filtering, segmentation and local features to solve image processing problems of real-world application. (C.1)
Build a statistical classifier and know how to use other classifiers. (D.1)
Apply image processing and pattern recognition techniques to detect objects and activities in images and video. (D.1)
Conduct collaborative research into image processing and pattern recognition techniques in a professional context. (E.1)

42203.title: Sustainable Engineering Design
42203.description: This subject immerses you in design, sustainability and innovation as core engineering activities through a real-world project. You'll select a problem, explore multiple solutions, and develop a prototype, honing your ability to meet stakeholder needs with an engineering mindset. Employing design and systems thinking you'll understand complex design contexts, stakeholder engagement, and requirements analysis, including legal and technical aspects. You'll also tackle design analysis, managing risks and uncertainties, focusing on manufacture, sustainability, and safety. By applying these concepts and scientific principles to your project, you'll grasp the models of design and innovation processes and the authentic practice of engineers.
learningOutcomes: Identify social, environmental and economic needs and constraints for a project using sustainability frameworks, methods and tools. (B.1)
Synthesise research findings to ideate interdisciplinary, sustainable solutions within complex and changing contexts. (C.1)

Apply design and systems thinking problem solving approaches to define problems in an effective manner to provide fit for purpose engineered solutions underpinned by a sustainability and innovation focus. (C.1)
Organise team work, manage interdisciplinary collaboration, and assess own and other team member’s contributions. (E.1)

42218.title: Basic Programming and Use of Collaborative Robots
42218.description: This subject introduces you to Collaborative Robots (cobots), a flexible and agile automation technology that operates safely alongside humans, requiring minimal safety and infrastructure adaptations. You will learn technical aspects, safety and ethical considerations, and gain hands-on experience in programming cobots, preparing you for their adoption in various industries.
learningOutcomes: Select cobots for common industry applications. (C.1)
Evaluate cobot safety implications, safety devices, and ethics. (B.1)
Program a cobot using relevant programming languages. (D.1)

42670.title: Research Foundations
42670.description: This subject introduces higher degree research students to the fundamentals of research, fostered through the initiation of their own studies. You will learn about the research ecosystem, including academic publishing, presentations, research integrity, assessing research literature, creating data management plans and ethical considerations. The subject also explores the broader impact of research through your attendance at intensive workshops geared to engage in skill development, core understanding and attitudinal expectations required for this level of study. This subject is a pre-requisite for the second subject in this series of research subjects and together they create the foundational knowledge needed for you to succeed as a researcher in your field of expertise.
learningOutcomes: Develop a research data management plan. (D.1)
Critically evaluate relevant academic literature. (C.1)
Demonstrate social responsibility in academic research. (B.1)
Communicate research outcomes effectively. (E.1)

42721.title: Introduction to Biomedical Engineering
42721.description: Biomedical engineering applies engineering principles to medicine, impacting healthcare from diagnostics to treatment. This subject covers the field's breadth, including tissue engineering, imaging, bio-instrumentation, and more futuristic areas like stem cell engineering and 3D organ printing. You'll explore these through lectures and labs, and then, working solo or in teams, you'll tackle a pressing medical issue using biomedical engineering methods, fostering innovation and practical problem-solving skills.
learningOutcomes: Identify the scope of biomedical engineering and its applications to healthcare. (D.1)
Design a biomedical engineering solution to real-life clinical problems. (C.1)
Communicate ideas and findings in biomedical engineering in verbal and written forms. (E.1)
Collaboratively generate a biomedical engineering solution to a complex biomedical problem. (E.1)

42722.title: Biomedical Engineering Design and Additive Manufacturing
42722.description:
Biomedical engineering design and optimisation is a critical stage in the development of medical devices, contributing to advancements in biomedical engineering by enhancing functionality, safety, and performance. Medical devices must be carefully designed to ensure optimal and safe functionality in real-world conditions. This requires consideration of various factors including mechanical properties and relevant biocompatibility requirements. Advances in manufacturing technologies, particularly additive manufacturing, have further expanded design possibilities by enabling the fabrication of complex and customized structures. These innovations play a key role in the development of high-performance medical devices tailored to specific clinical needs.

In this professional subject, you will explore the principles of biomedical engineering design, develop advanced computer-aided design (CAD) skills using industry-standard CAD software, gain knowledge of various national and international standards relevant to the design and evaluation of medical devices, learn patient-specific design techniques and the necessary software, and apply finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate the biomechanical behaviour of medical devices. Additionally, you will utilise additive manufacturing to create prototypes, reinforcing the connection between design, simulation, and fabrication. Through this process, you will design medical devices, evaluate their biomechanical properties, and optimize their performance to ensure safety and reliability.

The subject includes two project streams, with student teams selecting one stream for their final assessment. While each project focuses on a different medical challenge, both provide equivalent opportunities for you to engage with the technical content and achieve the intended learning outcomes of the subject.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate stakeholders and their needs in the design, development, and application of medical devices to identify key design constraints and considerations. (B.1)
Apply engineering design principles to develop complicated solutions for biomedical engineering challenges. (C.1)
Critically evaluate medical device designs in the context of existing research and industry advancements. (C.1)
Apply finite element analysis (FEA) to characterise and optimise biomechanical properties of medical devices. (D.1)
Apply relevant national and international standards to the analysis and evaluation of medical devices. (D.1)
Collaboratively manage biomedical engineering projects to professionally communicate findings. (E.1)

42724.title: Microfluidics in Biology and Medicine
42724.description: This subject introduces you to Microfluidics, the precise control of fluids at a micro-scale, revolutionising point-of-care diagnostics and cell biology. You'll learn to manipulate biological materials and chemicals on this scale, constructing miniaturised devices like Lab-on-a-chips for applications such as cell separation and single cell analysis. Through educational videos and interactive virtual labs, you'll learn how to build functional microfluidic devices and explore the use of microfluidics in real-world medical and biological scenarios, preparing you for cutting-edge research and diagnostic work.
learningOutcomes: Identify, and understand microfluidic principles in the context of the medical industry and current research problems. (C.1)
Formulate and apply prototyping and design methodologies to design and develop microfluidic technologies. (D.1)
Critically analyse and communicate disciplinary knowledge and practices to a wide range of audiences. (E.1)

42820.title: Machine Learning Foundations
42820.description: This microcredential equips you with the fundamentals of machine learning, the technique that allows machines to learn from data and improve their task performance. You'll be guided to apply cutting-edge algorithms practically within your professional field. You'll master core machine learning concepts and a generic framework, with a focus on foundational models like decision trees and linear families, which are vital both in theory and in real-world applications.
learningOutcomes: Apply machine learning algorithms with practical implementation for professional contexts. (D.1)

42821.title: Data Analytics Foundations
42821.description: Data Analytics Foundations imparts the essentials of data analytics, crucial for transforming vast data into actionable insights for business and societal benefit. You'll grasp data analytics' language and its role, learn about the prevalent CRISP-DM methodology, and practice core skills including dataset identification, data preparation, and cluster analysis. Advanced clustering techniques will refine your ability to discern and tackle analytical problems, allowing you to interpret datasets and explore data visually.
learningOutcomes: Apply pre-processing, transformation and visualisation to business data sets. (D.1)

42822.title: Advanced Data Analytics
42822.description: Advanced Data Analytics hones your ability to classify and predict data through hands-on experience with techniques like decision tree induction, support vector machines, ensemble methods, and random forests. Building on foundational skills, this microcredential teaches you to evaluate classification accuracy, identify prediction issues, and enhances your competencies in data visualisation and result evaluation.
learningOutcomes: Apply data mining and pattern discovery, and analysis skills in predictive analytics of data sets. (D.1)

42823.title: Applied Data Analytics
42823.description: Applied Data Analytics sharpens your ability to independently plan and execute a data mining project, utilising the widely-adopted CRISP-DM methodology. From preprocessing to deploying results, you'll engage with various representation techniques and apply your analytics expertise to real industry scenarios, effectively communicating your findings. This practical, problem-based microcredential is focused on developing both your analytical autonomy and professional articulation.
learningOutcomes: Implement a data mining project in a business environment. (D.1)

42824.title: Environmental Noise and Planning
42824.description: This microcredential covers the fundamentals of acoustics and noise control from a practical viewpoint. It focuses on assessing, regulating, and managing noise impacts. Key topics include developing a Noise Impact Assessment, applying relevant noise policies, and evaluating predictions and proposed mitigation measures. The subject is designed to equip the learner with the ability to interpret Noise Impact Assessment Reports and judge environmental noise and vibration impacts from projects using conceptual acoustical fundamentals.
learningOutcomes: Explore policy context and measurements in environmental noise and planning problems. (B.1)
Develop and interpret noise impact and management in local environments. (C.1)

42825.title: Inventive Problem-Solving with TRIZ
42825.description: This microcredential hones your problem-solving abilities through the application of TRIZ, the "Theory of Inventive Problem Solving." You'll learn to analyse engineering challenges, identify technical contradictions and devise innovative solutions. By mastering TRIZ methodologies and tools, you will develop the cognitive skills to tackle complex issues independently and transfer this knowledge to diverse problems.
learningOutcomes: Create function models identifying technical contradictions in engineering products or problems. (D.1)
Develop conceptual solutions to technical contradictions in engineering products or problems. (C.1)

42826.title: Introduction to Complex Systems Modelling
42826.description: This microcredential demystifies complexity and complex systems, guiding you through the modelling of such systems, which traditional analytics can't fully decipher. Modelling and simulation become tools to understand unpredictable system behaviours and the potential effects of our interventions. With complex systems pervasive across natural, social, and technological domains, mastering their modelling is crucial. You'll learn to identify, classify, and select the most appropriate modelling approach for a given system, enhancing your analytical proficiency in handling real-world complexity.
learningOutcomes: Explain what complex systems are and classify them according to their characteristics. (C.1)
Explain the role of models and simulations, and the key steps in modelling through a review of case studies involving applications of modelling of complex systems and analysis techniques. (B.1, D.1)

42889.title: iOS Application Development
42889.description: This microcredential introduces you to iOS application development, covering the Swift programming language, the iOS development environment, and key app frameworks. It emphasises practical experience, ensuring you gain hands-on skills in software development within the iOS context.
learningOutcomes: Design a well-structured programming solution that satisfies given software requirements. (C.1)
Implement the solution using Swift programming language under the iOS development environment. (D.1)
Independently explore and utilise various iOS frameworks and APIs. (D.1)
Demonstrate the fully tested software using iOS simulator for iPads and iPhones. (D.1)

42891.title: Infrastructure for Cloud Computing
42891.description: This subject expands on cloud computing, focusing on the setup and operation of cloud infrastructure. You'll explore cloud architecture, virtualisation, storage technologies, data centre basics, and cloud security and compliance. With strong industry relevance, the subject includes practical labs where you'll gain hands-on experience with tools prevalent in the cloud infrastructure sector, complementing your broader cloud computing education.
learningOutcomes: Compare and contrast the components of Cloud computing infrastructure through summarising the current theory behind Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) platform and analysing alternatives. (C.1)
Identify how virtualisation and cloud computing technologies come together to deliver a sustainable business advantage. (B.1)

Design a cloud infrastructure solution for a small business, allowing for dynamic scaling of applications, delivery on Service-Level Agreements (SLAs) in the most efficient way possible and comparing the core architectures and technologies used within current Cloud Platforms. (C.1)
Implement a small-scale enterprise cloud platform given cost, time, technical and business requirements. (D.1)

Assess the limitations and business risks of cloud computing, especially the adoption of public and hybrid cloud deployments, including the Sovereignty, Jurisdictional and Security implications of the cloud. (B.1)

42892.title: Applied Machine Learning
42892.description: Applied Machine Learning empowers you to independently plan and execute a machine learning project, covering the entire project lifecycle from problem comprehension to result deployment. This practical subject hones your expertise in machine learning and enhances your ability to professionally articulate your findings.
learningOutcomes: Implement a machine learning project in a business environment. (B.1)

42893.title: Data Engineering Foundations
42893.description: This microcredential offers you a foundational grounding in data engineering - the crucial infrastructure and processes for managing and deriving value from data. Suitable for learners of various backgrounds, it prepares you to collaborate effectively with data engineering teams and integrate data engineering into your projects and operations. You'll explore the data value chain, data infrastructure, data pipelines, and implementation technologies, alongside data quality, security, monitoring, and governance, to understand how data engineers enable organisations to harness their data assets.
learningOutcomes: Apply basic data engineering principles to plan infrastructure and strategies that allow organisations to derive value from their data. (D.1)

42894.title: Advanced Machine Learning
42894.description: Advanced Machine Learning deepens your understanding of sophisticated data models, algorithms, and theoretical principles, building upon existing machine learning knowledge. This subject provides a mix of theory and practical application, focusing on statistical learning theory and empirical risk minimization to refine your ML models and algorithms.
learningOutcomes: Design machine learning algorithms with practical implementation for professional contexts. (C.1)

42895.title: Data Literacy
42895.description: Data literacy, a critical skill for modern professionals, encompasses the ability to interpret, represent, and communicate data effectively. This subject introduces you to the essentials of data proficiency, preparing you for work in data-centric organisations and serving as a foundation for advanced study in data science, analytics, or statistics.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate an understanding and clearly communicate key concepts and relevant information from a data set. (D.1)

42896.title: Advanced Data Analytics for Cybersecurity
42896.description: Advanced Data Analytics for Cybersecurity equips you with big data and threat intelligence tools to tackle internal and external cyber threats. The subject covers statistical pattern recognition, inferencing and intelligent technologies for cybersecurity data analysis. You'll learn machine learning applications for cybersecurity, engage with the standard processes for data analytics, and gain practical experience in identifying and mitigating risks to corporate IT systems.
learningOutcomes: Detect and analyse cyber-attacks using data analytics to determine security robustness. (D.1)

42897.title: Data Analytics for Cybersecurity Foundations
42897.description: Data Analytics for Cybersecurity Foundations melds big data with threat intelligence, enabling you to detect and counter insider and external cyber threats. This subject introduces methods for identifying security issues, packet analysis, and techniques for handling DDoS attacks, among other intelligent data-driven cybersecurity technologies. You'll become versed in the language and significance of data analytics within cybersecurity, learn standard analytic processes, and practise identifying risks and vulnerabilities in corporate IT networks.
learningOutcomes: Apply data analytics to investigate cybersecurity datasets. (D.1)

42899.title: Applied Data Analytics for Cybersecurity
42899.description: Applied Data Analytics for Cybersecurity integrates big data and threat intelligence for detecting and mitigating insider and external cyber threats. You will explore emerging challenges such as malware analysis, adversarial machine learning, and privacy-preserving data analytics. The subject introduces artificial intelligence technologies relevant to cybersecurity and common data analytic approaches, providing hands-on experience in identifying risks and securing corporate IT networks.
learningOutcomes: Synthesise data analytics with other techniques to appropriately set rules indicators for intrusion detection. (D.1)

42904.title: Cloud Computing and Software as a Service
42904.description: This subject provides an introduction to cloud computing, covering architecture, Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS), Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS), Software-as-a-Service (SaaS), virtualisation, and multi-tenancy. You'll first critically analyse a cloud computing aspect through a group research report. Then, you'll develop practical cloud-based software engineering skills on an existing platform, culminating in the creation of a cloud-based software application with your group.
learningOutcomes: Articulate the need for cloud computing, elements of cloud computing for e-business, e-government, e-banking and e-learning. (B.1)
Describe the architecture of different types of Cloud Services (IaaS, PaaS and SaaS), different types of Virtualization and their industrial use. (D.1)
Critically understand the current issues in Cloud Computing for informed business decision making. (D.1)
Create a Cloud Computing prototype on a Cloud platform for areas such as e-business, e-government, e-banking and e-learning. (C.1)

42907.title: Design for Durability
42907.description: This subject focuses on the durability design of concrete structures, targeting a design life of 50 years for buildings and 100 years for infrastructure as mandated by Australian Standards. You'll learn about the specifications and quality control measures to prevent durability issues during construction, including the risk of early-age concrete cracking from restrained shrinkage. The subject will equip you with an understanding of concrete and steel deterioration mechanisms and the importance of control measures throughout the design, construction, and maintenance phases.
learningOutcomes: Identify and evaluate the dominant environmental loads affecting the durability performance of a concrete structure. Identify principal deterioration mechanism(s) and other inherent durability issues associated with various structural components of a concrete structure. (D.1)

Apply specific design life model(s) to design each structural component from first principles, and specify the various types of concrete and concrete cover required for the structure. Compare and contrast design solutions derived from first principles with design requirements in relevant Australian Standards AS 3600 or AS 5100. (C.1)
Prepare a Durability Plan report covering the durability design and concrete specifications, and key Quality Control measures beyond those recommended in current Australian Standards. (C.1)
Identify and evaluate the dominant processes leading to concrete cracking. (D.1)

Reducing the risk of restrained shrinkage induced concrete cracking by assessing the time to concrete cracking according to environmental conditions and determining the minimum required curing duration. (C.1)
