42908.title: Postgraduate Engineering Capstone A
42908.description: This subject equips you with research methodologies essential for engineering projects or advanced research. You'll develop specialised knowledge and skills to formulate research questions and craft project proposals within your field. Learning is interactive, combining large workshops with small-group discussions, covering topics from social perspectives in engineering to research ethics and proposal writing. Resources on Canvas and a curated reading list support your preparation, while consultations with subject staff and regular meetings with your supervisor guide your progress. Peer review seminars enhance your evaluative skills and project viability. Additionally, you'll refine academic and professional communication skills, with Language Development Tutorials available for those seeking extra support, ensuring your success in academia and the workplace.
learningOutcomes: Develop a research question that is related to their field of practice. (B.1)
Review the relevant research literature to identify an opportunity to contribute to an existing field of knowledge (B.1)
Design an ethical and sustainable research project with an appropriate methodology (C.1)
Create a feasible research proposal in collaboration with a supervisor (C.1)
Seek and respond to feedback from supervisor and peers to inform reflection upon performance (E.1)

42909.title: The Connected Studio
42909.description: In this subject, you'll enhance your creative and technical abilities, working under industry professionals and adopting professional studio standards. You'll tackle industry-style briefs in teams, exploring disciplines such as story development, art design, asset creation, performance, postproduction, technical management, and project coordination. Additionally, you'll formulate plans for professional growth and learn to apply culturally sensitive practices when engaging with Indigenous peoples and communities.
learningOutcomes: Apply knowledge of culturally appropriate processes and protocols when working for and with Indigenous peoples and communities. (A.1)
Engage with stakeholders to evaluate social and ethical impacts of relevant project-based activities. (B.1)
Apply relevant methodologies to respond to creative challenges and develop implementation strategies. (C.1)
Work empathically, iteratively and constructively in response to complex and changing challenges and environments. (C.1)
Apply expert technical knowledge and skills to complex project challenges. (D.1)
Research relevant existing and emerging technologies in order to extend knowledge and skill base. (D.1)
Contribute to informed, constructive and candid critique in group settings, grounded by disciplinary methods and theories. (E.1)
Collaborate professionally, strategically and respectfully with stakeholders to optimise outcomes. (E.1)
Demonstrate accountability by identifying risks and analysing outcomes to learn and improve the quality of individual and collaborative work. (F.1)

42910.description: The Collaboration Studio (Studio 2) sharpens your research skills in emerging visualisation technologies, enhancing critical thinking, collaboration, and technical proficiency for creative and professional practice. 42911.title: The Challenge Studio
42911.description: In Studio 3, you will complete a 3D animation project initiated in Studio 1 and advance an emerging technology prototype chosen by an industry panel from Studio 2. Working collaboratively in a simulated professional environment, you'll leverage group strengths to produce outcomes that meet high industry standards. Employing creative and technical problem-solving, you'll extend your skills to generate innovative solutions that surpass individual capabilities. Throughout the process, you'll critically assess your work, incorporate stakeholder feedback, and strive for excellence in production values. You will also reflect on team dynamics, forecast future possibilities, and adopt ethical research practices, particularly when engaging with Indigenous stakeholders.
learningOutcomes: Implement specialised knowledge of ethical Indigenous research approaches in professional contexts. (A.1)
Critically reflect on individual behaviours and collaborative practices experienced in a working animation/visualisation studio, and how these affect project outcomes and stakeholders. (B.1)

42991.title: Advanced Water and Wastewater Treatment
42991.description: This subject addresses the need for advanced water and wastewater treatment processes, which are essential due to emerging pollutants, population growth, industrial activities, and dwindling water resources. You'll learn to design advanced treatment processes using membrane technology, bridging fundamental principles with real applications and design parameters. A computer-based design tool will be demonstrated for designing membrane-based treatment systems. The subject integrates science—chemistry, physics, and biology—with engineering, encouraging learning from nature and the application of engineering solutions to contemporary challenges in water and wastewater management.
learningOutcomes: Undertake socio-technical analysis for the selection of suitable water and wastewater treatment technologies. (B.1)

Create a requirement analysis, system design and detailed design for an advanced water and wastewater treatment system which addresses practical water treatment process problems and select appropriate processes for target pollutants including emerging pollutants to meet specified water quality requirements based on the Australian standards. (C.1)

Describe principles of membrane processes for water purification, desalination and wastewater treatment including general and specific membrane problems such as fouling, scaling and cleaning, pre-treatment options, membrane elements and systems, and application and use of a practical computer-based design tool for the design of brackish or seawater reverse osmosis plants. (C.1)
Provide recommendations of appropriate treatment processes for upgrading water and wastewater treatment efficiency. (D.1)

43001.title: Cybersecurity Challenge Studio
43001.description: This studio develops practical cybersecurity capability through authentic, challenge-based learning. You will work individually or in a small team on a personalised challenge pathway, agreed through a learning contract with a supervisor, which defines the scope of the challenge, intended outcomes, and assessment expectations. The studio is designed to support industry readiness and professional development through hands-on practice, regular feedback, and evidence-based progress. Depending on your chosen stream, you may engage with activities aligned to contemporary cybersecurity practice, such as Capture The Flag-style problem solving, ethical hacking, digital forensics, or research-led investigation.
learningOutcomes: Analyse the security, organisational, and ethical requirements of a cybersecurity challenge within a complex socio-technical context. (B.1)
Design innovative, feasible and evidence-based cybersecurity solutions using structured technical and research methodologies. (C.1)
Apply appropriate cybersecurity tools and methodologies to investigate threats, evaluate system behaviour, implement defences, and deliver reproducible technical outcomes. (D.1)
Communicate cybersecurity processes, evidence and findings professionally, and refine work through critique, collaboration and peer engagement. (E.1)
Reflect critically on cybersecurity learning, technical decision-making and project development to improve professional practice and independent capability. (F.1)

43008.title: Reinforcement Learning
43008.description: This subject introduces you to reinforcement learning, the study of how machines learn from interactions with their environment. A subset of machine learning, it's essential for automated decision-making and AI, teaching programs to predict and act optimally through experience. You'll explore its applications in control systems, gaming, and inventory management. The subject covers both theory and practice, including Markov Decision Processes, classic and modern algorithms, and hands-on agent training using cutting-edge software tools. By the end, you'll understand value functions, explore exploration versus exploitation, and be able to deploy an AI system to solve real-world problems in your final project.
learningOutcomes: Design Reinforcement Learning algorithms to solve classic reinforcement learning problems. (C.1)
Apply state-of-the-art and customized Reinforcement Learning Algorithms to solve real-world problem. (D.1)
Communicate efficiently in a team, in both oral and written forms. (E.1)

43010.title: Cyber Threat Intelligence and Incident Response
43010.description:
Cyber threat intelligence involves gathering and analysing information about potential cyber threats and risks from a range of sources. It helps organisations understand the tactics used by malicious actors and enables them to proactively identify and mitigate cyber threats.

Incident response is a structured process that empowers organisations to identify and address cybersecurity incidents and encompasses various stages, including preparing, preventing, detecting, analysing, containing, eliminating, and recovering from cyber-attacks or security breaches. It involves preparing for potential incidents, promptly detecting incidents and assessing the impact of the incidents, containing and eliminating the threat, recovering systems and data, and learning from the experience to enhance future incident response capabilities.

This subject brings these two concepts together by equipping students with the skills and knowledge to both prepare for, and respond to, cyber-attacks in organisational contexts. Through industry case studies and practical exercises, students will develop their abilities to proactively defend against cyber threats, mitigate risks, and strategically respond to incidents.
learningOutcomes: Identify social, environmental, economic and ethical aspects of Security Operations (SecOps). (B.1)
Design a strategy for cyber threat intelligence and incident response that reflects contemporary research and industry practice. (C.1)
Analyse cyber threat intelligence from various sources to detect and respond to contemporary cyber incidents. (D.1)
Demonstrate the ability to respond appropriately to simulated cybersecurity incidents in a security operations (SecOps) context. (D.1)
43010.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have sound knowledge of computer networking; knowledge of internet security vulnerabilities and defences at the network and application level; awareness of security operations (SecOps) concepts.

43011.title: Industrial Control System Security
43011.description: This professional subject equips you with skills to protect critical infrastructures, like Industrial Control Systems (ICS) and Operational Technology (OT), from cyber threats. You will learn to identify vulnerabilities, assess risks, and implement security measures, including secure architectures and access controls. Your learning will be practical, involving lab exercises and real-world case studies, enabling you to defend against cyber-attacks on essential critical infrastructure systems.
learningOutcomes: Differentiate key concepts in Industrial Automation to apply standards architecture in industry. (D.1)
Apply various ICS security frameworks and standards to ensure security and to manage the industrial control system. (D.1)
Analyse cyber threats and attack vectors to identify the vulnerabilities of ICS controls and enhance security in different scenarios. (D.1)

43013.title: Intelligent Control Studio
43013.description: This studio subject focuses on aspects of advanced control engineering design for multivariable systems. This subject will provide you a rich and attractive practice-based learning environment to gain advanced control engineering skills, essential for managing complex, multivariable systems such as power grids and aircraft. You will become proficiency in sophisticated control techniques beyond classical methods, enhancing your ability to design and implement systems that handle nonlinear dynamics. Learning is hands-on, blending theory with practice as you progress from concept to product realisation. Through reflective design, teamwork, and deep learning, you will prepare for senior roles, mastering design, simulation, and practical validation of advanced control systems.
learningOutcomes: Mathematically model, simulate and analyse multivariable (not necessarily linear) systems for control purposes. (D.1)
Propose, design and validate advanced control strategies to create a multivariable autonomous control system conforming to given specifications. (C.1)
Identify model uncertainties and/or disturbances that can affect the control system performance in order to enhance robustness. (D.1)
Translate theoretical advanced control designs into control algorithms to achieve a practical implementation of the developed autonomous multivariable control system. (D.1)
43013.recommended: It is essential that students enrolled in this subject have completed previous study of simple control systems using transfer functions and state-variables is essential

43014.title: Applied Mechanics and Design B
43014.description: This subject explores the various failure modes in machine components and equips you with the skills to design and analyse frameworks and machines for multiple factors, including stiffness, strength, and fatigue life. You will learn to analyse loads, apply stress and strain principles, and select suitable materials and sizes to mitigate failure risks such as fatigue, fracture, and buckling. The subject also covers the application of relevant standards for safety assessment, the use of computational tools for design optimisation and simulation, and the conduction of experiments to confirm theoretical and simulated outcomes.
learningOutcomes: Design complex machine structural components for strength, durability, and life. (C.1)
Analyse machine structural components by applying advanced engineering mechanics and mechanics of materials concepts. (D.1)
Reference and apply relevant design standards to meet minimum safety and design requirements. (B.1)
Apply experimental and computational methods in conjunction with theoretical methods. (C.1)

43015.title: Thermofluids B
43015.description: This subject addresses the critical issue of engineered system failures and their consequences, guiding you through the analysis and design of machine components for robustness against various failure modes. You will learn to conduct load analysis using stress and strain principles, choose materials and dimensions to prevent fatigue, fracture, and buckling, and apply safety standards. Additionally, you'll integrate these concepts with computational tools for optimised design and simulations, and perform experiments to corroborate simulation and theory.
learningOutcomes: Assess the impact of efficiency and energy conservation in the engineering design process, including lifecycle costing. (B.1)
Apply the laws of thermodynamics to analyse engineering applications. (D.1)
Design practical engineering systems based on thermodynamic principles, according to Australian Standards. (C.1)

43017.title: Machines and Mechanisms B
43017.description: This subject will consolidate and apply the technical knowledge and skills acquired from your previous studies, with a focus on practical analysis and design of machine elements, machines and mechanisms. You will engage in tasks that require the application of the core principles of mechanical engineering, enhancing your technical proficiency in designing machines and mechanisms.
learningOutcomes: Analyse and design machines and mechanisms and their component parts. (D.1)
Refer to Standards relevant to the design and analysis of machines and mechanisms. (B.1)
Make decisions about the suitability of designs and recommend improvements. (C.1)

43018.title: Dynamic Systems and Control B
43018.description: Vibration and acoustics play a significant role in the behaviour, performance, design, life expectancy, and even failure, of mechanical and structural systems. Mechanical (and mechatronic) engineers design machines, with complex dynamic behaviour, which must be controlled for the reasons given and for meeting the appropriate design standards. In this subject you will be introduced to concepts and approaches to noise and vibration modelling, analysis, and measurement, including advanced approaches in rigid and flexible body modelling and analysis of mechanical systems as well as experimental techniques for the analysis and evaluation of existing systems. You will also be introduced to new concepts and approaches to control system design with modern control theories. Through in-class activities including laboratory and project work, you'll become proficient in the techniques of data acquisition, noise and vibration testing, measurement, signal processing and vibration and control engineering.
learningOutcomes: Model and analyse complex mechanical systems using concepts in dynamic modelling methods of multi-rigid body systems and flexible body systems. (D.1)
Develop and apply skills in instrumentation, measurement and signal processing through the vibration testing of physical, mechanical and structural dynamic systems. (D.1)
Critically review and analyse computational and theoretical results to verify their accuracy and applicability to problems in vibration and control. (D.1)
Resolve design challenges using vibration theory and experimental methods to meet the human health, safety, and wellbeing limits for noise and vibration as set by Australian Standards. (C.1)

43019.title: Design in Mechanical and Mechatronic Systems
43019.description: This studio challenges you to solve authentic real-world problems using engineered solutions, going beyond technical proficiency. You'll apply engineering design principles and methodologies to understand project requirements and drive your project to completion. The subject sharpens your ability to navigate the engineering design process, focusing on realistic interactions with teams, clients, and supervisors, as well as the exploration of needs, project development, and delivery. It also leverages the technical expertise you've cultivated throughout your course.
learningOutcomes: Develop well engineered solutions that solve genuine, real-world problems using design methodologies. (C.1)
Actively engage with stakeholders to analyse and evaluate project/client needs, constraints, priorities, risks, and the true need for an engineered solution. (B.1)
Actively shape the direction of an engineering project to achieve desired outcomes. (C.1)

43021.title: Advanced Biomedical Engineering Studio A
43021.description: In this advanced studio subject, you'll engage with cutting-edge biomedical engineering research through one of two project streams: Single Cell Sequencing in Cancer or Lateral Flow Assay. The first project equips you with bioinformatics skills to analyse cancer datasets using single-cell sequencing technology. The second offers hands-on experience in creating rapid diagnostic tests, similar to COVID-19 rapid antigen test, involving nanoparticle technology, assay fabrication, SolidWorks and MATLAB data analysis. By the end, you'll have honed project design and problem-solving abilities through both individual and team works, alongside knowledge and technical expertise in these emerging biomedical engineering fields.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate relevant scientific literature and apply insights to solve problems in biomedical projects (C.1)
Apply biomedical engineering design and data exploration techniques used in biomedical projects (D.1).
Apply data analytics techniques to problem solve and optimize outcomes for biomedical studio projects. (D.1)
Collaboratively communicate scientific findings consistent with research standards and industry practice (E.1)
Assess the proposed design solution for environmental, social and economic impacts. (B.1)

43022.title: Advanced Biomedical Engineering Studio B
43022.description: This pre-professional studio subject offers you an in-depth, hands-on experience in the development of innovative medical technologies. You will work in collaborative teams to solve real-world biomedical engineering problems through the design and development of both physical devices and software solutions. Projects may include the prototyping of Point-of-Care PCR diagnostic tools for pathogen detection, as well as the development of AI-driven applications for medical imaging and EEG signal classification. You will engage in 3D CAD design, additive manufacturing, system integration, and experimental testing, while also applying deep learning methods to address challenges in biomedical signal and image analysis. The subject emphasises the development of key pre-professional skills, including technical problem-solving, iterative design, stakeholder analysis, teamwork, and communication of complex technical concepts. By the end of the subject, you will have gained valuable experience in project execution and will be better prepared for professional roles in the biomedical device industry or further applied research.
learningOutcomes: Assess biomedical engineering design solutions such as diagnostic tools and artificial intelligence systems in relation to environmental, social, and economic impacts, incorporating stakeholder needs and regulatory constraints. (B.1)

Apply evidence-informed engineering design processes to refine biomedical solutions by integrating Computer-Aided Design hardware prototypes or Machine Learning software frameworks into project decisions. (C.1)

Evaluate biomedical engineering systems such as Nucleic Acid Amplification Devices or Clinical Imaging using appropriate technical methods, tools, and research evidence to ensure successful project implementation. (D.1)

Collaborate effectively within project teams to plan, manage, and communicate biomedical engineering work, producing industry-standard technical reports and presentations for both technical and non-technical audiences. (E.1)
Reflect on learning progress, team contributions, and professional conduct to identify strengths and future development needs as an emerging professional within the Medical Technology industry. (F.1)

43023.title: Emerging Topics in Artificial Intelligence
43023.description: This subject offers an introduction to current trends in artificial intelligence (AI), covering areas like autonomous machine learning, large language models, and natural language processing. You'll grasp key concepts, definitions, and algorithms, along with their real-world industry applications. Ideal for those keen on AI research or application development, you'll gain a broad understanding and deep expertise in a specific AI topic through a project mentored by UTS researchers. Your learning will be assessed through reflective exercises, technical implementations, research reports, and oral presentations.
learningOutcomes: Discuss the potential social/societal impacts of emerging AI technologies. (B.1)
Implement selected algorithms/demos/functions for applications. (D.1)
Communicate effectively in both oral and written forms. (E.1)
43023.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have experience with an integrated development environment such as Anaconda with Python.

43025.title: Introduction to Quantum Computing
43025.description:
This subject introduces quantum computation, a model of computation based on the physical laws of quantum mechanics. Quantum computers outperform traditional computers for a range of practical problems, and in many cases offer drastic advantages. In this subject, you will learn about the basic tools for understanding quantum information processing. You will apply this knowledge to study the key quantum protocols: teleportation, superdense coding, and simple quantum algorithms.

The subject covers key features of quantum theory which differentiate it from classical theory, including quantum entanglement and coherence.
learningOutcomes: Analyse quantum information protocols using the basic mathematical structure of quantum mechanics, including states, operations and measurements to validate performance claims. (D.1)
Design and create quantum circuits for quantum algorithms to run on quantum computers. (D.1)
Critically reflect and contrast the historical development of quantum and classical computation to differentiate computational capabilities. (D.1)
Effectively communicate quantum concepts to broad audiences. (E.1)

43026.title: Energy Economics, Optimisation and Policy
43026.description: This Pre-Professional subject equips you with critical skills for shaping the future energy sector, focusing on optimisation, energy efficiency, and policy to meet clean energy goals. You'll learn to assess energy economics, navigate electricity markets, and conduct techno-economic analyses. A focus on how to optimise energy use and drive sectors towards NetZero, fostering economic growth in a carbon-neutral economy are key outcomes for this subject.
learningOutcomes: Apply engineering requirements to optimising energy use and drive sectors towards a NetZero carbon economy in local and global contexts by engaging with stakeholders. (B.1)
Design optimisation techniques for energy projects to maximise techno-economic benefits. (C.1)
Apply models and optimisation techniques with the aid of state-of-the-art tools and technologies to enhance professional skills. (D.1)
Communicate implications of techno-economic aspects of sustainable energy solutions to broader communities. (E.1)

43029.title: Introduction to Humanitarian Engineering
43029.description:
Humanitarian engineering is the application of engineering skills and approaches to enable basic needs and contribute to social justice, with contexts ranging from community and technology development to emergency disaster response, both domestically and internationally. This subject equips you with skills transferable to all engineering fields, including stakeholder engagement, cross-cultural work, human-centred design, and environmental stewardship.

You'll build on prior experiences from the Engineers without Borders Challenge, learning about international development, effective humanitarian engineering practices, and key agencies in the field. The subject encourages personal reflection on the significance of humanitarian engineering for your development and allows you to delve into a topic of personal interest (such as a particular case study, approach, context, or how engineering relates to a particular Sustainable Development Goal) in more detail.

Interactive three-hour weekly workshops, complemented by online content, are central to the learning process, fostering collaboration and professional skill development. Canvas tools support both analog and digital collaboration, enhancing your learning experience. Industry guest speakers contribute real-world insights, and the workshop format provides ongoing formative feedback, crucial for your assessments and professional growth.
learningOutcomes: Apply the values and principles of humanitarian engineering in the evaluation of a case study, concept, or approach. (B.1)
Communicate research about humanitarian engineering to inform a multi-disciplinary audience. (E.1)
Reflect on the value of humanitarian engineering and, in particular, on perspectives on socio-technical thinking and co-design. (F.1)

Provide evidence of professionally relevant technical skills and knowledge that contribute to improved professional practice. (D.1)

43031.title: Python Programming for Data Processing
43031.description: This subject equips you with Python programming fundamentals, targeting data processing and visualisation. You'll learn Python programming concepts, data structures, visualisation methods, and how to develop programs in Jupyter notebooks. You will engage in practical case studies demonstrating the use of popular Python packages and libraries for data manipulation and visualisation.
learningOutcomes: Apply the fundamentals of the Python programming language. (D.1)
Apply common Python libraries for data processing and visualisation. (D.1)
Design custom Python programs to pre-process and visualise real-world datasets. (C.1)

43036.title: Natural Language Processing
43036.description: Natural Language Processing (NLP) develops AI algorithms and methods to enable machines to understand and interpret human languages. This subject provides a foundation in NLP technologies, explores advanced algorithms, and applies them to real-world problems. You'll gain both the knowledge to engage with NLP theories and the practical skills to craft NLP projects, bridging the gap between theoretical insights and hands-on application.
learningOutcomes: Identify NLP applications in business and social contexts. (B.1)
Design and implement solutions for real-world NLP problems. (C.1)
Explain the advantages and disadvantages of different NLP methods and algorithms and their applicability in different business situations. (D.1)
Interpret the results of an NLP project. (E.1)
Reflect on their own NLP skill development. (F.1)

43037.title: Network Servers
43037.description: This subject equips you with design principles and practical skills for deploying network servers using Windows and Linux operating systems. Your system administration techniques and skills will be developed through a well-designed combination of comprehensive laboratory exercises, focused mini-lectures, and design tasks.
learningOutcomes: Design basic network infrastructure and services. (C.1)
Demonstrate skills in deploying and administering Windows and Linux based network servers. (D.1)
Demonstrate the attitudes and record keeping methods required to be a system administrator. (E.1)

43038.title: Electronic Components and Fabrication
43038.description: This subject focuses on the hardware and components at the heart of the Internet of Things (IoT), with emphasis on miniaturisation and nanotechnology. You will delve into existing miniaturised technologies to understand their capabilities and constraints. This will enable you to design innovative IoT systems and anticipate technological breakthroughs. You will learn about various electronic and photonic components in miniaturised systems, the underlying semiconductor physics and technologies, and appreciate the fabrication and packaging of devices. By mastering the trade-offs between performance, quality, and reliability, you will be able to select appropriate component classes and approaches for creating miniaturised systems tailored to real-world problems.
learningOutcomes: Describe doping, junctions, diodes and transistors, and their fabrication in semiconductor technologies. (D.1)
Investigate the broad principles of sensing, transduction, and how sensors are realised and are fabricated in electronics and photonics. (D.1)
Deconstruct a microcomponent: fabrication, packaging and testing, to perform failure analysis in electronics products. (D.1)
Model a component and a small system, and identify the model limitations in the context of electronics performance. (C.1)
Identify the approach, type and specifications of components needed to design a specific IoT system, understanding packaging, reliability, supply chain and costs. (C.1)

43124.title: Renewable Energy Technology
43124.description: This subject equips you with a comprehensive understanding of renewable energy technologies, addressing the urgent need to shift from finite fossil fuels to sustainable alternatives. Initially, you'll learn the fundamentals of renewable energy, including their sources, energy flows, and principles, as well as the policies, opportunities, and challenges associated with their use. You'll then explore modern technologies and operational issues for solar, hydroelectric, ocean, geothermal, wind, and biological energy sources. Finally, through case studies, you'll apply theoretical and operational principles to explore the design and implementation of specific renewable energy projects in real-world contexts.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of the basic concepts, terminologies and key issues underpinning renewable energy technology. (D.1)
Evaluate and analyse technical advances of renewable energy technology based on understanding of the operational processes. (D.1)
Perform calculations on energy generation and consumption, design a renewable energy project and acquire proper technology in a given context. (D.1)
Undertake assessment and evaluation of renewable energy systems based on technical, environmental, economic and social criteria. (B.1)
Demonstrate competence in the recognition and application of alternative energy technology needed in environmental engineering practice. (D.1)

43801.title: Digital Engineering Fundamentals
43801.description: This subject introduces you to digital engineering, focusing on strategic asset information management and practical skills for digital delivery in building and civil infrastructure projects. You'll explore open data formats, metadata schemas, asset classification, data linking, and collaboration in a common data environment. The subject enhances your communication skills, both written and oral, in conveying digital engineering concepts. Through project-based learning and industry case studies, you'll understand the digital engineer's role and develop capabilities in data modelling workflows and information sharing. The subject comprises seven modules, blending workshops, computing labs, and online activities. Pre-class tasks on Canvas, including readings and videos, prepare you for in-depth discussions and computing labs where you'll practice digital engineering skills such as model interrogation and data exchange, essential for your assessments. These activities, supported by tutor-led small group sessions, are crucial for building your digital engineering proficiency.
learningOutcomes: Apply digital engineering concepts and principles to explore core enablers of digital engineering relative to data exchange using open data formats, applying metadata, and establishing common data environments. (D.1)
Discuss how the exchange of information between stakeholders and the providers and receivers of information is key to project success. (D.1)
Evaluate digital engineering standards, including technical requirements and tools, and how they are implemented in infrastructure projects. (D.1)
Analyse examples of collaborative digital engineering methods using case study data. (C.1)
Reflect on the digital engineer’s role in the asset lifecycle and strategic leadership responsibilities. (F.1)

48023.description: This subject teaches introductory-level Java programming and software design, with no assumed prior knowledge of programming. You will learn about object-oriented programming concepts, data flow, control flow, and basic data structures.

48024.title: Programming 2
48024.description: This subject teaches concepts, theories and technologies underlying the methods and techniques of OOP programming and GUI programming. You will learn through a combination of lectures, assignments, and practical labs designed to solve real-world problems using Java or Python. The subject will enable you to design, develop and evaluate software systems to meet predefined quality characteristics of functionality (suitability) and usability (understandability, learnability, operability, compliance). By gaining both theoretical understanding and practical skills, you will be equipped to apply all that you have learned to develop and implement the architecture of a business system in various domains.

Design a well-constructed OO solution from a specification. (C.1)
Demonstrate a working knowledge of lists. (D.1)
Use inheritance to improve the system design. (D.1)
Construct a GUI interface from a specification. (D.1)

48080.title: Introduction to Innovation
48080.description: This subject equips you with an understanding of innovation, commercialisation, technology life cycles, and change in engineering and technology. It prepares you for the commercial world by developing your understanding of different roles within an enterprise through a business planning framework. Covering strategy, marketing, operations, personnel, and finance, it offers a practical orientation with contemporary case studies to illustrate concept application. As you approach the end of your undergraduate studies, this knowledge will enable you to communicate effectively with various organisational functions.
learningOutcomes: Identify opportunities for innovation through analysis of current market or industry. (B.1)
Design a new product or service proposal to meet contemporary opportunities in market or industry. (C.1)
Use analysis techniques and business plan to assess viability of new product or service. (D.1)
Communicate with stakeholders on a new product or service using relevant documentation. (E.1)

48221.title: Engineering Computations
48221.description: The subject provides engineering students with the opportunity to acquire knowledge of numerical methods, programming, and engineering software and to apply this knowledge in engineering problem solving. Excel spreadsheeting and Matlab/Python programming is required to solve numerical problems in this subject with no prior knowledge of programming being assumed. There are opportunities to apply acquired skills through the assessment of project-based problem solving in the civil and mechanical engineering disciplines. Examples are chosen from within a broader engineering context and serve to reinforce material covered in other subjects in civil and mechanical engineering.
learningOutcomes: Design solutions for engineering projects using Excel spreadsheeting and Matlab programming. (C.1)
Apply computational and programming techniques to solve engineering problems. (D.1)
Collaboratively document contributions to engineering computations and analyse results for an engineering project (E.1)

48230.title: Introduction to Engineering Projects
48230.description:
This core subject exposes you to ideas regarding the scope of what engineering actually is, considerations regarding engineering in the Australian context, and the broad impacts engineering decisions have on people, community and the environment. Through authentic engineering experiences you will build your professional skills and knowledge, providing a solid foundation for your continuous professional development journey as a future engineer.

The subject is centred around completing the Engineers Without Borders Challenge for which you will work in a team to develop engineering solutions to local real-world challenges on behalf of a partner Australian Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Community Organisation. You will form a team with peers and working together in and outside class you will research and refine the problem and design considerations, ideate and prototype potential solutions that will work in the community context, and ultimately propose a fully developed design idea that would benefit the partner community.

In completing the challenge you will develop your professional interdisciplinary skills such as research skills, learn and apply the engineering design process, develop an understanding of and consider socio-technical issues, build your professional communications skills in engineering contexts, and learn to lead and participate in team processes.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate an awareness of Indigenous Australian cultural, historic, and contemporary contexts in order to inform work in a complex project. (A.1)
Identify user needs to inform the development of a design solution. (B. 1)
Apply a design thinking approach, using appropriate engineering techniques and tools, to develop a solution that meets user needs. (C.1)
Communicate a design solution clearly and concisely to stakeholders using appropriate format and presentation. (E.1)
Explain the collaboration and contributions of team planning, communication and problem-solving in developing a design solution. (E.1)

48260.title: Engineering Project Management
48260.description: In this subject you will learn about the most common frameworks, processes, techniques that are essential in managing engineering projects. It involves entire project lifecycle from project initiation to project closure. You will get to practice project management knowledge from an integrated perspective of scope, time and cost management. In the scope management component, topics including scope definition and control will be introduced. For the time management component, this subject includes the definition of project activities, estimating the duration and resources of activities, developing and controlling project schedule, as well as the planning of project resources. In the cost management component, you will learn about cost estimation and management and control of the project budget. Students work independently and in small groups on a range of assessment tasks.
learningOutcomes: Collaborate in engineering project teams to deliver stakeholder needs, a communication plan and project milestone deliverables. (E.1)
Apply project management concepts such as scope, assumptions, risk, milestones, cost, resources, and work breakdown structures to manage and review a small engineering project. (D.1)
Reflect on project management experience to conduct a post-project evaluation. (F.1)

48310.title: Introduction to Civil and Environmental Engineering
48310.description: This subject imparts a foundational understanding of Civil and Environmental Engineering (CEE), crucial for creating and maintaining infrastructure in both urban and rural areas. You'll develop core skills in design, solution presentation, report writing, and technical drawing, contextualised through diverse civil infrastructure projects. These projects will also require you to consider social, economic, and environmental factors. The subject lays the groundwork for advanced education in design, construction, operation, and maintenance of civil infrastructure and fosters the individual and collaborative skills needed for CEE project analysis and execution.
learningOutcomes: Identify and apply the fundamentals of civil and environmental engineering processes and terminologies. (D.1)
Develop engineering drawings using drafting techniques and CAD software, and define project plans and management processes using Microsoft-Project software. (D.1)
Acknowledge and comprehend current standards in professional practice associated with the design and construction of civil engineering infrastructure. (B.1)
Apply appropriate numerical and analytical procedures in the design of civil and environmental structures and infrastructure. (C.1)
Work and communicate professionally in a group environment and to reflect upon their performance to improve teams and themselves. (E.1, F.1)

48320.title: Surveying
48320.description: This subject equips students with essential surveying skills, both theoretical and practical, including the use of levels and theodolites. You'll learn to perform calculations, reduce observations, and understand potential errors and their mitigation associated with the equipment. This foundational subject covers accurate distance measurement with tapes and introduces electronic distance measuring tools. You'll conduct simple traverse and perform associated calculations for engineering applications of surveying and engage with the stadia method in practical exercises. The plotting and application of contour plans for road design, as well as vertical and horizontal alignments, are also introduced. Additionally, you'll gain a basic understanding of Geographic Information Systems (GIS), including its components and spatial data analysis. Modern surveying developments and equipment are discussed, with a strong emphasis on professional surveying and engineering practices throughout the subject.
learningOutcomes: Identify and apply the theory and practice of basic surveying skills. (D.1)
Be aware of the use of basic surveying equipment such as levels and theodolites, and perform the calculations and reductions of observations associated with such equipment. (D.1)
Assess the likely errors that may occur during observations, and of methods to eliminate or minimise such errors. (D.1)
Plotting and use contour plans, perform the preliminary design of vertical and horizontal alignments and volume calculations in road design. (C.1)
Recognise modern developments in surveying and develop introductory Geographic Information System (GIS) skills. (B.1)

48321.title: Engineering Mechanics
48321.description: This subject helps students grasp the fundamental concepts of static equilibrium, crucial for the analysis and design of engineered structures. You'll learn to analyse simple, statically determinate beams and trusses under different loads and supports. By the end of the subject, you'll be adept at applying static equilibrium conditions to analyse structures and appreciate civil engineering design. These principles underpin further studies in structural analysis and design and introduce you to dynamics in civil engineering, including fluid mechanics, hydraulics, and road design.
learningOutcomes: Apply the concept of equilibrium to systems which can be modelled as particles in 2D, and to rigid bodies in 2D. (D.1)
Simplify and clarify mechanics problems using free body diagrams. (D.1)
Analyse simple statically determinate structures such as beams, pin-jointed trusses and pin-jointed frames subject to various loadings and support conditions. (D.1)

Determine internal actions in statically determinate structures and draw internal action diagrams - Axial Force (AFD), Shear Force (SFD) and Bending Moment Diagrams (BMD) which are all important for designing structural members such as beams and columns. (D.1)
Determine simple dynamic variables and solve simple dynamic problems involving kinematics, energy and momentum. (D.1)

48330.title: Soil Behaviour
48330.description: This subject provides a comprehensive introduction to geosciences and a detailed understanding of soil as an engineering material, culminating in studies of soil settlement and shear strength. Through practical geology and soil laboratory sessions, you'll gain hands-on experience and insights into soil behaviour from a civil/geotechnical engineering perspective. By the end of the subject, you'll be conversant with earth surface processes, able to communicate with geotechnical professionals, comprehend soil behaviour, recognise soil's environmental impact, and solve soil-related problems, particularly those involving water flow and settlement. This foundation prepares you for advanced geotechnical studies and self-learning.
learningOutcomes: Determine and interpret the natural processes occurring on the surface of the earth for civil engineering design and construction applications. (D.1)
Apply fundamental knowledge of the behaviour of soil as an engineering material in Civil Engineering Projects. (D.1)
Identify and evaluate those aspects of soil behaviour which have a significant environmental impact on civil engineer projects. (D.1)
Analyse and solve a range of soil-related problems, especially those involving water flow and soil settlement. (D.1)

args.text: Admission into MAJ03513 Civil Engineering major

48331.title: Mechanics of Solids
48331.description: This foundational subject aims to deepen your understanding of the behaviour of structural components in engineered structures and machines. You'll develop the ability to analyse these components under various loads and supports using equilibrium principles and material constitutional relationships. The subject covers a range of topics including beam pure bending, shear stresses, composite beams, beam deflection, column buckling, torsion in shafts and sections, stress transformation, inelastic bending, and combined stresses. You'll also learn about the product of inertia, principal axes and principal moments of inertia, unsymmetric bending, and the concept of the shear centre. This knowledge is essential for designing and analysing structural and machine components effectively.
learningOutcomes: Apply engineering design methodologies to design simple structural members. (C.1)
Demonstrate knowledge of structural behaviour to solve practical structural and mechanical engineering problems (D.1)
Analyse the behaviour of structural and machine components subjected to various loadings and support conditions. (D.1)
Collaborate in a team to produce a technical engineering report for structures. (E.1)
48331.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject review the content covered in the pre-requisites - 48321 Engineering Mechanics and 48620 Fundamentals of Mechanical Engineering - before commencing the subject.

48340.title: Construction
48340.description: This subject introduces you to the construction industry, focusing on the technical, managerial, and collaborative skills essential for professionals in the field. You'll explore innovative management theories, concepts, and tools, and critically analyse and solve construction management issues. The subject also fosters teamwork skills crucial for the collaborative execution of construction projects.
learningOutcomes: Identify the relationships among theories, conceptualizations, and tools for effectively managing construction. (D.1)
Critically analyse management problems in construction that affect projects performance. (D.1)
Apply concepts, methods, and/or tools learnt from management theories to solve problems in construction projects. (D.1)
Communicate and work collaboratively for the successful planning of construction projects. (E.1)

48349.title: Structural Analysis
48349.description: This subject teaches you to apply classical structural theory to analyse load-bearing structures and their components. You'll learn to assess the response of linear elastic structures to mechanical loads and environmental effects, including temperature changes and foundation settlements. Additionally, you'll learn to predict structural behaviour, determine deformed shapes, support reactions, and internal force distributions. These concepts are foundational for advanced subjects in structural design, including Concrete Design and Steel and Timber Design.
learningOutcomes: Analyse statically determinate load bearing structural frames and trusses by computing support reactions and the internal forces (and moments). (D.1)
Draw internal action diagrams showing the distribution of axial forces, shear forces and bending moments in the structure. (D.1)

Determine elastic deformations in structures subjected to a range of applied actions including mechanical loads, temperature changes, foundation settlements and construction / manufacturing imperfections. (D.1)
Analyse statically indeterminate structures using the Force Method and the Moment Distribution Method. (D.1)
Qualitatively derive support reactions, deformed shape and internal action diagrams of a structure through diagrammatic reasoning and consideration of compatibility and equilibrium conditions. (D.1)

args.text: Admission into C11324 Graduate Certificate in Professional Practice
Admission into C11325 Graduate Certificate in Technology

48350.title: Environmental and Sanitation Engineering
48350.description: This subject equips civil engineering students with key environmental concepts and the impacts of engineering activities on the environment. It bridges academic knowledge with real-world challenges in planning and executing civil engineering projects, emphasising the interplay between engineering, the environment, and society. You'll develop awareness of environmental issues, understand the effects of construction on natural systems, and learn strategies to reduce air, water, soil, and noise pollution. The subject also covers water pollution control design. You'll gain knowledge and critical skills for wastewater treatment, environmental management, and resource protection, enhancing your ability to create economically viable and environmentally sustainable structures.
learningOutcomes: Acquire an awareness of environmental issues relevant to civil engineering-related activities. (B.1)
Reinforce the implications of certain processes such as construction within a natural system. (B.1)
Demonstrate familiarity with both preventive and management strategies to combat water, soil, air and noise pollution. (D.1)
Identify concepts of water pollution control mechanisms and their impact on design. (C.1)

48352.title: Construction Materials
48352.description: In this subject, you will learn about the engineering properties of construction materials and how to predict their behaviour in practical applications. This includes examining the composition of steel and concrete, with detailed analysis of the properties of various components, including cement, aggregates, and admixtures. You will gather experimental data using Australian Standard test methods to understand material properties and behaviours. This knowledge is then applied to design materials that meet specifications, sustainability, and service life criteria, considering environmental effects and failure modes. You will develop professional problem-solving and design skills, enabling you to select suitable materials for prescriptive and performance-based requirements and to justify your choices. The subject will also enhance your analytical and reflective skills for construction material analysis, design, and development.
learningOutcomes: Identify and analyse factors contributing to the properties of construction materials in structural and civil engineering design. (D.1)

Predict the behaviour of construction materials and synthesise appropriate solutions for selecting materials that address specification, sustainable environment and service life criteria, and apply Australian Standard test methods for the testing of construction materials. (C.1)

Reflect on the lifecycle of a segment of a construction project to develop a construction materials specification that documents solutions for prescriptive and performance-based requirements to an engineering team. (E.1)

48353.title: Concrete Design
48353.description: This subject advances your understanding of reinforced concrete (RC) and prestressed concrete (PSC) structures, essential for civil engineers in Australia. Building on prior knowledge of statics, solid mechanics, and structural analysis, you'll learn about the design and behaviour of RC beams, slabs, and columns, as well as PSC beams, focusing on both serviceability and strength. The subject introduces the Limit State Design philosophy of AS3600-2018 and material properties of concrete, steel reinforcement, and prestressing steel. You'll study both uncracked and cracked beam cross-section analysis, RC beam design for serviceability, bending, and shear, and explore ductility in various beam types. The subject also covers the analysis and design of one-way and two-way slabs, columns, reinforcement detailing, and an introduction to PSC beam design, including history, section analysis, load-balancing, and design for bending in determinate structures.
learningOutcomes: Discuss the behaviour and design of RC beams, slabs, columns and PSC beams, for both serviceability and strength. (D.1)
Apply the Limit State Design philosophy of Australian Standards AS3600-2018 for structural design. (C.1)
Discuss the material properties of concrete, reinforcement and prestressing steel. (D.1)
Discuss the behaviour of RC flexural members, for serviceability and for strength at ultimate, RC beams, slabs & columns to AS3600-2018 for strength at ultimate. (D.1)
Apply AS3600-2018 to analysis, design and detailing of PSC flexural members for serviceability and strength. (C.1)

args.text: Admission into MAJ03513 Civil Engineering major

48360.title: Geotechnical Engineering
48360.description: This subject enhances your technical competence in analysing soil masses and structures interacting with soil, such as footings, piles, retaining walls, and slopes. You will learn to understand soil failure, select appropriate analysis methods, recognise limitations, validate solutions, and contribute to design teams. The subject encourages engagement with literature and application of advanced analysis methods, alongside fieldwork for subsurface investigations. Key topics include geotechnical design principles, site investigation techniques, shallow and deep foundation design, earth pressure theories, retaining structure analysis, slope stability assessment, and soil improvement strategies. You'll gain the skills to critically evaluate geotechnical problems, apply engineering judgment, and understand the role of codes in design.
learningOutcomes: Understand the concept of soil failure and its consequences, and then and apply this understanding to the analysis of soil masses. (C.1)
Critically appraise a problem to decide which analysis should be used. (C.1)
Identify the limitations of design approaches and carry out appropriate solution validation. (D.1)
Apply appropriate numerical and analytical procedures in design of geotechnical engineering structures. (D.1)

48362.title: Hydraulics and Hydrology
48362.description: This subject provides you with a foundation in predicting water quantity (hydrology) and its movement (hydraulics), equipping you with the scientific principles and practical skills to tackle integrated hydraulic and hydrologic issues. Building on fluid mechanics knowledge, the subject introduces hydrology and essential design skills in water engineering. You'll explore core concepts relevant to open channel hydraulics, surface water hydrology, and design flood estimation, enabling you to apply these methods to a variety of water-related problems.
learningOutcomes: Explain the distribution and movement of the waters of the earth in the atmosphere, on the surface of the land, and in groundwater systems. (D.1)
Apply hydraulic and hydrologic methods and models to engineering problems in an integrated way. (C.1)
Select between alternative predictions of hydraulic and hydrologic phenomena using model-based designs. (D.1)

48366.title: Steel and Timber Design Studio
48366.description:
This Pre-Professional design studio introduces you to practical techniques in design of steel and timber structures. The emphasis is on analysis and design of structural members and connections of steel and timber structures, computer-aided structural design and design optimisation techniques, and producing construction sketches for the main structural components of buildings. This subject is based on authentic professional projects relevant to the building industry that you may wish to enter, providing material for a portfolio after graduation. You will work with a wide range of data inputs to apply innovative and thoughtful opportunities to learn critical review of engineering documents/projects and disciplinary research skills.

This Steel and Timber Design Studio enables you to demonstrate achievement of professional skills by working on real-world projects. Facilitated by a mixture of studio facilitators, academic experts, and industry partners, you will work in teams to define problems, and identify, develop, and implement solutions. Using a design-thinking framework and systems thinking, you will regularly engage in pitching and critiquing work among peers. In the assessments, you are required to demonstrate your achievement of each of the subject learning objectives using a collection of artefacts and reflections that meet the standard performance criteria for each grade.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate a range of stakeholder’s needs and translate to specifications for building design. (B.1)
Design building to specifications of stakeholders using computer-aided model and analysis. (C.1)
Analyse loads/load combinations as per the relevant Australian standards for structural members. (D.1)
Create professional design report and present construction sketches in accordance with the economic design solution. (E.1)
Critically reflect on structural engineering design skills to identify areas for future skills development. (F.1)

48370.title: Road and Transport Engineering
48370.description: This introductory subject explores transport engineering within civil and environmental engineering, emphasising sustainable design and planning. It encompasses transport planning, focusing on public transport systems analysis, design, and evaluation. In addition, you’ll learn the basics of traffic engineering, where you will develop a '4-step transport model' to assess regional travel demands, crucial for infrastructure feasibility and design. You'll also grasp traffic flow theory fundamentals, enabling you to evaluate transport capacity and infrastructure. Practical case studies, including local area traffic management schemes, illustrate applications of theory, equipping you with relevant assessment tools and skills to be a transport professional.
learningOutcomes: Analyse and evaluate the relationships between active, public and private transport users, different forms of transport infrastructure, vehicles and different transport modes in planning for a sustainable transport system. (B.1)
Apply the basic terminology, empirical data analysis and modelling concepts of transport planning and traffic engineering practice to effectively manage transport systems. (D.1)
Examine the interaction between land-use development, transport infrastructure supply and demand as well as overall traffic operations to develop transport management plans for the community. (C.1)

args.text: Admission into C11324 Graduate Certificate in Professional Practice
Admission into C11325 Graduate Certificate in Technology
Admission into MAJ03513 Civil Engineering major

48430.title: Fundamentals of C Programming
48430.description: In this subject, you will focus on the C programming language and will learn how to collect, process, and store data. You will explore essential programming concepts like conditional statements, loops, functions, arrays, file handling, data structures, and managing memory with pointers. You will also learn how to compile C code, link files, and run your programs using the GNU toolchain. You will experience the full development cycle just like an embedded/low-level system programmer, from analysing complex problems to designing, coding, debugging, and testing your solutions in C. This hands-on approach ensures you gain practical skills and confidence in programming.
learningOutcomes: Design, develop and test programs in C programming language to solve problems related to collecting, processing and storing data. (C.1)
Identify and explain the use and workings of programming tools (such as compilers, linkers and debuggers), standard libraries and operating system functions to support program execution. (D.1)
Demonstrate the understanding and the ability to follow professional programming practices to align with industry expectations. (D.1)
Communicate effectively and collaborate as a team member to solve complex problems using C programming language. (E.1)

48433.title: Software Architecture
48433.description: This subject covers essential concepts, methodologies, and practical skills for designing, developing, and assessing software architectures. You will gain hands-on experience with architectural tools, techniques, and real-world scenarios. This subject prepares you to tackle complex software architecture challenges and make informed architectural decisions in your professional career. You will apply the industry practices to architect a business system, ensuring it aligns with professional standards.
learningOutcomes: Describe the factors that affect the architectural context and requirements, including stakeholders and their interests, architectural qualities, business requirements and usage scenarios. (B.1)
Develop and refine multiple views of a software system architecture, based on the conceptual, execution and implementation architecture. (D.1)
Understand the key issues in choosing and implementing architectural patterns, including performance, testing, security, usability, maintainability and reliability qualities. (D.1)
Reason about alternative architectural designs to satisfy a system's quality attributes. (C.1)
Develop a complete software architecture for a proposed solution to a realistic industry problem. (C.1)
48433.recommended:
It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge of object-oriented design and unified modelling language (UML) – this can be demonstrated through completion of any of the prerequisite subjects or the Foundations of Programming: Object-Oriented Design course available on lynda.com through the UTS: Library.

A quiz is provided to check mastery of the expected prerequisite knowledge. Students are advised to attempt this quiz in the first few weeks of the session.

48434.title: Introductory Embedded Systems
48434.description: This subject covers the essentials of embedded systems, including microcontroller architectures, fundamental microcontroller components, such as IO, timer, serial communications, embedded system design and analysis techniques, and embedded programming. You will learn fundamental knowledge and first principles, allowing you to go much further beyond the introductory level. You'll also gain practical skills through extensive hands-on lab exercises and tasks, as well as group projects, where you learn and experience designing, programming, debugging, testing and pitching your embedded systems. A range of assessments are available for examining your learning performance, including quizzes, labs, projects, and exams.
learningOutcomes: Design, write and test a variety of software modules found in modern embedded systems, such as: hardware abstraction layers; data structures; and interrupt service routines. (C.1)
Design, write and test an embedded application that is modular, hierarchical, responsive to real-time requirements, and tightly constrained by time, size and cost. (C.1)
Utilise a variety of software tools to write, execute and test embedded software applications. (D.1)
Test software performance in an embedded system by selecting and using appropriate laboratory equipment. (D.1)
Research and evaluate knowledge from many sources. (D.1)

args.text: Admission into MAJ03539 54cp Telecommunications and Electronics (MPE)

48434.recommended: It is essential that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge of the C language and digital systems.

48436.title: Digital Forensics
48436.description: In this practice-based subject, you will engage in laboratory-based learning to determine if a crime has been committed through the acquisition, analysis, and reporting of digital evidence. Your studies will focus on forensic analysis of network data, including the recovery of website visitation evidence relevant for court cases, alongside scrutinising digital storage devices to identify and retrieve critical data. You will also delve into the examination of operating systems to unearth hidden data, perform detailed analysis of metadata to gain deeper insights, and apply rigorous forensic principles to produce sound and defensible reports. Through these hands-on activities, you will develop a comprehensive understanding of digital forensics and its applications in real-world scenarios.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate theories of digital forensics. (D.1)
Understand the structure of forensic evidence. (D.1)
Implement forensically sound digital security practices in industry. (B.1, C.1)
Demonstrate competence in applying industry-standard forensic analysis techniques. (D.1)
48436.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject be confident with using Windows command line utilities such as netstat, nslookup, net and ipconfig; Linux command line tools such as grep, ls, uname and ps.

48441.title: Introductory Digital Systems
48441.description: This subject equips you with a solid understanding of digital systems and programmable electronic circuits and their applications in engineering. You'll master the hardware architecture of small computer systems and learn to write basic assembly code. Key topics include digital combinational and sequential circuits, state diagrams, microcontroller architecture, machine-level software integration, low-level programming, interrupts, I/O, and hardware interfacing design techniques.
learningOutcomes: Design combinational and sequential logic circuits. (C.1)
Design and implement programmable logic devices and related input/output components. (C.1)
Analyse digital logic circuits. (D.1)
Create assembly programs using appropriate software tools. (D.1)

args.text: Admission into MAJ03539 54cp Telecommunications and Electronics (MPE)

48441.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge of basic electrical engineering circuits and soldering skills.

48451.title: Embedded Systems Studio A
48451.description: This studio delves into the analysis, design, and implementation of an advanced computing node, focusing on digital hardware at the medium-scale system level. It builds upon introductory digital systems knowledge, employing studio-based learning that covers the digital design process, functional design, implementation technologies, advanced digital architectures, and memory and I/O systems within project work. Post completion, you'll be adept at planning, designing, and developing digital intellectual property (IP) using FPGAs and hardware description languages (HDLs) such as Verilog and VHDL.
learningOutcomes: Analyse, design and implement a programmable digital system based on a user requirement specification, and investigate advanced digital systems architectures. (C.1)
Demonstrate in-depth understanding of the analysis/design and implementation of advanced digital hardware at medium scale computer system building block level. (C.1)

Utilise computer-aided design, including the use of VHDL or Verilog specification, simulation and programmable FPGA implementation technologies, Register transfer level, Data path and control units. (D.1)
48451.recommended: It is essential that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge of basic digital systems and microprocessor/computer architecture.

48510.title: Introduction to Electrical and Electronic Engineering
48510.description: This subject introduces you to engineering, emphasising problem identification, solution proposal, and implementation. It acknowledges the contextual nature of engineering, its real-world impact, and its reliance on scientific principles. Electrical and electronic engineering, which underpins our modern world, is a key focus. Central to the subject is a real-world problem and its electronic solution, serving as a basis for exploring both technical and non-technical aspects of engineering. You'll learn fundamental electrical concepts such as voltage, current, resistance, and power, alongside basic circuit analysis for DC and AC circuits, and the roles of capacitors and inductors. Practical skills are prioritised, with labs dedicated to circuit construction, testing, and troubleshooting, and using instruments like multimeters and oscilloscopes.
learningOutcomes: Solve simple sub-system design problems using fundamental principles of electronic systems. (C.1)
Apply circuit theory to the analysis and design of basic DC and AC electrical circuits. (D.1)
Recognise and correctly apply electric and magnetic field theory to simple applications. (D.1)
Design, construct, test and troubleshoot basic circuits using basic laboratory test equipment and/or simulation. (C.1)

48520.title: Electronics and Circuits
48520.description: The aim of this subject is to acquaint you with basic electronic circuits, particularly those using operational amplifiers (op-amps), and their practical applications. By the end, you should be adept at analysing basic circuits and constructing and testing them in a lab setting. The subject strongly focuses on hands-on learning to build a robust understanding of analog electronic circuits with op-amps. Lab work, which forms a substantial part of the subject, enhances your skills in circuit construction, testing, and troubleshooting, and familiarises you with test instruments. Additionally, the subject demonstrates the relevance of practical electronic applications across various engineering and technical fields and their broader societal and commercial significance.
learningOutcomes: Perform the DC, AC and transient analyses of simple passive and active non-linear and linear circuits. (D.1)
Analyse and design basic electronic circuits with operational amplifiers (op-amps) as active elements. (C.1)
Identify various op-amp circuit topologies and their applications. (D.1)
Build, test and troubleshoot basic analogue passive circuits and electronic circuits containing op-amps using appropriate laboratory equipment and/ simulation tools. (D.1)
48520.recommended: Students enrolled in this subject are required to be completent in basic physics and single-variable calculus, as well as a basic understanding of electrical circuits and their analysis.

48521.title: Foundations of Electrical and Electronic Technology
48521.description: This subject delves into essential concepts and technologies in electrical and electronic engineering, covering the principles of engineering electromagnetics and their practical applications in various devices. From amplifiers and transformers to motors, antennas, and even wireless power transfer systems, you will explore how these technologies operate and interact. By mastering the design and analysis of low-frequency electromagnetic devices and high-frequency electronic components, you will be equipped to tackle challenges in power/energy systems, telecommunications, and electronics. Engaging laboratory sessions further reinforce your understanding through hands-on exercises in electrical safety, measurements, and design verification, preparing you with essential practical skills for real-world applications in the field.
learningOutcomes: Explain the key conceptual underpinnings and principles of electromagnetic phenomena, electrical machines, electronic amplifiers and their applications. (D.1)
Illustrate basic construction of semiconductor and magnetic devices. (D.1)

Predict and measure basic quantities in electric and magnetic circuits; and analyse and design them. Apply first-principles to the analysis of complex problems and in the use of simplifications and valid engineering assumptions for system design. (D.1)
Mathematically model a wide variety of electromagnetic and electronic phenomena. (D.1)
Apply technical terms and notation in classroom discussions and assessment tasks. (D.1)

Admission into MAJ03534 54cp Electrical Energy Systems (MPE)
Admission into MAJ03512 Biomedical Engineering Major

48521.recommended: It is essential that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge of basic physics and single-variable calculus, as well as basic electric circuit theory.

48530.title: Circuit Analysis and Design
48530.description: This subject deepens your understanding of the fundamental concepts of circuit analysis, with a particular focus on frequency domain techniques. You'll engage in both theoretical and computer-aided circuit design and validate circuit behaviour through lab experiments and simulation software. Building on your prior knowledge gained on basic circuit elements/devices and circuit analysis skills, the subject introduces theoretical models for signals and systems analysis. Key topics include sinusoidal steady-state analysis with phasor transformation, circuit modelling with differential equations and their solution via Laplace transforms, power in single and three-phase AC circuits, Transfer functions, Bode plots, system responses to various inputs, frequency selective circuits, Fourier series; and two-port network theory. You'll use tools like MATLAB for analytical modelling and simulation, with a strong emphasis on correlating experimental data with theoretical predictions during lab sessions.
learningOutcomes: Analyse linear circuits at an appropriate level of accuracy. (D.1)
Transform problems that arise in the analysis of circuits into simplified equivalent forms that facilitate easy solutions. (D.1)
Analyse circuits using advanced frequency-domain transformation techniques. (D.1)
Design circuits to achieve a required specification and confirm compliance experimentally. (C.1)
