54430.title: Creative Production: Sound and Moving Image
54430.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54430.description: In this subject organised around learning through creative exploration, you will gain basic skills in image and sound content creation, gathering, mixing, editing, and collaborative work practices. In classes that combine animation, music and sound, and media arts students, you will engage with relevant theoretical frameworks, sound and moving image histories, and the work of key practitioners in the field. You will get hands-on experience making sound and video projects in response to a thematic prompt. You will reflect on and gain a better understanding of your working preferences and how to be an effective collaborator. Framing your own creative output within the broader community of practice, you will learn how to apply established sound and image standards, producing short creative media projects that demonstrate a solid understanding of contemporary and historical practices.
learningOutcomes: Integrate historical and theoretical approaches to sound and moving image production.
Respond creatively to a project brief using sound and moving image tools.
Apply relevant technical requirements and professional standards to the production of audio and moving image projects.
Collaborate on a creative media arts project.
Reflect on your own creative collaboration profile and working preferences.

54431.title: Creative Production and Citizenship
54431.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54431.description: In this subject you will examine your identity as a creative citizen, assessing practices, policies and established protocols within your industry as you consider what it means to be an ethical producer of creative content. Topics covered include indigenous creative practitioners and practices, gender and cultural representation, collaboration, workplace culture, intellectual property, the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) and sustainable production. These topics will be applied to real-world situations using problem-solving exercises with an emphasis on creative play and collaboration.
learningOutcomes: Apply understanding of ethical communication and engagement practices when working with, and for, Indigenous Australian peoples in your field of creative practice.
Critically analyse and reflect on creative production decision-making and practice.
Collaborate effectively and respectfully in interdisciplinary teams to produce technically and aesthetically proficient creative media projects.
Apply critical perspectives on evolving technological, cultural and workplace environments to originate and produce innovative creative media projects.
Apply individual creative production skills in pursuit of a collaborative project.

54432.title: Creative Production and Entrepreneurship
54432.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54432.description: In this subject you will explore scenario-based models of working in a changing commercial creative field. By investigating contemporary transformations in creative industries and developing creative business proposals in collaboration with your fellow students, you will develop approaches to managing the demands of clients while staying fiscally solvent and producing creative work. Alongside this, you will develop skills in collaborative project management, the production of promotional materials, and refining your pitches in response to feedback.
learningOutcomes: Identify a range of business structures for creative enterprises and analyse strategic industry considerations in the growth of creative enterprises
Investigate key transformations within creative industries in Australia, including challenges and opportunities for Indigenous Australians
Work collaboratively to develop original and feasible creative projects
Reflect on and critically evaluate creative enterprises and business models
Research and communicate scholarly ideas in a clear manner accessible to a variety of academic and non-academic audiences and publics

54433.description: The Global Studio program is a short-term mobility program which provides opportunities for you to engage in overseas studies in a variety of global locations. In this subject, you will gain an international perspective, develop cross cultural literacy and interact with organisations and peers in other countries. Global Studio has several formats ranging from project-based work to field work and engagement with international organisations and institutions. This subject encourages you to immerse yourself within another country’s creative practice and educational culture; to develop institutional relationships; personal maturity around your creative practice; an appreciation and understanding of a specific country or region; and promotes international networking and intercultural engagement. The subject is ideal for people wanting to expand their understanding of creative practice within a contemporary international framework.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate a professional approach to cross-cultural collaboration in relation to creative practice
Develop and produce creative practice outcomes within a new context
Showcase understanding of international perspectives and cross-cultural literacy.

54440.title: Animation Studio: Drawing from Life
54440.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54440.description: In this subject, you will learn how to use observational drawing as a form of primary research. You will build practical skills while making drawings of real-world stimuli such as the human body, architecture, landscapes and natural forms. You will learn how to document rich lived experiences and cultivate a distinct approach to the creation of new visual ideas and creative concepts, building a foundation for animation and visual development.
learningOutcomes: Employ a range of primary research methods through first-hand experience, observation and drawing.
Participate in experimentation, risk taking and play with drawing materials and processes.
Explore and iterate in the process of capturing anatomy, morphology and architecture on paper.
Document, reproduce and reflect upon primary visual research using traditional and digital tools.

54441.title: Animation Studio: Character Foundations
54441.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54441.description: This subject explores animation pre-production with a focus on character design. You will learn to generate new character concepts and visual ideas through observation and creative play. These concepts are then taken through rigorous iterative development to become a new character design, a key building block of a new screen story. Through playful exercises, model making, material experimentation, and critical feedback you will refine your character design and learn best practice in producing finished art in industry ready character sheets.
learningOutcomes: Employ a range of primary and secondary research methods using field drawing, key texts, internet, social media and discussion.
Use iterative drawing with experimentation, risk taking and play to generate new and novel character concepts.
Explore materials, technical processes and technologies for visualising authentic characters, scenarios and environments.
Apply effective time management, communication and organisation for clearly defined project deliverables

54442.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54442.description: In this subject, you will develop fundamental animation skills by completing a variety of exercises that focus on the universally recognised, “12 principles of animation”. Relevant 2D digital software is used in this class.
learningOutcomes: Apply a professional approach to process and practice.
Develop performance skills for believable and engaging character animation.
Apply knowledge of body mechanics and locomotion
Employ key animation principles.

54444.description: This subject advances your knowledge and skills in the development of storytelling and performance in animation. Building on the foundations set in earlier subjects, you will produce an animatic, with a strong emphasis on character performance and coherence in visual storytelling.  In this subject as we continue to develop your 2D character animation skills we will begin to expand your use and understanding of film language. You will explore the art of contextual storytelling, timing, staging, and acting through the creation of an animatic. In this subject we will train you to use several industry-specific software platforms, thereby expanding your professional skillset.
learningOutcomes: Employ a range of primary visual research methods through first-hand experience, including drawing, note making, photography, film-making and sound recording.
Employ a range of secondary research methods through the use of the library, internet, social media and discussion
Generate and discuss animation ideas and explore a wide range of set problems, including both narrative and non-narrative sequences
Participate in experimentation; risk taking and play within production design and in animation
Explore and iterate in the process of creating original, authentic production designs and narrative scenarios

54445.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design

In this subject you will build upon the 12 principles of animation that were introduced in Introduction to 2D Animation, and further develop the fundamental animation skills required for creating compelling 3D character animations.
learningOutcomes: Employ software technical skills and processes in the production and delivery of animation files
Engage in iteration and experimentation through critical enquiry
Contribute and respond to critique and feedback
Apply key animation principles in relation to the 3D interface

54446.title: Animation Studio: Narrative Investigations
54446.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54446.description: This studio advances your critical and creative thinking, focusing on the critical analysis of animation as a powerful communication medium and the impact of design, character, and performance in communicating ideas. Building on the fundamental animation skills acquired in first year, you will advance and apply these skills to the synthesis of complex ideas in a narrative-driven project that takes you from conception and pre-production to full animation. In this subject you will develop your understanding of film language, design, narrative, music and sound in relation to animation production, whilst learning how to avoid cliché when developing original concepts and designs. Working with industry partners, you will gain collaborative skills, essential for professional practice, teamwork, idea exchange, negotiation, and effective communication with creative partners.
learningOutcomes: Negotiate individual responsibility and contribution for effective participation in collaborative creative productions.

Synthesise and articulate the connections between research, critical thinking and creative outcomes, exploring and documenting alternative design and story possibilities through multiple iterations and the use of semiotics and metaphor
Design and execute original and highly crafted narrative outcome for animation.
Understand ethical, respectful and professional creative practice
Reflect critically on your own creative and professional practice

54447.title: 3D Animation Asset Introduction
54447.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54447.description: This subject introduces you to 3D modelling and rigging. Through practical lab assignments, you will engage with a character design brief and construct fully functional, original, 3D character assets. By combining creativity with technical expertise, you will develop valuable skills for future animation projects.
learningOutcomes: Research and design an original character in response to a set brief
Demonstrate an understanding of the process of modelling and rigging a 3D character
Create a fully functioning character with all performance controls operational
Manage workload and time to meet deadline

54448.title: Animation Studio: Narrative Experimentation
54448.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54448.description: This studio equips you with the skills to create socially responsible and inclusive animation projects, fostering critical thinking and research and an understanding of animation in relation to new technologies, experimental, interactive and experiential animation projects. The subject explores professional practice for alternative animation platforms through the process of developing a professional proposal document for pitching to stakeholders and producing a prototype proof-of-concept animated work for public exhibition. You will learn to conceptualise, pitch and execute complex ideas, suitable for a global audience, and how to successfully position yourself and your creative concepts to external stakeholders. The subject prepares you to engage with creative partners, secure funding, and communicate effectively within a team.
learningOutcomes: Negotiate individual responsibility and contribution for effective participation in collaborative creative productions.
Articulate and position experimental creative concepts and practice in a real-world professional context
Design and execute experimental, experiential, immersive animation outcomes that utilise historical and contemporary technology in original and innovative ways
Understand the role of social responsibility, cultural exchange, and inclusion in conceptual public exhibition contexts

54449.title: Animation Industry Project
54449.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54449.description: In this subject, you will create original short works, engaging with animation industry partners to develop concepts and characters for various formats and audiences. You will gain field experience in project development, presentation, creative negotiation, reiteration, and assessing idea viability. This subject provides the opportunity to experience professional animation team dynamics, emphasising collaboration, deadline adherence, milestone recognition, and responding to critical feedback with openness and determination.
learningOutcomes: Negotiate individual responsibility, leadership, and contribution for effective participation in professional production practices.
Engage and critically reflect on wide-ranging primary and secondary research, exploring and documenting alternative possibilities and designs through multiple iterations.
Design and execute original and highly crafted animation outcomes for diverse audiences.
Generate creative and original written and visual story ideas for animation.
Communicate concepts and visual ideas clearly during presentations.

54450.title: 2D Animation Asset Development
54450.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54450.description: In this subject, you will develop more complex competencies developing 2D character assets for digital animation. Building upon traditional modes and techniques of production, you will engage in a series of in-depth, practical exercises that will build upon your 2D animation knowledge. A focus upon character performability is central to this subject, building on the twelve principles of animation learned in year one. While engaging with a character task brief informing third-year projects, you will be designing, testing and completing professional standard animation assets, balancing your creativity and innovation with proving your expanding technical competence as a 2D animation specialist.
learningOutcomes: Research, design and develop an original character asset in response to a set brief

Demonstrate an understanding of the process of creating an industry standard rigged 2D character for production which express and displays creative skill in lighting, colour, texture for cinematic composition
Demonstrate a capacity to absorb and apply reference and technical information to serve a creative outcome and go beyond software-led design and aesthetics
Apply professional approaches to asset revisioning, file structures and naming conventions.
Engage in advanced craft techniques while managing workload resources and production deadlines.

54451.title: 2D Animation Project A
54451.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54451.description:
In this subject and its partner, 2D Animation Project B, you will draw upon the knowledge and skills you have acquired throughout the course to plan, execute and deliver a short narrative animation centred upon 2D or hybrid animated characters and craft.

As animation is a highly collaborative practice, valuable time will be spent fostering and nourishing your production team and creative partnerships, paying particular attention to the innovative and technical capabilities of the group and the needs and demands of your evolving  project. At milestone stages throughout development, you will formally present your work-in-progress for critique.

Along the way, you will manage and track the evolution of your production in regular weekly review sessions, respond to notes, and utilise industry-standard production management systems. Higher-level craft techniques and toolsets, typically found in professional 2D animation pipelines, will be introduced.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate a willingness to explore story ideas and visual development for diverse audiences, through multiple iterations underpinned by thorough and authentic research.
Communicate nuanced and engaging story ideas visually, cinematically and poetically through Animation.
Practice and integrate high levels of animation craft, experimentation and originality.
Lead and take responsibility for delivering critical milestones in production, including finding solutions to creative and technical challenges that arise.
Share, reflect, discuss and respond to feedback continually with collaborators and mentors.

args.text: Admission into STM92011 30cp 2D Animation Stream

54452.title: 2D Animation Project B
54452.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54452.description:
In this subject and its pre-production focused partner, 2D Animation Project A, you will draw upon the knowledge and skills you have acquired throughout the course to plan, execute and deliver a short narrative animated film, driven by 2D or hybrid animated characters and craft.  

You will continue to work in your group, progressing the film project by completing shot-based production work, then refining and mastering in post-production. At milestone stages throughout development you will present your work in progress formally for critique. Along the way you will be required to manage and track the evolution of your production as a creative conversation, responding to review and notes, as you utilise industry-standard production management systems.   

All projects will be made with reference to an appropriate audience, and mode of distribution, such as online, festivals, broadcast or other hybrid models. Finally, you will develop promotional material and strategies for securing distribution and employment in the creative industries.
learningOutcomes: Execute a highly crafted animation film or related work at a professional production level.
Shape coherent and engaging narrative and non-narrative outcomes, communicating effectively with the intended audience.
Explore outcomes that go beyond mainstream ideas and aesthetics, show originality and challenge of contemporary practice.
Manage complex technical and organisational challenges within a strict time frame.
Recruit and nurture fruitful relationships with key creative partners.

54453.description: In this subject, you will be introduced to the technical complexities and creative possibilities of 3D character rigging for professional production. Develop competency in the process of creating a rigged 3D character for various uses in a production pipeline including operational performance controls.

54456.title: Indigenous Creative Practices
54456.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54456.description: In this subject you are introduced to the rich body of work by Indigenous creative practitioners across a variety of different modes and forms such as literature, music, film, television, animation, theatre and multi-disciplinary art. You develop deeper understandings of the ways that Indigenous creative practitioners speak back via their creative work to issues faced by Indigenous people and learn how to situate Indigenous creative work in the context of colonisation. Through the presentation of case studies in lectures and tutorials, you engage deeply with the creative aspects of Indigenous practice and learn about the ways that Indigenous creative practitioners navigate the creative industries. You develop skills in writing and discussing Indigenous creative work in a culturally sensitive way and have the opportunity to work on a creative response to topics covered in the subject.
learningOutcomes: Develop knowledge about Indigenous creative practices across a wide range of forms
Write about Indigenous creative practices in a culturally sensitive way
Situate Indigenous creative practices in the context of colonisation and contemporary Australian politics
Produce effective responses to topics related to Indigenous creative practices

54457.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54457.description: Graphic storytelling is the foundation of animation pre-production and a narrative skillset useful in a variety of different professional settings. In this subject you will try your hand at different forms of narrative illustration, such as comics, graphic novels, comics journalism and comics research. By engaging weekly with visual stories in various forms and formats you will develop literacy in the uses of visual narrative for applications such as entertainment, reportage, education and research, all while acquiring practical experience in illustration and graphic story development through exercises and technical tasks. By the end of this class all students will have had an opportunity to compose and receive feedback on their own short work of graphic literature.
learningOutcomes: Critically engage with visual narrative culture

54458.title: Performance Animation
54458.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54458.description: This subject aims to deepen your understanding of character acting for animation and build upon your skills in character performance. In this subject you will work on developing unique performance and movement languages with pre-rigged characters to prioritise the animation and performance process. In this subject you will study human behaviour and analyse how articulation, gesture, weight, and timing impact performance animation. After completing this subject, you will be ready to deliver a believable character performance that connects emotionally with your audience.
learningOutcomes: Assess the significance of gesture, posture and body language
Analyse and understand human behaviour and appeal in animation
Create a short character performance that showcases an advanced understanding of the body mechanics and a range of emotional stages.

54459.title: Drawing the Human Form
54459.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54459.description: In this subject, you will develop your visual vocabulary with a focus on becoming better acquainted with human anatomy and movement through drawing a live model. The various ways of how to depict a three-dimensional form in a two-dimensional medium are explored.  The subject supports an understanding of depth, space, weight and solidity, gesture, movement, line of action, weight, balance and force as well as teaching techniques in the use of line, tone and composition. The study of life drawing is excellent for strengthening your technical and observational skills, understanding movement and composition, and for seeing the human body in a new light.
learningOutcomes: Acquire a basic competency in anatomical drawing depicted in the human form
Convey competencies in the use of proportion, volume, weight, balance, line, tone and materials
Communicate a reflective perspective on personal process and progress through weekly blog
Represent skills development through the curation of a portfolio presentation

54462.description: This subject introduces you to the core principles of screenwriting. By reading and analysing contemporary screenplays, and engaging with relevant theory, you will gain an understanding of how common literary concepts have been adapted for the purpose of telling stories on screen. As you craft your own short screenplay, we will ask you to consider the ethical questions surrounding narrative ownership and who gets to tell what stories. Your understanding of screen story will deepen through practical exercises, enriched by feedback from tutors and peers, developing your skills as a cinematic storyteller.

Analyse and write about screen story in a scholarly way
Consider and apply ethical frameworks to screen story development

54463.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design

54467.description: In this capstone subject for Media Arts you will apply your accumulated knowledge and skills to plan, execute, and deliver a short media arts project. 54468.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54468.description: In this subject, you are introduced to the creative practices of microbudget screen production. Through historical and contemporary lenses, you will gain an understanding of the ways in which microbudget screen creators have pursued bold visions, critiqued industrial norms, and revitalised screen production. Following this example, you will explore the ethos and practices of microbudget production using fast, agile and flexible models, including for online and social media contexts. Throughout this subject you will be required to engage with innovative models of writing/producing, shooting and editing for a diverse range of platforms.

Collaboratively produce microbudget content that demonstrates technical proficiencies
Critically analyse microbudget practices and the resulting screen content projects

54469.title: Longform Screenwriting
54469.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54469.description: Writing a feature film or a television series is a fundamentally different exercise than writing a short screenplay; one that requires long-term thinking, depth in the chosen material, and strategies to ensure the writer emerges with a sustained and coherent narrative. In this subject you will apply screen story principles to the planning and creation of a longform work. Starting with a treatment or story bible, you will explore how to set up and develop a sustained story arc for a feature film or television series pilot, then write a section of it. Across the session you will share your work-in-progress in regularly scheduled table reads and use peer feedback to further your craft and ideas. By the end of the session, you will emerge with a partly written feature film or television pilot and a road map for completing it.
learningOutcomes: Devise, plan and partially execute an original longform screenplay.
Consider and apply ethical frameworks to screen story development.
Give and receive detailed feedback on a developing creative work.
Locate your creative practice in the context of Australian and International markets.

54470.title: Creative Media Critical Contexts
54470.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54470.description: This subject offers an introduction to the theoretical underpinnings, sector debates and broader contexts of media art. You will have the opportunity to examine the diverse forms and contexts of contemporary media art as you develop critical thinking skills in response to non-traditional media art works. You will explore the relationship between form, content, and context in media art and gain an understanding of the evolving curatorial and exhibition factors that impact the production of experimental media. You will apply critical frameworks to the evaluation and interpretation of contemporary works through field trips to view media art exhibitions, gaining a deeper understanding of professional artistic practices. Close analysis of current media art projects enables you to better discern the concerns and real-world issues at play in realising artistic concepts. You will then go on to develop strategies for applying innovative approaches and techniques developed by diverse media artists and curators to your own creative practice projects.
learningOutcomes: Explain key concepts and broader debates that are at play in contemporary media art and apply appropriate frameworks to the analysis of media arts projects.

Identify and integrate strategies for diverse audiences and global contexts.

54471.title: Real-time Animation and VFX
54471.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54471.description: In this subject, you will explore and apply the knowledge, skills and resources required to develop and execute real-time animation and visual effects projects. The term ‘real-time animation’ refers to the use of 3D game engines in the creation of animations for the screen and/or games. Apart from the film and television industry, animation and games, real-time animation tools and techniques are being applied in an increasingly diverse range of creative and other industries such as theatre and live events, installations, architecture and construction, digital fashion, data visualisation, manufacturing and health sciences and beyond. In this subject, you will use industry-standard real-time game engines and associated technologies and tools, including AI, to create animations and visual effects. You will develop original content alongside preexisting digital assets such as environments, props, and characters and apply processes such as modelling, rigging, blocking, layout, motion and facial capture, animation, and post-production.
learningOutcomes: Develop a solid understanding of real-time animation and VFX's core principles and workflows.

Gain proficiency in industry-standard tools and techniques for 3D modelling, texturing, rigging, animation, lighting, camera work, visual effects, and post-production, addressing technical and creative challenges throughout the production pipeline.
Explore the creative possibilities and technical challenges of building content for the digital environments.
Learn how to plan, stage, and composite scenes for optimal audiovisual storytelling and character performance.
Develop effective teamwork, problem-solving, critical thinking and communication skills in a collaborative production setting.

54472.title: Streaming Television
54472.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54472.description: Streaming Television examines the impact of digital streaming on creative practitioners and viewers. In this subject you will analyse how streaming has altered creative practice and evolved the audience’s relationship with a range of television formats and genres. You will also consider the challenges that Australian screen creatives face in telling local stories on global platforms. By connecting industrial and technological changes to storytelling, screen aesthetics, sound design, and everyday viewing practices, this subject will illuminate the profound shifts of the post-broadcast era.
learningOutcomes: Identify and explain key scholarly frameworks and concepts in the study of screen production and creative industries.
Conduct independent industry research in relation to television streaming industries.
Develop a critical understanding of the creative approaches and storytelling elements of television texts.
Write clearly and cogently to effectively communicate scholarly ideas, arguments, and research.
Use audio-visual techniques to effectively communicate scholarly analyses and arguments.

54473.title: Previsualisation for Animation and VFX
54473.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54473.description: This subject is focused upon the craft of digital previsualisation for the hybrid animation and VFX industries. Previsualisation, often abbreviated as 'previz', is an increasingly essential stage in the production of animation and visual effects and involves the creation of simplified digital prototypes moving as planned within a simulated set to accurately explore and asses what might be possible before production begins. Previsualisation is increasingly employed to explore narrative lensing possibilities, environmental construction requirements, and practical safety or technical issues that may need to be tested before the more costly phase of actual production commences.
learningOutcomes: Create an effective previsualisation sequence that informs the next stage of production.
Accuracy and attention to detail across all processes.
Originality and clarity of visual storytelling
Analyse the creative and financial effectiveness of the processes deployed.
Evaluate and communicate the strengths and weaknesses of the result.

54474.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design

Through the application of professional practices of storyboard process, you will visualise a script and explore sequential narrative communication, revision and editorial refinement through iteration and experimentation to create a pre-production storyboard and animatic with sound.
learningOutcomes: Understand Cinema Language
Develop the ability to visually communicate narrative structure
Explore iteration and editorial process
Engage in professional standards and practice

54480.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54480.description: This subject provides you with an introduction to the creative concepts and production techniques involved in professional audio and music production. Identify, develop, and implement genre specific techniques in mixing and recording multi-track music
Evaluate the aesthetic and technical consideration in audio and music mastering
Reflect on and communicate effectively about the concepts and techniques involved in audio and music production

54483.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54483.description: This subject provides you with creative concepts and production techniques involved in professional sound design as practiced in animation, film, television, and radio. Evaluate the creative, technical and collaborative considerations for animation, film, and TV

54484.title: Music Business: 450 Records
54484.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54484.description: In this subject, you will explore the business models and professional practices that have developed in the music and sound sector. You will take part in a simulation project that requires you to apply industry knowledge and professional skills to the running of an independent digital record label. You and your fellow students will lead and operate a record label as if it were an ongoing business. You will select a role to fulfil from a range of relevant roles including label management, event management, digital distribution, marketing and design, merchandising, music composition, music performance and music production. Depending on the specific role, you will participate in teams to achieve the objective of a public label launch event in the final weeks of the subject and launching new music on digital platforms. You will be exposed to guest lectures from industry professionals and consequently you will learn how the music industry adapts to change. You will learn how to deliver a complex project in a timely manner and how to manage professional relationships with your student colleagues. Authentic learning and assessment strategies arise from the project and are aligned with industry documentation such as proposals, career portfolios and grant acquittal reports.
learningOutcomes: Apply music copyright knowledge in a commercial context
Manage professional relationships
Plan and deliver professional projects
Develop and deliver professional portfolio documentation
Explain and reflect on professional practice with reference to concepts from the literature

54485.title: Live and Production Sound
54485.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54485.description:
In this subject you acquire the knowledge and skills to operate as an audio professional in the fields of live and production sound. You gain an understanding of the theories, principles, technologies and procedures associated with current production workflows in sound reinforcement and location sound recording.

Working in small teams you will progress from simulated project scenarios to real-world work environments undertaking live sound or location recording duties on a range of projects.

On successful completion of the subject you will not only be capable as a well-informed and useful production crew member, but also able to adapt to the rapid transformations impacting the live and media production sectors.
learningOutcomes: Plan and execute small live and production sound projects
Demonstrate a capacity to learn and adapt to new production technologies
Work systematically and collaboratively under time constraints
Reflect on learning and professional experience

requisite.scope: spk(s): STM92016 - 54cp Music and Sound Design Stream

54486.title: Screen Soundtrack Production
54486.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54486.description: In this subject, you will explore screen soundtrack production from a theoretical and practical perspective. In particular, you will examine how the soundtrack develops narrative, character, genre, and affect for screen, with a particular emphasis on different screen media forms. You will learn about film and sound theory, build skills in working with online library music, and engage with cultural protocols around licencing and copyright. You will also form part of a collaborative effort between students across music and animation in creating original, short animation works from scratch, where your sound design and music composition skills will be put to real-world use according to industry standards. In this way, you will be provided with opportunities to follow your own interests in sound analysis and creative design, with the opportunity to demonstrate new innovative approaches to screen soundtrack production in your final work.
learningOutcomes: Analyse the role of the screen soundtrack in multimedia communication
Evaluate screen sound productions, using appropriate research and examples
Critique the nuances of specific screen soundtracks across media forms
Create responses to existing screen soundtracks in written or other formats

54487.title: Music and Sound Project
54487.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54487.description: In this subject, you will develop and complete a major, original, music and sound design project. This flexible and highly creative subject allows you as the composer/sound designer to demonstrate your technical skills and expertise in screen sound, game sound, electronic, electroacoustic or art music composition, performance, multimedia or interactive sonic media, or other relevant music and sound media, to establish your professional portfolio and prepare you for success in the creative industries. You will be guided in project management, collaboration processes, research techniques, critical reflection and documentation, and the technical, aesthetic and structural development of the work, culminating in a final public presentation. In this subject, you will also be encouraged to collaborate across the creative production disciplines, including game design.
learningOutcomes: Reflect critically on major formative genres, cultural, theoretical and technological trends in music/sound composition
Incorporate a variety of media and technology in creative production process
Consider the diverse audiences that may be engaged by your practice
Apply accrued technical fluency and structure creative ideas in their creative work
Manage a creative project through all stages of production, as an individual artist or within a team

54488.title: Creative Audio Programming
54488.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54488.description: This subject introduces you to the principles of sound creation and composition using electronic and digital processes. It provides you with a foundation for computational approaches to sound manipulation enabling you to explore innovative approaches to sound synthesis, interactive systems, algorithmic and data-driven sound composition. You will investigate issues and current practices at the intersection of art, music and sound design, providing a context for you to develop your own creative sound works within the subject.
learningOutcomes: Create novel sound compositions using dataflow programming
Apply computational approaches to creative audio practice
Relate technical and compositional concepts from historical and contemporary sound practice to new works
Design, plan, and realise digital music and sound design projects
Employ the language and concepts of electronic music production to identify and describe technical processes

54489.title: Advanced Music Production
54489.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54489.description: In this subject you will develop advanced composition, sound design and music production skills, as well as production techniques for professional music creation. You will acquire practical skills in multi-channel, immersive and binaural sound production for a range of media and deliverables, including XR, immersive and interactive environments, and popular music. The subject also covers advanced microphone techniques, multi-channel and immersive microphone array techniques, and advanced psychoacoustics, along with approaches to procedural music generation. You will learn to incorporate emerging and disruptive technologies in music creation and production, working on collaborative and industry-focused projects.
learningOutcomes: Analyse and evaluate the techniques utilised in sound and music production in a range of genres.
Develop production techniques in multichannel, immersive and binaural sound.
Evaluate the aesthetic, technical and collaborative considerations for advanced music production.
Reflect and communicate on creative, technical and conceptual practice
Ability to work independently within a creative and technical context

54490.title: Sound and Music for Games
54490.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54490.description: In this subject you will explore the theories, concepts, creative approaches and technical skills required for audio and music in games and interactive environments. This includes game audio workflows, sound production, sound design consideration, interactive considerations, mixing techniques, as well as skills in middleware and games engines. The subject aims to develop your game-specific approaches to creative sound design and music composition, with a focus on collaborations and team-based approaches to practical work.
learningOutcomes: Develop an understanding of the development of the video game industry.
Analyse current game audio practices, techniques and trends.
Develop practical skills in sound and music production and workflows for interactive games.
Ability to critically reflect on sound and music design for games.
Reflect and communicate on technical and conceptual practice.

54491.title: World Music: A History
54491.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54491.description: This subject explores the histories, philosophies and diversities of musical traditions from around the world. You will begin by exploring origin narratives for music, both mythical and scientific, before moving to consider particular styles, contact zones, philosophies, migrations, and controversies that have shaped the music of the world through to the 20th century. You will then explore the challenges of listening to, understanding, and appreciating music cultures that are vastly different from your own experience. In doing so, World Music: A History provides context for salient moments of cultural exchange and mobility across the world’s music cultures up until the advent of recorded music. By considering the histories of the world’s music traditions, you will gain a deep awareness of the diversities of musical experience, practice, knowledge, and most importantly, an appreciation of why music matters to us as human beings.
learningOutcomes: Reflect on the ethical challenges of representing diverse musical cultures
Investigate diverse musical philosophies and sonorities
Evaluate the importance of music to human societies in different historical epochs
Identify points of connection and influence between diverse musical cultures
Communicate complex ideas clearly and effectively

54492.title: Global Pop Music
54492.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54492.description: Global Popular Music explores the musical, cultural, and economic dimensions of the international music industry. The subject focuses on the ways that transnational movements of artists and audiences, recorded works, audio technologies, and intellectual property shape the kinds of music that we listen to, and create the conditions for emerging musical styles and communities. In doing so, Global Popular Music offers an understanding of the role of music in relation to wider social and industrial processes, including those related to screen industries, creative content production on digital media, subscription-based media distribution models, and the impact of global media industries on local media industries and community identities.

Research and evaluate the impacts of music technologies, creative value chains, and regulatory contexts on global musical practices and creative industries
Identify key musical artists, works, genres, and instruments through attentive and critical listening
Communicate theories and concepts around musical practices and creative industries in a clear, concise, and scholarly manner

54495.description: This subject operates in tandem with 54496 Studio: Project Pre-production to advance students' understanding of industry production practices. In this subject you will identify and work towards specific creative industry career paths by focusing on your chosen specialist area.  Working on iterative interdisciplinary creative tasks throughout the session, you will engage in independent research and practice around contemporary global creative and industrial developments. The subject asks you to critically reflect on changes and challenges around specific roles within your creative practice. This subject mirrors production models in the creative industries and supports you in attaining the level of production value and management skill necessary to complete your major Honours project.
learningOutcomes: Explore specialist creative practice skills in depth, including personal and professional capabilities
Demonstrate an informed understanding of creative industry roles and practices
Investigate methods that communications professionals use to collaborate respectfully with and for Indigenous Australians
Actively engage in the roles and functions within team-based production
Communicate ideas, information, and planning around creative practices in a clear, concise, and professional manner

54496.title: Studio: Project Pre-Production
54496.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
54496.description: Pre-production is an important phase in the development of a creative project. It encompasses many standard practices and steps, for example, draft score and/or audio files, script development, core concept development for pre-visualisation and/or temp soundtrack, storyboarding, and story pitching to an audience. In this subject, you will embark on research, generate ideas, develop content and/or form collaborative teams for your project. Working closely with your tutors, you will negotiate and refine the feasibility of your proposed project, developing clear strategies for production. On completion of this subject, you will have a fully resolved package of pre-production assets, such as: a script, a production bible, concept design artwork, final animatic, draft components of sound design, score and arrangements, and a detailed production schedule.
learningOutcomes: Independently identify, analyse, and utilise research materials relevant to creative practice
Develop ideas, designs, and prototypes across multiple iterations and feedback cycles
Communicate theories and concepts around creative practice in a clear, concise, and scholarly manner
Develop organisational skills suitable to the management of complex creative projects and timelines

The Honours creative project provides you with an opportunity to demonstrate advanced craft skills and technical competency around your relevant creative practice, and to show a high-level of understanding of emerging aesthetic and theoretical paradigms linked to your domain of practice. By the end of this subject, you will have produced a creative work at the standards expected for public broadcast, performance, or exhibition.

57304.description: This subject addresses the ethical dilemmas surrounding data-driven AI systems in decision-making across various sectors. You will engage in debates on AI's function and development, informed by humanities and social science perspectives. The course emphasises moral and ethical considerations like transparency, fairness, and algorithmic bias, and applies these to real and hypothetical case studies concerning data ethics, regulation, and accountability.

In this practice-based subject, students write sustained creative work as they explore this popular and growing area of international publishing. You'll learn the editor's role, master copyediting and proofreading, understand house style, and use the latest editing technology. 57604.title: Communication Theory and Practice
57604.description: The subject explores key theories and concepts that inform human communication and strategic communication practices such as advertising, public relations, organisational communication, communication management, and social media. It draws on significant interdisciplinary knowledges and traditions: rhetoric, systems theory, psychology, semiotics, interpretation (phenomenology), sociology, cultural studies, and critical theory. The subject introduces students to de-Westernised processes and practices to recognise the importance of cultural nuances in negotiating meaning. Students review communication models that inform their understanding of factors that either contribute to, or challenge, effective communication in diverse communication contexts and issues. The learning process is interactive, blending theoretical knowledge with practical application to real-world contexts.
learningOutcomes: Identify key concepts in communication traditions and theories
Critique how different communication traditions inform strategic communication
Critically apply communication theory across communication phenomena, issues and cultural contexts

57607.title: Ethics, Responsibility and Sustainability
57607.description:
In the modern world, communications professionals have an increasing role to play in their employers’ adherence to ethical decision making and socially responsible practices that make our broad society, community, and environment sustainable in the long term.

By critically analysing and applying different ethical perspectives to selected case studies, you’ll learn the significance of ethics in an organisation’s communication practices. In addition, you’ll investigate the difference between corporate social responsibility (CSR) and sustainability. You’ll demonstrate how an organisation can retain its social licence to operate by adapting to changing stakeholder expectations around sustainability.
learningOutcomes: Apply theories and concepts to critically analyse issues and to develop solutions for an organisation’s challenges.
Identify stakeholders and publics that affect or are affected by an organisation’s ethical decision-making, CSR, or sustainability practices.

57690.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
57690.description: This subject provides you with practical skills in screen directing for film and television, in partnership with the Australian Directors Guild. You'll gain expertise in screen development, screenplay analysis, directing actors, cinematic storytelling, and post-production management. Your learning journey includes hands-on exercises, workshops, and insights from industry professionals through guest lectures, enabling you to craft compelling narratives and engage audiences effectively. This comprehensive approach ensures you emerge as a confident director, ready to lead in the dynamic world of screen production.
learningOutcomes: Analyse narrative drama scripts and scenes from a directorial point-of-view.
Generate vivid and meaningful screen language for cinematic storytelling.
Creatively execute a visualisation package and production plan for a drama scene.
Evaluate the role of the screen director in post-production.

57691.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
57691.description: This subject equips you with the expertise to operate ARRI digital camera systems, leading to ARRI Academy user certification, a credential recognised globally in the film industry. You'll develop practical skills in camera operation, colour science, recording formats, and post-production workflows, mirroring professional cinematography practices. Through hands-on exercises with ARRI equipment and software, you will learn to manage real-world production demands, ensuring your readiness for a career in high-end digital filmmaking.
learningOutcomes: Develop proficiency in ARRI digital cinema camera systems and workflows.
Manage typical on-set ARRI camera situations and workflows to professional and industry standards.
Apply ARRI camera system knowledge and techniques to produce a portfolio of in-class creative cinematographic works.
Analyse and critically reflect on cinematographic work.

57692.title: Creative Producing
57692.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
57692.description:
This subject introduces you to concepts, strategies and practices of content creation in established and emerging screen environments, enhancing your understanding of the creative producer's role in both domestic and global media landscapes. You'll hone your ability to initiate concepts and stories, and translate these into tangible media arts projects, both individually and collaboratively. Your skill set will expand to include creativity techniques, story development, pitching, financial sourcing, budgeting, scheduling, and navigating marketing, distribution, and legalities.

You will also learn to foster ethical practices, build strategic partnerships, and adopt innovative methods in project development and distribution, preparing you for a dynamic career in media production. Learning is hands-on, blending theoretical insights with practical application to ensure a comprehensive grasp of content creation.
learningOutcomes: Identify key issues and concerns for creative producers in the screen industry.
Initiate and develop projects in screen production.
Research and justify the viability of a proposed project and its release strategy.
Appraise engagement of creative project ideas with a potential audience.
Work effectively and ethically in collaborative creative environments.

57693.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
57693.description: This subject equips you with the expertise to navigate the evolving landscape of screen curation, enhancing your ability to evaluate, promote, and exhibit screen content within diverse industry and institutional frameworks. You will develop critical skills in assessment and review, learning to discern what elevates screen content and to apply various standards of merit. Through practical exploration, you'll examine the interplay between commercial success and cultural impact, and the responsibilities of curators in shaping public discourse. Your learning unfolds through interactive case studies, fostering an understanding of gatekeeping dynamics and success metrics from multiple viewpoints.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate the practices of screen curation of Indigenous content.
Describe and implement screen curatorial practices and techniques in a range of cultural contexts.
Critique and apply screen curation industry practices.
Synthesise and apply knowledge of screen curation through culturally relevant and impactful concept development.

Informed by your own research, you’ll develop communication products across multiple media channels and content formats, and address identified publics for a client or issue.
learningOutcomes: Critically examine and apply relevant concepts and theories on industry practices.
Assess and select media channels relevant to media users, issues, or organisations’ communication strategies.

58130.title: Thesis (Creative Writing)
58130.description: The MRes thesis in Creative Writing is suitable for writers wishing to diversify and strengthen their creative practice. It is also suitable for those in the writing, publishing or related industries wishing to undertake a formal research project with academic guidance. Students learn how to identify and frame an original creative project or industry-related research project, identify and analyse research within the field, and apply those findings to your research. They develop an understanding of various professional and ethical traditions, key drivers, and challenges within the fields of writing and publishing, while producing a work on an international scale. As they study, students build, design, and produce a major work, a ‘non-traditional thesis’ tailored to their career aspirations and area of interest in writing or publishing. With educational opportunities to develop a thesis as either a practice-led work of creative writing, work-based inquiry project, industry-based research project or a scholarly/conceptual research project, students acquire valuable skills such as practical problem-solving, textual analysis, applied research methodologies, and critical thinking. Students also develop proficiency in writing and narrative skills, digital tools and technologies for research that can be directly applied to real-world industry settings.

requisite.text: Admission into C03067 Master of Arts (Research)

58131.title: Thesis (Digital and Social Media)
58131.description: The MRes in Digital and Social Media provides methodological and theoretical training for students interested in researching digital media, including on topics such as social media platforms, apps, AI, data visualisation and analysis, digital activism, and digital identity politics. Through the thesis students may explore and apply a variety of digital research methods including digital ethnography, the walkthrough method, the scrollback method, platform analysis, and qualitative/quantitative coding of digital data. Students also can engage with foundational digital media theories, enabling them to design and conduct an independent research project supervised by a faculty member in the field. This course is a pathway to further research programs, including the PhD, as well as professional roles that involve digital and social media research, data collection and analysis.

requisite.text: Admission into C03067 Master of Arts (Research)

58132.title: Thesis (Journalism)
58132.description: The MRes thesis in Journalism is an accredited postgraduate degree leading to professional recognition as a journalist, journalist-researcher and news media practitioner. Students participate in various research training courses including those that are useful for journalism researchers and professionals in an international field of practice. They learn how to gather and analyse information effectively, and accurately, and understand the importance of researching and reporting diverse subjects and communities. As part of their degree, students have the opportunity to participate in a cross-cultural exchange with an international partner university and acquire the necessary skills and knowledge to become a global citizen in the field of journalism. They also develop an understanding of various professional traditions, conventions, cultures, and challenges while producing journalism and research on an international scale. Classes involve students engaging in skills-based research training guided by academic and industry mentors and are informed by conceptual and current discourses on contemporary journalism practice, with consideration for the importance of ethics and diversity principles. As students study, they are able to gain international experience with our partner university, at the same time as building, designing, and producing

requisite.text: Admission into C03067 Master of Arts (Research)

58133.title: Thesis (Media Arts and Production)
58133.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
58133.description: This subject offers students the opportunity to undertake a major creative practice research project for, about or through media arts and production activities. they receive one-to-one supervision from discipline experts as well as access to facilities and equipment support for high-end post graduate research production projects and a seminar program focusing on contemporary concerns in creative practice research. The major research thesis incorporates a significant research based creative work and a 15,000-word thesis or a 40,000-word traditional thesis, with both options being externally examined. The scope and feasibility of the research projects would be determined in close consultation with their research supervisor. Emphasising and recognising the unique contributions to knowledge that can be gleaned through creative practice research in media arts and production, students can address issues within their own creative media arts practice, questions drawn from industry practices, in collaboration with industry, or explore other complex problems with creative media arts practice as the central mode of inquiry.

requisite.text: Admission into C03067 Master of Arts (Research)

58134.title: Thesis (Music and Sound Design)
58134.school: MAP and Sound and Music Design
58134.description: The MRes Thesis in Music and Sound Design supports supervised research projects in music composition and production, sound design for media, entertainment and sound arts, popular music studies and music industry. Students develop either a creative practice work of professional standard, supported by a written exegesis or an in-depth research project resulting in a scholarly thesis. A broad range of research methods can be supported by the Music and Sound Design discipline. Projects with industry focus and collaboration are encouraged and students can engage in regular colloquia with peers, academics and industry mentors, as well as address contemporary and emerging production technologies and research practices that can be applied in real-world industry settings.

requisite.text: Admission into C03067 Master of Arts (Research)

58135.title: Thesis (Society, Politics and Environment)
58135.description: Through the thesis in Society, Politics and Environment students conduct a significant research project. Their project may be empirical, analytical, comparative, individual or collaborative. It may be conducted independently or embedded in a workplace to strengthen research impact. Students' projects address societal challenges, develop tools for critical thinking and help bring about positive change. They receive guidance and support from a tailored supervisory panel selected from staff in sociology, politics and political economy, science and technology studies, geography, history and anthropology. Through the thesis project students develop the necessary analytical, knowledge and methodological skills to conduct impactful research. Seminars and workshops help deepen and broaden students' knowledge, immersing them in a research community and providing support in thesis writing and research communication.

requisite.text: Admission into C03067 Master of Arts (Research)

58136.title: Thesis (Strategic Communication)
58136.description: The thesis in Strategic Communication provides students with a rigorous, comprehensive, and advanced understanding of communication research methodologies and analytical skills that can be used to generate insights to better understand and engage diverse stakeholders in society. Students design and conduct research to extend foundational and contemporary communication theories within the discipline of Strategic Communication. The subject aims to equip students with the necessary capabilities to contribute to the practice of strategic communication through innovative and impactful research that addresses complex communication issues. Topics may include risk/issue/crisis communication, reputation management, brand health tracking and evaluation, advertising creative development and campaign tracking, stakeholder engagement, corporate social responsibility, sustainability, organisational listening, measurement, public behaviour, cultural insights, digital/social/mobile practices and engagement, and public diplomacy.

requisite.text: Admission into C03067 Master of Arts (Research)

58138.title: Theory and Narrative
58138.school: Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences
58138.description: In this research training subject you develop a deep understanding of key theories relevant to your field of research. You apply established and emerging theories to a body of knowledge to deepen the thesis topic. Through this you develop your capacity for critical reflection, exploring theoretical perspectives to establish your own research narrative. You reflect on ways to bring theory into practice to produces outcomes, be they creative or otherwise. You lead seminars and participate with others to cross-fertilise and co-inspire. You gain an appreciation of the process of critical reflection and the uses of theory to illuminate practice, enabling new insights, original narratives and wider social impact.
learningOutcomes: Identify, synthesise, and apply theoretical approaches to specific areas of inquiry across the humanities and social sciences
Demonstrate a capacity to analyse and critique theoretical works in the humanities and social sciences
Demonstrate a critical understanding of values and assumptions embedded in different ways of knowing
Communicate theoretical ideas in a clear, logical, and persuasive way

59718.title: Developing English: Studies of the Australian Natural Environment
59718.description: This subject is designed to consolidate your written and oral academic skills and literacies. You will develop these skills through a range of studies that relate to Australia's natural environment, and may include: the meanings attached to land, landscape, beach and bush; to concepts of native, introduced, companion and feral species; to patterns of population, consumption and waste; and to the ways in which Australians participate in green cultures and organisations.
learningOutcomes: develop academic reading, listening, speaking and writing skills
develop accuracy in use of English in academic contexts
develop research skills

59719.description: This subject is designed to develop your capabilities in academic English so that you may participate effectively in your Australian university studies. You will develop your language capabilities through intensive practice in listening, speaking, reading and writing using textual forms that are appropriate for Australian university contexts. In terms of content, you will investigate issues to do with Australia's engagement with the world of work. This content may include: patterns of labour, migration, and employment in the Australian economy; workplace practices; sociocultural issues of gender, age, ethnicity, and language in the Australian workplace; and Australia's place in the global economy
learningOutcomes: Develop academic reading, listening, writing and speaking skills to a level that allows effective participation in university study
Develop research skills appropriate for undergraduate study

59720.title: Academic English: Communication Fundamentals
59720.description: This subject introduces you to the nature of effective spoken and written communication in academic contexts. It examines what makes this form of communication different from communication in other contexts and makes its sometimes hidden rules explicit to students. You will examine a range of spoken and written academic texts, unpack the features of the texts that make the communication effective, practise using these features, and receive peer and teacher feedback on your academic communicative competence.
learningOutcomes: Read critically and identify relevant information in academic texts
Locate and evaluate relevant texts to support an academic argument
Recognise the generic stages and features of academic texts written and spoken in English
Produce written texts appropriate to the register and genres of academic writing
Produce spoken texts appropriate to the register and genres of academic speaking

60005.title: Wildlife Field Techniques: Animal Handling and Survey Methods
60005.description: This subject offers you practical skills in identifying, handling, and conserving Australia's wildlife, combining online learning with a hands-on field trip. You'll study the ethical treatment of wildlife, safety protocols, first aid, and survey design. During the three-day field trip, you will conduct wildlife surveys and will learn how to safely and effectively handle various native species of mammals, birds and reptiles. Your wildlife survey skills will be assessed by leading Australian wildlife experts. You'll also collaborate in teams to evaluate, coordinate, and implement an effective response to a range of wildlife emergencies. This experience prepares you for real-world encounters with wildlife in professional environments.
learningOutcomes: Conduct a risk assessment by applying relevant guidelines, legislation, work, health and safety requirements, and regulations governing working with wildlife.
Describe the key concepts for managing and conserving wildlife, including Indigenous fire management.
Use scientific keys and guides to accurately identify Australian mammals, reptiles, frogs, and birds.
Identify and apply the appropriate first aid in a wildlife emergency while demonstrating competency in wildlife handling skills for a range of species.
Identify and apply the six steps involved with planning and performing fauna surveys, including threatened species.

60006.title: Scientific Perspectives for Global Issues
60006.description: Our planet is undergoing significant change at multiple scales. This subject equips you with the skills to investigate current and future global challenges through scientific inquiry. You’ll explore the importance and application of scientific thinking and diverse knowledge systems, focusing on those of Indigenous peoples of Australia, in addressing complex global issues and sustainability. You will examine how knowledge is produced through scientific processes, and learn to evaluate and synthesise scientific information from multiple sources. You’ll develop critical thinking, communication skills, professional and ethical attributes essential for a successful scientific career.
learningOutcomes: Analyse and summarise major global challenges within Australian and sustainability contexts.
Explain the process of scientific knowledge production, and evaluate and synthesise scientific information from multiple sources.
Critically examine the process, responsibilities and limitations of science in addressing global challenges.
Critically reflect on and communicate new scientific perspectives on global issues and sustainability.
Explain ethical communication strategies and considerations to engage with Indigenous peoples and communities in scientific research.

60101.title: Chemistry and Materials Science
60101.description: This subject lays the groundwork for advanced materials and engineering studies, fostering collaboration among professionals and honing problem-solving skills in chemistry and materials. It covers chemical bonding, materials classification, structure-property correlations, mechanical characteristics, heat treatments, alloys, ceramics, polymers, composites, degradation, recycling, and selection of materials. Applied examples, laboratory work, and workshops are key components, reinforcing theory with practical skills.
learningOutcomes: Understand and apply fundamental concepts and technical terms of materials science and engineering.
Describe the mechanical and physical behaviour of materials and evaluate the impact of standards on material performance.
Solve materials selection problems and critically assess selection procedures.
Apply various chemistry terms, molar calculations and chemical equations appropriately.
Prepare a professional consultancy report evaluating mechanical properties of materials.

60102.title: Ethics in Animal Research
60102.description: This subject introduces you to the ethical considerations and humane treatment of animals in research across various fields, including medical, wildlife, and agricultural studies, as recognised by Australian law. You will learn about the significance of animals in research, the strict legal frameworks governing their use, and the maintenance of their wellbeing. The course also covers the roles of care and ethics committees in ensuring compliance with regulations and guidelines, preparing you to conduct animal research responsibly.
learningOutcomes: Consider the complexities of using animals in research and be able to reframe opinions based on ethical use, legislation and regulation of animals in research.
Examine the role that animal ethics plays in research and responsibilities of both animal ethics and research stakeholders
Assess and apply animal ethics legislation, regulation and guidelines in animal research laboratories, agriculture and in the natural environment.

60117.description: This subject equips students with the skills to apply experimental methods across scientific disciplines, essential for science careers. It offers a framework for scientific research, including hypothesis testing, sample size determination, data analysis, and modelling. It introduces the concept of uncertainty in experiments and touches on ethics in statistical practice, instilling an understanding of the 'scientific method' vital for research-focused professions.

implement statistical analysis methodology in R programming language
communicate analysis results and conclusions clearly and write critical reports assessing papers and journal articles
critically reflect on ethical study design and data collection strategies and analyses when engaging with Indigenous Australians in scientific and research contexts.

60119.title: Science Business Models and Intellectual Property
60119.description: This subject bridges the gap between business and science, teaching you how to apply business principles to scientific issues. You'll learn to deconstruct ideas and optimise outcomes by understanding the nine elements of a business model in a scientific context, using case studies. The course also covers intellectual property fundamentals, including identification, protection, and commercialisation, with a focus on patents, trademarks, and licensing. You'll develop a business model for a project and learn to effectively communicate it to potential investors, enhancing your ability to manage and leverage intellectual property in the scientific realm.
learningOutcomes: Apply different types of IP, patents and trademarks to commercialise research findings (intellectual property) from case studies
Create a business model for a scientific project/idea
Summarise and communicate your business model to an appropriate audience, in this case a potential investor

60713.title: Masters Research Internship
60713.description: In this subject, you will complete a session-long science research project either with a UTS research group or an external partner. This experience will enhance your research and communication skills in a professional context. You will work with your supervisors to define your project scope, conduct research, critically analyse data, and compile your findings into a formal report. Supervisor and Faculty of Science approval is required before enrolling in this subject due to the limited availability of research places. Contact the Program Director for more information.
learningOutcomes: Develop and execute a project plan with your supervisor, within the field of your research area.
Apply knowledge and skills into professional scientific practice to gain new expertise.
Review existing academic literature to develop an executable experimental plan
Apply appropriate methods of statistical analysis to interpret data
Communicate the findings of your research through both written and oral communication, including the contribution of the research to the scientific field.

60904.title: Research Translation and Clinical Trials
60904.description:
This subject examines research translation in medical science, focusing on how scientific discoveries are transformed into clinical practice. Students will explore the processes, frameworks, and challenges involved in moving evidence from research settings into real-world trials and further application, with particular attention to the factors that enable or hinder successful implementation within healthcare systems.

Building on this foundation, the subject provides a comprehensive understanding of clinical trials as a cornerstone of evidence-based medicine and a critical mechanism through which new medical interventions are evaluated. Students will examine key elements of clinical trial design, conduct, and analysis, and critically assess how methodological decisions influence the robustness, reliability, and applicability of the evidence generated.

The subject develops students' ability to interpret and appraise clinical data which is an essential skill for careers in research, pharmaceutical development, clinical practice, regulatory decision-making, and health policy. This integrated perspective enables students to examine how evidence is generated, interrogated, and implemented to shape therapeutic innovations and community health outcomes.
learningOutcomes: Identify and apply the principles of design thinking to real world problems.
Formulate a strategy on how to take a product to the marketplace.
Select and apply principles of intellectual property.
Communicate clearly a novel product and business idea to investors, industry, the media and to the public.
Work effectively in a collaborative manner to create a new product.
