60912.title: Science Thesis (Life Sciences) 1
60912.description: The Master of Philosophy course provides advanced research training in life and environmental sciences, enhancing your skills and knowledge for a research career. Centred around a research project spanning two 24-credit-point sessions, you'll work closely with an academic supervisor to conduct research in your chosen area. You'll learn to formulate hypotheses, set objectives, manage time and resources, employ appropriate research methods, evaluate evidence critically, and construct detailed arguments. Under supervision, you'll analyse and interpret scientific data from your project. Your science communication skills will be honed through written works and oral presentations. The culmination of your work is a thesis, which is the primary assessment component of the course.
learningOutcomes: Conduct independent research to generate new knowledge relating to a medical, environmental or biotechnology problem.
Develop a research plan and design suitable experiments to address an existing gap in disciplinary knowledge based on a review of existing literature.
Communicate research findings effectively in diverse contexts.
Collaborate effectively within a research team.
Critically situate research and professional capabilities within the current state of the field, articulating how the work contributes to, extends, or challenges existing knowledge.

65000.title: Master Research Capstone (Chemical and Forensic Sciences)
65000.description:
This capstone subject provides you with advanced, hands‑on experience in the development, optimisation and validation of analytical methods within an authentic research context. Working under expert supervision, you will apply and extend your laboratory skills to investigate a real‑world problem in analytical chemistry or forensic science. Throughout the project, you will strengthen your research literacy, enhance your ability to interpret and critically evaluate experimental data, and effectively communicate scientific outcomes.

The subject emphasises independent investigation supported by collaborative problem‑solving. You will design and conduct experiments, assess method performance, troubleshoot experimental challenges, and present your findings in a professionally structured scientific report. This experience prepares you for professional practice or further research by building confidence, technical capability, and discipline‑specific analytical expertise.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate the ability to critically evaluate and synthesize research literature to formulate research questions and interpret experimental results.
Design and conduct experiments to address research questions, applying appropriate tools and techniques for data generation and analysis.
Maintain accurate and detailed experimental records by effectively incorporating methods, results, and observations into a laboratory notebook.
Communicate experimental plans and findings effectively through written, visual, and verbal formats.

65001.title: Medicinal Chemistry
65001.description: You will cover the drug discovery process, from lead compounds to clinical trials, highlighting the interdisciplinary essence of medicinal chemistry. You'll explore the chemical, pharmacological, and biological principles of drug development, learn about macromolecules involved in disease, and study drug synthesis, design, and the body's influence on drug efficacy. This will equip you with knowledge crucial for practicing medicinal chemistry.
learningOutcomes: Apply fundamental principles of drug pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics and computational molecular modelling to drug design.
Explain the role of clinical trials and intellectual property in drug development.
Demonstrate practical laboratory skills and record-keeping in medicinal chemistry.
Communicate scientific research effectively through various formats.
Collaborate effectively within a team to manage and execute projects.

65006.title: Advanced Chemical Criminalistics
65006.description: This subject delves into chemical criminalistics, an area of forensic science focusing on trace analysis through chemical methods, alongside fundamental forensic principles and skills. Students start with foundational concepts, progressing to advanced forensic reasoning with complex case analysis. Learning is self-directed via online modules on Canvas, supplemented by practicals and workshops that evolve from skill introduction to student-led complex cases. By the end, students are adept at managing forensic investigations, applying analytical techniques, interpreting advanced forensic evidence, and providing expert witness reports.
learningOutcomes: Use current forensic analytical procedures to accurately and effectively analyse traces
Formulate and test hypotheses about the source and activity that created a trace
Synthesise and communicate expert opinion and complex information to a wide range of audiences in a variety of formats
Interpret and evaluate complex traces in general and within the context of a complex case scenario
Demonstrate the utility and value of chemical traces and micro traces within modern forensic science

65007.title: Biometrics and Identification Sciences
65007.description: Building on 65019 Foundations of Forensic Science and 65009 Forensic Inference and Interpretation, this subject focuses on the analysis and interpretation of biometric traces used for forensic identification. You will gain hands-on experience in detecting, analysing, interpreting and reporting biometric evidence through simulated case work in practical classes and associated workshops. You will also discuss privacy and ethical issues with the use of emerging biometric technologies.
learningOutcomes: Develop hypotheses and critically examine forensic traces in the context of a case using appropriate methods
Evaluate the results of forensic analyses in a variety of case scenarios
Explain complex forensic science concepts to diverse audiences in oral and written formats
Discuss emerging issues in biometrics and human identification sciences and their impact on shaping modern professional practice
Develop independent research skills, including formulating research questions, selecting the appropriate methodology, data collection and interpretation, and synthesising information

65009.title: Forensic Inference and Interpretation
65009.description: This subject equips students with the skills to evaluate and interpret forensic traces using probabilistic inferences. Through practical examples, case studies, and data, students learn to apply logical reasoning and probability theory, including Bayesian networks and likelihood ratio approaches, to forensic evidence analysis. The aim is to impart comprehensive knowledge in evidence evaluation principles and their application in forensic contexts.
learningOutcomes: Understand the role of propositions and the case’s contextual information in the interpretation of traces in forensic science
Apply probability theory and Bayesian networks to the evaluation of the observations made on the traces and the results obtained from their analyses
Evaluate the value of traces in a wide range of scenarios encountered in forensic science (including source level and activity level propositions, database hits, and multiple traces)
Explain the value of the evidence in verbal and written forms without committing any logical fallacies

65010.title: Forensic Toxicology and Drug Analysis
65010.description: This subject delves into forensic toxicology, exploring the science behind drugs and poisons in legal contexts. It covers the chemistry, pharmacology, and societal impact of various illicit substances, including their mechanisms, bodily processing, and associated signs and symptoms. You will examine drug classes such as stimulants, depressants, and hallucinogens, focusing on synthesis, profiling, analysis, and clandestine lab operations. You will also learn the relevant state and federal legislation and social issues surrounding drug use. Practical work reinforces online learning, providing experience in analysing biological samples pertinent to the field.
learningOutcomes: Explain key principles and methodologies in forensic toxicology and their application to case studies.
Collaborate effectively within a team and document processes appropriately.
Communicate research findings in the context of current scientific literature relating to forensic toxicology.
Apply legal frameworks to drug use and assess their societal impact.
Perform and interpret forensic toxicology experiments and data analysis.

65019.description: This subject provides you with an introduction to forensic science for those with a scientific background, covering the investigative process from crime scene to lab analysis. You'll explore the evolution of forensic principles and their current applications, gaining insight into various sub-disciplines. The aim is to introduce you to forensic methodologies and concepts, enriching your understanding for further specialised study. Topics include crime scene procedures, forensic lab techniques, and documentation practices.
learningOutcomes: Scrutinise and discuss the foundational concepts of forensic science, both practical and theoretical
Critically analyse forensic traces, exhibits and case context to develop forensically relevant hypotheses and methodologies.
Examine a crime scene and identify relevant evidence as part of the investigation.
Evaluate complex case scenarios to gain a greater understanding of forensic processes and interpretation
Demonstrate high quality written and oral communication skills to convey scientific information to diverse audiences.

65111.title: Chemistry 1
65111.description: Chemistry is central to understanding the world around us and it provides foundational knowledge for many other scientific disciplines such as medicine, biochemistry, energy and technology. This subject will provide you with fundamental knowledge and skills in chemistry. Through the lectures you will learn about atomic theory, structure and bonding, chemical reactions and equilibria, quantitative chemistry, molecular geometry, and intermolecular forces. Through the practical program you will develop key scientific skills such as laboratory techniques, teamwork, observation, measurement, analysis, and problem-solving.
learningOutcomes: Understand and apply key chemistry principles.
Qualitatively monitor chemical reactions and explain observations with chemical equations.
Apply quantitative skills to solve chemistry problems.
Demonstrate proficiency in laboratory techniques and practice.
Effectively communicate chemical knowledge and the significance of chemistry and its applications to diverse audiences.

65202.title: Organic Chemistry 1
65202.description: This subject explores the reactions and mechanisms of carbon compound families, highlighting the link between molecular structure and reactivity. Students conduct laboratory experiments, assess outcomes using infra-red spectroscopy, and measure melting points, key skills for professional chemists.
learningOutcomes: Apply fundamental concepts in chemical structure and electron pushing to organic reaction mechanisms.
Analyse and solve problems in organic chemistry based on analysis and evaluation of relevant information.
Conduct experiments and analyse and communicate findings.
Collaborate effectively in a professional scientific environment.

65212.title: Chemistry 2
65212.description: Chemistry is vital for understanding the physical world and underpins biology, geology, and environmental science. This subject advances concepts from 65111 Chemistry 1, focusing on physical chemistry—equilibria, kinetics, thermochemistry—and organic chemistry, including reactions of carbon compounds and biological molecules like proteins, sugars, and nucleic acids. Physical chemistry elucidates chemical reactivity and energetics, while organic chemistry unravels the complexity of nature.
learningOutcomes: Explain fundamental concepts in chemistry and their application in research and professional contexts.
Analyse chemical reactions in terms of yield, rates, mechanisms, and thermodynamics.
Apply principles of chemical equilibrium to various chemical systems.
Understand and predict the behaviour of organic compounds based on their structure and stereochemistry.
Develop practical laboratory skills and effectively communicate chemical information.

65242.title: Principles of Forensic Science
65242.description: This subject introduces the discipline of forensic science and its relevant subdisciplines. Starting with the trace, a vector of information that can be detected, recovered, examined and interpreting. You will explore this concept across physic and digital traces and how forensic scientists use traces to understand events of public interest (e.g. crimes, security incidents).
learningOutcomes: Understand and apply the principles and concepts of the scientific method to the discipline of forensic science
Apply critical thinking and problem solving skills in the interpretation of evidence and case data
Explain the role of forensic science in the legal system and the larger community
Analyse case-like scenarios to demonstrate understanding of forensic processes and interpretation
Develop written and oral communication skills to convey scientific information to diverse audience

65306.title: Analytical Chemistry 1
65306.description: This subject equips students with essential data analysis skills and laboratory techniques fundamental to analytical chemistry. It includes quantification, statistical data analysis, and hands-on experience with analytical instruments, chromatography, and mass spectrometry. Students learn to prepare calibration curves for chromatographic analysis and evaluate analytical data statistically.
learningOutcomes: Explain theoretical concepts for various instrumental techniques
Identify and apply the appropriate statistical analysis to interpret experimental data
Develop practical skills in acquiring quantified data on chromatographic instrumentation
Work collaboratively as a team to achieve experimental goals

65307.title: Thermodynamics, Energy and Spectroscopy
65307.description: This subject provides you with a working knowledge of thermodynamics, energy, and optical spectroscopy. You will develop an understanding of the fundamental physical principles underlying systems that generate, convert, or store energy. Emphasis is placed on applying these principles to practical problem‑solving contexts in energy science and related disciplines.
learningOutcomes: Explain the fundamental laws and concepts of thermodynamics and relate microscopic behaviour to macroscopic properties in physical and chemical systems.
Apply thermodynamic principles to analyse energy transformations, spontaneity, equilibrium and efficiency in physical, chemical and technological processes.

Explain and apply spectroscopic principles, including vibrational and optical spectroscopy, to interpret spectra and infer molecular structure and equilibrium behaviour in chemical and energy-related systems.
Collect, analyse and interpret thermodynamic and spectroscopic data using appropriate units, graphs, uncertainties and scientific conventions.
Communicate thermodynamic reasoning, methods and findings clearly and logically using appropriate scientific language and literature.

65312.title: Forensic Imaging
65312.description: This subject introduces forensic imaging, blending online learning modules, practicals, and computer labs to teach the use of digital cameras and other imaging equipment in forensics for the imaging and documentation of crime scenes. Students learn to capture and digitally enhance images with software like Adobe Photoshop and GIMP, documenting the forensic process effectively. These skills form a foundation for all forensic science subjects.
learningOutcomes: Understand and apply the concepts related to light theory, image formation and digital imaging
Apply basic digital photography principles to take high-quality photographs of crime scene and forensic relevant material (exhibits and traces)
Demonstrate basic image processing skills using photography editing software, such as Adobe Photoshop
Generate a digital chain of custody and maintain its integrity throughout all steps in the workflow
Assess the quality of images and explain their value in a forensic context

args.text: Admission into MAJ01123 Forensic Science Major

65313.title: Forensic Intelligence
65313.description: Building on prior forensic science knowledge, this subject explores forensic science's broader role beyond serving the criminal justice system. It introduces the concept of forensic intelligence, focusing on the significance of traces, intellectual reasoning, and practical application. Through lectures, computer labs, and online activities, students learn to use forensic traces for intelligence, enhancing critical thinking and inquiry skills. They will extract profiles from traces or cases, identify patterns, and communicate their findings through presentations and reports.
learningOutcomes: Integrate information from collective forensic analyses through intelligence frameworks.
Discuss the extended use of forensic traces to provide knowledge about crime and deviant activities.
Extract information from a trace or case, compare it to other traces or cases and analyse the information.
Use general software (Excel) and specialist software (I2 Analyst’s Notebook) to analyse and visualise forensic case data.
Synthesise and communicate results (links and trends) through written and verbal reporting formats.

65314.title: Complex Cases
65314.description: This advanced practical subject allows students to apply techniques and principles from previous studies to a simulated forensic case, from exhibit and trace triaging to expert witness report writing. It focuses on managing complex cases with multiple trace types, prioritising tasks, and interpreting results. Laboratory work is supplemented by workshops, group discussions, and presentations, where students refine their scientific approach, develop propositions, and present case findings, deepening their overall forensic science understanding.
learningOutcomes: Apply knowledge of forensic traces to complex case scenarios and prioritise traces based on relevant case information
Process a forensic case involving multiple types of traces, from crime scene investigation to expert report writing
Evaluate the value of analysed traces and justify the analysis through verbal and written forms
Apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills in the interpretation of evidence and case data
Synthesise and communicate the findings through an expert witness report

65315.title: Forensic Research Project
65315.description: In this subject, students function as forensic science research consultants, tackling industry-relevant projects collaboratively. They design, conduct, analyse, and report on operational forensic research. Congruently they develop skill in research literacy, data analysis, and communication through workshops. Practical classes focus on developing hands-on skills via inquiry-based activities. By the end, students contribute original research to forensic science and lay a solid foundation for further postgraduate study.
learningOutcomes: Critically assess and interpret forensic science literature and experimental outcomes.
Design experiments that aim to address a research question.
Generate and analyse results using appropriate tools and techniques.
Document experimental procedures, results, and insights accurately.
Communicate experimental plans and research findings effectively.

65316.title: Criminalistics
65316.description: This subject advances skills introduced in 65242 Principles of Forensic Science and complements learning in 65342 Crime Scene Investigation. In this subject, you will learn how to analyse, interpret and report on forensic traces including fingermarks, tool marks, shoe marks and biological materials. Through mock casework in the practicals and workshops, you will gain hands-on experience with decision making, processing, and interpreting forensic traces in the context of different case scenarios – key skills for a career in forensic science.
learningOutcomes: Describe the common types of forensic traces and the basic processes that lead to their creation.
Identify and explain issues in forensic science and their impact on shaping modern professional practice.
Select and apply the least destructive sequence of procedures to enhance and analyse the trace in a particular case scenario.
Interpret and evaluate the results of forensic analyses in the context of a case scenario.
Clearly communicate expert opinion to a lay audience in a variety of formats.

65318.title: Forensic Genotyping Technologies
65318.description: Since its introduction in the 1980s, DNA profiling has revolutionised forensic science with high sensitivity and specificity. In this subject, you will explore emerging DNA technologies that go beyond standard short tandem repeat (STR) profiling and first-generation sequencing and which are useful when a STR profile doesn’t match a suspect or a database record. You will investigate alternative genetic and epigenetic markers like single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), microhaplotypes, methylated DNA and RNA. You will explore advanced genotyping strategies like second- and third-generation sequencing and microarrays. Finally, you will perform bioinformatic analyses to extract intelligence value from DNA while considering the ethical and legal issues associated with this information.
learningOutcomes: Explain the principles and applications of advanced DNA sequencing in forensic analysis.
Apply the basic principles of forensic DNA profiling using massively parallel sequencing (MPS) platforms.
Document laboratory work accurately.
Conduct bioinformatic analyses and interpret sequencing metrics.
Analyse and report DNA sequencing results and forensic investigative leads.

65319.title: Biological Criminalistics
65319.description: This subject details the Forensic Biologist's role from receiving crime scene exhibits to providing biological evidence to court. You will gain experience in locating, detecting, and collecting biological traces (specifically blood, semen and trace DNA), mirroring real forensic laboratory processes. The subject then teaches you to evaluate these biological traces and DNA results within the Hierarchy of Propositions, avoiding source and activity level fallacies. You will apply these skills to mock cases to present findings in writing for court, supported by online resources, laboratory work, and workshops.
learningOutcomes: Understand and effectively document the forensic process for biological traces.
Assess case background information and determine a suitable examination strategy for items.
Apply practical and theoretical skills to detect, collect and interpret biological traces.
Conduct an evaluation of biological traces given source and activity level propositions with reference to examination results, case circumstances and published research.
Communicate findings and expert opinion effectively in an evaluative court report.

65321.title: Homicide and Human Remains Investigation
65321.description: This subject equips students with interdisciplinary approaches to investigate forensic cases involving human remains, focusing on homicides. Students learn to locate and recover remains, process complex scenes, establish identity, and determine cause and circumstances of death. The subject enhances understanding of handling cases with varying degrees of decomposition, through expert guest presentations. Building on Crime Scene Investigation skills and complementing Criminalistics content, it prepares students to apply their knowledge to the unique challenges of homicide scenes and human remains analysis.
learningOutcomes: Understand the principles and practices of crime scene investigation.
Develop a search strategy and accurately document, photograph and manage a homicide crime scene.
Explain the difference between the characteristics of disturbed and pristine crime scenes and illustrate the importance of obtaining all contextual and background information.
Reflect on and apply the concepts and techniques of homicide crime scene investigation including ethics around working with human remains.
Demonstrate effective communication, collaboration and reflective skills.

65322.title: Major Scene Investigation
65322.description: This subject deepens students' mastery of forensic science techniques, methods, and interpretation, building on Crime Scene Investigation, Forensic Imaging, and Criminalistics. It focuses on industry-relevant crime scene procedures for major incidents, hazard identification and control, and trace evidence exploitation in realistic scenarios. Upon completion, students are adept in major crime scene examination, mirroring the proficiency of a forensic investigator.
learningOutcomes: Apply advanced forensic investigation techniques to major crime scenes.
Identify and evaluate different types of major scenes, the types of traces that may be present and the use of appropriate PPE and EHS controls.
Devise and apply sequential examination techniques used in the detection and enhancement of latent and blood marks in the scene and laboratory.
Evaluate and appropriately package exhibits from a major scene.
Prepare and deliver court-admissible case documentation.

65323.title: Advanced Imaging and Specialist Recovery
65323.description: This subject equips you with advanced forensic imaging skills, crucial for careers in forensic investigation and digital evidence analysis. You'll learn to capture and scrutinise image evidence, mastering techniques for image enhancement and authentication. Through computer labs and practical exercises, you'll refine your ability to document complex scenes, analyse digital images as evidence, exhibit specialised search skills. and effectively communicate your findings. This training not only deepens your theoretical understanding but also prepares you to apply these skills in real-world scenarios.
learningOutcomes: Apply advanced photography, digital imaging techniques, and analysis in forensic contexts.
Identify and explain various imaging artefacts and digital indicators and their relevance in a forensic context.
Assess digital imagery as evidence and discern information that is useful for forensic investigation.
Produce comprehensive forensic documentation in a professional format.

65325.title: Digital Trace and Identity
65325.description: This subject introduces students to the underlying principles and applications of digital forensic science. You’ll learn about the development and expansion of the role of digital forensic science and its importance to the future of criminal investigations. The course will enhance your knowledge of the digital traces you leave behind in your own life and how these traces can be used to assist in the investigation of crime and understanding criminal phenomena. You’ll develop your practical digital investigation skills through the use of computer laboratory classes using industry standard software.
learningOutcomes: Explain the importance of digital traces to modern forensic science and evaluate their value in the investigative process
Apply forensic science principles to digital traces and investigations
Recognise and apply the appropriate tools to identify, acquire and analyse digital traces for investigative purposes
Communicate complex findings from investigations and generate an expert witness report

65326.title: Digital and Cyber Crime
65326.description: This subject examines digital and cyber crime through the identification, analysis and interpretation of digital traces. Building on prior learning in digital trace and identity and digital forensics, you will explore how digitally mediated activities generate traces across a broad and distributed digital sphere of investigation. The subject considers selected forms of digital and cyber crime, with emphasis on the investigative value, limitations and uncertainty associated with online, device-based, multimedia and other digital traces. Through asynchronous learning activities and computer laboratory classes, you will develop foundational capabilities in working with digital traces and communicating findings in digital and cyber crime contexts.
learningOutcomes: Discuss key forms of digital and cyber crime and the digital traces associated with these activities.
Characterise the digital sphere of investigation and identify relevant sources of digital traces.
Extract and analyse information from digital traces in selected digital and cyber crime case contexts.
Integrate heterogeneous digital traces to reconstruct activities, assess links and evaluate uncertainty.
Synthesise and communicate investigative findings through written, visual and/or verbal reporting formats

65342.title: Crime Scene Investigation
65342.description: This subject deepens your understanding of forensic science principles at the crime scene, focusing on the concept of trace and its applications. You will develop practical skills in scene examination, with online learning materials on Canvas supplemented by hands-on sessions in the Crime Scene Simulation Facility. By integrating theoretical knowledge with practical experience, you will gain the foundational skills crucial to crime scene examination.
learningOutcomes: Apply relevant principles and techniques to the examination of physical and biological traces at a crime scene.
Develop a crime scene examination strategy.
Systematically search and document a crime scene through note taking, sketching and photography.
Recognise the items and/or traces at a crime scene that could be informative to an investigation and/or used as potential evidence in court.
Execute techniques to appropriately collect and preserve crime scene items and traces.

65409.title: Analytical Chemistry 2
65409.description:
This subject builds on the foundational concepts introduced in 65306 Analytical Chemistry 1, advancing students' theoretical knowledge and practical skills in analytical techniques relevant to industry and research. It emphasises the methods for the separation, identification, and quantification of chemical compounds and elements.

Key topics include method validation and quality assurance within analytical chemistry laboratories, with a focus on method development, theoretical principles, operational techniques, instrumentation, and practical applications of essential analytical techniques such as chromatography, mass spectrometry, and elemental spectroscopy.

Practical learning is a core component, offering hands-on experience in sample preparation techniques for each instrumental method. By integrating theory with practical skills, students develop proficiency in analytical chemistry, equipping them for careers in fields such as forensic science, clinical diagnostics, environmental monitoring, and pharmaceutical quality control.
learningOutcomes: Explain the theoretical concepts for each of the instrumental techniques and apply them to generate analytical data.
Use and apply various sample preparation methods appropriately and efficiently.
Design an experiment to analyse samples using appropriate instrumentation and critically interpret data.
Prepare a scientific journal report.
Collaborate effectively in a research team.

65411.title: Inorganic Chemistry 1
65411.description: This subject delves into the chemistry of transition metals, covering their structural properties, bonding theories, spectroscopy, magnetism, complex stability, and medical uses. Building on prior chemistry knowledge, it aids in developing models to understand transition metal compounds. The concepts serve as a foundation for further study in advanced materials and bioinorganic chemistry, essential for grasping the role of transition metals in biological systems and materials science.
learningOutcomes: Appropriately name transition metal compounds and describe the formation of transition metal complexes.
Apply basic theories to complete problem-solving tasks.
Synthesise fundamental principles to evaluate the use of ligands and complexes in the field of applications.
Conduct experiments to determine physical and chemical properties of transition metal compounds.
Work individually and collaboratively in the laboratory to produce, analyse and report on experimental findings.

65508.title: Organic Chemistry 2
65508.description: This subject advances your understanding of organic synthesis, applying functional group reactions and spectroscopy to create complex molecules. You'll explore the chemistry of benzene, heterocycles, carbanions, phenols, aryl halides, and learn about palladium-catalysed coupling and pericyclic reactions. There is an emphasis on practical applications of chemical synthesis. You'll also develop chemical research literacy, utilising tools like SciFinder to navigate chemical literature effectively. In the lab, you'll synthesise bioactive molecules through multi-step reactions, gaining hands-on experience in organic transformations.
learningOutcomes: Apply key concepts and mechanisms in organic chemistry.
Synthesise organic compounds in the laboratory using modern synthetic methods and strategies.
Apply analytical and problem-solving skills to investigate organic chemical synthesis.
Analyse experimental results and scholarly sources to communicate findings in the context of current research.
Manage workload and work effectively in a scientific context.

65509.title: Inorganic Chemistry 2
65509.description: This subject explores the chemistry of advanced inorganic materials, blending key theoretical concepts with real-world applications through research and case studies. You'll examine crystalline structures, bond theory, and the electrochemistry of inorganic materials. Building on foundational knowledge from previous studies, the course enhances your ability to model and understand the properties of these materials, crucial for advancements in technology and materials science.
learningOutcomes: Understand and apply fundamental principles of inorganic chemistry and crystallography.
Synthesise fundamental spectroscopic and crystallographic principles to evaluate the use of materials in the growing field of medical applications.
Conduct experiments to determine the physical, spectroscopic and crystallographic properties of advanced inorganic materials.
Evaluate experimental data and scholarly research and report findings effectively.
Work effectively both individually and collaboratively.

65544.title: Chemical Criminalistics
65544.description: In this subject you will apply advanced analytical chemistry and forensic reasoning to analyse, interpret and report on microtraces and chemical traces. This subject combines workplace-inspired practical classes with workshops that focus on forensic interpretation and the translation of research into practice. By the end of this subject, you’ll be adept at analysing, evaluating and reporting expert opinion on microtraces.
learningOutcomes: Illustrate the utility of chemical and microtraces in modern forensic science
Evaluate the results of forensic analyses in the context of a case scenario
Formulate and test hypotheses about the source and activity that created a trace
Employ the most appropriate sequences of analytical procedures to analyse the trace in a particular case scenario
Synthesise and communicate expert opinion to a lay audience in a variety of formats

65545.description: This subject delves into forensic toxicology, the science behind drugs and poisons in legal contexts. You'll learn about pharmacology and toxicology, including drug actions, bodily processes affecting substances, and symptoms linked to various drugs and poisons. Additionally, you'll study relevant state and federal laws in relation to both licit and illicit drugs. Practical sessions complement lectures, offering experience in analysing drugs and poisons in biological samples, equipping you with problem-solving skills essential for professional practice.
learningOutcomes: Explain the fundamental concepts of forensic toxicology and the legislation controlling the use of poisons and drugs.
Assess specific types of drugs and poisons and their pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics.
Conduct accurate laboratory and data analyses in forensic toxicology, interpret the results and infer their legal implications.
Collaborate effectively and contribute to formal recording of process.

65621.title: Environmental Chemistry
65621.description:
The four major subsystems of the Earth; atmosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere and biosphere, are all impacted by natural and anthropogenic changes. This subject introduces core chemical concepts and techniques required to monitor these changes. Concepts that you will gain knowledge of include acid-base chemistry, water quality and management, the greenhouse effect and photochemical reactions, organic and inorganic pollutants, toxicology, and sustainable chemical technologies.

The practical component will require you to perform environmental monitoring investigations, that utilise titrimetric and spectrophotometric analysis, as well as bulk data analysis and synthetic chemistry.
learningOutcomes: Conduct environmental chemical analyses using appropriate analytical techniques and mathematical methods.
Use laboratory equipment and instruments correctly and safely.
Communicate experimental data in an appropriate format.
Design and execute an appropriate research plan to investigate environmental chemistry problems.
Demonstrate professionalism in the laboratory.

65710.title: Foundations of Forensic Science
65710.description: This subject provides you with an introduction to forensic science for those with a scientific background, covering the investigative process from crime scene to lab analysis. You'll explore the evolution of forensic principles and their current applications, gaining insight into various sub-disciplines. The aim is to introduce you to forensic methodologies and concepts, enriching your understanding for further specialised study. Topics include crime scene procedures, forensic lab techniques, and documentation practices.
learningOutcomes: Scrutinise and discuss the foundational concepts of forensic science, both practical and theoretical
Critically analyse forensic traces, exhibits and case context to develop forensically relevant hypotheses and methodologies
Examine a crime scene and identify relevant evidence as part of the investigation
Evaluate complex case scenarios to gain a greater understanding of forensic processes and interpretation
Demonstrate high quality written and oral communication skills to convey scientific information to diverse audiences

65711.title: Forensic Inference and Interpretation
65711.description: This subject equips students with the skills to evaluate and interpret forensic traces using probabilistic inferences. Through practical examples, case studies, and data, students learn to apply logical reasoning and probability theory, including Bayesian networks and likelihood ratio approaches, to forensic evidence analysis. The aim is to impart comprehensive knowledge in evidence evaluation principles and their application in forensic contexts.
learningOutcomes: Understand the role of propositions and the case’s contextual information in the interpretation of traces in forensic science
Apply probability theory and Bayesian networks to the evaluation of the observations made on the traces and the results obtained from their analyses
Evaluate the value of traces in a wide range of scenarios encountered in forensic science (including source level and activity level propositions, database hits, and multiple traces)
Explain the value of the evidence in verbal and written forms without committing any logical fallacies

65712.title: Advanced Chemical Criminalistics

Students start with foundational concepts, progressing to advanced forensic reasoning with complex case analysis. Learning is self-directed via online modules on Canvas, supplemented by practicals and workshops that evolve from skill introduction to student-led complex cases. By the end, students are adept at managing forensic investigations, applying analytical techniques, interpreting advanced forensic evidence, and providing expert witness reports.
learningOutcomes: Use current forensic analytical procedures to accurately and effectively analyse traces
Formulate and test hypotheses about the source and activity that created a trace
Synthesise and communicate expert opinion and complex information to a wide range of audiences in a variety of formats
Interpret and evaluate complex traces in general and within the context of a complex case scenario

You will gain hands-on experience in detecting, analysing, interpreting and reporting biometric evidence through simulated case work in practical classes and associated workshops. You will also discuss privacy and ethical issues with the use of emerging biometric technologies.

Evaluate the results of forensic analyses in a variety of case scenarios
Explain complex forensic science concepts to diverse audiences in oral and written formats
Discuss emerging issues in biometrics and human identification sciences and their impact on shaping modern professional practice
Develop independent research skills, including formulating research questions, selecting the appropriate methodology, data collection and interpretation, and synthesising information

68037.title: Physics 1
68037.description: This foundational subject introduces you to calculus-based physics, covering mechanics (kinetics, dynamics and rotational), thermodynamics, electricity, fluid dynamics and waves. You'll learn measurement techniques, uncertainty analysis, and technical communication. The course aims to deepen your understanding of physical principles and their application in predictive modelling for engineered systems, while recognising model limitations through testing and analysis. Emphasising quantitative problem-solving using calculus and algebra, it provides a framework for modelling natural phenomena relevant to engineering design and analysis. You'll understand how physics both enables and constrains engineering, requiring compliance with physical laws and often demanding new insights or innovative model applications. The subject also offers a glimpse into the professional discipline of physics, developing analytical and observational skills, and technical communication, which are essential for innovation and will be further developed in advanced subjects. ical understanding and new physics plays a key role. This subject initiates the insights and attitudes relevant to this goal.
learningOutcomes: Solve fundamental physics problems based on understanding of the conceptual basis in mechanics, thermal physics, oscillations, waves, electricity and fluids.
Measure basic physical phenomena, analyse data and verify and apply mathematical models to describe and understand the natural world.
Demonstrate technical communication, project planning, team and time management skills.
Demonstrate understanding of the nature of physics as a professional discipline of great importance to engineering innovation.
68037.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have either completed 35010 Foundation Mathematics or are enrolled in or have completed 33130 Mathematical Modelling 1.

68038.title: Advanced Mathematics and Physics
68038.description: Delivered by the School of Mathematics and Physical Sciences, this subject equips second-year engineering and science undergraduates with the essential mathematical and physical knowledge needed in their fields. It offers a comprehensive set of mathematical tools for analysing electric and magnetic fields, circuits, and signal processing, alongside theoretical and applied quantum physics. The physics component introduces quantum physics, bridging from classical mechanics to its applications in semiconductor devices. Mathematics topics include vector calculus, complex variable functions, Divergence and Stokes theorems, Cauchy-Riemann equations, the Residue theorem, and Laplace transforms.
learningOutcomes: Solve core mathematical problems required in the engineering discipline;
Solve problems in applied and quantum physics using a range of mathematical and practical techniques;
Evaluate how the quantum properties of electrons in solids can be used to develop new electronic devices;
Interpret how the quantum and physical properties of materials have relevance to the practice of engineers and applied scientists.

68075.title: Advanced Materials
68075.description: This subject comprises two interrelated parts: the creation of nanostructures, nanomaterials, and nanodevices through deposition, growth, and self-assembly; and the practical application of their unique properties. You'll learn how to tailor these nanomaterials for diverse uses, including innovative construction materials, medical prosthetics, and advanced electronic devices.
learningOutcomes: Describe the latest developments and impact of nanoscale science in the engineering of materials and processes for industrial applications.
Apply fundamental knowledge and principles of materials science to address challenges in nanotechnology.
Identify and explain the unique properties and behaviours of nanomaterials.
Evaluate the role of standards with respect to nanomaterial performance.
Use technical terms relating to nanomaterials science and engineering.

68109.title: Advanced Communication Skills in Science
68109.description:
Advanced Communication Skills in Science provides you with the essential tools to effectively communicate scientific concepts in a rapidly evolving digital landscape.

You'll investigate topics and career opportunities tailored to your own personal and professional interests, practice professional communication strategies across a range of media and enhance your storytelling techniques to engage and inform different audiences. You'll also gain a deeper understanding of the political and cultural contexts of science in Australian and global contexts.

This subject is delivered through a sequence of self-praced online modules complemented with interactive workshops. These are designed to enhance your critical thinking, research, and communication skills to help you synthesise new and complex information and create original and effective multimedia content. With continuous feedback and support from teachers, this subject prepares you for professional growth and impactful science communication.

Critically evaluate information and sources to ensure accurate and ethical communication of scientific concepts.
Analyse diverse career opportunities in science and formulate strategies to enhance employability in local and global job markets.

Distil scientific evidence and community perspectives to produce balanced and in-depth analyses of scientific topics.

68110.title: Safe Laboratory Practice
68110.description: This subject equips you with essential knowledge and core skills you need to feel confident working in, and eventually managing, a scientific laboratory. You’ll be equipped with the skills to recognise hazards, assess risks, and apply the risk‑management frameworks commonly used in scientific environments. Alongside this, you’ll explore Workplace Health and Safety regulations and develop the leadership, communication, and ethical skills that help create a safe, positive, and productive lab culture. This includes learning how to delegate tasks, handle conflict, support team morale, and prepare for accreditation and compliance inspections. You’ll also solidify and finesse a range of fundamental laboratory skills that apply across many scientific fields. By the end of this subject, you will be adept at creating clear risk assessment and management plans, maintaining safe laboratory practices and confidently carrying out lab induction and management responsibilities.
learningOutcomes: Communicate effectively to a broad audience, including managers, colleagues and subordinates, in collaboration with a range of stakeholders to ensure an efficient, safe and productive laboratory environment.

Demonstrate and evaluate the role and responsibilities of a laboratory worker and manager, including fundamental laboratory skills, staff training and supervision, workplace health and safety (WHS) and risk assessment and management.

68111.title: Ethics of Science and Technology
68111.description: In an era when scientific advancements increasingly shape our lives, understanding the ethical landscapes behind research and practice is vital to ensure science and technology continue to serve the public good. Ethics of Science and Technology explores the foundations for ethical science and technologies, equipping you with the essential tools for critical engagement and ethical decision-making. Grounded in UNESCO’s global ethics frameworks, the subject begins with core principles of individual and organisational ethics relevant for all career journeys. You will then select one specialised domain to further deepen your expertise. Through contemporary case studies and reflective practice, you will develop your skills to think ethically, act with integrity, and lead responsibly, to promote socially beneficial innovation.

Apply ethical reasoning to complex dilemmas in research, innovation, and organisational practice.
Communicate ethical positions effectively integrating stakeholder perspectives and professional standards.
Demonstrate specialised knowledge in one domain of applied ethics.

The course allows you to critically evaluate the theories and methods used to develop key science policies. Additionally, it fosters an understanding of the complexities behind decision-making in public policy, highlighting the interplay between scientific, economic, social, and political factors.

Identify relevant regulatory frameworks and governing bodies in Australian and global contexts.

68316.description: This subject explores the use of AC electronic circuits for precision measurement and control, extending to microwave frequencies relevant to quantum technologies. It builds on foundational electricity studies, assuming proficiency in calculus and complex numbers. You'll develop practical and theoretical skills in applying electronic circuits in the lab, focusing on measurement and control techniques. The course treats op-amps and passive components as fundamental elements for constructing complex measurement systems and signal processing, discussing basic and advanced techniques within the context of sophisticated applications.
learningOutcomes: Explain and apply the basic concepts of electronics and circuit operation, including op-amp applications, measurement and control
Construct, test and troubleshoot circuits with reference to schematic diagrams
Design and develop circuits to address measurement and control application requirements
Document, analyse and reflect on your practical work by maintaining an accurate and sufficiently complete labbook record that can be understood and verified by others with relevant expertise

68320.title: Nanofabrication and Nanocharacterization Techniques
68320.description: This subject addresses the high-precision techniques required for characterising and fabricating nano-materials and devices, which are core enablers of nanotechnology and materials physics. You'll learn about nano-scale fabrication techniques, such as chemical vapour deposition, reactive ion etching, electron beam lithography, and focused ion beam microscopy. You will also learn about nano-resolution imaging and analysis such as electron microscopy, scanning tunnelling microscopy, and advanced fluorescence microscopy. You'll explore the application of these techniques in various scientific and technological fields, stay abreast of recent advancements, and gain hands-on experience with a range of imaging, analysis and nanofabrication methods.
learningOutcomes: Apply theory and working principles to the practice of nano scale fabrication and analysis.
Competently operate a Scanning Electron Microscope.
Analyse experimental analytical microscopy results and prepare a formal scientific report.
Interpret data collected from nano scale analysis techniques.
Use nano scale analysis techniques in nanotechnology and nanoscience practical research applications.

68413.title: Quantum Physics
68413.description: Expanding on waves and classical mechanics, this subject investigates the distinct behaviour of the atomic world compared to the macroscopic world we experience daily. You will learn the conceptual and mathematical basis of quantum mechanics, including quantum state vectors and operations. Using this knowledge, you will explore key phenomena in quantum physics, such as bound states, quantum tunnelling, and entanglement. The subject culminates with applications to quantum technologies, focusing particularly on qubits and quantum computation. This subject provides you with fundamental material for understanding many areas of physics and chemistry, as well as contemporary applications relevant to nanotechnologists.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate how quantum-mechanical systems, states and observables are represented by mathematical entities and analyse the measurement process and the time-evolution of states.
Solve the Schrödinger equation for common one-dimensional situations e.g. the quantum well, the tunnel barrier and the harmonic oscillator.
Apply the most common quantum-mechanical operators, especially the Hamiltonian, the position, momentum, angular momentum and the ladder operators.
Calculate and apply the stationary states and energies of the unperturbed hydrogen atom.
Apply core principles of quantum mechanics to analyse the physical basis of quantum computing, including the behaviour of qubits and basic quantum operations.

68414.title: Advanced Mechanics
68414.description: Advancing from foundational mechanics and mathematical methods, this subject delves into complex classical mechanics topics, including rotational dynamics, coupled oscillators, fundamentals of Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formalisms, and Special Relativity. The focus is on developing advanced problem-solving skills, equipping you with the ability to tackle intricate mechanical systems.
learningOutcomes: Develop problem solving skills in the area of statics and dynamics of particles and solid bodies, oscillating systems, motion in potential and force fields
Apply mathematical skills to understand mechanical systems, including analysis of rotational motion of solid bodies and Lagrangian method for mechanical systems
Develop problem solving presentation skills in a peer audience environment
Communicate physics concepts and problem solving arguments in a structured way

68416.title: Computational Methods
68416.description: This subject introduces the theory and practice of numerical and computational methods for solving mathematical and physical problems. You will study key techniques including optimisation, numerical integration and Monte Carlo methods, matrix methods, and the numerical solution of ordinary and partial differential equations, with an emphasis on practical implementation in Python. These methods are applied to modelling and simulating complex physical systems through project work, with applications drawn from areas such as quantum mechanics, statistical mechanics, electrodynamics, and molecular dynamics. You will develop skills in computational modelling, data analysis, visualisation, and professional communication of results.
learningOutcomes: Describe the main algorithms for solving a range of important problems in maths, physics, and related areas
Design and implement code to solve a range of problems numerically
Explain why various numerical algorithms work, and what their limitations are
Communicate results and information in a professional and competent way appropriate to the discipline

68492.title: Principles of Pharmaceutical Science
68492.description: This subject equips you with an understanding of pharmaceutical science, focusing on the physicochemical principles that underpin drug formulation and delivery. You'll gain knowledge of drug administration routes, dosage design, and factors influencing drug solubility and dissolution, alongside predictive models for these properties. You'll also explore drug delivery systems, including colloids, emulsions, and creams, and their pharmaceutical applications. Your learning is reinforced through case studies that illustrate the practical application of theoretical concepts.
learningOutcomes: Apply chemical principles including solubility, rates of dissolution and diffusion to drug dosage forms
Devise a strategy to perform accelerated stability studies to determine shelf life of dosage forms
Retrieve and analyse the scientific literature in the context of coarse and colloidal dosage forms
Develop written communication skills to convey information to specific audiences
Work as an effective and reliable team member, demonstrating the necessary organisation and planning skills, collaboration and project management

68493.title: Advanced Pharmaceutical Science
68493.description: From early preformulation studies to advanced drug delivery systems, this course provides you with specialist expertise to address challenges in pharmaceutical research and industry.  In Advanced Pharmaceutical Science, you bring together the principles of pharmaceutics, biopharmaceutics and pharmacokinetics through an applied learning experience. You develop skills in the design and evaluation of conventional oral dosage forms, modified-release systems, parenteral formulations, and alternative routes of administration including transdermal, mucosal, pulmonary, and nasal delivery. You are also introduced to advanced and targeted drug delivery technologies and biological products.  Through hands-on laboratory sessions using industry-standard methods, combined with interactive workshops, you apply scientific principles to real-world challenges in dosage form design and development. Emphasis is placed on quality control testing, in vitro product performance evaluation, and the relationship between formulation and drug bioperformance, in alignment with Australian and international pharmaceutical regulatory standards. The use of in silico predictive tools to simulate and predict drug bioperformance is also covered. Collectively, these learning activities enable you to develop the scientific knowledge and practical skills required for a career in pharmaceutical sciences and related industries.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of the scientific and technological aspects of the design, manufacture, and evaluation of drug dosage forms and delivery systems.
Identify emerging technologies in drug delivery, including nanotechnology, biotechnology-derived products, and understand the principles underlying their formulation design.
Perform laboratory-based experiments to evaluate the in vitro performance and quality control of dosage forms, including preformulation studies.
Collaborate effectively in team-based settings to plan and evaluate drug product performance, demonstrating leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills.

Apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills to interpret laboratory data and propose potential improvements in formulation or processing, with the goal of enhancing the performance, safety, and quality of drug products.

68494.title: Cosmetics and Nutraceuticals
68494.description: The course in Cosmetics and Nutraceuticals offers a comprehensive introduction to two rapidly growing sectors within the cosmetics and nutraceutical industry. You will develop a strong scientific foundation in the formulation, evaluation, and commercialization of skincare and haircare products. The course begins by exploring the anatomy and physiology of skin and hair, the function of key cosmetic ingredients, and the processes behind product development. It further introduces innovative technologies such as nanotechnology, artificial intelligence, and green chemistry, alongside current trends like personalized skincare and sustainable beauty solutions. The nutraceutical segment focuses on functional foods and plant-derived health products, emphasizing their physiological benefits, formulation challenges, and enhancement of bioavailability. You will also study drug–nutraceutical interactions, safety considerations, and the regulatory frameworks that govern product approval and market access. Career prospects across the cosmetic and food sectors are also discussed. The course includes laboratory sessions where you will design, prepare, and evaluate your own cosmetic and nutraceutical formulations. Real-world case studies, quizzes, and a final lab assessment support applied learning. By the end of the course, you will be equipped with essential industry skills in product classification, stability and efficacy testing, formulation science, and regulatory compliance. Emphasis is placed on understanding ingredient interactions, the role of emulsifiers and surfactants, and consumer-centered product design.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of scientific principles behind cosmetic science and nutraceuticals, including skin/hair physiology, formulation techniques, and sources of functional foods.
Design and develop innovative cosmetic and nutraceutical products by applying formulation science, nanotechnology, and green chemistry approaches.
Perform laboratory-based preparation, characterization, and evaluation of cosmetic and nutraceutical formulations, and interpret results using appropriate scientific techniques and quality criteria.
Collaborate effectively in team-based settings to plan, execute, and evaluate product development tasks, demonstrating leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills.
Apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills to propose evidence-based improvements to product formulations, considering current research, technological advances, and consumer needs

68495.title: Inorganic Pharmaceuticals
68495.description: Inorganic chemistry is essential for understanding the role of metals in pharmaceuticals and medical diagnostics. This subject introduces the fundamentals of transition metal chemistry, including coordination chemistry, electron configurations, ligand behavior, and molecular geometry. Crystal field theory is used to relate electronic structure to key properties such as stability and reactivity. This provides the foundation for exploring pharmaceutical applications of metal-based compounds, including metallodrugs, chelation therapy for heavy metal poisoning, and metal-based drug delivery systems, with selected examples of diagnostic agents such as contrast media and radiopharmaceuticals. Through the practical program, you will develop core laboratory and analytical skills, including observation, measurement, analysis, teamwork, and problem-solving in pharmaceutical contexts.
learningOutcomes: Understand the role of inorganic chemistry in pharmaceuticals and selected medical diagnostic applications.
Apply key principles of inorganic chemistry to explain the structure and behavior of metal-based compounds.
Apply quantitative skills to solve chemistry-related problems.
Demonstrate proficiency in laboratory and analytical skills relevant to pharmaceutical inorganic chemistry.

68513.title: Nanoscale and Quantum Photonics
68513.description: This subject enhances your understanding of light and its interactions with matter, crucial for careers in optics R&D, optical engineering, and related fields like telecommunications and biomedical optics. Building on introductory waves and optics, it employs vector calculus and differential equations to examine field interactions with matter, highlighting the significance of nanoscale field distributions in photonic components. You will be introduced to quantum photonics concepts with real-world applications such as quantum communication.  Your understanding will be enhanced through lab experiments and computer simulations.
learningOutcomes: Apply the fundamental principles of electromagnetic waves to straightforward modern optical systems.
Identify and explain the underlying optical principles in naturally occurring and complicated cutting-edge optical systems.
Generalise themes and techniques and apply them to a wider, multidisciplinary context (e.g. superposition)
Achieve a given level of competence in the use of various optical techniques and equipment.
Effectively manage a scientific investigation from designing the experiment to defending the results and interpretation.

A substantial laboratory and project component provides hands-on experience with electronic and optical equipment, data analysis and scientific reporting, reinforcing theoretical concepts through practical investigation.

Conduct and accurately record measurements using modern equipment and analysis techniques in solid state physics.
Explain and calculate the operating performance of semiconductor and quantum devices.

Analyse and solve problems relevant to real-world quantum information processing hardware systems

69363.title: Shaping Policies for the Future
69363.description: This subject equips you with a critical understanding of how public policy, shaped by scientific, economic, social, and political factors, affects health, wellbeing and sustainability. You'll study the creation of evidence-based science policies, including climate action and vaccination programs, and learn about the regulatory frameworks and authorities that govern science in Australia and internationally. You’ll develop a critical understanding of the theories and practices behind developing some of the most influential evidence-based science policies. You will also develop an appreciation of the complexity of decision-making processes in the public sphere, where the formulation of public policies depends on a variety of scientific, economic, social, and political forces.
learningOutcomes: Appreciate the influence public policy has on the health and wellbeing of people and the environment.
Critically analyse the established scientific theories and practices that underpin evidence-based policies.
Develop an integrated understanding of how science interplays with economic, social, environmental, and political influences during policy development
Identify relevant regulatory frameworks and governing bodies in Australian and global contexts

69367.description: This subject delves into the analysis and management of big data, an exponentially growing presence in our lives, with projections of reaching 180 zettabytes by 2025. You'll learn introductory data analysis through graphical and statistical techniques and tackle privacy and ethical issues in managing large datasets, including in health, ecology, and sustainability. The course also addresses sovereignty and informed consent, particularly concerning Indigenous Australians, highlighting big data's potential to transform research and its associated ethical considerations.
learningOutcomes: Conduct analyses and interpret findings to leverage data for science applications.
Articulate key governance and accountability requirements for interconnected science data management, including privacy and ethics.
Evaluate the critical importance of adhering to Indigenous Data Sovereignty (IDS) and appropriate privacy protocols for working with and for Indigenous groups.

69369.title: Sustainability Practices in Industry
69369.description: The transition to a sustainable future requires collaboration between industry, government and other stakeholders to achieve sectoral change. The guiding vision for action on sustainability comes from the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). This subject introduces you to a six-step transition management planning framework to identify sustainability practices that are context-specific and contribute towards achieving the SDGs. The framework covers system analysis, stakeholder engagement, foresighting, option development and selection, implementation and evaluation. You'll be able to apply the framework in any industry. Case studies from industries such as energy, manufacturing, agriculture and the built environment demonstrate practical applications. You will learn to apply the framework in your own context by working through each of the steps in an individual project on a system of your choosing.
learningOutcomes: Build capacity to investigate and advocate opportunities for organisations to develop and implement sustainability practices
Apply transition management planning to identify, prioritise, select and implement industry-specific sustainability practices
Contextualise, synthesise, and evaluate sustainability practices in order to influence future implementation

69501.title: Infection and Immune Diagnostics
69501.description: Infectious diseases are one of the world’s leading causes of death. Accurate and rapid diagnostics for pathogens are critical to treatment and control because if we cannot detect it then we cannot treat it. This subject equips you with vital knowledge and skills to tackle infectious diseases. You will learn to identify and understand different human pathogens—bacterial, viral, fungal, and parasitic— how they cause disease, how our immune system responds, and key antimicrobial treatments and vaccines. You will gain practical hands-on-experience using modern clinical, molecular and serological diagnostic methods to identify causative pathogens in clinical samples and evaluate the most suitable antimicrobial treatment. Finally, you will design and assess your own diagnostic assay, honing your research and critical thinking abilities. This practical approach ensures that you are prepared to contribute effectively to infectious disease control.
learningOutcomes: Describe the major types of human pathogens including the disease they cause, their epidemiology, pathogenesis, treatment and prevention, and methods of detection (including antimicrobial sensitivity testing).
Work safely in a PC2 laboratory and implement microbial diagnostic approaches, methods and technologies to identify the causative pathogen(s) in clinical specimens.

Apply research methodology, including critically analysing scientific literature, to design novel diagnostic assays and evaluate its performance against other diagnostic approaches for infectious diseases.
Critically evaluate and interpret results from laboratory investigations, and where appropriate, reflect and provide suggestions to problem solve and troubleshoot experiments.
Communicate scientific knowledge and findings to a range of relevant scientific audience.

69503.description: This capstone subject provides an opportunity for you to integrate and build on the disciplinary knowledge acquired in your course through a collaborative, non‑laboratory research project. Working in teams, you will investigate a topic aligned with your study theme, drawing on evidence‑based inquiry, critical analysis, and disciplinary research practices. The subject emphasises professional teamwork, project planning, and the development of advanced communication skills. Guided workshops support you through each stage of the research process, from defining a question to analysing findings. The subject culminates in a conference‑style presentation event where you will showcase your research outcomes to peers, staff, and invited guests.

69508.title: Clinical Trials: Evidence and Design
69508.description: This subject provides you with a thorough understanding of clinical trials, a cornerstone in determining the safety and efficacy of medical treatments and a fundamental aspect of evidence-based medicine. You'll explore various aspects of clinical trial design and how they influence the robustness of evidence generated. You'll also develop the ability to interpret clinical trial data, a skill crucial for pharmaceutical development, clinical practice, and health policy-making, ensuring you can contribute to drug development, patient care, and the regulatory approval process.
learningOutcomes: Explain the context of clinical trials and why they are used
Identify different elements of trial design and their associated advantages and limitations
Evaluate evidence from clinical trials with reference to the study design, reported statistics and study objectives
Describe how evidence from clinical trials can be translated into treatments, policy and clinical guidelines

69514.description: This subject equips you with an understanding of how tissue samples are analysed for diagnostic purposes in contemporary labs. You'll learn about normal tissue morphology, routine histological processing, and the importance of considering patient backgrounds and cultural diversity in pathology. The course introduces molecular biology and diagnostic techniques used in research and diagnostic pathology. 69516.title: Infection and Immune Diagnostics
69516.description: Infectious diseases are one of the world’s leading causes of death. Accurate and rapid diagnostics for pathogens are critical to treatment and control because if we cannot detect it then we cannot treat it. This subject equips you with vital knowledge and skills to tackle infectious diseases. You will learn to identify and understand different human pathogens—bacterial, viral, fungal, and parasitic— how they cause disease, how our immune system responds, and key antimicrobial treatments and vaccines. You will gain practical hands-on-experience using modern clinical, molecular and serological diagnostic methods to identify causative pathogens in clinical samples and evaluate the most suitable antimicrobial treatment. Finally, you will design and assess your own diagnostic assay, honing your research and critical thinking abilities. This practical approach ensures that you are prepared to contribute effectively to infectious disease control.
learningOutcomes: Describe the major types of human pathogens including the disease they cause, their epidemiology, pathogenesis, treatment and prevention, and methods of detection (including antimicrobial sensitivity testing)
Work safely in a PC2 laboratory and implement microbial diagnostic approaches, methods and technologies to identify the causative pathogen(s) in clinical specimens

Apply research methodology, including critically analysing scientific literature, to design novel diagnostic assays and evaluate its performance against other diagnostic approaches for infectious diseases
Critically evaluate and interpret results from laboratory investigations, and where appropriate, reflect and provide suggestions to problem solve and troubleshoot experiments
Communicate scientific knowledge and findings to a range of relevant scientific audience

70102.title: Foundations of Law
70102.description:
This subject explores the origins of the Australian legal system and examines how its present operation is informed by its historical and cultural contexts. You will examine key ideas that underpin legal institutions, including democracy, sovereignty, the rule of law, and the separation of powers. Using several critical legal perspectives, you will also examine how the law impacts on different social groups, including those that have been historically marginalised from society’s power structures.

 The subject introduces you to the primary sources of law – judicial decisions and statutes - and you will develop key skills in analysing judge-made law and in statutory interpretation.

 Your learning in this subject will be informed by diverse academic literature, case studies, group work, student-lead discussion, and skills-based instruction on legal research. Together, the research skills and critical legal thinking taught in this subject will build a foundation for the successful completion of later subjects in your law degree.
learningOutcomes: Explain foundational legal concepts and their historical and cultural contexts.
Analyse the classification and resolution of disputes within legal frameworks and broader societal contexts.
Apply critical thinking in legal analysis to evaluate different perspectives on a variety of contemporary legal issues.
Conduct comprehensive legal research using and evaluating a variety of primary and secondary sources and methodologies.
Demonstrate integrated legal skills to independently address legal questions.

70103.description:
This subject explores the critical role that legal ethics play in shaping the profession and the broader justice system. You will examine barriers to accessing justice while also considering the reforms underway to eradicate such barriers. You'll gain insights into the conduct rules and responsibilities that govern legal practitioners and how these might be applied to members of the profession, as well as the frameworks to help you integrate ethical considerations into your decision-making processes.

Learning in this subject is dynamic and interactive. You'll engage in a series of collaborative activities, including regular small group discussion-based seminars. Through workshops on legal writing skills and peer review writing exercises, you will also focus on developing the legal writing skills you’ll need in the legal profession.

Recognise ethical issues and discuss the relationship between personal and professional attitudes, values and approaches to decision making, developing their own ethical framework.
Plan and complete a variety of critical legal writing tasks using academic styles, structures and expression, supported by accurate referencing.
Respond appropriately in group discussions, identifying different roles within the group dynamic and practising active listening; developing strategies and skills to collaborate effectively.
