83882.description: This subject advances your skills from 'Foundations in Patternmaking and Construction 1', focusing on interpreting complex fashion designs into tangible garments. You'll master creating intricate garment components, both in flat patterns and three-dimensional forms.

Learn the value and importance of taking risks, decision making and challenging boundaries.
Self-direct learning and in-class participation demonstrating progress each week.

84000.description: The Product Design program emphasises international networking through site visits, excursions, study tours and collaborative studios to build a global perspective within an individual's practice. The Global Studio provides students with the opportunity to immerse themselves in another design culture, developing creative as well as professional maturity. Global Studios offer students the opportunity to gain an understanding of the issues and practices of product and industrial design from a perspective beyond the local professional experience. A combination of connections between international design schools, design institutions, companies, and, or practitioners; are engaged as appropriate for the Global Studio project.
learningOutcomes: Prepare for and conduct international travel in an organised and professional way.
Design Collaboratively in teams.
Appreciate and better understand international perspectives on design innovation.
Understand the evolving relationship between design, business, and technology in an international context.

84711.title: User-centred Design
84711.description: This subject equips you with user-centred design skills, focusing on understanding end-user needs and limitations to create products with optimal usability and performance. You'll analyse users, their environments, and circumstances, employing interventions, testing, and experimentation grounded in research. The goal is to foster creative exploration, analysis, and reflection, using design thinking and prototyping to innovate solutions that align with ergonomic principles and commercial objectives.
learningOutcomes: Access and interpret ergonomics and anthropometric data to inform product design.
Apply design methods to develop and integrate product designs, considering human factors and systems context.
Test and report on design concepts and progress through practical modelling and sketching techniques.
Understand and apply the principles of structure, form, and material in product design.
Produce professional design communication, including detailed production drawings.

84712.title: Product Engineering
84712.description: This subject introduces you to key manufacturing principles, materials, and processes vital for new product design, including mechanics and electronics where relevant. You'll engage in projects that apply design thinking to explore technical solutions for future-oriented products, systems, and interfaces. You'll develop the ability to innovate and experiment, honing design skills such as sketching and prototyping, to create ecologically responsible and technically sound products that are intuitive for the end-user. Collaboration is also a critical component, ensuring your designs are both feasible and operationally effective.
learningOutcomes: Establish the fundamental knowledge of manufacturing and engineering as it applies to product design.
Apply engineering drafting standards relevant to product manufacture.
Refine design attributes through iterative design development.
Justify and articulate the links between concept, design, manufacture and commercialisation.
Integrate engineering elements into an original design aesthetic.

84811.title: Smart Design
84811.description: This subject prepares you to thrive amidst rapid technological and social shifts by developing 'smart' and innovative products, systems, and environments. Leveraging skills and design thinking from earlier studies, you'll delve into the functionality of products and their sociocultural impact. You'll gain a deep understanding of the technologies that power products and facilitate human interaction and control, equipping you to create solutions that resonate with contemporary societal needs.
learningOutcomes: Identify opportunities within socio-cultural and technological contexts through design thinking.
Apply design methods and translate them into a Product Design outcome.
Demonstrate a rudimentary understanding of electronics and microprocessor programming in relation to Product Design.
Understand appropriate integration of micro-controller and sensor technologies in the development of functional experience prototypes.
Develop design proposals iteratively through exploratory and experimental design development methods relevant to Product Design.
Manage complex design projects through commitment to studio and design iteration.

84812.title: Product Design Major Studio
84812.description: This subject hones your understanding of the product designer's role and the significance of design-driven innovation. You'll explore the synergy between design and business through a research-supported design project, online content, and active studio participation. Innovation, as a market differentiator, demands strategic and culturally attuned design practices that transcend traditional manufacturing norms. You'll consider ethics, intellectual property, and design-led research, equipping you for graduation or advanced design studies.
learningOutcomes: Understand how to innovate for socio-cultural and technological change.
Use research methods and data analysis to improve design performance and understand knowledge-directed design practice.
Use design methods and techniques to explore, reflect, improve and refine concepts, and create prototypes and three-dimensional representations to a high standard.
Understand academic writing relevant to product design.
Communicate and present product design research methods and product designs to a high standard.

84813.title: Product Design Professional Communication
84813.description: This subject sharpens your ability to professionally communicate design intent, a crucial skill for engaging clients, team members, and stakeholders throughout the design process. You'll master techniques specific to product design, creating persuasive presentation materials that visually convey research and innovation outcomes. You'll learn to select and apply the most effective communication methods for any given scenario, deepening your understanding of the vital role communication plays in professional practice.
learningOutcomes: Develop effective use of methods to generate innovative product design outcomes.
Exercise critical reflection and evaluation on communication process.
Prepare and deliver well-structured presentations that clearly communicate design work.
Consolidate a number of presentation techniques in a cohesive and sophisticated manner.
Document and communicate the evolution of design work through a considered and cohesive portfolio.

84909.title: Product Design and Sustainability
84909.description: This subject addresses the critical need for sustainable design amidst significant environmental and technological shifts. You'll explore strategies to enhance the sustainability of products and their life cycles, considering the materials, form, and influence on human behaviour. Engaging in studio projects, you'll craft product design proposals rooted in values that foster healthier relationships within our planet's ecosystems, reflecting a commitment to sustainable principles and positive adaptation to ecological feedback.
learningOutcomes: Display an in-depth understanding of the underlying sustainability drivers in context
Identify and evaluate relevant sustainability strategies for product design applications
Demonstrate critical thinking on the use of sustainability strategies within different contexts
Demonstrate skills in the development, explanation and realisation of research-led product design responses to sustainability challenges in the current context
Discuss and debate co-operatively and professionally with their peers and staff on topics within sustainability.

84910.title: Analogue and Digital UX
84910.description:
This subject is about designing for optimal user experiences (UX) when engaging with interactive products, which includes the physical and mechanical ('analogue') aspects as well as the interaction through digital elements such as screens and controls.
The lectures in this subject present a background of historical aspects of interaction between people and technologies, as well as exploring the application of multiple sensory and expressive modalities, and various modes of interaction and communication as part of the user experience. This is practiced in depth through the development of case studies, and a design project, working in teams in studios.
In the design project, a research-based approach is applied: in the first phase through design research methods such as domain research, participatory design and user studies, and finally in the implementation phase through user testing, iterative development, and validation of the interfaces.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate an in-depth understanding of all aspects of UX and Interactive Product Design.
Identify, evaluate and apply appropriate Interactive Product Design and UX tools and techniques.
Study and apply design research methods to appropriately inform the design processes for interactive products and environments
Collaborate in teams to address complex and open-ended design challenges for Interaction and UX
Communicate Interactive Product Design and UX work to a professional standard, in writing, demonstrations and presentations.

84911.title: Advanced Manufacturing Technology
84911.description: This subject immerses you in the latest manufacturing processes and digital technologies that are reshaping industry norms. As a future designer, you'll understand how these advancements alter work, industry organisation, and your role in relation to products, consumers, and producers. You'll learn about the potential of new manufacturing tech, examine shifts in business models and production systems, and explore product design changes, equipping you for a forward-thinking career in product design.
learningOutcomes: Design for a diverse range of industrial additive manufacturing technologies.
Use prototyping as a key research method to work successfully with both industrial and consumer-grade additive manufacturing machinery.
Demonstrate an understanding of associated digital technologies, such as robotic 3D printing, parametric CAD and 3D scanning.
Understand the implications of advanced manufacturing as a component of industry 4.0 for product development and production systems.
Develop professional written and visual presentation skills to communicate technical design tasks.

85001.title: The Bio Kitchen
85001.description:
In order to combat climate change there is an urgent need to transition from unsustainable manufacturing and consumption practises, and to develop sustainable materials and systems that promote ecological resilience, repair, and that support the health of our planet. For designers, the transformative possibilities of bio-based materials can offer alternative approaches for thinking through the future of fashion, consumer products, systems of manufacturing, as well as architecture and the built environment.

The Bio Kitchen provides students with an understanding of bio-based material futures. This is a hands-on laboratory where students learn design principles and practices for undertaking materials research, using these to speculate on the possible social and scientific applications for bio-based materials and biotechnologies in the future. In this design lab the kitchen operates as both a vibrant system and as a practical studio space for futures-oriented material thinking. Students will undertake experiments with starches, bioplastics, agar, gels, protein and cellulose manipulations, with the opportunity to view and interact with material recipe demonstrations, before recreating, improvising and expanding on these experimental recipes themselves.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate foundational knowledge of bio-based materials and their potential future applications.
Plan and conduct observational, engaged, and iterative bio-based materials testing.
Communicate design ideas and systems thinking through visual and verbal methods.
Articulate the nature of a situated context through sensitive experimental design research.

85202.title: Designing Social Change
85202.description: The subject will introduce social and service design concepts and tools to support students’ understanding of and response to social change scenarios. Students will be encouraged to become problem seekers, who can use their design skills to respond proactively to society's problems. Students will interrogate design quality from a social design perspective and will learn key principles of inclusive design. The subject will introduce practical and creative social design research approaches, such as how to design and facilitate a workshop and collaborate with, rather than design for, people. Students will also learn novel/ creative ways of presenting social research in service of social change, including how to write and present a social design report based on industry models.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate an introductory conceptual and practical understanding of concepts and tools used in social and service design.
Articulate the nature of a situated context through sensitive experimental design research
Generate meaningful insights for social design outcomes.
Develop confidence in communicating design ideas and reflecting on feedback in collaborative contexts

85302.title: Social Media Cultures
85302.description: This subject explores the profound impact of the internet and social media on society, examining how they've redefined presence and interaction. You'll critically analyse these platforms as networks of power and technology, learning to craft impactful design interventions. The course focuses on interaction designs that enable digital connectivity and cultural responses to these designs. Your personal experiences with social media will enrich our collective understanding of online cultures. Combining desk and design research, you'll engage reflectively in the environments you're studying. Your assessments will include designed responses reflecting your research insights.
learningOutcomes: Explain the histories behind the design of current social media platforms
Identify critical perspectives on the cultural impacts of social media platforms
Articulate the nature of a situated context through sensitive experimental design research
Develop design interventions into social media platforms that enhance collective well-being

85502.title: Researching Design Histories
85502.description: This subject underscores the importance of history in comprehending today's design landscape. By studying design histories and concepts, you'll articulate your work persuasively and make informed, ethical decisions regarding products, services, and technologies. Historical knowledge equips you to evaluate and critique your design practice and the broader industry. You'll develop a critical understanding of design forms and practices within their historical contexts and hone your visual analysis skills. Additionally, the course enhances your academic research, writing, and communication abilities, laying a foundation for your future academic and professional pursuits. It is strongly recommended that Design students complete this subject in their first year.
learningOutcomes: Describe and critically analyse a range of design artefacts, drawing on observational and conceptual frameworks.

Develop research skills, analyse data from a range of appropriate sources (including museum collections and academic literature), and use academic writing and referencing to acknowledge those sources.
Clearly communicate design's relationship to historical contexts, including social, political, cross-cultural and environmental histories.

85503.title: Thinking Through Design
85503.description: This subject is designed to shape your mindset and conduct as a designer, offering an insider's view of the field and challenging existing notions. You'll learn universal design processes and research techniques, alongside strategies for teamwork, problem definition, context research, creative ideation, proposal evaluation and argument visualisation. It also acquaints you with the School of Design's demanding and autonomous learning environment. It is strongly recommended that Design students complete this subject in their first year.

Critically reflect on personal strengths and weaknesses, and make connections between creativity, critical analysis, and reflective practice.
Demonstrate the application of curiosity, experimentation and risk taking in design.
Show cultural awareness and sensitivity towards Indigenous perspectives through project site research.

85840.title: Biodesign
85840.description: In response to the climate crisis and the need for sustainable industry transformation, this subject equips designers with an understanding of biosynthesis and cell metabolism, essential for integrating biology into design innovation. It offers design students insight into emerging biotechnologies and introduces science students to design methodologies. You will work both independently and in interdisciplinary teams to conceive and execute a speculative biodesign project grounded in scientific plausibility.

Apply design principles and methods to biotechnologies
Collaborate in an interdisciplinary context and work effectively in teams
Communicate visually and verbally using design and scientific data
Understand the nature and demands of complex project briefs
Connect scientific research to design generation and development
Undertake advanced reflective practice and understand the importance of this

85843.title: Design Project Realisation
85843.description:
This subject involves the production and realisation of a significant design project in your chosen discipline of Fashion and Textiles, Product Design or Visual Communication. Building on the direction established in Autumn, you will refine your project through continued research, testing and critical decision making.

In a studio setting, you will develop and resolve advanced design outcomes and produce a refined set of artefacts appropriate to your discipline, such as product prototypes, communication artefacts, fashion garments and innovative textiles. You will document your process and communicate the value and intent of your project through written, visual and material forms that meet high professional and academic standards.

Students also hone their skills through specialised workshops to amplify their voice as skilled design practitioners and to showcase their Honours project through captivating photographs, videos, documents and events.

Throughout the semester, you will manage the practical and professional demands of a major project, including planning, time management and relevant stakeholder engagement, guided by an ethical and sustainable approach to design decision making.
learningOutcomes: Independently develop and apply practice-based design research methods to refine a major project
Test and resolve complex design outcomes through iterative experimentation that challenges disciplinary conventions and demonstrates advanced technical, aesthetic, and technological capability
Effectively communicate the processes and value of design research and outcomes through presentations, prototypes, artefacts and documentation that reflect professional and scholarly standards
Deliver a major design project using strong project management and context appropriate, ethical, sustainable, and professionally aligned decision making

requisite.text: Admission into C09131 Bachelor of Design (Honours)

85845.title: Design Research Studio
85845.description:
This subject immerses you in the exploration, development, and documentation of a substantial design project within your chosen discipline of Fashion and Textiles, Product Design, or Visual Communication. Through hands on activities and workshops, you will develop and apply a range of practice-based design research methods to investigate your initial ideas and define the scope of your project. You will refine your concepts through independent research and experimentation, leading to a set of innovative prototypes that propose the trajectory of your major project.

Throughout the semester, you will develop your ability to articulate the intent, value and significance of your designs. You will communicate these ideas through refined design documentation and professional presentations aligned with your design discipline. You will also explore approaches for engaging respectfully with place based and cultural considerations as part of responsible contemporary design practice.
 
By leading the development of a substantial design project, you will strengthen your capacity to plan and manage a complex creative undertaking and begin to articulate your emerging position within your professional design field.
learningOutcomes: Apply practice-based design research methods to initiate and frame a major design project.
Develop and test design outcomes through iterative experimentation that challenges disciplinary conventions and demonstrates emerging technical, aesthetic, and technological capability.
Effectively communicate the intent, context, processes, and value of design research and outcomes through presentations, prototypes, artefacts and documentation.
Initiate a major design project and professionally manage each phase of its development.
Reflect on ethical engagement practices to work for and with Indigenous Australians in professional design contexts.

85846.title: Design Research Paper
85846.description:
This subject introduces you to the scholarly research foundations needed to define and contextualise your major design project. Through lectures, workshops and tutorials you will learn key design research approaches, analyse relevant literature and precedents, frame research questions, and articulate the significance of your project direction.
 
Throughout the semester, you will build your ability to communicate project context and design rationale through clear, coherent scholarly and reflective writing. You will work with academic conventions to structure arguments and synthesise research insights to support your design direction.
 
You will also develop your research output through an iterative process of drafting, reflection, and feedback. By the end of the subject, you will produce a substantial written essay that demonstrates professional rigour, critical insight, and provides a strong foundation for your project’s development in the following session.
learningOutcomes: Apply critical scholarly design research to establish and articulate the contextual foundations for a major design project.
Produce clear and engaging scholarly and reflective writing that communicates project context and provides a clear rationale for design decisions.
Develop a substantial written research output through a professionally managed, iterative process that incorporates feedback and demonstrates reflective improvement.

86004.title: Design Studio: Inhabitations
86004.description:
In this subject, you'll grasp the essentials of interior architecture, including design theories and spatial concepts, preparing you for your degree and career. You'll explore materials, model-making, ergonomics, and learn about performative spaces and urban interiors. In this studio, you'll enhance your interior architecture design methods, focusing on site analysis, client interaction, domestic typologies, and space planning

Your learning will be supported by comprehensive design projects, emphasising adaptive reuse and mixed-use living spaces. The design project is central to your learning, supported by lectures and tutorials that dissect case studies and theoretical concepts related to housing. You'll cultivate spatial intelligence and innovative design methods, working closely with studio leaders to apply lecture insights through iterative modelling and sketches, culminating in weekly presentations.
learningOutcomes: Develop formal and informal experimentation methods.
Engage with ideas of event, programme and spatial organisation.
Develop and evolve individual design intuition and spatial creativity.
Develop and employ a rigorous iterative method-based design process.
Engage in the realisation and presentation of design concepts across four dimensions.

86005.title: Design Studio: Scenographic Spaces
86005.description: In this studio, you will design an immersive scenographic retail environment and learn to translate conceptual ideas into a contemporary setting, to activate spaces, objects, and people. Deliverables include: sketches, drawings, models, visual storyboards, digital media, and technical plans. You will learn to perform historical and contemporary interior architecture detail and object research. You will learn the importance of physical and digital models, as well as digital media and moving images, as tools for experimentation, iteration, and representation in the common history of interior architecture. You will gain a broad understanding of historical and current scenographic and interior architecture practices, as well as specific and detailed knowledge of the scenographic language and techniques currently employed by major players in the field. Finally, you will experiment with and develop your individual and creative design language in concept and representation.
learningOutcomes: Develop formal and informal experimentation methods.
Engage with ideas of event, programme and spatial organisation.
Develop and evolve individual design intuition and spatial creativity.
Develop and employ a rigorous iterative method-based design process.
Engage in the realisation and presentation of design concepts across four dimensions.

86006.title: History and Theory 1
86006.description:
This subject explores the interplay between history, theory, and contemporary interior architecture practice. You'll examine global historical precedents and their influence on modern design, covering diverse regions from Australia to the Americas. The course begins by defining theory and history's roles within the discipline, alongside academic writing and analysis skills.

Concurrent tutorial modules delve into historical and contemporary themes using various theoretical perspectives, such as memory, nature, and technology. These modules, combining lectures, readings, and discussions, aim to enhance your design vocabulary and support your ability to articulate and justify design choices, both academically and professionally. You'll also engage in drawing, model making, and photography, culminating in essays that develop your descriptive and analytical skills.
learningOutcomes: Articulate key chronologies of interior and architectural histories in Western and Non Western contexts.
Become a more effective verbal and visual communicator
Gain a basic repertoire of the language,influences,  history and theoretical themes underpinning interior architecture.
Demonstrate basic competency in the analysis of interior spaces, formal written arguments, interpretation of texts, academic referencing, use of precedent and scholarly language.

86007.title: History and Theory 2
86007.description: The subject explores formations of the interior since the beginning of the 19th century. Lectures take a thematic approach, discussing topics including modernity, domesticity, social organisation, work, technology, and urbanism. The subject allows you to develop skills in the critical analysis of key texts and case studies, and you will gain a deeper understanding of the interior’s relationship to historical change in society and culture.
learningOutcomes: Understand the development of the interior since the beginning of the 19th century.
Understand the relationship between the interior and historical change in society and culture.
Critically analyse and interpret selected texts and case studies of interiors.
Express ideas clearly in written and visual formats using academic conventions.

86008.title: Communication and Construction: Representation
86008.description: This subject hones your ability to communicate interior architecture through foundational representation principles and methods. You'll learn to use drawings as a means to document, explore, and convey spatial concepts, considering their cultural, technological, and spatial dimensions. Through practice, you'll master various communication techniques such as orthographic projections, axonometric and perspective drawings, understanding scale, hierarchy, and composition. You'll actively engage with both analogue and digital methods to map and articulate interior conditions, enhancing your representational skills for professional application.
learningOutcomes: Use architectural drawing conventions to observe, survey and accurately represent spatial information and relations between objects, bodies and events.
Observe and accurately represent hierarchies between material and immaterial spatial entities.
Use iterative processes to explore and integrate diverse communication techniques.
Synthesise and demonstrate an understanding of critical positions on representing the interior.

86009.description: This subject equips you with the skills to communicate spatial interiors and understand the impact of structural and material choices on built environments. You'll explore the relationship between materiality and sustainability within a project brief, gaining practical skills relevant to the industry. You'll learn to depict construction materials, components, and finishes in orthographic drawings and models, honing your ability to detail assemblies that meet environmental, social, and material criteria. Research-based tasks will enhance your strategic decision-making and understanding of structural performance, preparing you to tackle diverse project briefs. This knowledge fosters critical and ethical design thinking, enabling you to deliver high-quality design solutions.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate a capacity to differentiate various construction components within simple structural systems
Understand and apply the construction specific grammars and drawing conventions to communicate construction systems
Respond to environmental and sustainable concerns regarding material choices through a research-led investigations of structured solutions.
Develop, construct and present a physical model that demonstrates an understanding of materiality, structural framework and cladding systems
Synthesise an understanding of materiality, construction components and sustainable practice in drawn, fabricated and spoken modes

86023.title: Light, New Materials and Form 1
86023.description: This subject delves into how light, materials, form, and space shape human environments and experiences. You'll investigate how these elements influence perception and interaction within interior spaces, examining the impact of spatial forms, lighting, colour, and materials. Encouraged to creatively explore emerging materials, form-making, and lighting, you'll challenge conventional design approaches and consider innovative solutions that enhance the human experience.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate knowledge and technical application of lighting characteristics, principles and technologies in interior architecture.
Communicate interior design concepts effectively through various representation techniques.
Explore and explain the effects of illuminated objects in private and public spaces.
Apply lateral thinking to select, test and use appropriate lighting techniques for installations and scale models.
Examine the effects of material technologies on the spatial qualities of interior environments.

Apply and understand construction and detailing methods and techniques and define considerations relating to detail design, materials and specifications.
Research, analyse and document precedents and synthesise information relating to materials, processes, production and ecological sustainability.

86044.title: Rhino 1
86044.description: This subject advances your understanding of NURBS-based modelling in Rhinoceros 3D, starting with a review of the essentials and progressing to sophisticated 3D techniques applicable to interior architecture. You'll learn to navigate between detailed 3D models and 2D representations, and integrate Rhinoceros with Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop, and VRAY for efficient post-production. By the end, you'll confidently represent design ideas, preparing you for future academic and professional tasks.
learningOutcomes: Participate actively during lab sessions individually or in group work activities.
Utilise software tools in the development of accurate spatial representations.
Demonstrate proficiency in clear and industry related representational conventions.
Manage complex environments and multiple tools for the execution of highly sophisticated representation techniques.
Understand, manage and explore three dimensional forms of representation.

86113.title: Communication and Construction: Technologies
86113.description: This subject hones your practice skills in construction documentation and communication, in your second year of Interior Architecture. You'll refine your construction thinking, detailing abilities, and material knowledge, with a focus on sustainability and industry standards. Engaging with tasks, you'll design modular joinery for specific sites, producing a comprehensive drawing package for builders. You'll also coordinate design with building services like lighting and HVAC, developing detailed plans, elevations, and schedules. These skills will enable you to create precise, integrated architectural drawings for professional use.
learningOutcomes: Use iterative processes to generate spatial design solutions in response to project briefs.
Apply detailed design thinking to resolve complex requirements.
Apply research methodology into methods of representation and documentation.
Use spatial design documentation software to produce technical documentation that addresses spatial design elements and aligns with industry conventions.

86114.title: Communication and Construction: Material Futures
86114.description: In this subject, you'll build upon your Interior Architecture studies, focusing on technical representation and material understanding. You'll dissect an object through 3D exercises to grasp its systems and human interaction, then design an installation that redefines the human-space dynamic, envisioning a material future. Emphasising a cycle of making, testing, and fabricating, you'll engage deeply with materials and develop skills in 3D modelling, digital and analogue fabrication, prototyping, and innovative representation methods. This prepares you for sophisticated design and construction challenges.
learningOutcomes: Differentiate the specific role of materials and fabrication technologies within complex systems.
Apply the specific grammars of representation and narrate constructed entities as a hierarchical relationship between materials, systems and components.
Understand the role of digital and analogue techniques of fabrication and assembly.
Explore and implement representation techniques, construction solutions and innovative modes of fabrication and assembly.
Collaborate effectively in team environments and produce detailed architectural documentation.

86133.title: Spatial Design Practices
86133.description: In this subject, you'll learn that details, while small, are pivotal in shaping spaces and experiences, a fundamental skill for an Interior Architect. You'll approach architecture with the precision of a jeweller, examining local buildings with the scrutiny of a botanist. This exploration of intimate spaces will lead you to consider how details influence our daily interactions, such as the relationship between a pocket's shape and a bar's height. Through three key themes, you'll study how details can empathise with users, reflect material understanding and craftsmanship, and respond adaptively to design challenges, balancing care with practicality in the act of making.
learningOutcomes: Observe, survey, and accurately sketch spatial information. Sketches demonstrate ability to observe, survey, analyse and sketch with accuracy and detail.
Demonstrate competency in the accurate representation of space, utilising the drawing conventions and specific grammars of architectural drawings.
Observe, survey, and accurately represent relations between context, objects, bodies and events.
Iterative processes explore, refine, and integrate a range of communication techniques
Synthesise and demonstrate an understanding of critical positions on designing the interior

86150.title: The Interior In Film
86150.description: In this subject, you'll explore how film shapes and creates spaces, going beyond mere reflection to actively organise interiors through framing and montage. You'll delve into the role of interiors in film as spaces of drama and interaction, where architectural elements are imbued with meaning through detail and design. By analysing production design, from wicked houses to industrial settings, you'll present findings on various elements such as light, technology, composition, and atmosphere, understanding how these contribute to the narrative and mood of cinematic spaces.
learningOutcomes: Interpret and sketch interior scenes and spaces.
Effectively annotate drawings.
Demonstrate understanding of the principles of production design and historical changes of the interior in film.

86160.title: Care in the City
86160.description: This design studio elective focuses on drawing, care-practice, and access to the city by developing tools and perspectives to renegotiate places of care, to live, work, age, and create change. It asks: “What do we want the world to become?” You'll explore how urban sites support or impact older people's ability to continue to engage with the city. You will identify whether physical environments are inclusive, safe, and responsive for those marginalised or silenced because of their age, gender, or ability. Outcomes of this subject include a series of drawings reflecting site observations, leading to a series of design principles presented in an illustrated guide. A prize is offered for the best Design Guide.
learningOutcomes: Develop and establish an informed and ethical understanding and/or position toward social, technical and environmental practices
Ability to recognise cultural diversity, including Indigenous, gender and multicultural perspectives
Demonstrate ability to analyse inhabitation of built environments through illustrative techniques to highlight issues for older people.
Develop an 'activist' position through illustration, discussion, and questioning.
Demonstrate ability to participate, share, and ask questions during workshop sessions.

86221.title: Communication and Construction: Interior Technologies
86221.description: This subject, part of a series on representation and construction, delves into designing interior atmospheres, teaching you to understand their creation, materials, and supporting technologies. You'll research atmospheric interiors and apply your findings to assessments. Through technical exercises, you'll learn how construction, materials, and technology interrelate. Lectures and tutorials will guide you in transforming designs into industry-standard production-ready projects. You'll produce technical plans, sections, details, 3D models, images and other documents, mastering the art of conveying interior atmospheres with both precision and subjective interpretation.

Research, test and explain the role of interior technologies in the production of atmospheric controls - Materials, lighting, acoustics, temperature control - through technical drawing.
Explore and experiment with subjective representations of atmospheric conditions in space.
Test multiple strategies and techniques of graphic representation that professionally describes the technical and constructive processes of atmosphere production.
Understand the relevance and use of software in the production of documentation that accurately represents interior space at an industry standard.

86222.description: This subject culminates three years of technical and graphic communication training in interior architecture, focusing on orthographic drawings and construction documentation. You'll refine your skills in creating a professional drawing package for development applications and tendering residential projects. This package, adhering to industry standards, will include a drawing index and detailed drawings for accurate pricing by builders. You'll enhance your ability to produce measured drawings and comprehensive architectural plans, including elevations, lighting, kitchen layouts, shadow diagrams, and schedules for materials and equipment.

Generate spatial design solutions that respond to project briefs and functional requirements
Identify, select and specify a range of Interior Architecture technologies including lighting, joinery, wall, floor and ceiling finishes

86223.title: Design Studio: Interior Architecture Major Project
86223.description: In this final design subject, you'll integrate all the conceptual, technical, and representational skills acquired throughout the interior architecture program. You'll apply these to your studio project, crafting spatial strategies that embody your design's conceptual core. Engaging with contemporary themes, you'll refine your design process and sensitivity to the formal and theoretical aspects of interior space. Guided by theoretical texts, you'll explore spatial typologies, reevaluate programmatic intent, and articulate a stance on interiority. Your challenge is to translate this into a compelling design that enhances interior-spatial relationships and contributes to discourse on the contemporary city. Design studios, selected through balloting, are central to your learning, offering a blend of tutorials, lectures, workshops, and critiques within a unified thematic framework.
learningOutcomes: Actively conceptualise the content within design briefs.
Examine the networks between ideas, information and space.
Understand, create and resolve space through two and three dimensional planning techniques.
Present a resolved and cohesive final design project.
Demonstrate proficiency in advanced and engaging communication.

86529.description: This Studio explores the interior design of knowledge spaces such as galleries, libraries, archives, museums, and learning environments, blending design with curatorial insight. You'll engage in research, writing, and extensive design and documentation, with projects ranging from large-scale exhibitions to the remediation of industrial building for cultural purposes. The focus is on transforming existing buildings into knowledge spaces, emphasizing narrative, circulation, lighting, materials, colour, and display strategies. Practical aspects like sustainability, accessibility, safety, cultural sensitivity, and heritage preservation are also integral to your design approach.
learningOutcomes: Conceptualise design briefs
Articulate and evaluate individual design practice
Understand and challenge given precedents.
Present a resolved and cohesive final design project.
Demonstrate proficiency in advanced and engaging communication.

Weekly lectures and tutorials will deepen your understanding of contemporary and historical influences, enriching your design approach.

Draw from and activate networks between ideas, information and objects

86882.description: This elective sharpens your architectural drawing skills, blending theory with practice to explore the intersection of art and architecture. You'll study influential spatial designers and produce large-scale drawings that push your creative boundaries, culminating in a group exhibition. Ideal for students in Architecture, Interior Architecture, Visual Communications, and Animation, the course encourages experimental and multimedia drawing techniques. Personalised guidance and visits to prestigious architectural drawing collections enrich your learning experience.
learningOutcomes: Develop knowledge of critical and creative spatial design drawing practices
Develop knowledge of experimental theories of image production in spatial design
Foster a ‘risk-taking’ agenda through an experimental approach to image-making techniques
Develop skills in understanding, analysing and responding to a design brief by developing an individual, ethical and informed response

87007.title: Pre-press and Print Production
87007.description: This subject delves into print media's creative scope and industry print technologies. You'll learn about the print design and production process, comparing digital and offset printing, and study paper types, colour management, and finishing touches like embellishments and binding. You'll master pre-press tasks such as imposition and trapping, create professional packaging mock-ups, and generate print-ready artwork with a focus on polished typography and image quality. The aim is to equip you with hands-on experience in file preparation for print and proficiency in associated software.
learningOutcomes: Investigate and present the potential and constraints of printed media including sustainability
Develop the capacity to learn software and technologies in the context of a professional design process
Produce visual work which is clear and engaging, considers issues of sustainability and responds to the project brief
Produce visual work which demonstrates thought, care, attention to detail, technical expertise and an understanding of practical constraints

87009.title: VC Design Studio: Visualising Experience
87009.description: This subject immerses you in visual communication design within complex information and technology systems. You'll design interactions by observing the world and employing basic research methods to discern connections between people, environments, and technology, informing innovative design outcomes. Responding to a brief, you'll craft concepts for interactive applications, objects, or spaces, starting with contextual research, concept development and digital skills acquisition before progressing to a partial realisation of your design concept as a prototype. You'll select suitable technical media and prototyping techniques to create an interactive prototype, enabling you to test, iterate, and refine your designs.
learningOutcomes: Employ primary and secondary research methods including but not limited to observation, the analysis of material culture, library and internet research
Devise creative design concepts and outcomes in response to the specific objectives of a project brief and insights from research
Iterate and refine design concepts and outcomes through processes of critical reflection, feedback, and prototyping
Present design processes, concepts and outcomes in visual, oral and written forms with thought, care and skill
Demonstrate a basic understanding of the fundamentals and possibilities of digital technologies covered in the subject material

87010.title: VC Design Studio: Socially Responsive Design
87010.description: Socially Responsive Design has matured, with projects now larger and more polished, leading to increased real-world application. Emphasizing client collaboration and design leadership, you'll learn to conduct briefing workshops with clients. This subject is grounded in teamwork, professionalism, and a human-centred design ethos. You'll engage in live projects for community-based organisations, crafting solutions informed by global research. It hones your design skills for professional collaborative work, encompassing project management, client briefings, empathy research, user testing, and product sourcing. Projects evolve through iterative development, peer critiques, and formal presentations to clients. Positioned in the third year, this subject offers real-world experience, fostering ethical and socially responsible practices as you transition into a professional design role, often partnering with non-profit organisations to bridge funding gaps.
learningOutcomes: Design in Social and Cultural Contexts Engage with and apply an understanding of the social, cultural, and ethical dimensions that inform design practices.
Client and Stakeholder Engagement Collaborate and engage effectively with clients, peers, and stakeholders to respond to live briefs.
Reflective and Research-Driven Practice Utilise appropriate research methods and critically reflect on design processes and outcomes.
Visual and Craft Sensitivity Demonstrate sensitivity to craft, aesthetic detail, and visual processing in design execution.
Effective Communication Communicate design concepts and outcomes clearly through oral, visual, and written presentation.

87011.title: VC Project: Visual Communication and Emergent Practices
87011.description: This subject explores new social and technological shifts in visual communication design, focusing on the intersection of emergent practice with design fundamentals. You'll examine the evolving role and responsibilities of visual communication designers in Australia, engaging with current literature, including Indigenous perspectives, and conducting creative experiments. This approach challenges human-centred narratives and fosters a design methodology that embraces diverse worldviews.
learningOutcomes: Engage with primary creative research through sustained visual experimentation with emerging technologies.

Develop critical perspectives through actively engaging with academic secondary research, including First Nations scholarship and the Indigenous Design Charter, contemporary academic journals, video and multimedia.

Demonstrate professional documentation and presentation skills. This will include research documentation of secondary research and creative experiments ensuring APA referencing of all text and images, respectful representations of ideas and professional visual communication design.

Demonstrate commitment to experimental and iterative design practice through the development of a suite of experiments, presented as a digital or physical folio, that also demonstrates an understanding of visual communication fundamentals.

87012.title: VC Project: Research Through Design
87012.description: This subject equips you with research approaches and methods from design scholarship and practice through studio workshops and independent activities. You'll learn to integrate research into your practice and establish a perspective aligned with your future professional role. A critical aspect is your ability to articulate how research informs your projects, reflecting your values and ethics—vital for employability and industry transition. Later, you'll master strategies to express how research underpins your practice within a professional visual communication design portfolio, showcasing your distinct standpoint.
learningOutcomes: Critically apply a range of research methods, processes and approaches to their design practice
Through research and iteration, develop a manifesto/position statement that communicates their unique standpoint as a designer
Design a portfolio that communicates that clear standpoint, with examples of design processes and research methods, to an industry standard
Demonstrate professional standard of visual, oral and written presentation skills for research, critical documentation of process, and design outcomes.
Self-direct your learning experience, through time management and reflective practice.

87100.title: VC Design Theory: Critical Approaches to Visual Culture
87100.description: This subject offers a framework to grasp the techniques and technologies shaping visual culture, delving into significant image theories, past and present. You'll learn to contextualise and critique visual culture, positioning your own design practice and analysing others' work. Through lectures and tutorials, you'll explore discourses influencing visual culture, discussing the nature of images and their media environments, spanning from Renaissance art to digital networks.
learningOutcomes: Develop your ability to visually analyse images and apply a range of frameworks in visual culture to consider images.

Develop your ability to critically analyse written texts, give public presentations and develop sound essay writing skills. By the end of the semester you should be able to identify arguments in academic texts and critically respond to them. You should be able to develop an argument in your own essay writing, as well as employ visual examples to support your argument.
By the end of the semester, you will be able to undertake visual and theoretical research and be able to employ the Harvard style of referencing in your assessments.
Develop your knowledge of the social and technical history of visual culture.

87222.description: This subject allows you to apply core visual communication design principles through extended projects. Lectures and studio tasks focus on the interplay between text and imagery in communication. You'll be guided through an iterative design process, from research and concept development to creating drafts and polished designs. The lectures cover communication strategies through form and materiality, the use of constraints, graphic wit, series design, sequencing, and visual metaphors. Additionally, you'll learn to actively participate in critiques, honing your skills in both providing and receiving feedback.

Develop original designs (typography and images) relevant to the specific demands of the project brief, through an iterative process of experimentation, critical reflection, evaluation and refinement.

87441.title: VC Project: Contexts of Visual Communication
87441.description: This subject introduces core areas of contemporary visual communication design, including human‑centred and justice‑oriented design, more‑than‑human approaches, decolonial design, and the ethical use of emerging technologies. You will examine the origins of these perspectives and assess their impact on current design practice through case studies and research tasks. These activities will help you understand best practice and support you to contribute to fair, inclusive, and equitable design outcomes.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate a critical understanding of diverse theoretical approaches and how they apply to visual communication design
Analyse and synthesise research generated through secondary and visual research
Effectively communicate research insights using both written language and visual representations
Demonstrate an understanding of how to use culturally appropriate principles and protocols when working with Indigenous cultures, knowledges and contexts
Use appropriate academic referencing (APA) protocols including the referencing of Indigenous materials

87443.title: VC Project: Typography in Context
87443.description: This subject builds on prior typographic principles, requiring you to research reading habits, critically analyse texts, and understand grid structures and visual hierarchy. You'll develop a keen eye for typographic detail, leading to advanced typography and print design. Topics include legibility, readability, and print design navigation systems. Practical sessions in computer labs will enhance your skills in integrating typography with images, preparing you for more complex subjects ahead.
learningOutcomes: understand the origins and development of letterforms, typefaces, grids and typographic principles
thoughtfully structure the visual organisation of words and images in a given format
process visuals through critical reflection, evaluation and progressive digital refinement
indicate attention to typographic detailing and visual refinement showing thought, care and skill.
understand design context through relevant research

87539.title: Webmedia
87539.description: This subject enhances your understanding of visual communication for the web, focusing on responsive, data-driven, and interactive designs. You'll explore the screen's design environment, including constraints and considerations, and learn to create adaptable design systems for various devices and screens. The course covers HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, equipping you with the skills to develop dynamic projects, while also touching on usability and interaction theories. You're encouraged to experiment, pursue self-directed learning, and blend research with practice. As visual communicators increasingly engage with coding, this subject aims to deepen your grasp of the web as a medium by understanding its core technologies.
learningOutcomes: Research and plan a project for the web and gain experience in the production, structuring and designation of content for web media
Have a developing critical awarness of the social, environmental and ethical considerations of working with webmedia
Understand and apply design principles and fundamentals within the design constraints and affordances of the screen-based web environment
Develop a capacity for basic problem solving skills relevant to the design and realisation of web media
Demonstrate an introductory understanding of the client-side web technologies of HTML, CSS and JavaScript
Demonstrate a basic understanding of the fundamentals and possibilities of web-based visual communication design
Engage with technical and conceptual development within the context of the studio group

87549.title: Creative Code
87549.description: This subject immerses you in the digital realm of design, where understanding interaction and expression through code is crucial. You'll learn to use code to create, read, manipulate, and display digital data, resulting in dynamic designs. By observing, making, and experimenting, you'll explore new expressive possibilities like generative graphics and interactive structures. The core theories and skills you acquire lay the groundwork for further study. You'll use P5.js, an open-source programming environment, to enhance your coding proficiency and bring your concepts to life.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate a basic understanding of the fundamentals and possibilities of the digital and code as a creative medium and the ability to apply this knowledge to creative projects
Demonstrate an introductory level understanding of programming fundamentals and problem-solving skills relevant to the design and realisation of code-based designs
Create simple generative and/or interactive works using code that successfully communicate concepts and ideas
Understand and apply design fundamentals and sensitivity to visual language within the design constraints and affordances of digital technologies
Have the capacity to document and reflect on process and outcomes

87559.title: Motion Graphics
87559.description: This subject advances your proficiency in motion graphics within a professional context. You'll experiment with diverse image-making methods, merging media like live-action video, graphics, typography, stills, and sound. Critique response and feedback integration are emphasised to refine your communication skills. You'll develop a critical vocabulary through visual research and analysis, enhancing your ability to articulate design concepts and outcomes. Further, you'll deepen your knowledge of relevant software and screen design techniques. Projects often involve integrating text and imagery and collaborative research, fostering a robust understanding of design principles and technical skills in visual communication for moving images.
learningOutcomes: Develop an appropriate visual language that is original, refined and effective for the context of the work.

Effectively engage with the subject through active participation in and application of iterative, studio-based practices alongside research methods to develop and refine a conceptually driven final outcome.
Learn and apply appropriate technical skills in the creation of a final outcome.

87631.title: VC Design Studio: The Politics of Image and Text
87631.description: Learn the foundations of visual communication design through studio projects that explore the relationship between image and text in publication design. In responding to practical design briefs, you will develop your creative, research, and technical abilities while gaining critical insight into how visual communication shapes society and culture.
learningOutcomes: Create designs that respond to project briefs in formally or conceptually innovative ways and demonstrate a respectful engagement with First Nations' Knowledges.
Understand the foundational principles of design practice, including the iterative and reflective process and a professional attitude towards communication and participation in the studio.
Develop and maintain high level craft skills for the production, presentation and documentation of work.
Develop a research practice to inform the critical awareness of the political, social, environmental and cultural considerations of working as a visual communicator.

87632.title: VC Design Studio: The Ethics of Image and Text
87632.description: This subject explores the ethical challenges posed by the influential roles of image and text in today's information-saturated society. You'll engage with studio briefs to cultivate ethical design practices, examining how designers navigate ethical dilemmas and incorporate ethical considerations into their work. You'll learn to use the aesthetic aspects of image and text as tools for ethical expression, building upon your existing formal and technical skills in visual communication.
learningOutcomes: Develop an iterative design outcomes that respond to their context in formally or conceptually innovative ways.
Understand the value of participation and professionalism in studio practice.
Develop a research practice that begins to position you within a wider field of design.
Develop and maintain high level craft skills for the production, presentation and documentation of work.

Develop a critical awareness of the political, social, environmental and ethical considerations of working as a visual communicator, including understand professional and academic ethics and copyright issues.

87659.title: VC Moving Image Design: Video
87659.description: This subject delves into the moving image, covering documentary and short film genres, and focuses on content articulation. You'll explore narrative and conceptual frameworks, and learn current digital video planning and production practices. Gain practical skills in recording, compositing, colour-grading, and soundtrack design. You'll also learn to refine your work based on critiques and feedback, and conduct visual research and critical analysis to support your projects.
learningOutcomes: Rigorously and coherently research, process, document and present information to a professional standard.
Thoroughly apply professional work practices as demonstrated in the correct use of files formats, codecs, meeting deadlines and engagement in class.
Develop conceptual and critical thinking in the production of a creative concept and final outcome.

Apply technology in the communication of a creative concept and idea.

87731.title: VC Design Studio: Narrative, Form and Time
87731.description: This subject advances first-year skills, focusing on time-based media creation, including graphic narratives, motion, and video design, using contemporary practices. You'll refine image-making techniques and navigate the iterative process from concept to final product. Critical engagement comes through regular feedback and peer critiques, enhancing your analytical abilities. You'll also craft an original visual language, examining the interplay between images and text. Technical proficiency is developed through hands-on use of software, cameras, and audio equipment, underpinned by studio exercises and expert guidance.
learningOutcomes: Develop an appropriate visual language that is original, refined and effective for the context of the work.

Effectively engage with the subject through active participation in and application of iterative, studio-based practices alongside research methods to develop and refine a conceptually driven final outcome.
Learn and apply appropriate technical skills in the creation of a final outcome

87749.title: User Experience Design
87749.description: This subject equips you with experience design skills, a research-driven approach shaping the interaction between users and products, services, or environments. You'll learn to use research methods to understand user needs and contexts, apply these insights to ideate design concepts, and iteratively prototype and evaluate solutions. The focus is on enhancing user experience and value for digital designs, preparing you to present your ideas effectively.
learningOutcomes: Present design processes and concepts in a compelling manner, by articulating and validating them in light of discovered human needs through research methods.
Deliver a research informed design response.
Iterate and refine a design response through processes of collaboration, testing and prototyping.
Develop insights and hypotheses through an analysis of research findings.
Employ qualitative research methods from the field of experience design to gather information on a design context and its possibilities and constraints.

87832.title: VC Design Studio: Design Practice
87832.description: This subject prepares you for the design industry by engaging with real-world briefs and industry best practices. You'll develop practical skills for employment, including a professional portfolio. Lectures and workshops will enhance your professional skills and foster an understanding of visual communication design both locally and globally. You'll learn to interpret briefs, pitch and present design responses, refine your work through critique, and deliver polished design outcomes. The Professional Experience Program (PEP) is also introduced to complement your learning.
learningOutcomes: Development of an original and/or strategic concept in response to the brief (concept pitch)
Depth of research supporting concept (research report)
Refinement of concept into a final project through iterative design processes (final project)
Clarity and professionalism of final presentation in communicating your concept and design outcome.
Presentation of portfolio

87849.title: Creative Technologies
87849.description: This subject immerses you in innovative ways to interact with digital environments, focusing on emerging technologies for future design applications. You'll move beyond traditional computing interfaces to a wider, more informed engagement with technology. Learn to design immersive experiences with virtual and augmented reality, and create physical interfaces using various controllers and sensors. You're encouraged to critically evaluate contemporary media technologies and explore existing projects that utilise speculative technologies.
learningOutcomes: Research and plan a simple project for physical interaction with a virtual environment
Understand and apply design principles and fundamentals within the design constraints and affordances of emerging and speculative technologies.
Gain the technical skills to make and develop projects using of emerging technologies.
Develop skills to produce an aesthetically resolved outcome and the ability to communicate ideas
Reflect on process and outcomes
Identify, contextualise and analyse relevant works that demonstrate emerging and speculative technologies as expressive and communicative media

88000.title: Object and Accessory Design 1: Foundations
88000.description: This subject serves as a foundation in designing small, aesthetically driven products, crucial for launching successful design-focused businesses. You'll learn what makes a design appealing and viable for low-volume production, a key factor in the success of companies with international acclaim. The course enhances your design and communication skills through various 2D and 3D graphic and physical modelling exercises, laying the groundwork for understanding design proportion, form, and visualisation.
learningOutcomes: Develop a research methodology for conducting design explorations.
Use prototyping as a vehicle to explore, reflect, improve and refine design concepts
Demonstrate the ability to create and develop a design so that manufacturing a small series is possible.
Communicate and present research and concepts to a high standard.
Develop a design brief outlining requirements for a design outcome and understanding of a manufacturing technology.

88002.title: Object and Accessory Design 2: The Cast Object
88002.description: This subject equips you with the skills to design small, aesthetically pleasing products that are fundamental to the success of many design-centric start-ups. You'll learn to create designs that are not only attractive but also feasible and economical to produce on a small scale, a strategy that has propelled companies like Fink Design and Dinosaur Designs to international success.
learningOutcomes: Develop the beginning of a personal design aesthetic for low function products
Engage with several manufacturing processes suited to low volume production
Design for manufacture
Document a design to a level suited to discussion with professional manufacturers
Articulate the economic/strategic realities surrounding the successful development of small, low volume – low budget designed objects.

88004.title: Textiles: Print
88004.description: This subject introduces you to textile print and pattern design, focusing on creative drawing and image-making techniques. You'll develop unique artwork, experimenting with scale and imagery for textiles. Learn industry methods for generating print designs, including repeat systems and engineered placement prints. You'll also master screen preparation, textile production, and hand screen-printing, along with pigment colour mixing and specialty ink techniques such as transfer, foil, and flock printing. A professional and sustainable approach to print room practice is emphasised throughout.
learningOutcomes: gain knowledge into the requirements for screen preparation for printed textiles
develop relevant design skills and explore the potential of printed textiles
utilise mark-making techniques in order to produce conceptual surface design work
know the fundamental elements of textile and surface design
demonstrate professional workshop practice and knowledge of Workplace Health and Safety requirements in the Print Room.
88004.recommended: Students need to meet relevant prerequisites as advertised in the handbook

88006.title: Textiles: Dye Methods
88006.description: In this twelve-week on-campus elective, you'll delve into the world of natural dyes, mordants, and resist patterning. Engage in workshops that encourage innovative colouring and patterning of cloth. You'll learn resist patterning methods and unique printing techniques, including binding, stitching, and clamp resist. The course also covers the interaction of natural fibres with various natural dyes and mordants. You'll develop sophisticated textile concepts and a refined colour sense, all while maintaining a focus on professional and sustainable print room practices.
learningOutcomes: Develop a fundamental understanding of the elements of textile and surface design.
Gain knowledge into commercial dyes and their applications in industry.
Explore ancient forms of dyestuff and mordants.
Experiment with various Shibori techniques together with an understanding of cultural significance in dyes and patterning.
Apply dye techniques to various textile surfaces.
88006.recommended: Students need to meet relevant prerequisites as advertised in the handbook

88007.title: Textiles: Surface Form
88007.description: This subject explores three-dimensional textiles, focusing on thermoplastic techniques and surface forms, which are pivotal in fashion and textiles for creating innovative fabrics. You'll learn to shape synthetics with heat to achieve permanent textures and forms. Through studio experimentation, you'll uncover new pleat geometries and the design possibilities of sculpted surfaces. The course also includes working with undyed natural raffia, transforming 2D woven, knitted, or braided textiles into 3D accessories. You'll study the work of leading contemporary textile designers and maintain a professional, sustainable studio practice. Suitable for all skill levels, the subject challenges students according to their expertise.
learningOutcomes: Investigate the possibilities of experimental textile processes as a vehicle for expressing ideas.
Develop skills and explore the potential of various fabric manipulation and surface treatments.
Utilise mark-making skills in order to produce conceptual surface design work
Identify and understand a broad range of contemporary textile design practices.
Apply the knowledge of construction and chemical treatments on fabrics.

88011.title: Darkroom Photography
88011.description: This subject provides a hands-on introduction to black and white photography, immersing you in the alchemical process of the darkroom. You'll learn to use a 35mm manual SLR camera, process black and white film, and master darkroom printing techniques, including film exposure and print enlargement. Darkroom photography offers a meditative practice that contrasts with the fast pace of modern life, producing evocative images that encourage a slower, more reflective approach. This elective welcomes students from all disciplines.
learningOutcomes: Engage in and contribute to studio discussion
Develop innovative approaches to analogue photographic pratice
Demonstrate technical skills in analogue photography
Reflect and engage in self-critique and critical thinking

88014.title: The Photo Book
88014.description: This subject delves into the photobook's role in photography, from its inception with Henry Fox Talbot's The Pencil of Nature to its contemporary significance. You'll explore how the photobook, as a form of experimentation and communication, informs the history of photography and creative practice. You'll create your own photobook, learning how meaning is crafted through the interplay of images, text, and the physicality of the page.
learningOutcomes: Continually develop your photobook between classes
Contributibute to class discussion on yours and others photobooks as they develop
Use appropriate photographic techniques in the production of your work
Research and articulate how the work of other photographers resonantes with your own work
Refine your photobook through a process of self-critique and critical thinking

88015.title: Design Studies Global Studio
88015.description: This subject enhances your cross-cultural design literacy by engaging you in work-integrated learning with a global partner on a live brief. You'll collaborate on sustainable design solutions, using the UN Sustainable Development Goals as a framework for evaluation and practice. Learning takes place through a combination of studio work, seminars, and off-campus fieldwork.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate an informed understanding of design briefs in cross-cultural contexts.
Plan and execute design research in a professional manner and use research insights to guide the development and presentation of design outcomes.
Work productively in interdisciplinary and intercultural teams through clear communication, shared responsibility, and respect for diverse design roles and cultural perspectives
Demonstrate advanced reflective practice and the ability to clearly articulate and justify design decisions and rationales.
Articulate the nature of a situated context through sensitive experimental design research.

88304.description: In this subject, you'll explore illustration as a communication medium, experimenting with diverse media and techniques during studio sessions and in your own time through project briefs. You'll learn to conceptualise and produce 2D animated content using professional techniques, which includes research, design boards, and creating animated sequences.

Understand the fundamentals of how to create stable structures through application of theory and practice.
Develop an original aesthetic sensibility in furniture design.

Formulate their own ideas of event, programme and spatial organisation
Develop formal and informal methods of visual and verbal communication and presentation
Realise and present design concepts within a new context

88831.title: Global Studio: Fashion and Textiles A
88831.description: The Knit Innovation Global Studio is a four-week mobility program based in Hong Kong. It combines cultural immersion, language training, and hands-on engagement with the knitwear and textile industry. This project will immerse undergraduate students from the UTS School of Design in an interdisciplinary, credit-bearing global studio that advances Australia’s international design capabilities and deepens institutional and industry linkages in the Indo-Pacific.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate integration of Cultural Elements into Design.
Demonstrate a capacity to challenge boundaries and take risks.
Showcase understanding of knitting and yarns.
Demonstrate a capacity to reflect on practice and research.

88832.title: Global Studio: Fashion and Textiles B
88832.description: The UTS Fashion and Textile course offers global studios, enabling you to study in diverse locations and gain international perspectives. You'll engage in interactive workshops and immerse in different design cultures, fostering creativity, institutional ties, and personal growth. These short-term projects deepen your appreciation of specific regions, social engagement, and language, while collaborating with local artisans. Ideal for those keen on integrating global practices into their design work, this study tour broadens your understanding of fashion and textiles within a wider cultural and contemporary context.
learningOutcomes: Develop an awareness of the creative possibilities of traditional textile processes
Gain cultural awareness and knowledge through learning about artisan design methods
Benefit from increased cultural awareness and the potential for cross-cultural collaboration
Understand sourcing appropriate materials for textiles
Reflect on practice and research through daily reflective documentation
Increase knowledge in developing textile designs, scale, pattern and repeats
