88834.title: Advanced Fashion Technologies
88834.description: You'll explore emerging digital tools in fashion and textile design, such as garment simulation in augmented reality spaces. These tools augment your understanding of material practices digitally. You'll contextualise technologies within historical and speculative industry practices, examining their connections to sustainability and social justice. The subject highlights both the potential and limitations of these technologies in fashion and textile design.
learningOutcomes: Research and debate issues relating to advanced technologies in fashion and textile systems
Effectively apply 3D fashion and textile design skills using appropriate fashion technologies.
Experiment with the creation of garments using fashion technologies while challenging traditional methods
Develop communication skills using digital technologies competently and professionally
Understand how to combine technologies incorporating digital and non-digital skills

88990.title: Generative Design Principles
88990.description: You'll deepen your understanding of generative design, employing a methodology that spans concept generation through CAD, iterative design refinement, and digital fabrication with advanced manufacturing. Lectures cover context, natural structures and patterns, optimisation for 3D printing, topology, and software tools, equipping you to integrate generative design into your skillset. You'll create digital files for prototyping and engage with a 3D printing bureau to produce your designs, including a site visit to experience the additive manufacturing environment firsthand.
learningOutcomes: Gain effective visual presentation and storytelling skills through the production of a video journal.
Explore, experiment and innovate via an iterative design process.
Develop an understanding of structural efficiency through simulation processes.
Develop an original aesthetic sensibility.
Develop Product Design specific analogue and digital skills, to implement a generative design process.

89044.title: Planning Professional Research
89044.description: In this subject, you will develop the research and planning skills required to undertake advanced design projects. You will learn how to frame problems, conduct a contextual review, and determine the appropriate selection and sequencing of methods relevant to research into, through, and for design. The subject focuses on ethical engagement, including in relation to First Nations communities and Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property. The subject supports informed and responsible approaches to independent and collaborative design research, balancing academic rigour with professional relevance, laying the groundwork for your capstone research project.
learningOutcomes: Frame a complex design research problem with reference to relevant professional, scholarly and contextual considerations.
Develop a coherent research plan that sequences appropriate methods, activities, resources and project milestones.
Evaluate ethical, cultural and professional responsibilities in the planning of design research, including engagement with First Nations communities, collaborators and knowledge systems.

args.text: Admission into C04311 Master of Design
Admission into C04312 Master of Design (Extension)

89045.title: Design Research Project
89045.description: In this capstone subject, you will consolidate and apply the knowledge and skills you have developed across your studies. You will undertake a major research project that demonstrates advanced design reasoning and professional capability. You will define a research question or problem relevant to your discipline, deploy appropriate research and practice methods, and produce a resolved body of work supported by critical reflection and contextualisation. The subject foregrounds rigorous research and innovation, in order to further your scholarly contribution and professional practice.
learningOutcomes: Articulate a significant design research question or problem grounded in relevant disciplinary, professional and scholarly contexts.
Conduct a major design research project using appropriate research and practice methods, with attention to ethical and cultural responsibilities.
Produce a resolved body of design work, research findings or professional outputs that evidence advanced design reasoning
Critically contextualise and communicate the contribution of the project to design practice, knowledge or scholarly discourse

89046.title: Industry-Partnered Design Studio
89046.description: This subject provides you with industry experience by addressing real-world discipline-specific challenges set in collaboration with external partner organisations. You will learn how to frame, develop, and deliver strategic design responses that balance innovation, feasibility, professional standards, and stakeholder needs. The subject develops your ability to critically interpret complex briefs, formulate and justify sophisticated design responses, and iteratively refine your work through informed peer critique. It also builds advanced capability in articulating, evidencing, and professionally communicating design proposals for specialist and non-specialist audiences.
learningOutcomes: Critically interpret an industry-partnered brief in relation to stakeholder needs, disciplinary contexts and professional constraints.
Develop and justify strategic design responses through an iterative, research-informed studio practice.
Refine design propositions in response to peer, industry and/or stakeholder feedback, demonstrating professional judgement and feasibility.
Communicate a resolved design proposal to specialist and non-specialist audiences using appropriate evidence, formats and design language.

89047.title: Fashion Media
89047.description: In this subject, you will explore fashion media as an object of study and as a site of practice. You will examine the history of fashion media and trends in fashion communication, and the evolution from legacy formats to the contemporary digital landscape, including ecosystems of journalism, social media, and influencers. You will learn to design an innovative fashion media strategy using compelling narratives tailored for specific audiences, while adhering to consumer communications regulations.
learningOutcomes: Critically investigate fashion media histories, platforms and communication practices across legacy and digital contexts
Apply research-informed experimentation to develop fashion narratives, communication strategies or audience engagement approaches
Develop an innovative fashion media strategy that responds to audience, platform, narrative and regulatory considerations

requisite.text: Admission into MAJ10034 36cp Fashion Strategy major MDes

89048.title: Fashion Industry Futures
89048.description: In this subject, you will examine the fashion industry as a dynamic system shaped by global, cultural, and environmental change, with a focus on fashion industry futures. You will analyse key drivers of transformation, including emerging technologies, circular practices, and Indigenous knowledge systems, and their influence on industry structures and value chains. You will develop strategic thinking skills to respond to complex challenges across design, business, and production contexts. Upon completion of this subject, you will be able to develop and communicate informed strategies that support innovation and long-term industry transformation.
learningOutcomes: Critically analyse key drivers of transformation shaping fashion industry futures, including global, cultural, environmental and technological change.
Apply strategic thinking and professional analysis methods to evaluate changing fashion value chains and industry structures.
Develop and communicate an informed strategy that supports innovation and long-term transformation in fashion industry contexts.

requisite.text: Admission into MAJ10034 36cp Fashion Strategy major MDes

89049.title: Advanced Fashion Technologies
89049.description: In this subject, you will investigate emerging technologies shaping fashion businesses and the different workflows and processes within them. Through research-led experimentation and learning from industry-leading practice, you will explore how technological innovation can inform new forms of digitally connected fashion business across design, communication, material sourcing, production, and distribution. You will learn about the ethical dimensions of emerging technologies, including how artificial intelligence (AI) is shaping creative and professional practices in fashion.
learningOutcomes: Critically analyse emerging technologies and their implications for contemporary fashion business workflows and professional practices
Apply research-informed and industry-informed methods to evaluate technological opportunities across fashion design, communication, sourcing, production or distribution
Develop a digitally connected fashion business proposition that demonstrates professional judgement and ethical awareness of emerging technologies

requisite.text: Admission into MAJ10034 36cp Fashion Strategy major MDes

89050.title: Fashion Brand Management
89050.description: In this subject, you will engage with fashion brand management practices and explore the tangible and intangible aspects of successful fashion branding. You will develop skills related to brand identity, purpose, and values. You will learn about market and customer analysis, product positioning, and the measuring and management of branding activities. Upon completion of this subject, you will be able to develop and deliver brand strategies for businesses of diverse scales and types in the fashion industry, with a focus on current and future audiences, stakeholders, and suppliers.
learningOutcomes: Critically investigate fashion brand management practices, including brand identity, purpose, values and market positioning
Apply research-informed experimentation to analyse audiences, stakeholders, suppliers and brand opportunities across diverse fashion contexts
Develop an innovative fashion brand strategy that integrates brand positioning, audience insight and management considerations

requisite.text: Admission into MAJ10034 36cp Fashion Strategy major MDes

89051.title: Fashion and Textiles Sustainability
89051.description: In this subject, you will develop an understanding of sustainability in fashion and textiles, including the shifting regulatory landscape around the globe. You will explore circular economy principles within fashion and textile systems, drawing from state-of-the-art developments in industry and research, as well as historical developments in the field. You will investigate sustainable materials, production models, and lifecycle strategies through a lens of systems thinking. You will develop professional capabilities to articulate and design systems that enable responsible and regenerative fashion futures, including skills for effective collaboration and influence.
learningOutcomes: Critically analyse sustainability challenges, regulatory shifts and circular economy principles within fashion and textile systems
Apply systems thinking and professional sustainability methods to evaluate materials, production models and lifecycle strategies
Develop a responsible fashion or textile systems strategy that supports circular, regenerative or more sustainable industry futures

requisite.text: Admission into MAJ10034 36cp Fashion Strategy major MDes

89052.title: Fashion, Ethics and Law
89052.description: In this subject, you will examine the ethical and legal frameworks shaping contemporary fashion business, preparing you for a rapidly evolving regulatory landscape in fashion and textiles globally. These frameworks include intellectual property, modern slavery, and sustainability reporting. The subject develops your capability in assessing the implications of regulation within the fashion industry. You will engage with issues of traceability, risk management, and social impact, developing informed and principled approaches to professional fashion business and strategy.
learningOutcomes: Critically analyse ethical and legal frameworks shaping contemporary fashion business and textile industries
Apply professional judgement to evaluate regulatory, traceability, risk management and social impact considerations in fashion contexts
Develop an informed and principled fashion business strategy that addresses ethical, legal and social responsibilities

requisite.text: Admission into MAJ10034 36cp Fashion Strategy major MDes

89053.title: Advanced Creative Technologies
89053.description: In this subject, you will develop advanced knowledge of new and emerging technologies and how they can be creatively applied to shape experience. Through material play and research-led experimentation, you will develop your technical skills and learn how to strategically incorporate creative technologies in the design of innovative user experiences, including and beyond generative AI. This subject develops your ability to research and critically evaluate the benefits and potential risks of contemporary media technologies, enabling you to thoughtfully and ethically incorporate them into your design practice.
learningOutcomes: Critically investigate emerging creative technologies and evaluate their potential applications, benefits and risks in experience design practice.
Apply research-informed experimentation to test how creative technologies can shape innovative user experiences.
Develop an innovative experience design outcome that demonstrates considered, ethical and technically informed use of contemporary media technologies.

requisite.text: Admission into MAJ10032 36cp User Experience major MDes

89054.title: Strategic Design
89054.description: In this subject, you will learn how to integrate visual communication design into strategy within increasingly complex organisational and social contexts. You will develop your ability to critically engage with systems, stakeholders, and technologies to navigate uncertainty, negotiate values, and make socially responsible design decisions. Through case studies and industry-informed projects, you will learn to create strategic design responses grounded in care, accountability, and long-term social value.
learningOutcomes: Critically analyse organisational, social and technological contexts to identify opportunities for strategic design intervention.
Apply professional design methods to engage systems, stakeholders and values in the development of strategic responses.
Develop and communicate a strategic design proposal that addresses complexity, uncertainty and long-term social value

requisite.text: Admission into MAJ10032 36cp User Experience major MDes

89055.title: Design for Social Innovation
89055.description: In this subject, you will engage with social and service design concepts and tools to develop your understanding of social innovation. You will apply visual communication skills to respond proactively to social and technological problems. You will learn about co-design and participatory design, including principles of social justice and inclusion. The subject introduces practical social design research approaches such as designing and facilitating workshops, and creative ways of presenting social research.
learningOutcomes: Critically analyse social innovation contexts, including social justice, inclusion and technologically mediated change.
Apply co-design, participatory design and social design research methods to investigate complex social or service challenges.
Develop and communicate a socially responsible design response that translates social research into actionable design opportunities.

requisite.text: Admission into MAJ10032 36cp User Experience major MDes

89056.title: Visualisation and Immersive Experiences
89056.description: In this subject, you will learn to design visualisations, immersive media, and interactive experiences using VR, AR, and multimodal storytelling. Through experimental projects, you will learn to use spatial, temporal, and sensory dimensions of digital design to translate data and produce research-informed outcomes. This subject builds on foundational pre-production processes of prototyping through journey mapping, user testing, and sequential and non-linear storytelling. You will apply visual communication fundamentals to create engaging digital user experience projects that respond to data, context, and audience.
learningOutcomes: Critically investigate visualisation, immersive media and interactive experience practices in relation to data, context and audience.
Apply experimental prototyping methods to develop spatial, temporal, sensory or multimodal experience scenarios.
Develop an innovative visualisation or immersive experience outcome that translates research insights into an engaging user experience.

requisite.text: Admission into MAJ10032 36cp User Experience major MDes

89057.title: Visual Design Methods
89057.description: In this subject, you will explore the professional foundations of experience design practice, learning the methods, tools, and workflows needed to operate effectively in contemporary visual communication design environments. You will engage with core conceptual and studio-based skills across typography, image-making, and interface design, working creatively and critically with and for AI. Inclusive and accessible practices are embedded throughout. Project briefs encourage independent problem solving, user testing, and prototyping.
learningOutcomes: Critically analyse professional visual design methods, tools and workflows used in contemporary experience design practice.
Apply visual communication, prototyping and user testing methods to develop accessible and inclusive design responses.
Develop a resolved visual design outcome that demonstrates professional judgement, technical capability and critical engagement with contemporary tools, including AI.

requisite.text: Admission into MAJ10032 36cp User Experience major MDes

89058.title: Designing User Experiences
89058.description: This subject develops an advanced understanding of user experience design as a research‑driven practice that shapes interactions between people, products, services, systems, and environments. You will learn to critically analyse user needs, behaviours, and contexts through a range of social and visual research methods, including interviews, observation, personas, journey mapping, and scenario building. You will  synthesise qualitative insights and communicate them effectively through visual and narrative forms.You will apply this research to ideate, prototype, and iteratively test design responses, developing thoughtful and evidence-based visual communication outcomes. This may include social and service design interventions, as well as visualisations, wayfinding systems, co-design workshops, and digital experiences.
learningOutcomes: Critically analyse user needs, behaviours and contexts using social and visual research methods.
Apply evidence-based user experience methods to synthesise insights, generate concepts, prototype and test design responses.
Develop a thoughtful and responsible user experience outcome that demonstrates how research insights inform design decisions.

requisite.text: Admission into MAJ10032 36cp User Experience major MDes

89059.title: Digital Manufacturing Technologies
89059.description: In this subject, you will investigate advanced manufacturing technologies and their implications for contemporary product design practice. Through project-based experimentation, you will explore how emerging fabrication processes, digital production systems, and material technologies can be applied and adapted to generate innovative product outcomes. The subject emphasises critical enquiry, technical exploration, and speculative application of digital manufacturing technologies in response to complex design challenges.
learningOutcomes: Critically investigate contemporary digital manufacturing technologies and evaluate their implications for advanced product design practice, emerging production models, and future design applications

Apply research-informed, experimental approaches to explore the affordances, constraints and applications of digital fabrication, production systems, and material technologies through project‑based investigation
Develop an innovative product design outcome that synthesises technical exploration, material understanding and conceptual rigour

requisite.text: Admission into MAJ10033 36cp Strategic Product Innovation major MDes

89060.title: Advanced Product Design Development
89060.description: In this subject, you will develop advanced product design concepts through iterative research, prototyping, and refinement in response to complex, open-ended design briefs. You will engage with user research methods, ergonomics, standards, and industry case studies to inform design decisions and translate insights into testable product propositions. Emphasis is placed on experimental, practice-led approaches to design development through rapid prototyping, user testing, and critical evaluation. You will integrate form, function, and performance within real-world constraints.
learningOutcomes: Critically investigate and frame product design challenges through the application of advanced user research methods, ergonomic analysis, standards, and industry case studies to develop a well-evidenced design brief
Apply iterative, research-led design development processes to generate, test, and refine product design propositions through analysis and critical evaluation
Develop and articulate an advanced product design proposition that integrates form, function, performance while responding to user needs, technical considerations, and real-world constraints

requisite.text: Admission into MAJ10033 36cp Strategic Product Innovation major MDes

89061.title: Product Innovation and Commercialisation
89061.description: In this subject, you will examine how product ideas are developed, positioned, and translated into commercially viable outcomes. You will explore innovation frameworks, market contexts, and value propositions, developing the capacity to articulate and justify complex design decisions to a variety of stakeholders. The subject emphasises professional communication and strategic thinking within contemporary product domains.
learningOutcomes: Critically analyse innovation frameworks, market contexts and value propositions relevant to contemporary product design
Develop a commercially informed product innovation proposition that responds to stakeholder needs, market conditions and professional design contexts
Apply professional communication and strategic evaluation methods to position, test and justify product innovation opportunities

requisite.text: Admission into MAJ10033 36cp Strategic Product Innovation major MDes

89062.title: Product Design Entrepreneurship
89062.description: In this subject, you will explore entrepreneurial approaches to product design, extending to the service and system parameters that need to be considered when translating new product concepts into viable business propositions. You will learn how product designers coordinate the development of physical products within designed product ecosystems and collaborative practices within professional contexts.
learningOutcomes: Critically analyse entrepreneurial approaches to product design within service, system and business contexts.
Apply professional methods to evaluate the viability, positioning and development pathways of product-based propositions.
Develop an entrepreneurial product design proposition that integrates business model thinking, ecosystem awareness and professional communication.

requisite.text: Admission into MAJ10033 36cp Strategic Product Innovation major MDes

89063.title: Sustainable Production
89063.description: In this subject, you will examine how systems and technologies can support more sustainable approaches to product consumption through product design. You will explore the relationship between design and consumption, with a focus on environmental responsibility, systems thinking, and professional design practice.
learningOutcomes: Critically analyse relationships between product design, consumption, production systems and environmental responsibility
Apply systems thinking and responsible design methods to evaluate opportunities for more sustainable product design, manufacture, use, and end-of-life solutions
Develop a professional product design strategy or proposition that supports more sustainable patterns of manufacture, use, and end-of-life solutions

requisite.text: Admission into MAJ10033 36cp Strategic Product Innovation major MDes

89064.title: Design for Manufacture and Material Innovation
89064.description: In this subject, you will explore state-of-the-art manufacturing technologies (Internet of Things, AI, and Industry 4.0) and material innovation as drivers of environmentally responsible product design. Through applied projects, you will investigate material selection, production constraints, and lifecycle considerations, developing design solutions that respond to sustainability and resource efficiency in professional manufacturing contexts.
learningOutcomes: Critically analyse manufacturing technologies, material innovation and lifecycle considerations in relation to environmentally responsible product design
Apply professional material selection, manufacturing and lifecycle evaluation methods to inform sustainable design decisions
Develop a responsible product design outcome that integrates material innovation, manufacturing constraints and resource efficiency

requisite.text: Admission into MAJ10033 36cp Strategic Product Innovation major MDes

89065.title: Design Innovation Studio
89065.description: In this extension studio subject, you will amplify the knowledge and capabilities developed within your specialist studies. Working in cross‑disciplinary teams, you will respond to complex sector‑wide challenges, addressing wicked problems such as sustainability, food security, and climate resilience. You will deploy research skills, systems thinking, and design methods to develop strategic responses that demonstrate advanced professional judgement, collaboration, and communication capabilities.
learningOutcomes: Critically analyse complex sector-wide challenges through systems thinking, contextual research and cross-disciplinary design inquiry.
Frame opportunities for design innovation in response to wicked problems.
Develop and evaluate innovative design propositions that balance feasibility, impact, professional judgement and stakeholder value.
Communicate a strategic design proposal that demonstrates advanced reasoning, collaboration and evidence-based decision-making.

args.text: Admission into C04312 Master of Design (Extension)

90010.title: PhD Thesis: Health Economics
90010.description:
This subject focuses on the prevention, detection, management, and control of communicable diseases affecting human populations. It explores disease transmission dynamics, susceptibility, and primary prevention. By examining global epidemiology, students gain insights into the social and ecological determinants of communicable diseases. Historical and contemporary examples, including the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, inform public health responses and challenges.

The subject covers principles of communicable disease control, such as surveillance, outbreak investigation, and prevention, using case studies. Additionally, it emphasises integrated, collaborative approaches, consumer engagement, and advocacy. Students engage in interactive activities, critical analysis, discussions, and problem-solving, working independently and participating in online forums and Zoom meetings.

91001.title: Applied Pathology Technology
91001.description: This subject equips you with essential pathology skills to conduct and interpret tests that determine disease presence using histopathological and cytological methods. You'll enhance your understanding of tissue analysis and cytology, learning to prepare specimens and identify normal and pathological characteristics in various samples. Your skill set will expand to include dissection, microtomy, staining, and advanced techniques like immunohistochemistry and electron microscopy. Industry experts facilitate your learning, ensuring practical, real-world application.
learningOutcomes: Undertake preparation of histological and cytological samples. Show competency at performing special stains and immunohistochemical stains.
Identify and rectify technical issues that may lead to inappropriate diagnosis.
Recognise normal and pathological features on prepared specimen.
Demonstrate the need for quality control and quality assessment for all laboratory tests.

requisite.text: Admission into C10481 Bachelor of Medical Science (Laboratory Medicine Professional)

91002.title: Molecular Pathology
91002.description: This subject equips you with the expertise to harness molecular pathology in modern diagnostic laboratories, and to enhance patient care by compliance with NATA accreditation on test validation. You'll refine your understanding on the role of genetics and genomic diagnosis across the four major pathology disciplines - chemical pathology, haematology, medical microbiology and anatomical pathology. You'll develop practical skills in hands-on sample preparation, molecular techniques, results interpretation, and diagnostic test validation by integrating prior knowledge from molecular biology, genetics, histopathology, biochemistry, haematology, and infectious diseases. Learning unfolds through hands-on experience, simulating the work environment of diagnostic pathology laboratories to ensure you're job-ready.
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods of collection and preservation of specimen for molecular testing, and critical analysis of results.
Articulate, and interpret the applications of molecular techniques commonly used in the Pathology sector, such as PCR, RT-PCR, mass spectrometry, sequencing, in situ hybridization.
Identify, apply, and troubleshoot technical and analytical processes involved in laboratory medicine diagnosis.
Articulate the need for quality control and quality assessment for all laboratory tests.
Describe, reflect, and evaluate the importance of patient confidentiality and preservation of privacy in the context of laboratory medicine.

requisite.text: Admission into C10481 Bachelor of Medical Science (Laboratory Medicine Professional)

91003.title: Laboratory Medicine Professional Placement
91003.description: This subject equips you with vital industry experience, making you work-ready by aligning your skills with current professional standards. You will spend 560 hours in a pathology diagnostic laboratory, honing practical skills under expert supervision. You'll gain insights into various specialties and roles within the laboratory setting, enhancing your existing knowledge and mastering new competencies that are evaluated on-site. Your learning experience will be enriched through active participation in a range of laboratory activities, ensuring a comprehensive understanding of the field.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate a professional level knowledge of the structure of a pathology laboratory and its different specialties.
Articulate the flow of the work from specimen reception to report of results.
Achieve practical skills on selected activities and competencies, using safe work practises..
Implement and critically interpret the tests and results that are routinely performed in the pathology laboratory.
Demonstrate professionalism and ability to work in a team.

requisite.text: Admission into C10481 Bachelor of Medical Science (Laboratory Medicine Professional)

91004.title: Laboratory Management and Quality Control
91004.description: This subject equips you with essential knowledge and skills for effective laboratory management, focusing on process control, accreditation standards, safety, quality assurance, and patient confidentiality. You'll gain proficiency in Laboratory Integrated Management Systems for comprehensive record-keeping. The learning approach is practical, blending theory with real-world applications to ensure you can maintain high standards in a pathology laboratory setting.
learningOutcomes: Design and implement laboratory workflows to optimise operational efficiency and ensure quality and safety outcomes while complying with appropriate legislation and standards.
Demonstrate an understanding of the Australian laboratory accreditation process, including the roles of accreditation bodies and key requirements/documents
Identify risks in various laboratory environments and how quality control and quality assurance procedures can mitigate these risks.
Evaluate the practical use cases of Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS) in optimising laboratory operations.
Cultivate laboratory management skills, with a focus on recruitment, team leadership, and resource allocation.

Admission into Bachelor's combined degree owned by Science
Admission into Bachelor's combined degree co-owned by Science

91100.title: Urban Sustainability and Resilience
91100.description: Urban Sustainability and Resilience addresses the environmental challenges cities face, such as climate change and population growth, by exploring sustainable solutions from science engineering. This subject prepares you for the expanding job market in urban sustainability, focusing on essential knowledge and skills for professionals in the field. It emphasises a transdisciplinary approach, incorporating government and industry insights to understand the collaborative nature of addressing sustainability issues. The flexible online format includes recorded lectures, expert interviews, interactive discussions, and student-chosen assessment topics, allowing you to tailor your learning to your professional interests and career aspirations.
learningOutcomes: Understand the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals relevant to Urban Systems, and show an appreciation of directions that may be taken to achieve these goals.
Understand the need for engaging transdisciplinary expertise in the process of developing sustainable and resilient systems.
Collaboratively research and propose best-practice solutions to achieve environmental sustainability through the application of environmental assessments, policies, planning, and urban design.
Understand and communicate the major issues that impact on and contribute to urban sustainability and resilience.
Communicate urban sustainability and resilience concepts in a convincing, clear, and concise manner and appropriate for multiple disciplines and stakeholders.

91103.title: Honours (Life Sciences) 1
91103.description: The Honours course provides advanced research training in life and environmental sciences, enhancing your skills and knowledge for a research career. Centred around a research project spanning two 24-credit-point sessions, you'll work closely with an academic supervisor to conduct research in your chosen area. You'll learn to formulate hypotheses, set objectives, manage time and resources, employ appropriate research methods, evaluate evidence critically, and construct detailed arguments. Under supervision, you'll analyse and interpret scientific data from your project. Your science communication skills will be honed through written works and oral presentations. The culmination of your work is a thesis, which is the primary assessment component of the course.
learningOutcomes: Conduct independent research to generate new knowledge relating to a medical, biomedical, environmental or biotechnology problem.
Develop a research plan and design suitable experiments to address an existing gap in disciplinary knowledge based on a review of existing literature.
Communicate research findings effectively in diverse contexts.
Collaborate effectively within a research team.

91104.description: This honours subject advances your research training in life and environmental sciences, preparing you for a research-focused career. You'll refine your ability to craft hypotheses, manage resources, apply research methods, critically evaluate evidence, and articulate complex arguments. Analysis and interpretation of scientific data will be conducted under supervision. Your communication skills will be developed through both written and oral presentations of your work. 91107.title: The Biosphere
91107.description: The Biosphere, encompassing all life on Earth, is unique to our planet. This subject introduces you to environmental sciences, tracing the evolution of Earth's structure and species, and examining current environmental changes. You'll explore interactions among living organisms, non-living elements, and external factors such as the atmosphere and solar energy. The subject also focuses on human impacts on the biosphere, addressing critical issues such as climate change, sustainability, and resource depletion.
learningOutcomes: Describe the concept of the biosphere and the parallel history of geological and biological evolution of planet Earth.
Identify professional requirements for environmental scientists and how they contribute to protection of the environment through fieldwork, education and research.
Identify the diverse range and function of ecosystems, how they have been impacted by human behaviours and how these impacts can be mitigated.
Evaluate complex environmental problems from diverse perspectives.
Demonstrate professional practice through effective collaboration and documentation.

91116.title: Australian Wildlife and Management
91116.description: This subject examines the conservation, management, and biology of Australian wildlife amidst growing human pressures such as land clearing, mining, and invasive species. You'll explore wildlife diversity, current ecological issues, and practical conservation solutions. The subject includes a field trip for hands-on experience handling native species and you’ll learn techniques used to survey, identify and study wildlife. You'll gain the expertise needed for professional roles in wildlife conservation and management, covering topics like conservation biology, endangered species, human impacts, captive breeding, and the role of zoos and parks. Guest speakers from research and management backgrounds will share insights on contemporary issues in wildlife ecology.
learningOutcomes: Apply ecological principles and ethical considerations to Australian wildlife management and conservation.
Analyse diverse stakeholder perspectives and current literature relating to complex wildlife management issues.
Use contemporary field skills in wildlife ecology to survey and identify terrestrial vertebrates.
Interpret and communicate research findings effectively using appropriate scientific conventions.
Collaborate effectively to evaluate the potential impact of a proposed development on native fauna.

91118.description: This subject delves into fish biology and biodiversity across marine, estuarine, and freshwater environments. You'll study fisheries sustainability and practices in the context of climate change, focusing on the ecological management needed for sustainable fisheries development. You'll compare NSW and Australian practices with global best practices and engage in field excursions and workshops with fisheries professionals.
learningOutcomes: understand and apply basic taxonomy and ecological knowledge of key marine fish resources and key field survey methods for fish stock assessment
identify appropriate key lab techniques and analyse/interpret data for fish stock assessment
use established modeling techniques and interpret results for fish stock assessment and management and apply to issues and conflicts in fishery management

91120.title: GIS and Remote Sensing
91120.description: This subject equips you with foundational geospatial skills, increasingly sought after in environmental science careers for sustainable resource management. You'll learn to use GIS, remote sensing, and digital image processing to analyse ecological landscapes, aquatic systems, biodiversity, and environmental health. The course includes practical training in ArcGIS, principles of satellite earth observation, and integrating remote sensing data into GIS. You'll apply this knowledge to address both hypothetical and real-world environmental management challenges, enhancing your employability in the global environmental sector.
learningOutcomes: Apply comprehensive knowledge and practical skills in geospatial technologies and data collection for environmental science.
Apply geovisualisation methods to convey environmental spatial information.
Design and develop a GIS project for natural resources and environmental management applications.
Use and process satellite imagery for ecosystem monitoring and analysis.
Articulate GIS models related to spatially distributed natural phenomena and their evolution through time.

91121.title: Aquatic Ecosystems
91121.description: This subject provides a thorough understanding of aquatic ecosystems,  encompassing freshwater, marine,and estuarine environments. You'll learn about the physical, chemical, and biological processes within these systems and how human activities impact their integrity. You'll appreciate the importance of ecological knowledge in informing management approaches to maintaining ecosystem health. The subject covers biodiversity patterns, ecosystem structure, processes and function, and impacts and management. You'll develop research skills through an independent written report, discussing your findings in the context of aquatic ecology and management.
learningOutcomes: Describe major aquatic habitats and their distribution and biological components.
Analyse the impact of human activities on aquatic environments and apply this knowledge to data collection and interpretation.
Use keys to identify aquatic organisms and interpret data to evaluate the ecological condition of aquatic environments.
Synthesise and communicate knowledge of aquatic systems in written scientific reports.

91123.title: Nature and Evolution
91123.description: The existence of all species on Earth today has been made possible through the evolution of a vast diversity of biota. This subject explores the considerable variation among living organisms and how they interact with their environment, addressing the question what enables life to exist in the range of habitats across the globe. You’ll examine the adaptations that bacteria, archaea, protists, plants, animals and fungi have evolved over time in response to changing environmental conditions and that allow biota to inhabit the vast array of ecosystems on Earth. The major taxa are explored with reference to  their evolution over time, that is movement from water to land and in some cases back again. You’ll conduct a short-term monitoring experiment to explore the important biotic and abiotic requirements for a sustainable ecosystem, generate testable hypotheses, collect scientific data and communicate the research findings. The subject concludes with a reflection of today’s pressures on biodiversity and how these shape current trends in evolution and species diversity.
learningOutcomes: Explain the fundamental principles of evolution by natural selection and its role in shaping the diversity of life on Earth.
Evaluate the role of environmental factors in driving evolutionary processes and shaping species distributions.
Distinguish among the major groups of organisms within each biological kingdom using key adaptations over evolutionary history.
Design and test a hypothesis about ecosystem function, collect data and interpret experimental findings.
Communicate effectively about evolutionary biology topics through scientific discussions, written syntheses and oral presentations.

91126.title: Coral Reef Ecosystems
91126.description: This subject investigates coral reefs, vital for their biodiversity and the livelihoods they support, yet facing an uncertain future due to overfishing, pollution, and climate change. You'll study how environmental and societal factors influence reef health and function. The course examines the diversity and evolution of reef ecosystems across different conditions, challenging the notion of 'pristine' and 'healthy' reefs. You'll learn about emerging technologies that revolutionise biodiversity assessment, ecosystem monitoring, and reef restoration equipping you with contemporary tools for effective reef management. Understanding these dynamics is key to developing strategies that protect these critical ecosystems.
learningOutcomes: Apply knowledge of coral reef organisms, habitats and ecological principles to produce habitat assessments describing reef condition.
Discuss technological approaches used to quantify reef ecosystem diversity for different spatial/temporal scales.
Conduct and effectively communicate scientific research on coral reefs.
Develop and execute effective team-based inquiry of a research question/goal.
Explain the principles and applications of coral reef ecosystem management based on critical evaluation of relevant sources.

91132.title: Molecular Biology
91132.description: This subject introduces you to molecular biology fundamentals and the experimental techniques for DNA manipulation. You'll learn about DNA, RNA, protein handling, molecular cloning, and DNA sequencing, including PCR. This subject encourages you to become adept at the techniques required for molecular analysis in a modern scientific laboratory. It lays the groundwork for advanced molecular biology studies and equips you with skills you will need for a career in pharmaceuticals, gene technology or research and development.
learningOutcomes: Explain and summarise the scientific principles of the molecular biology of DNA, RNA, and proteins.

Use specialised DNA, RNA, and protein isolation, manipulation, and cloning methods both individually and collaboratively; that are typical of molecular biology laboratory investigations; and communicate the results as laboratory reports.
Describe and explain the results of DNA and/or RNA experiments based on the scientific principles of nucleic acid structure.
Explain the relationships between DNA/RNA structures and molecular biology techniques.
Explain the relationships between DNA, RNA, protein structures and functions and associated molecular biology techniques.

91137.title: DNA Profiling
91137.description: This subject delves into DNA profiling, a pivotal tool in forensic science since the 1980s, now capable of identifying DNA from just a few human cells. You will explore the molecular biological techniques for producing DNA profiles, including DNA extraction, quantitation, amplification, and electrophoresis. You will also apply forensic procedures necessary for presenting DNA evidence in court, including item receipt and handling, item examination, chain of custody, profile interpretation and evaluation of the “weight of evidence”.
learningOutcomes: Appraise and explain the history and principles of forensic DNA profiling and the importance of DNA evidence.
Analyse forensic biological traces typically recovered from crime scenes.
Apply the basic principles of forensic DNA profiling using appropriate laboratory techniques and forensic procedures.
Evaluate the probative value of forensic DNA evidence.

91142.title: Biotechnology
91142.description: Biotechnology harnesses biological systems to develop products that benefit both human health and the environment. This subject introduces you to biotechnology fields like pharmaceuticals, agriculture, and environmental management. You’ll gain insights into the advances in biotechnology, learn how to design a controlled scientific protocol, be able to critically evaluate experimental findings, and communicate outcomes through a scientific report. Additionally, you will learn how innovations in biotechnology can be translated into commercial success considering intellectual property and market potentials. Through a blend of theory and hands-on experience, you'll become adept at bridging science and commerce, ready to contribute to this dynamic industry.
learningOutcomes: Articulate the biotechnology processes involved in synthesising food products and recombinant proteins; in the use of gene therapy; in the isolation and manipulation of stem cells
Apply biotechnology processes to propose better diagnosis and treatment of disease
Develop proficiency in laboratory-based techniques and research methodologies
Critically evaluate experimental findings and communicate outcomes through a formal scientific report
Appraise the market potential of a novel biotechnology product and translate this to a business, non-scientific audience in the form of an oral pitch
91142.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have completed 91161 Cell Biology and Genetics.

91145.title: Environmental Protection and Management
91145.description: Environmental protection and management practices apply scientific principles to plan for, and mitigate the effects of, human activity on the environment to ensure provision of ecosystem goods and services into the future. You will be introduced to approaches in environmental protection and management, investigate the role and contribution of science to environmental decision making, and explore the development of solutions to environmental issues.
learningOutcomes: Identify various perspectives on local and global environmental challenges and complex array of factors influencing management strategies.
Describe the role of science in shaping environmental laws and policies.
Apply a critical and evidence-based approach to environmental problem-solving.
Communicate and collaborate effectively in diverse contexts.

91154.title: Ecology
91154.description: Ecology examines the interplay between living species and abiotic environments. This field of science provides critical insights for conserving species and maintaining healthy, sustainable ecosystems for future generations.   In this subject, you’ll study a diverse range of species ranging from microbes and insects up to plants and vertebrate fauna, gaining insights on how they influence complex ecological patterns and processes across global environments. You’ll practice essential ecology field techniques by working in three different Australian biomes and discover how to analyse, visualise, and interpret your field-collected data using R coding.   This knowledge and hands-on experience are essential for a wide range of careers and provides a stepping stone to advanced environmental studies, equipping you to understand and address ecological challenges.
learningOutcomes: Explain how spatial, temporal, and environmental variations influence the structure and functions of ecosystems and the distribution and abundance of species.
Assess and identify a diverse range of species and environmental features.
Plan and perform ecological field research and conduct statistical tests to analyse, interpret, and visualise field-collected data.
Communicate ecological knowledge to educate and inform different audiences.

91155.title: Stream and Lake Assessment
91155.description: Australia's scarce surface water is vital for both biodiversity and human needs, including irrigation, drinking, and industry. This subject teaches you to assess the health of streams and lakes, using biomonitoring and water quality analysis to manage freshwater ecosystems effectively. You'll learn about Australian freshwater systems and the implications of human activities such as water removal for consumption, water regulation, and contamination. Designed for aspiring freshwater ecologists, the course includes a two-day field trip, preparing you for roles in government, consultancy, industry, or academia. Your understanding will inform critical discussions on water resource management and environmental protection.
learningOutcomes: Use a range of indicators to conduct assessments of stream ecosystem health based on current approaches to water quality assessment.
Distinguish the various approaches to freshwater ecosystem assessment, management, and their strengths and limitations.
Describe the biological, chemical and hydrological characteristics of freshwater ecosystems.
Apply practical project management skills for freshwater ecosystem assessment.

91156.title: Ocean Systems and Climate Change
91156.description:
Healthy oceans underpin Earth’s climate, biodiversity and human wellbeing, yet they are increasingly threatened by climate change and other human pressures. This subject explores ocean systems across biological, ecological and social scales, from microbes and primary producers to habitat-forming species, food webs and conservation strategies, and from scientific evidence to policy and management solutions.

You will examine how marine ecosystems regulate climate and provide essential ecosystem services, how they respond to stressors such as ocean warming, acidification and deoxygenation, and how these changes are measured, interpreted and used to inform marine protection and conservation. Through Australian and global case studies, including place-based and Sea Country perspectives, you will engage with contemporary approaches to monitoring, restoration and innovation in ocean science.

The subject integrates fieldwork, laboratory analysis, data interpretation and science communication, and aligns with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, particularly SDG 13 (Climate Action) and SDG 14 (Life Below Water). Graduates of this subject will be well prepared for careers in environmental science, sustainability, conservation, policy, and non-government organisations, and equipped with the knowledge and skills to contribute to a more sustainable future for our oceans.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of how ocean systems—from microbes to macrophytes—regulate Earth’s climate, support marine biodiversity, and provide ecosystem services across local, Australian and global contexts.

Analyse the impacts of climate change stressors on marine ecosystems and coastal communities, and evaluate how scientific evidence and Indigenous knowledge systems, including Sea Country, informs marine protection, conservation and management.

Work autonomously or in teams to apply field, laboratory and data-driven approaches to develop skills in marine ecosystem condition and productivity assessments, and critically evaluate their use in environmental monitoring, conservation and decision-making.
Design and reflect an independent, inquiry-based project that integrates scientific, social and policy perspectives.
Develop written communication skills in designing a research proposal and oral communication skills in engaging in a scientific debate.

91157.title: Marine Algae and Productivity
91157.description: Marine algae sustain all marine life. They are the oxygen-providing powerhouses of our oceans and the foundation of marine food webs. This subject covers the biology, physiology, and ecology of marine algae, from microscopic phytoplankton to towering kelp forests found on our rocky shores. Emphasising problem-based learning, you'll design and conduct experiments to investigate algal responses to environmental change. You will learn to assess algal photosynthetic health and explore adaptation strategies. The course blends theory with practical research in labs and a three-day field excursion, fostering skills in experimental design, data analysis, and collaborative learning. By the end, you'll understand the diversity, adaptability and critical role of algae and in marine ecosystems.
learningOutcomes: Identify and describe characteristics of key microalgal and macroalgal groups.
Evaluate the physiological condition of algae under different environmental stressors.
Design and conduct experiments to assess the effects of climate change on algal physiology and ecology.
Demonstrate understanding of the significance of marine algae in ocean systems and describe the various roles key groups play in oceanic processes.
Analyse the environmental factors and ecological processes shaping marine algal communities.

91159.title: Environmental Remediation
91159.description: Environmental Remediation introduces you to the practice and philosophies behind responsibly remediating degraded landscapes. It builds on your foundational understanding of ecosystem processes and investigates major environmental problems and effective solutions through a range of real-world case studies, cutting-edge research discoveries, and current industry practices.  You’ll learn through hands-on laboratory practicals, field work experience, interactive online classes, and an independent research project tailored to your own interests. You'll examine anthropogenic processes and their impacts on natural environments, plan and conduct a local site assessment, and create a professional-level report providing evidence-based solutions for complex environmental problems.   The skills you develop - practical, analytical, and translational - are highly valued across a spectrum of careers within and beyond environmental science.
learningOutcomes: Identify and contextualise the science that underpins effective, responsible environmental remediation practices across global contexts.
Investigate and summarise evidence of past, current, and future states of sites via desktop research.
Conduct independent field work to assess site health and environmental degradation using safe, ethical, and culturally respectful professional practices.
Design evidence-based remediation projects tailored to improve local contexts and solve environmental problems.
91159.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have completed 91154 Ecology; 91107 The Biosphere.

91161.title: Cell Biology and Genetics
91161.description: This subject introduces you to cell biology, focusing on cell structure and function, biological molecules, genetics, and theories of inheritance. You'll develop professional skills in laboratory techniques, data analysis, and quantitative methods to study cellular organisation. You will also learn how to utilise modern library resources to find and review published research literature, evaluate its content and significance, and create both written and oral presentations that can be used to communicate scientific concepts. By the end of this subject, you'll be adept at sourcing, assessing, and utilising information to address scientific problems.
learningOutcomes: Explain key concepts of cell biology and genetics clearly and concisely.
Perform laboratory experiments accurately and analyse resulting data.
Present scientific data in graphical, tabular and written formats.
Research a scientific topic relevant to cell biology and genetics.

91168.title: Ecological Genetics
91168.description: Molecular genetic techniques are rapidly becoming essential for fields as diverse as conservation biology, marine and fisheries management, biosecurity and human disease and health.  This subject provides you with a comprehensive understanding of molecular genetic techniques and their applications in answering ecological questions and addressing human interactions with the biosphere.  You'll explore how to use environmental DNA to detect invasive or problem species, understand species units for conservation, model evolutionary changes infectious diseases and uncover the genetic basis of traits. This subject is equally relevant for students in environmental, conservation, and health sciences, and offers hands-on learning, focusing on the practical application of molecular genetics in real-world scenarios using the latest research in the field.
learningOutcomes: Explain how evolutionary theory underpins molecular ecology and the ways in which environmental factors impact the functional biology of organisms.
Identify the question/s asked in a biological research study and compare and contrast the molecular ecological techniques used to answer these question/s.
Analyse and interpret genetic sequence data using bioinformatics tools and databases.
Apply molecular ecological techniques to assess organismal identity, distribution, abundance, and phylogeography.
Interpret and communicate scientific findings to discuss contemporary issues relating to ecological genetics.

91178.title: Applications of Molecular Biology
91178.description: This subject introduces you to the eukaryotic genome's structure and 'omics' technologies such as genomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics. It explores gene expression regulation, including transcriptional, post-transcriptional, and epigenetic mechanisms, alongside RNA roles. You will learn about gene therapy, microarray, and next-generation sequencing technologies, as well as the detection of genetic mutations causing disease. The significance of computational biology and bioinformatics in analysing molecular data is highlighted, with a continuous focus on molecular biology's role in enhancing human health.
learningOutcomes: Understand the fundamentals of eukaryotic gene structure, function, and expression in relation to health and disease.
Perform molecular biology experiments and bioinformatics analyses, employing professional skills to link theory with practical applications.
Critically evaluate scientific literature and apply molecular biology knowledge and skills to new problems.
Analyse and communicate molecular biology data effectively, understanding the significance of peer-reviewed research in scientific advancement.
Work collaboratively in a team environment to discuss and solve computer-based bioinformatics problems.

91180.title: Immunology and Human Health
91180.description: With this subject, you will be equipped with an understanding of the immune system and its role in combating diseases, and you'll be guided to apply this insight to immunological research. You'll develop knowledge of the immune system's components and their collective efforts to protect health, fight infections, inhibit tumours, and repair tissues. You'll learn how modulation of the immune system can either help overcome infection or may lead to autoimmune disease and you'll explore the potential for therapeutic interventions. This subject will enhance your grasp of immunological concepts and their practical applications in medicine and industry, fostering skills relevant to both academic and professional settings. Through this subject, you'll gain the expertise to contribute to advancements in health and disease management.
learningOutcomes: Explain the relevance, role and responses of the immune system in human health, infection and disease.
Distinguish and describe the characteristics and functions of molecules and cells of the innate and adaptive immune systems and how they operate synergistically and antagonistically.
Examine and apply strategies to modulate immune responses to improve human health in local and global contexts.
Apply safe laboratory practices when isolating, characterising, and analysing immune cells and their function using blood, animal tissues, and cell products.
Acquire, critically evaluate and communicate scientific data in the context of the immune system and latest immunological findings.

91189.title: Urban Sustainability and Resilience
91189.description: Urban Sustainability and Resilience explores the creation of sustainable cities amidst environmental challenges like climate change and population growth. This subject scrutinises green technologies, waste reduction, renewable energy, sustainable materials, water recycling, urban heat mitigation, and carbon neutrality. It offers a scientific and ecological perspective on building healthier communities and sustainable urban practices for the future.
learningOutcomes: Understand the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals relevant to Urban Systems and show an appreciation of directions that may be taken to achieve these goals.
Understand the factors affecting the growth of urban regions both globally and locally.
Collaboratively research and propose best-practice solutions to achieve environmental sustainability through the application of environmental assessments, policies, planning, and urban design.
Evaluate the major issues that impact on and contribute to urban sustainability and resilience
Communicate urban sustainability and resilience concepts in a convincing, clear, and concise manner and appropriate for multiple disciplines and stakeholders.

91191.title: Bionanotechnology
91191.description: This subject delves into how biological systems inspire nanotechnology, highlighting nature's proficiency in self-assembling complex structures like cell membranes and DNA. By examining the underlying science of these processes and their applications in biosensing, biomedical, and materials innovations, such as the ion-channel biosensor, you will understand how biological insights are harnessed in cutting-edge nanotechnologies.
learningOutcomes: Describe the biological processes of signal transduction, neuronal signaling and molecular recognition systems and how these can be mimicked and applied in biosensing and other nanotechnology applications.
Discuss and compare biomedical applications of nanotechnology and contemporary biosensor technologies.
Evaluate and discuss potential safety risks associated with various nanomaterials and nanoparticles and their interactions with biological systems.
Critique and synthesize current primary literature on a given topic in bionanotechnology and communicate the findings as a written critical review.

Effectively communicate to, peers and experts in the field, using both verbal and visual display (powerpoint presentation), the outcomes of primary research sourced from the literature and respond to questions and feedback from peers and experts.

91195.title: Epidemiology and Pathogenesis of Infections
91195.description: Infectious diseases have had an enormous impact on human civilisation, killing more people than all wars combined. Most viruses and bacteria do not cause infections in humans. In Epidemiology and Pathogenesis of Infections you will explore the how and why some organisms cause infections in humans. You'll learn about the challenges of treatment, antibiotic resistance, vaccination and pandemic control. Through practical work, you'll examine food poisoning outbreaks, hand bacteria sanitiser effectiveness, and test cellular responses to viruses. You'll develop skills in learning to analyse evidence and apply critical thinking to investigate and identify pathogens. Additionally, you'll enhance your science communication abilities by creating educational videos on current pathogens and infection prevention strategies.
learningOutcomes: Describe the mechanisms of pathogenesis, epidemiology of infectious diseases and features that enable organisms to cause disease in humans.
Identify and evaluate infections of public health concern.
Interpret statistics pertinent to epidemiology to evaluate transmission and infection outbreaks and risk factors.

Critically analyse scientific literature, government and social websites and creatively apply communication skills to advance knowledge and education on organisms that cause diseases that are important in society today.

91251.title: Foundations of Food Science
91251.description: This subject introduces the foundation concepts in food science, providing a detailed overview of the properties and functions of foods. The pipeline from primary production, whether it is in the wild, farm or factory, to product formulation and production, to packaging and distribution, to the end consumer is explored. The challenges of providing sufficient food to the global population to support the overall health and wellbeing of individuals and communities, in an economic and environmentally sustainable manner is investigated. Particular consideration of how innovative technologies can be applied to address global challenges related to sustainable production of food is investigated.
learningOutcomes: Define foundation concepts in food science and technology including the components, properties and function of foods.
Explain how food science and technology contributes to health and wellbeing at the individual, community and global level.
Use systems thinking approach to address challenges facing the globe in providing nutritional and sustainable food to meet the needs of the global population.
Articulate how food scientists and technologists contribute to addressing the food challenges facing the planet.
Critically analyse information from a range of sources to evaluate the potential of technological advancements in food science.

91252.title: Food Processing
91252.description: Virtually all foods produced and consumed are processed in some way. Even ready-to-eat whole foods undergo processing to facilitate distribution, extend shelf life, and ensure safety. In this subject, you will examine the physicochemical and biochemical transformations that occur during food processing and their effects on the nutritional and sensory qualities, shelf life, and safety of the final product. The subject specifically focuses on food processing to (1) modify the structure of foods, (2) improve preservation and shelf life, (3) enhance nutritional quality, and (4) increase the sustainability of food products. You will be introduced to a variety of tests used in the food and beverage sector to evaluate product properties and assess the impact of different processing approaches. The practical component of this subject will develop your troubleshooting and analytical skills, which are applicable across the food and beverage industry.
learningOutcomes: Describe how food processing can be used to enhance the shelf-life, nutritional quality, and sensory qualities of food.
Analyse industry standards that are used to assess processed foods.
Identify infrastructure and engineering used for industrial scale production of foods..

91253.title: Food Product Development
91253.description: This capstone subject allows students to work in a team to apply their food science and technology knowledge to develop a novel food or beverage product. The entire product development pipeline from idea generation through to design, formulation development and product assessment is covered.
learningOutcomes: Ability to apply food science and technology discipline knowledge to innovate and problem solve during the development of a novel food product.
Ability to work effectively, professionally and ethically as a member of a team.
Ability to apply systems thinking and sustainability approaches to the development of a food product.
Ability to synthesise commercial, scientific and social concepts and data and apply to the development of a novel product.
Communicate research findings to a diverse range of stakeholders.

91254.title: Food Safety and Quality
91254.description: Food products are only viable if they are safe and of consistent quality. Therefore, food companies must implement plans and processes to ensure both the safety and quality of their products. This helps them not only comply with regulatory requirements but also produce products of consistent quality. This subject will enable you to understand the techniques and regulatory frameworks that food companies use to ensure their products are safe and consistently meet consumer expectations. You will investigate the risks associated with the production and consumption of food and beverages, as well as the strategies used by industry, governments, and consumers to manage these risks. You will begin by studying regulatory frameworks related to food safety, using risk assessment approaches to identify physical and biological hazards. You will then examine quality control, quality assurance, and quality management systems used by food and beverage companies.
learningOutcomes: Interpret an apply the legislative and industry approaches used to control food safety and quality at a state, national and international level.
Identify safety hazards in the food and beverage industry and assess their impact on both human health and manufacturing practices.
Apply a risk assessment framework to assess health and safety risks associated with specific food or beverage products.
Design an effective quality management program.

91255.title: Chemistry and Physics of Food
91255.description: The chemical and physical properties of food constituents and their interactions at a molecular level, underpin the properties of all foods. In this subject, students gain a deeper understanding of the form and functionality of both macro-constituents (water, carbohydrate, protein and lipid) and micro-constituents (vitamins, minerals, antioxidants, and colour, flavour and antinutritional compounds). This knowledge can be applied to the development of plant or animal based or fermented food products. Analytical techniques used in the food and beverage industry to assess and manage the quality of food through food processing are reinforced through the laboratory component of the subject.
learningOutcomes: Understand the range of food constituents available globally from plant and animal sources.
Describe the relationship between the chemical and physical properties of the constituents and the form and functionality of the food product.
Describe the importance of micro-constituents (vitamins, antioxidants, colour and flavour compounds) on the nutritional and sensory qualities of food.
Understand and analyse the macro-constituents (water, carbohydrate, proteins and lipids) and their contribution to the food properties.
Describe the physical chemistry, biochemistry and processing behaviour of the major food constituents.

91256.title: Food and Nutrition
91256.description: This subject aims to develop students' understanding of the association between nutrition, health, and disease. It examines the role of nutrition in maintaining human health and preventing diseases, with a particular focus on exploring: (1) nutrition requirements across the various stages of the human lifecycle; (2) eating patterns and behaviours of vulnerable groups at risk of food insecurity; (3) nutrient requirements, deficiency and excess intake on the aetiology of diseases, such as obesity, cardiovascular disease, diabetes and cancer; (4) methods of dietary assessment, including an appraisal of effectiveness; and (5) current nutrition policies, systems and guidelines aimed at preventing and managing disease in the Australian population.
learningOutcomes: Describe the nutrient intake requirements, food sources and significance of macronutrients and micronutrients at different stages of the human life cycle.
Explain the role of food in the maintenance of a healthy lifestyle and the prevention of diet-related diseases.
Examine the role of the current Australian nutrition guidelines and synthesise the evidence into practical and easy-to-understand information.
Describe and appraise the evidence for eating patterns and behaviours of vulnerable groups at risk of food insecurity in Australia.
Compare and contrast key elements and effectiveness for different dietary assessment methods.
