91270.title: Plant Physiology and Climate Change
91270.description: This subject provides a comprehensive understanding of plant physiology and ecophysiology, central to many careers in environmental science. You'll learn about plant productivity and the key role of land plants in water, carbon, nutrient, and energy cycles. These concepts are central to understanding how ecosystems and agriculture affect the climate and vice versa. Through practical experiments, including a major team-led glasshouse project, weekly self-paced videos and peer interaction you'll master concepts such as how plants fix carbon in photosynthesis, transport water from soil to atmosphere, absorb nutrients, transport the carbohydrates they produce, and what happens when they are exposed to environmental stress. This knowledge is essential for understanding how plants interact with the environment and respond to our changing climate.
learningOutcomes: Distinguish and evaluate different plant strategies for capturing light and fixing carbon, transporting water, taking up nutrients and responding to environmental stress associated with climate change.
Design and conduct a glasshouse experiment to investigate the effects of environmental stress on plants, using current ecophysiological methodologies and techniques.
Actively and respectfully engage with peers and team members in collaborative learning and professional research contexts.

Apply an understanding of plant physiology and ecophysiology to critically interpret experimental findings and effectively communicate these insights in an appropriately framed and referenced scientific research report.
Identify and explain important cultural considerations for working effectively with and for Indigenous Australians in plant ecophysiological research on Country.
91270.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have completed a subject or training in basic ecology and/or biological science.

91309.title: Biodiversity Conservation
91309.description: Human activities are contributing to the extinction of native biodiversity, which leads to reduced ecosystem function, and diminished provision of ecosystem services essential for human welfare. In this subject, you gain knowledge and practical skills targeting the conservation of native biodiversity – using a scientific approach – to halt species extinction and to ensure healthy ecosystem function and services. In practical classes in the laboratory and field, supported by lectures each week covering disciplinary knowledge, you learn how to identify terrestrial flora and fauna using taxonomic principles, and how to use these identification skills to perform field surveys of biodiversity and assessments of species interactions (e.g. plant-pollinator interactions). This subject provides you with a next-level understanding of the application of ecological principles to applied conservation settings involving processes such as climate change, altered fire regimes, invasive species, and urbanisation.
learningOutcomes: Describe the characteristics that define the Anthropocene, including global patterns of species extinction, and spatial and temporal patterns in biodiversity; and use appropriate ecological methods to measure biodiversity for effective conservation.

Explain how anthropogenic disturbances such as climate change and altered fire regimes can lead to extinction of native biodiversity; develop a positive mindset to cope with ecological grief when working in the field of biodiversity conservation; and articulate how Traditional Ecological Knowledge contributes to successful conservation efforts.

Evaluate and adopt appropriate scientific approaches for use in the conservation of native biodiversity; and explain mechanistic links between biodiversity, ecosystem function, and ecosystem services, while appreciating different ways to value biodiversity.

Identify terrestrial Australian plant and animal species using taxonomic principles; and apply identification skills in ecological field surveys of biodiversity and assessments of species interactions (e.g. plant-pollinator interactions).
Conduct statistical tests to analyse field-collected data; interpret findings in relation to conservation objectives; and communicate ecological results in a clear scientific way.

91314.title: General Microbiology
91314.description: This subject provides you with an introduction to the structure, function and taxonomy of microorganisms, including bacteria, archaea, protozoa, fungi, and viruses. Key topics include microscopy, sterilisation, microbial growth, identification, and the use of antibiotics and molecular techniques. Practical sessions will equip you with essential laboratory skills for isolating, growing, and identifying microbes, as well as aseptic techniques widely used in scientific research.

describe how microorganisms and their components relate to growth, disease, and survival in natural environments and in the laboratory
describe the nutritional and physical factors affecting microbial growth and apply these to identify appropriate methods to culture and control microorganisms
apply techniques to visualise, culture, identify and investigate microorganisms in the laboratory

91320.title: Metabolic Biochemistry
91320.description:
This subject introduces you to cellular metabolism and energy transfer mechanisms. It provides an overview of the main carbohydrate catabolic and anabolic pathways including glycolysis, the Krebs cycle, oxidative phosphorylation.

It provides an understanding of nitrogen and fatty acid metabolism, and the metabolic specialisation of tissues. Additionally, you'll study cell signalling and hormonal regulation of homeostasis. This knowledge underpins further studies in biological and biomedical sciences, focusing on the principles of cellular reactions and their relevance to various cell types. The subject will also introduce you to the basic tools and methods of enzymatic biochemical experimentation.
learningOutcomes: Explain the major biochemical pathways in nature whereby organisms store and use energy.
Critically analyse and report on laboratory data.
Apply logical thought, critical thinking and problem solving skills in a scientific context.
Demonstrate excellence in written scientific communication.
Evaluate and use information from different sources such as research and review articles, textbooks, catalogues and technical references.

91368.title: Bioreactors and Bioprocessing
91368.description: This subject focuses on design, setup, operations and application of bioreactors in biotechnology. It covers growth of different feedstock biomass in bioreactors, downstream processing and creating high-value products from the biomass. You'll gain insights into the cellular and biochemical characteristics of key organisms like algae, bacteria and yeast. Additionally, you'll consider the sustainability and economic aspects of bioreactor application in industry. Your learning journey will include a combination of independent study, practical experiences and field trips, giving you hands on experience and real-world insights into bioreactor operations and bioprocessing.
learningOutcomes: Apply knowledge to design and operate a simple bioreactor and gain relevant insights to apply in biotechnological processes.
Analyse upstream and downstream bioprocesses and evaluate strategies for the development and scale-up of high-value bioproducts.
Identify and apply appropriate downstream processing techniques for the extraction, isolation, purification, and characterisation of biomass-derived products and molecules of interest.
Conduct and communicate independent research on scientific topics, interact with biotech industry leaders

91369.description: In this subject, you'll learn the business aspects of biotechnology, including innovation, entrepreneurship, career management, ethics, risk management in clinical trials, quality control, and compliance with standards like ISO (International Organisation for Standardisation) and GMP (Good Manufacturing Process). You'll explore career development and risk management tools, and business strategies for financial viability in biotech. The course also covers the commercialisation process, business planning, and sustainability. Case studies from medical and environmental biotech sectors provide practical insights. You'll refine communication skills and keep your scientific knowledge current, preparing you for future challenges in the biotech industry.
learningOutcomes: Reflect on and discuss the biobusinesses sector including types of biobusinesses, challenges they encounter, and the skills required to succeed in the industry.
Describe the integration of biotechnology and business, including product development and growth strategies.
Reflect on and participate in ethical practices in modern biobusiness.

91400.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology
91400.description: This subject equips you with foundational knowledge in human physiology, which is essential for advanced biomedical studies. You'll develop an understanding of human anatomy and body functions, enhancing your knowledge and practical skills. Your learning combines lectures, hands-on campus activities, and online resources. You will learn about the body's anatomical structure, major systems, and relevant medical terminology. Additionally, you'll develop presentation, research, and report writing skills, preparing you for future subjects.
learningOutcomes: Apply your knowledge of human anatomy and physiology in communicating the processes that underlie the healthy human state and also selected diseases

Identify and locate the key organs of the organ systems presented in the subject and be able to best describe their particular functions as well as be able to relate their structure, composition and location to their particular functions.

91401.title: Immunology
91401.description: This subject introduces you to immunology fundamentals, preparing you for careers in biomedical research, biotechnology, and diagnostic pathology. You will study the identification, morphology, and function of blood, bone marrow, and immune cells, exploring their development and roles in haemostasis and immunity. Learning progresses from initial immune reactions to adaptive responses and memory formation, focusing on foreign body recognition and infection response. Practical sessions familiarise you with key immunological techniques, including serial dilutions, Coombs test, ELISA, and flow cytometry, vital for pathology and research settings.
learningOutcomes: Practice laboratory safety and perform blood-related tests adhering to guidelines.
Identify, describe and relate innate immune cell morphology and function.
Analyse the complement system and its role in immune responses.
Describe the morphology, function, and differentiation of different components of the adaptive immune system including B and T cells, antibodies and thymus.
Explain the two T cell MHC-restricted antigen processing and presentation pathways.

91429.title: Physiological Bases of Human Movement
91429.description: This subject explores the normal structure and function of the human body's key organ systems and their interactions, vital for activities like running, eating, and even sleeping. You'll learn how cells form tissues with specialised functions and how systems like the integumentary, nervous, endocrine, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, respiratory, and urinary work both independently and together. Within this course, you will emphasise the relevance of these systems to sports and healthy living, highlighting the importance of organs such as the lungs, liver, kidneys, brain, heart, and blood vessels in maintaining life and enabling movement.
learningOutcomes: Correctly use anatomical terms and nomenclature.
Describe and explain the structure and function of major organ systems of the human body, including the constituent cells types and tissues.
Apply data analysis skills to critically examine experimental data.

Communicate clearly and succinctly to a general lay audience in written form.

91500.title: Histology
91500.description: Building on your existing knowledge from Anatomy and Physiology, this subject delves into the micro-architecture of human tissues and organs. You'll engage in independent study, practical classes, and workshops to understand the tissue structure of the body's major systems. You will learn about the preparation and diagnosis of histological samples through participation in a major project, with particular emphasis on laboratory safety, professional practice and written communication.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate laboratory safety and proficiency in histological techniques.
Set up a light microscope correctly for Köhler illumination.
Identify and describe various tissue types and organ systems and infer their functions.

91529.title: Pathophysiology and Pharmacology 1
91529.description: This subject introduces the science underpinning common diseases encountered in clinical practice, including diabetes, asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), cardiovascular disease, stroke, and dementia. It examines the pathophysiology of these conditions and the pharmacology of commonly used treatments. Students develop an understanding of normal and altered body function and apply this knowledge to support evidence-informed nursing care. The subject emphasises the recognition of clinical signs and symptoms, the interpretation of patient information and investigations, and the principles of pharmacological and non-pharmacological management. Ethical and legal considerations relevant to nursing practice are integrated throughout the subject.
learningOutcomes: Outline the aetiology and pathophysiological basis of obesity and diabetes, and the treatment and management of these conditions.
Describe the pathophysiological processes associated with common cardiovascular, respiratory, and renal diseases and their treatment and management.
Identify the physiological and cognitive changes associated with neural injury and related conditions, including principles of pain assessment and management.
Apply clinical knowledge and reasoning in collaborative settings to evaluate patient status and develop effective treatment strategies and nursing care plans in clinical scenarios.

Demonstrate respectful, inclusive communication of health information to the general public, integrating clinical accuracy with patient-centred explanations appropriate for diverse Australian communities, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples.

91561.title: Health and Homeostasis 2
91561.description:
Understanding human anatomy and physiology is fundamental to safe and effective nursing practice. Building on the anatomical, physiological and homeostatic concepts introduced in 91562 Health and Homeostasis1, this subject extends your understanding of human body structure, function and physiological regulation.

You will examine the endocrine, neural, haematological, immune, urinary and reproductive systems, together with nutrition, body fluid regulation, pregnancy and fetal development, and principles of inheritance.

Through practical activities and introductory clinical case scenarios, you will apply physiological knowledge to explain normal body processes and disruptions to homeostasis. You will also develop your ability to communicate accurate scientific information clearly to peers and non-specialist audiences. Through its study of anatomy, physiology and introductory pharmacological principles, this subject develops the scientific foundation for later learning in pathophysiology, pharmacology and clinical nursing practice.
learningOutcomes: Identify and explain the structures and functions of the organs and body systems studied in this subject.
Explain how body systems interact and are regulated to maintain homeostasis.
Apply physiological knowledge to interpret clinical case scenarios and explain disruptions to homeostasis.

Explain key physiological processes related to neural and endocrine regulation, blood and haemostasis, immunity, nutrient metabolism, body fluid regulation, reproduction, pregnancy, fetal development and principles of inheritance
Locate, critically evaluate and use appropriate physiological information, and communicate it clearly and accurately to non-specialist audiences.

It covers foundational chemistry and biology, and through homeostasis, illustrates how organ systems like the skeletal, muscular, cardiovascular, respiratory, and gastrointestinal maintain health. The course introduces medical terminology and uses clinical case scenarios to demonstrate the practical application of your learning in professional settings. To prepare for Pathophysiology and Pharmacology 1 and 2, a primer on pharmacology and pharmacokinetics is also included.

Explain how the interrelationships between organs achieve system functions and maintain homeostasis.

91563.title: Haematology
91563.description:
This subject introduces you to haematology's core concepts and their application in modern laboratories. You will study blood and bone marrow cells, focusing on identification, morphology, and function, as well as their development and roles in haemostasis and immunity. You will learn about haematological diseases and the implications of haematological changes in illness. You will become familiar with modern laboratory analysers, learning to interpret data and resolve issues with these automated systems.

Practical sessions will train you in manual haematological techniques essential for pathology and research labs. You will practice these techniques, interpret results, and develop proficiency in haematology morphology through microscopy, enabling you to make clinical interpretations and diagnose haematological disorders accurately.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate safe laboratory practices and proficiency in haematological testing.
Measure, calculate and interpret normal and abnormal blood indices and relate the finding to a provision haematological diagnosis.
Explain the development and function of blood cells and coagulation pathways and identify changes associated with blood and coagulation disorders in the diagnosis of haematological disease.
Compare different manual testing methods to laboratory automation, and critically evaluate their limitations and sources of error.

91572.title: Proteomics
91572.description: This subject immerses you in proteomics, the study of all proteoforms expressed by a cell or organism at a given time. You'll learn to use analytical tools and bioinformatics to detect proteoform abundance changes, crucial for disease understanding. The course covers advanced sample preparation, proteoform fractionation, mass spectrometry, and data analysis techniques. It also sharpens your critical thinking and encourages an inquisitive approach to experimental design and data interpretation. Through practical work, including a lab project reported in publication style, you'll apply best practices to diverse sample types and demonstrate your ability to conduct independent research and analysis.
learningOutcomes: Articulate how proteomics fits into the broader picture of systems biology, biological research and medical biotechnology.
Plan an experiment using appropriate methods; taking into account the constraints of the available technology, sample numbers and amounts, and the underlying hypothesis.
Perform basic sample preparation on cellular and fluid samples, protein separation by 1-D electrophoresis, sample preparation for liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry and basic data analysis.
Collect, review and critically analyse published proteomics research and methodological literature.
Synthesise the collected data and supporting literature into a report that describes how the proteome of an organism can undergo biological changes due to a change in its environmental conditions.

Prepare, fix and stain cells for microscopic analysis.

91574.title: Biotechnology and Innovation Practice
91574.description: This subject introduces you to innovative technologies transforming the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of infectious diseases. You will study diagnostic methods including pathogen sequencing and microbiome analysis, therapeutic techniques such as genome editing, and strategies for vaccine development and biomarker discovery. The course also explores the dynamics of antimicrobial resistance. By its conclusion, you will not only comprehend the science behind these technologies but also appreciate the rapid progression of this field and the global challenges emerging from new biotechnological advances.
learningOutcomes: Analyse the foundation of molecular biology methods relevant to the development of new technologies to tackle important public health issues caused by infectious diseases.
Identify how new biotechnologies are developed and applied to solve medical problems related to infectious diseases.
Critique and apply learned concepts to specific scenarios and support the knowledge with scientific literature.
Work professionally in a team environment to summaries and present findings of a research topic

91575.title: Proteomics
91575.description: This subject immerses you in proteomics, the study of all proteoforms expressed by a cell or organism at a given time. You'll learn to use analytical tools and bioinformatics to detect proteoform abundance changes, crucial for disease understanding. The course covers advanced sample preparation, proteoform fractionation, mass spectrometry, and data analysis techniques. It also sharpens your critical thinking and encourages an inquisitive approach to experimental design and data interpretation. Through practical work, including a lab project reported in publication style, you'll apply best practices to diverse sample types and demonstrate your ability to conduct independent research and analysis.
learningOutcomes: Articulate how proteomics fits into the broader picture of systems biology, biological research and medical biotechnology.
Plan an experiment using appropriate methods; taking into account the constraints of the available technology, sample numbers and amounts, and the underlying hypothesis.
Perform basic sample preparation on cellular and fluid samples, protein separation by 1-D electrophoresis, sample preparation for liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry and basic data analysis.
Collect, review and critically analyse published proteomics research and methodological literature.
Synthesise the collected data and supporting literature into a report that describes how the proteome of an organism can undergo biological changes due to a change in its environmental conditions.

91576.title: Personalised Medicine
91576.description: This subject delves into personalised medicine, a cutting-edge approach to individual healthcare that considers each person's unique genetic makeup, environment, and lifestyle. You'll explore its current role and clinical value in health care, while examining the latest scientific breakthroughs in 'omics' technologies, tailored treatments, and molecular profiling. Through evaluation of authentic clinical scenarios, you will gain insights into the newest sector innovations and understand the existing challenges. The subject also considers the future directions for personalised medicine, focusing on individualised prevention strategies, diagnosis, treatments, and prognosis.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate the current utility of personalised medicine in the contexts of medical and health applications
Critically analyse new innovations, current challenges, and limitations in personalised medicine
Research and authenticate potential solutions for future advancement in personalised medicine

91705.title: Medical Devices and Diagnostics
91705.description: This subject looks at the science underlying medical devices used in clinical settings, as well as cutting-edge technologies poised to shape the future of medical diagnosis and treatment. You will explore a wide array of topics, including biomedical implants, diagnostic devices, biomaterials and biocompatibility within the body, microfluidic devices for medical applications, conducting clinical trials for medical devices, 3D bioprinting in healthcare, detecting oligonucleotides, portable and point-of-care devices, and the regulatory standards governing medical devices. Additionally, you'll examine the ethical, legal, social, cultural, and economic impacts of integrating these devices into medical practice. The course also introduces you to medical device regulatory frameworks and classification systems, while addressing challenges related to designing and executing clinical trials.
learningOutcomes: Identify the role of medical devices within the healthcare system and explain the regulatory environment.
Describe the key components and scientific principles of medical devices used in physiological function, diagnosis and treatment.
Investigate the scientific principles behind implantable medical technologies.
Critically analyse and communicate complex scientific, technical and regulatory information in the medical device sector, including ethical, social, cultural and economic considerations.

91707.title: Fundamentals of Pharmacology
91707.description: Fundamentals of Pharmacology introduces the principles of drug action, preparing you for 91709 (Advanced Pharmacology). You'll explore dose-response relationships, drug targets, receptors, chemical properties of drugs, and their effects on distribution and metabolism. The subject covers toxicology, precision (personalised) medicine, drug design, and issues around drugs of abuse and addiction. Practical sessions complement lectures by applying concepts to clinical scenarios. This foundational knowledge is vital for careers in medicine, biosciences, teaching, law, and more. Additionally, you'll learn to communicate scientific findings effectively to both professionals and the public, including creating content for digital platforms.
learningOutcomes: Apply pharmacological principles to various contexts including drug metabolism, therapeutic uses, and specific population treatments.
Explain the mechanisms of drug action and their interactions with biological systems.
Describe the pharmacology of venoms, toxins and insecticides and their effects on the human nervous system.
Perform enzyme-inhibitor kinetic experiments and explain the principles of substrate specificity and the structure activity relationships.
Conduct, analyse and communicate pharmacology research in diverse contexts.

91709.title: Advanced Pharmacology
91709.description: This subject advances your understanding of drug and xenobiotic action from 91707 (Fundamentals of Pharmacology). It encourages you to adopt a problem-solving approach, with a focus on molecular pharmacology in relation to pathophysiological issues. You'll delve deeper into the role of receptors and ion channels in drug action, selective toxicity for treating infections, and factors influencing target organ toxicity. The efficacy of major drug classes for the treatment of cancer, mental health, and respiratory, cardiovascular, and metabolic diseases, among others, is critically examined. Tutorials and case studies reinforce the clinical relevance of the material studied, enhancing your ability to apply pharmacological concepts to real-world scenarios.
learningOutcomes: Analyse the pharmacological principles and therapeutic applications of drugs across various diseases.
Evaluate the complexities of drug addiction, including its treatment and the pharmacological challenges of dependence.
Explain the process of drug development, from discovery to post-marketing surveillance, including the role of clinical trials and biomarkers.
Describe the use of monoclonal antibodies as both diagnostic and therapeutic agents.
Communicate pharmacological concepts effectively to a non-specialist audience using various presentation methods.

91817.title: Medical Biotechnology
91817.description: This subject allows you to apply your scientific and molecular biology knowledge to the discovery and development of medical biotechnologies. You'll enhance your laboratory skills through cell culture techniques in the HIVE laboratory, exploring treatments for diseases like cancer and respiratory disease. Through practicals, workshops, and inquiry-based activities, you'll master experimental design, data analysis, and interpretation, contributing to biotechnology research projects. You'll also learn about the clinical translation and commercialisation of new discoveries. Assessments focus on developing research skills, literature critique, experimental planning, and scientific communication, including ethical considerations. You'll stay abreast of clinical needs and advanced technologies for biomarker and drug discovery, understanding the development of cell-based therapies, biologics, gene therapies, regenerative medicine, and drug repurposing. This equips you with the expertise to innovate in medical biotechnology research.
learningOutcomes: Develop experimental plans to interrogate research questions based on ethical considerations and critical evaluation of relevant literature.
Develop laboratory-based and research skills in cell culture and in vitro models of disease.
Critically analyse and effectively communicate experimental findings in the context of existing literature on the topic.
Compare and describe clinical applications of different biotechnologies and methodologies in the medical field.
Foster creative thinking to identify knowledge gaps and meet clinical needs.

91818.title: Environmental Biotechnology
91818.description:
Environmental biotechnology uses advanced biotechnological tools to handle increasing environmental challenges, including waste management, renewable energy, and pollution control. This subject equips you with the knowledge and skills to utilise microbes for soil remediation, industrial waste recycling, and water purification. You will investigate into microbial ecology and develop strategic bioremediation plans to restore contaminated environments effectively.

You will explore the growing bio-economy, focusing on the production of biofuels and the development of high-value products. By integrating these sustainable industry practices, you will be at the forefront of creating innovative solutions that drive environmental sustainability and foster a greener future. You will learn through a combination of case study analysis, field trips, and practical laboratory sessions, providing hands-on experience and real-world insights into the applications of environmental biotechnology.
learningOutcomes: Explain the adaptation strategies of organisms in microbial habitats.

Identify and apply innovative biological solutions and advanced techniques to address environmental contamination issues, including effective bioremediation strategies and the tools necessary for monitoring environmental systems.
Apply engineering design principles to develop and optimise environmental biotechnological processes, ensuring efficiency and sustainability.

Combine chemical, microbiological, and molecular protocols to conduct robust experiments, formulate hypotheses, and communicate findings effectively in the form of a peer-reviewed journal articles, supported by primary literature.
Critically evaluate the commercial potential and environmental impact of novel biotechnological products, ensuring economic feasibility and sustainability.

91821.title: Transfusion Science
91821.description:
In this subject you will delve into human blood group systems and the antigens on red blood cells that differentiate individuals, crucial for recognizing foreign cells. You will learn about the body's immune response, antibody detection, blood compatibility, the importance of safety and infectious disease prevention in blood supply, transfusion reactions, haemolytic disease of the newborn, and immuno-haematology of platelets and leucocytes. You will also become familiar with transfusion in emergencies, legalities, stem cell transplantation, and cytokine use in hemopoiesis.

You will learn the core principles and techniques used by transfusion scientists in both clinical and research settings, including antibody identification and ensuring safe blood transfusion practices. The subject combines theory with practical workshops, employing various learning formats such as video lectures, presentations, readings, and interactive activities, fostering a comprehensive understanding of transfusion science.
learningOutcomes: Describe the principles and requirements for safe blood transfusion and transplantation.
Explain blood group systems, antigens, and antibodies as defined by the Australian and New Zealand Society of Blood Transfusion (ANZSBT).
Identify and apply quality assurance and regulatory frameworks in transfusion science.
Perform and interpret laboratory techniques for blood grouping and antibody identification.
Evaluate and communicate transfusion science information using various resources and methods.

91822.title: Human Genetics and Precision Medicine
91822.description: This subject equips you with an understanding of human genetics, bridging the gap between research and clinical application, particularly in precision medicine. You'll gain knowledge in Mendelian and molecular genetics, explore molecular diagnostics and gene therapy, and consider the practical and ethical implications of genetic advancements. Learning is interactive, blending theory with real-world applications to prepare you for the evolving landscape of medical genetics.
learningOutcomes: Describe and apply both the principles of Mendelian genetics and the molecular basis of genetics to demonstrate understanding of inheritance, and how whole populations are altered through the process of evolution.

Comprehend the broad applications of genetics within biology, biotechnology and medicine, the technologies currently being used in these fields, and the ways in which precision medicine can tailor an individual’s diagnosis and treatment to their unique genomic content.
Analyse, interpret and explain genetic information.
Demonstrate practical skills and learn laboratory techniques currently used in the field of genetics and precision medicine.
Effectively communicate experimental, interpretative and ethical aspects of science via oral presentations and written work.

91826.title: Advanced Haematology and Pathology Diagnosis
91826.description: This subject enhances your understanding of diseases affecting blood and organ systems, focusing on pathophysiology and diagnostic techniques. You'll learn to distinguish between healthy and diseased tissues, employing advanced microscopy and digital image analysis. The subject integrates interactive workshops and online learning led by field experts. You’ll gain professional digital competencies and diagnostic skills in line with modern laboratory practices applicable to the health sector.
learningOutcomes: Explain and interpret the pathophysiology of haematological and anatomical disorders and diseases
Examine via digital microscopy changes in human diseases and assess the relationship of these changes in diseased states
Describe how techniques such as immunohistochemistry and flow cytometry are used in the diagnosis of disease and be able to interpret data from these techniques.
Be able to gather and critically assess scientific information in order to improve professional written communication skills

91827.title: Advanced Medical Biochemistry
91827.description: In this subject you will be introduced to the fundamentals of medical and clinical biochemistry, crucial for biotechnology, medical research, and pathology lab analysis. You will study biochemical abnormalities underlying diseases, their diagnosis, clinical analysis, and treatment, with a focus on kidney and liver function, diabetes, lipid disorders, clinical enzymology, and serum proteins. Emphasis is also placed on safety, quality control and automation. You will be offered insights into clinical biochemistry's role in health, ensuring precise and relevant testing, which will be beneficial for those aspiring to careers in diagnostic pathology, clinical research, or laboratory management.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate effective collaboration and communication skills in diverse scientific contexts.
Describe and perform and interpret standard biochemical laboratory techniques for analysing blood and urine.
Apply research-based biomedical knowledge to explain common human biochemical pathologies.
Describe and explain fundamental requirements of quality assurance, quality control and reference intervals within a medical science laboratory.

91828.title: Evidence Based Practice in Medical Science
91828.description: This subject equips you with the skills to evaluate medical literature to make informed, evidence-based health recommendations, and to communicate this information to a variety of audiences using different modes. You'll learn to formulate clinical questions, source relevant evidence, and critically appraise evidence for its validity and applicability to specific patient groups. You’ll apply this knowledge to propose health solutions. The subject focuses on clinical trials. You'll gain insights into clinical trial design, methodology, ethics, data analysis, and factors affecting trial validity. Additionally, you'll enhance your communication skills, learning to adapt information for diverse audiences, crucial for various medical science careers.
learningOutcomes: Create comprehensive clinical questions and integrate literature evidence to evaluate, interpret, and synthesise answers.
Innovate and refine optimised search strategies to efficiently retrieve comprehensive evidence and communicate findings that effectively support clinical decision-making.
Evaluate and enhance clinical trial protocols to emphasise ethical considerations.
Reflect on personal goal setting strategies to enhance relevant professional skills by also leveraging GenAI for extending continuous self-improvement.
Identify and evaluate available medical science evidence and apply this to supporting Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people’s health and wellbeing.

The subject offers hands-on diagnostic lab experience, utilising the latest technologies to diagnose infectious diseases and select appropriate antimicrobial therapies. Through interactive workshops and practical sessions in the HIVE Superlab, you'll engage in critical analysis and interpretation of real case studies, honing professional skills such as quality assurance and laboratory safety. 91830.title: Human Pathophysiology
91830.description: This subject equips you with a comprehensive understanding of disease processes across major body systems, enhancing your grasp of changes in organ structure and function during the development of a disease. You will develop skills in clinical analysis and decision-making by examining real-life case scenarios and engaging in team-based problem-solving exercises. Learning is hands-on: in the laboratory, you will conduct medical tests such as ECGs, blood pressure readings, spirometry, and urine analysis, laying the foundation for your future as a skilled medical technician, healthcare professional, or carer.
learningOutcomes: Recognise changes in physiological function and organ structure of common disorders in each of the major body systems and the interactions between different systems
Use the pathophysiology concepts to analyse disease in different scenarios using appropriate inquiry methods with a ‘patient’ in a clinician’s style
Understand the unique health needs of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people
Select the appropriate diagnostic measures of the disorders, and use physical examinations and laboratory methods to make correct diagnosis as per practice by the clinicians.
Use the appropriate knowledge of pathophysiology to educate the general public without a medical background using creative approaches (presentation, short film, social media, talk show etc).

91838.title: Structural Anatomy and Neuroanatomy
91838.description:
Structural Anatomy and Neuroanatomy provides you with a comprehensive understanding of the human body, focusing on musculoskeletal anatomy and the neuroanatomical systems that enable sensory perception and motor functions. You'll study the body in regions, identifying bones, muscles, joints, and neurovascular structures, while also examining neural circuits responsible for movement and sensory experiences, including special senses like vision and hearing.

Through lectures, workshops, and cadaveric sessions, you'll explore the central and peripheral nervous systems, gaining insight into motor control and the basis of neurological disorders. The subject also delves into the neuroanatomy of sensory organs, teaching you how sensory information is processed and transmitted to the brain. Emphasising clinical relevance, you'll apply anatomical knowledge to medical scenarios, enhancing your expertise for healthcare professions and deepening your appreciation for human body complexity.
learningOutcomes: Apply anatomical knowledge and terminology to identify and discuss body structures.
Categorise musculoskeletal components and explain their functional relationships.
Analyse the correlation between anatomical structures and functions how they impact the overall human function.
Demonstrate teamwork and reflective practices in group projects.
Communicate effectively the interplay between anatomical structure and function.

91976.title: Optimising Health and Wellness In Older Persons
91976.description:
This subject is designed to build on your foundational knowledge and skills in the care of the older person across various healthcare environments. You will deepen your understanding of the ageing process and learn to manage complex health conditions in older persons, focusing on delivering high-quality, person-centred care. This subject emphasises practical skills for comprehensive health assessments, detection of patient deterioration, and advanced wound care management as it relates to the older person.

You will develop skills in interprofessional care coordination, effective communication, and end-of-life care strategies. Interactive online modules will facilitate your learning, ensuring you are well-prepared to meet the challenges in caring for older persons.

Students develop an understanding of The Aged Care Standards and how they relate to their nursing practice, with reference to the Royal Commission into the Aged Care Quality and Safety.
learningOutcomes: Determine the processes of and supports for healthy ageing in contemporary Australian society using a health promotion framework.
Perform comprehensive assessments and care for the older person with a focus on individual needs and gerontological knowledge and skills.
Recognise the complexities of chronic illness in the older person and the role of nursing in providing high-quality care.
Explore collaborative healthcare approaches for the older person across various settings.
Integrate evidence-based practice and effective therapeutic communication in nursing care for the older person with complex health needs.

92354.title: Introductory Pharmacology and Microbiology
92354.description: This subject introduces you to the principles of drug action and microbial infections, tailored for midwifery. You will engage with pharmacology and microbiology theories and their practical applications in midwifery practice. You will explore the biology of microorganisms, infection control and prevention, and apply these concepts to real-world scenarios. In pharmacology, you will learn about drug discovery, nomenclature and regulation, drug targets and pharmacokinetics, focusing on medications relevant to pregnancy, such as those for cardiovascular health, inflammation, pain, diabetes, blood clotting, infections, and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. Your learning will be grounded in experimental work and case studies, bridging theory with clinical practice.
learningOutcomes: Explain and apply the biology of microorganisms, sources of infection, and strategies to control microbial growth and transmission in midwifery practice.
Identify and critically evaluate key microbial infections and their effects on pregnancy, labour, birth, the puerperium, and neonatal adaptation.
Apply pharmacodynamic principles to midwifery scenarios, demonstrating understanding of drug actions, interactions, and implications for care.
Develop and justify treatment plans for midwifery case studies using evidence-informed knowledge of pharmaceutical interventions.

92383.title: Translating Research into Midwifery Practice
92383.description: This subject introduces you to the knowledge, skills, and values required to integrate evidence into safe and ethical midwifery practice. You will explore the foundations of research, including qualitative and quantitative methodologies, ethical principles, and the role of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence in health research. Emphasis is placed on developing skills in sourcing, critiquing, and applying research findings to support woman-centred decision-making. You will also learn to communicate evidence in culturally responsive and accessible ways, considering health literacy and supporting a midwifery culture that values inquiry, reflection, and evidence-informed care.
learningOutcomes: Critically analyse the role of research in midwifery practice, including the integration of consumer perspectives, to foster a culture of inquiry and evidence-informed care.
Differentiate between qualitative and quantitative research methodologies, including their epistemological foundations, and apply advanced knowledge to evaluate midwifery-specific research.
Apply advanced research skills to locate, appraise, and synthesise evidence from diverse sources, including emerging technologies, to inform midwifery practice, policy, and guideline development.
Communicate research findings effectively using culturally safe, inclusive, and woman-centred language to support informed decision-making, recognising that decisions rest solely with the woman.

Evaluate ethical, social, and cultural considerations in the design, conduct, and translation of midwifery research, demonstrating sound judgment and commitment to respectful, responsible research practice.

args.text: Admission into C07070 Graduate Diploma in Midwifery

92384.title: Midwifery as a Public Health Strategy
92384.description: This subject explores midwifery as a public health strategy grounded in primary health care and woman-centred frameworks. You will critically examine social, cultural, political, and economic factors including systemic inequities and the Social Determinants of Health that shape maternal and newborn health in Australia and globally. Guided by the Sustainable Development Goals, you will analyse midwifery’s role in promoting equity, access, and health across the lifespan. Emphasis is placed on consultation, collaboration, health promotion, systems thinking, and the midwife’s role as advocate and leader, particularly in improving outcomes for Indigenous women and families.
learningOutcomes: Critically evaluate midwifery as a public health strategy within a primary health care framework, evaluating its contribution to population health outcomes and policy development.

Evaluate the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals and synthesise the role of midwives in promoting global maternal and newborn health, with particular attention to advancing health equity for Indigenous populations.
Apply advanced knowledge of the Social Determinants of Health to critically examine their impact on equitable access to safe and appropriate maternity care.
Design and apply culturally safe, evidence-informed health promotion strategies in the perinatal period that foster positive, long-term health outcomes for women, infants, and families.

Critically reflect on personal and professional assumptions, values, behaviours, and positionality, and evaluate how these influence professional relationships and communication in midwifery practice, especially engagement and partnership with Indigenous women and families.

requisite.text: Admission into C07070 Graduate Diploma in Midwifery

92385.title: Promoting, Supporting and Protecting Breastfeeding
92385.description: This subject supports you in developing the foundational knowledge, skills, and attitudes necessary to promote, protect, and support breastfeeding within midwifery practice. Grounded in the Baby Friendly Health Initiative, WHO’s Ten Steps to Successful Breastfeeding, and the International Code of Marketing of Breastmilk Substitutes, the subject explores the anatomy and physiology of lactogenesis, the health and social benefits of breastfeeding, and the midwife’s role in helping women initiate and sustain breastfeeding. You will critically examine factors that influence breastfeeding outcomes, develop culturally safe communication strategies, and evaluate the broader public health and environmental implications of breastfeeding. Knowledge is applied through simulation, reflection, and practice-focused learning.
learningOutcomes: Describe the anatomy and physiology of lactogenesis and apply this knowledge to support breastfeeding in midwifery care.
Communicate the benefits of breastfeeding to women and families using culturally safe and inclusive language.
Apply evidence-informed strategies to support women initiating and sustaining breastfeeding and respond to common breastfeeding challenges.
Analyse the modifiable and non-modifiable factors that impact breastfeeding outcomes across diverse populations.
Evaluate the contribution of breastfeeding to environmental sustainability and public health.

requisite.text: Admission into C07070 Graduate Diploma in Midwifery

92386.title: Power, Politics and Midwifery
92386.description: This subject explores how gender, power, and socio-political contexts influence childbearing, examining midwifery through a feminist lens. You'll examine the historical medicalisation of childbirth, contemporary technological impacts, and the portrayal of childbearing in popular culture. Engage with case studies and online resources, including human rights and respectful care movements, to develop critical thinking and advocacy skills. Discussions in online forums and classes will deepen your understanding of midwifery practice within the framework of power dynamics, politics, and human rights.
learningOutcomes: Examine midwifery from a feminist perspective and identify aspects of the profession that have been and remain affected by gender and other inequalities
Recognise power structures in the current health and political systems and the influence these have on women, childbearing and in midwifery
Critique the role of the midwife within the broad political agenda of Australia and internationally
Explore the role of the woman in the politics of maternity care and midwifery and how advocacy can bring about reforms and health policy change

args.text: Admission into C07070 Graduate Diploma in Midwifery

92388.title: Midwifery Practice 1
92388.description: This subject introduces you to midwifery practice, focusing on the transition from the profession of nursing to the profession of midwifery. You will develop an understanding of midwifery philosophy, scope of practice, and professional identity while consolidating essential clinical skills specific to the context of midwifery practice. Emphasis is placed on supporting normal physiological processes, building respectful, culturally safe relationships, and engaging in continuity-of-care experiences. Through simulation, clinical placement, and reflective learning using the Midwifery Professional Experience Practice Portfolio (MPEPP), you begin integrating woman-centred evidence-based care, regulatory standards, and collaborative practice into your evolving midwifery identity.
learningOutcomes: Apply midwifery philosophy, regulatory standards, and evidence-based practice to provide safe, woman-centred care within scope of practice.
Demonstrate core midwifery skills to support normal physiological processes in pregnancy, labour, birth, and the postnatal period.
Establish culturally safe, respectful relationships with women and families, incorporating effective communication and shared decision-making.
Collaborate with health professionals to coordinate care and initiate consultation, referral, and escalation where appropriate.
Critically reflect on clinical experiences using the MPEPP to consolidate professional identity and support ongoing development.

args.text: Admission into C07070 Graduate Diploma in Midwifery

92389.title: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health: Women and Babies
92389.description: This subject deepens your professional and cultural capability in supporting the health and wellbeing of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander women, babies, and families. You will critically reflect on your own values, assumptions, and professional behaviours as you explore the ongoing impacts of colonisation, systemic racism, and intergenerational trauma. Through a strengths-based lens, you will examine Indigenous-led models of care, including the role of community-controlled health services. You will develop and apply culturally safe, responsive, and collaborative midwifery practices that uphold the rights, resilience, and sovereignty of First Nations peoples, contributing to equity and justice in maternity care.
learningOutcomes: Critically analyse the historical and contemporary impacts of colonisation, systemic racism, and intergenerational trauma on the health and wellbeing of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander women, babies, and families, and apply this understanding to inform culturally responsive and equity-focused midwifery practice.

Critically reflect on personal and professional assumptions, values, and behaviours, and evaluate how these influence culturally safe, respectful, and ongoing engagement with First Nations peoples in midwifery practice.

Demonstrate advanced cognitive and communication skills to support culturally safe, strength-based, and collaborative midwifery care that respects and integrates the knowledge, rights, and resilience of First Nations communities.

Evaluate and apply technical and theoretical knowledge to critique current maternity service models for First Nations women, and propose innovative, culturally secure, and Indigenous-led approaches to perinatal care that promote systemic change and equity.

Apply well-developed judgement and adaptability to recognise professional cultural capability as a lifelong, iterative journey, and implement this understanding through reflective practice, advocacy, and culturally responsive care across diverse midwifery settings.

args.text: Admission into C07070 Graduate Diploma in Midwifery

92390.title: Perinatal Mental Health
92390.description: This subject is based on a population health approach to perinatal mental health promotion. The role of the midwife in early recognition of protective and risk factors that impact on a woman’s mental health and the development of her infant is explored. You’ll build the clinical midwifery skills required to work both in primary healthcare and within multidisciplinary contexts to support a woman’s emotional and psychological health and wellbeing during pregnancy, birth and the across the transition to motherhood.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate the role and scope of practice of the midwife in supporting women’s emotional health and well-being during the perinatal period, including a comprehensive understanding of community resources to support maternal wellness.
Undertake universal evidence based screening and appropriate woman centred referral to and collaboration with psychiatric, psychological, community and other relevant services.
Reflect and discuss the relevance of a strengths-based approach to perinatal mental health care.

Critically explore and discuss depression, anxiety and related conditions that may occur during the perinatal period and understand the implications of pre-existing mental illness upon childbearing and early parenting.

args.text: Admission into C07070 Graduate Diploma in Midwifery

92391.title: Midwifery Practice 2
92391.description: To enrol in this subject, you must have passed 92388 Midwifery Practice 1. This subject builds on your learnings from Midwifery Practice 1 with a focus on managing maternity emergencies where prompt recognition and response are crucial. Content will be delivered via tutorials, online and in the simulation laboratories. Compulsory professional practice employment is integral and must be undertaken to pass this subject.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate clinical competency and effective teamwork in the context of a maternity emergency.
Apply and integrate knowledge of pathophysiology in maternity and neonatal emergencies.
Recognise, interpret, and respond appropriately to non-reassuring fetal heart rate patterns.
Communicate effectively and engage in reflective practice within midwifery.
Use evidence-based strategies and critical reflection to adhere to ethical and legal standards in midwifery care.

args.text: Admission into C07070 Graduate Diploma in Midwifery

92392.title: Midwifery in Complex Situations
92392.description: This subject prepares you to provide safe, evidence-informed midwifery care to pregnant women experiencing complex health conditions. You will integrate theoretical knowledge with clinical skills to assess, plan, implement, and evaluate care in diverse and challenging scenarios. Emphasis is placed on collaborative practice, effective consultation and referral and the use of digital health technologies. You will also strengthen your capacity for clinical communication, documentation, and reflective practice. You will explore how systemic factors and maternity service structures support or constrain physiology and evaluate how midwives can advocate for care that promotes safety, autonomy, and satisfaction for women with pregnancy complexities.
learningOutcomes: Integrate advanced theoretical and clinical midwifery knowledge to critically assess, plan, implement, and evaluate care for women experiencing complex pregnancies, demonstrating sound clinical judgement and responsibility.

Apply advanced cognitive, technical, and communication skills to initiate and manage effective consultation, referral strategies, ensuring responsive and appropriate care during pre-conception, pregnancy, labour, birth and the postpartum period.

Critically reflect on complex clinical experiences to develop adaptive strategies that enhance professional resilience, demonstrating autonomy and well-developed judgement in evolving practice contexts.
Employ digital and AI-based technologies safely and effectively, using advanced technical knowledge and problem-solving skills to support informed, ethical, and evidence-based midwifery care.

92473.title: Introduction to Specialty Practice: Critical Care Nursing
92473.description:
This subject introduces you to the clinical foundations of critical care nursing. In this subject, you'll learn how to respond to patient deterioration swiftly, and how to escalate care when necessary. Choose this elective if you are interested in working in critical care environments including Intensive care units, high dependency units and emergency departments.

In clinical laboratories, you will learn and practice selected critical care nursing skills. You will enhance core skills for effective communication, teamwork, safe medication practices, and ethical-legal principles, which are vital for ensuring patient safety in critical care settings.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of key principles and practices of a comprehensive assessment in the critical care environment (RN Standards for Practice 1.1-1.6, 3.1-3.7, 4.1-4.4, 6.1-6.5).
Develop a beginning understanding of how to deliver person-centred clinical management in the critical care environment (RN Standards for Practice 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7).
Identify key concepts related to the nurse experience in the critical care setting and the impact of the technology (RN Standards for Practice (1.1-1.6, 3.1-3.7, 4.1-4.4, 6.1-6.5).
Discuss the legal obligations and ethical considerations of the nurse in the critical care environment (RN Standards for Practice 3.1-3.7, 6.1-6.5, 7.3).
Identify the contribution of the interprofessional healthcare team in providing safe clinical care (Standards for Practice 1.1, 2.1-2.7, 3.1-3.7,4.1-4.3, 6.1-6.5).

92474.title: Introduction to Specialty Practice: Child and Family Health Nursing

92475.title: Introduction to Specialty Practice: Global Health
92475.description:
This subject introduces you to global health principles, highlighting how economic, political, and environmental factors influence health and illness worldwide. Choose this elective if you are interested in working in population health roles in local health services, or global health roles such as WHO.

Through discussion and debate, you'll learn about health systems, the influence of key organisations on health policy, and explore the role of nursing in international health contexts, gaining valuable insights for your future work in the field.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate key global public health concepts.
Analyse the influence of globalisation on disease spread and prevention.
Discuss the effects of social determinants on a society's morbidity and mortality and potential approaches to prevention and control.
Identify and assess global health issues and the role of organisations and technologies in addressing these challenges.
Demonstrate culturally safe nursing care, identify the role of the nurse and the career possibilities in the context of global health.
92475.requisiteText: ((1 OR 1a) AND (2 OR 2a) AND (3 OR 3a) AND (4 OR 4a))

92476.title: Introduction to Specialty Practice: Mental Health Nursing
92476.description:
This subject prepares you to practice as a registered nurse in mental health care, focusing on collaborative, recovery-oriented and trauma-informed frameworks of practice that place people with lived experience of mental health challenges at the centre of their own care and recovery.

You'll enhance your skills in building therapeutic relationships, conducting assessments through effective strengths-based communication, and employing collaborative, recovery-oriented, and trauma-informed approaches to care planning. You'll learn to apply this knowledge and skills to support people with a lived experience of mental health challenges and their families and carers across various healthcare settings.
learningOutcomes: Identify the dimensions and scope of specialty mental health nursing practice.
Examine and apply therapeutic communication, collaborative, and recovery-oriented mental health nursing frameworks.
Demonstrate effective communication, collaboration, and assessment skills in mental health care.

Critically reflect upon the service experiences of people with a lived experience of mental health, families and carers, and nursing practice and its contribution to their overall health and wellbeing.
Develop competence by critically reflecting to identify areas for improvement in relation to mental health nursing practice.
92476.requisiteText: ((1 OR 1a) AND (2 OR 2a) AND (3 OR 3a) AND (4 OR 4a))

92477.title: Introduction to Specialty Practice: Paediatric Nursing
92477.description:
This subject allows you to enhance your nursing skills and knowledge in the specialty area of paediatric nursing. Choose this elective if you are interested in working with children and their families and/or carers in relation to illness and development.

You will develop a deeper understanding of caring for sick children and their families, exploring illness and hospitalisation from their perspective. Through activities and simulations undertaken in clinical laboratories, you will broaden your expertise in paediatric nursing and assess your affinity for paediatric nursing which can bolster your prospects for future employment in the specialty.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate the capacity to assess, plan, deliver and evaluate both clinical nursing care and therapeutic interventions of sick children, in partnership with their families (RN Standards for Practice 1.1,1.4,1.6,2.1,2.2,2.3,2.5,2.6,3.1,4.1,4.2,4.3,5.1,5.2,6.1,6.2,6.5,7.1)
Identify the contribution of the interprofessional healthcare team in providing safe clinical care (RN standards for Practice 1.1,1.4,2.1,2.2,2.6,2.7,3.3,3.4,7.3)

Demonstrate an understanding of the relevant developmental, legal, ethical, social and environmental factors that impact the delivery of best practice nursing care to children and families (RN Standards for Practice 1.2,1.3,1.4,1.5,5.1,5.2,5.5,7.1,7.3)

Recognise the importance of promoting and maintaining the wellbeing of infants and children, including responsibilities related to child protection and mandatory reporting (RN Standards for Practice 1.1,1.2,1.4,2.2,2.3,2.5,4.1,4.3,5.1,5.2,6.1,6.2,6.5)

Examine the concept of family and family-centred care in contemporary Australian society and recognise common issues faced by vulnerable families (RN Standards for Practice 1.1,1.2,1.3,1.4,1.5,3.1,3.2,4.1,4.2,4.3,4.4,5.1,5.2,5.5)
92477.requisiteText: ((1 OR 1a) AND (2 OR 2a) AND (3 OR 3a) AND (4 OR 4a))

92478.title: Introduction to Specialty Practice: Palliative Care

92479.title: Introduction to Specialty Practice: Perioperative Nursing
92479.description: This subject introduces you to the foundational knowledge and skills related to the management of patients undergoing surgery. The subject integrates the principles and practices outlined by the Australian College of Operating Room Nurses (ACORN). It explores the four key roles performed by nurses in the perioperative environment. You will engage in simulated learning to deliver care to the patient at each stage of the surgical journey (pre-admission, anaesthetics, intraoperative and post-anaesthetic care) with a focus on patient safety and team communication. You will also perform the four nursing roles in a simulated operating theatre to develop knowledge and skills at the level of a beginning practitioner. Also, you will meet multidisciplinary team members while navigating a complex health management environment.
learningOutcomes: Discuss the roles and responsibilities of the RN in the operating theatre department and their collaboration with the inter-professional healthcare team (RN Standards of Practice 1.4,1.6, 2.6,2.7).
Develop a beginning understanding of clinical skills within the perioperative environment (RN Standards of Practice 3.4,3.5,5.2, 6.5,6.6,7.1,7.3).

Develop knowledge and skills to assist with performing a perioperative nursing assessment and planning patient care with the patient and members of the interprofessional health care team (RN Standards of Practice 1.4,1.6, 2.6,2.7, 3.4,3.5,6.5,6.6,7).

Develop and demonstrate perioperative nursing knowledge through evaluating relevant professional and scholarly evidence and using such evidence to plan, explain and justify the management of the perioperative patient (RN Standards of Practice 3.4,3.5,5.2, 6.5,6.6,7.1,7.3).
Discuss the legal obligations and ethical considerations of the nurse in the perioperative environment (RN Standards of Practice 1.4,1.6,7.1,7.3).
92479.requisiteText: ((1 OR 1a) AND (2 OR 2a) AND (3 OR 3a) AND (4 OR 4a))

92511.title: Structural Anatomy
92511.description: This subject explores the anatomy of bones, joints, muscles, and nerves, focusing on their identification and role in human movement. You will engage with life-size anatomy models and interactive platforms to build a solid foundation in the anatomical, physiological and biomechanical aspects of human motion. This knowledge is essential for advanced studies and a career in the exercise and sports science industry.
learningOutcomes: Describe and classify the structure and function of the human musculoskeletal system, particularly under movement conditions
Identify and interpret components of the neuromuscular body segments, joints and related connective tissues
Analyse the growth and development of the neuromuscular system

92515.title: Collaboration, Creativity and Critical Thinking
92515.description:
This subject equips you with collaboration, creativity, and critical thinking skills that prepare you for success at university, and in your sport and exercise career. Person-Centred Care and Coaching are core foci of the subject content. You will connect with peers and learn how to communicate effectively within teams and professional settings to address complex real-world issues using evidence-based practice. Through critical reflection and exploration of foundational Indigenous knowledge, you will develop your cultural capability to work with, and for Indigenous Australians, and people from different sociocultural backgrounds.

These transferable skills will empower you to be a better learner and better equipped for your future university studies and career in sport, exercise, and rehabilitation.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate professional communication, collaboration, and critical thinking skills to support effective practice in sport and exercise contexts.
Apply evidence-informed approaches to decision making and problem-solving in diverse professional settings.
Engage in reflective and reflexive practice to evaluate personal actions and their impact on outcomes
Develop creative and inclusive strategies to address complex challenges in sport and exercise environments.
Respect and integrate diverse cultural perspectives into practice including the knowledge and lived experiences of Indigenous Australians, in a culturally safe and responsible manner.

92521.description: This subject expands on your knowledge of structural anatomy by applying neuromechanical principles to human motion analysis. You will gain a deeper understanding of muscle coordination, postural control, stability, and injury factors. Practical sessions will enhance your foundational skills, preparing you for advanced studies in biomechanics, motor control, and exercise prescription.

Conduct a movement analysis of a sporting skill or exercise, identifying which muscles are active in producing and controlling a movement at a particular joint

Integrate functional anatomy knowledge with other exercise science subdisciplines, and apply to fitness, sport and workplace contexts
Explain and classify results from anthropometric, flexibility and posture testing, and present a summary of actions required

92523.title: Strength and Conditioning
92523.description: This subject examines the essential physical capacities for human performance including strength, speed, power, endurance, agility, and flexibility. You will explore the physiological and mechanical foundations of these capacities, along with methods to test, train, and deliver these for athletic development. You will develop expertise in assessing and improving these fundamental capacities, equipping you with practical skills to advance human movement.
learningOutcomes: Identify, describe and analyse the interrelationships between physical activity and the physiological and anatomical development of the individual
Demonstrate critical judgement to select appropriate strength and conditioning solutions to suit the needs of diverse individuals or groups
Apply the principles of exercise prescription in planning and instruction for different groups within sport, exercise and health
Measure and interpret physiological capacities to prescribe strength and conditioning activities
Describe the practical applications of strength and conditioning in the development of human performance

92524.title: Health and Lifespan Development
92524.description: This subject examines human development in cognitive, psychosocial, and physical domains within sport and exercise, covering changes from birth to old age. You will explore how age, gender, ethnicity, and culture influence health and development. Through pre-class activities, case studies, discussions, and lectures, you will gain a strong theoretical understanding and the ability to assess real-world scenarios, applying this knowledge to health and lifespan development.
learningOutcomes: Describe and discuss the processes of human growth and development over the lifespan with particular reference to physical, cognitive and socioemotional development
Examine the influence of age, gender, cultural background and developmental stages on individual exercise capacity and motivation to adopt a healthy and active lifestyle
Evaluate the impact of health and physical activity on human growth and development across the lifespan

92526.title: Data Management in Sport and Exercise
92526.description: This subject equips you with essential data literacy skills for modern roles in sports organizations. You will learn to collect, manage, and interpret data to inform decisions, and explore the wider implications of data use, including governance and ethics. Through individual and collaborative efforts, you will understand the relevance of data science to sport and exercise, preparing you for employment in this dynamic field. The subject combines interactive learning, theory, and practical application to ensure job readiness.
learningOutcomes: Identify and understand first principles of managing and storing data.
Apply first principles and justify their choice in sport and exercise related contexts.
Identify how and when data can (and should) be used for decision making.
Communicate and translate data into a usable form, which can be utilised in practice.
Recognise and apply varied organisation and system considerations when using data in sporting environments.

92530.title: Sport and Exercise Psychology
92530.description: This subject explores the cognitive and social aspects of sport performance and exercise behaviour, focusing on how psychology can enhance athletic performance and influence exercise adherence. You will apply psychosocial theories, constructs, and approaches to sport and exercise contexts. These skills will prepare and equip you to support individuals, teams, and communities in achieving their fitness and psychological goals.
learningOutcomes: Apply fundamental theoretical concepts in sport and exercise psychology
Critically analyse behavioural determinants of sport and exercise
Develop and explain various performance enhancing strategies for sport and exercise
Discuss contemporary issues related to culture, diversity and inclusion in sport and exercise contexts
Describe effective communication strategies to promote sport and exercise for individuals and groups

92533.title: Exercise Physiology
92533.description: This subject explores how the body responds and adapts to exercise, both immediately and over time. You will learn about how energy systems, respiratory and cardiovascular systems and muscles respond and adapt to different exercise intensities. The subject develops your laboratory skills, critical thinking, and understanding of the body's overall response to exercise, preparing you for professional practice in exercise physiology.
learningOutcomes: Identify and explain the function, regulation and interaction of each of the physiological systems related to exercise
Analyse, interpret and explain the acute and chronic physiological responses to diverse exercise conditions
Describe how the use of ergogenic aids affect physiological responses to exercise
Select and apply appropriate technology to quantify physiological response to exercise
Discuss the physiological adaptations to various exercise modalities in terms of energy production, optimal training and maximal performance.

92536.title: Research Methods for Sport and Exercise
92536.description: This subject introduces research design and statistical methods tailored to the sport and exercise sector, with a focus on evidence-based practice for exercise scientists. You will learn to critically evaluate scientific literature, use software to manage and analyse data, and effectively interpret and report findings, mastering both quantitative and qualitative research techniques.
learningOutcomes: Critically appraise the role of research and ethics in sport, exercise and health
Understand and utilise a range of statistical analysis techniques employed in sport, exercise and health research
Discuss and critique the validity and reliability of research findings published in the sport, exercise and health literature
Design research with a scientific approach to the study of sport, exercise and health in order to identify and solve problems
Cite the research of others in written and oral communication

92542.title: Applied Biomechanics
92542.description: This subject builds on biomechanical principles to advance your understanding of human motion. You will tackle complex biomechanical problems, explore a variety of quantitative measurement tools, and undertake a substantive research project. Emphasis is placed on developing practical skills to capture, analyse and interpret biomechanical data to enhance performance and prevent injuries.
learningOutcomes: Identify, describe and critically analyse movements related to performance enhancement and injury prevention.
Determine the biomechanical principles related to physical performance, disability and disease.
Evaluate the limitations imposed by physical laws on human motion, equipment and the environment.
Apply video motion analysis techniques to investigate movement patterns.
Design, report and defend scientific research in health, sport and exercise in order to identify and solve problems.

92544.title: Health Promotion and Physical Activity
92544.description: This subject enhances your understanding of factors influencing health and strategies for health promotion, focusing on preventing lifestyle-related diseases through physical activity. You will study health behaviour theories, sociocultural determinants, and health policy, and learn to design and evaluate interventions to improve physical and mental wellbeing. The subject emphasizes health as a resource for everyday life and promotes a collective approach to wellbeing beyond individual choices.
learningOutcomes: Describe health and health promotion in Australia, and evaluate the impact of public policy on physical activity and health behaviours

Discuss and analyse major health and physical activity promotion approaches and principles at individual, community, and population levels, including behaviour change theories, models, and evaluation methods
Apply population-level guidelines for physical activity, sedentary behaviour, and sleep to promote optimal health and wellbeing
Assess needs at individual and population levels to plan and implement targeted programs, and identify relevant agencies for promotion
Evaluate socio-cultural, psychological, and ethical influences on physical activity and health, and modify strategies based on health promotion models to improve health outcomes in different settings
