92547.title: Nutrition for Health and Physical Activity
92547.description: This subject equips you with an understanding of the impact of nutrition on health and sports performance, teaching you to assess dietary habits and address current nutritional challenges faced in society. Foundational aspects of macronutrients, hydration and dietary supplements will be presented to underpin a thorough understanding of nutrition. You will learn to apply nutritional guidelines, optimise diets for health and athletic excellence and identify poor eating practices. Interactive learning, case studies, facilitated discussions and an authentic assessment requiring dietary appraisal foster your ability to devise informed nutritional strategies.
learningOutcomes: Understand and relate the role of macro- and micro-nutrients to health, sport and exercise contexts
Critically analyse and design modifications to food intake to satisfy a client's nutritional requirements
Discuss the role of nutritional supplements in exercise prescription/adherence and sports performance
Evaluate the social, behavioural and psychological determinants of health and nutrition
Describe the unique challenges for Indigenous Australians in relation to nutritional aspects of health

92550.title: Sport and Exercise Science Practicum
92550.description:
This subject is designed for aspiring exercise science professionals seeking to meet the Exercise and Sports Science (ESSA) practicum guidelines. The subject develops hands-on experience and practical skills crucial for entry-level positions in exercise science. Its unique feature is the alignment with ESSA standards, ensuring industry-relevant learning.

You will develop skills in exercise assessment, prescription, and implementation, applying theoretical knowledge in real-world settings. Placements may also involve performance analysis and sports science. This subject requires at least 80 hours of practical experience, with assessments designed to enhance your practical skills within the ESSA Accredited Exercise Scientist Scope of Practice. Teaching methods include interactive coursework, direct industry engagement through placements, continuous feedback, and reflective practices. An ESSA record of student engagement will support your growth, ultimately helping you build a strong professional identity.
learningOutcomes: Apply exercise science knowledge and skills to design and deliver exercise programs and assessments for healthy clients
Apply evidence-based practice to evaluate and communicate the scientific rationale for professional decision-making and service delivery
Conduct themselves ethically, respecting client diversity and equity, in alignment with the ESSA Code of Professional Conduct and Ethical Practice
Practice competently within the scope of exercise science training, recognizing when to refer clients to other professionals
Consolidate a clear professional identity through reflection of applied accredited exercise science (AES) knowledge and skills

92551.title: Sport and Exercise Internship
92551.description:
This subject is designed for individuals seeking practical experience in the sport and exercise industry, aiming to enhance their professional skills and network. It offers a unique blend of interactive coursework and a professional internship, providing hands-on exposure to the sector's managerial and operational aspects and in some cases strength and conditioning, coaching and media placements. You will acquire practical skills and apply your academic knowledge in a real-world setting, facilitating career advancement. Distinctively, the subject combines 140 to 210 hours of industry work with targeted learning objectives, ensuring that your experience is both structured and relevant. Formative and summative feedback from academic staff and site supervisors will guide your progress.

You will develop practical competencies, expand your industry knowledge, and gain insights into the sports sector's functions. An integral part of your learning involves maintaining a logbook and crafting reflective evaluations, which will enhance your ability to critically assess your professional growth. Teaching methods include interactive coursework followed by direct industry engagement through an internship, supplemented by continuous feedback and reflective practices to solidify your learning outcomes.
learningOutcomes: Identify personal work-ready skills and attributes and articulate career goals and interests
Apply work-ready management and industry knowledge in a workplace environment
Critically reflect on the learning and developmental outcomes of a workplace experience
Demonstrate appropriate professional performance, conduct and attitudes in a working environment

92553.title: Complex Exercise Management
92553.description: Targeted at individuals seeking expertise in exercise science and its impact on the management of health, this subject equips you with a comprehensive understanding of chronic disease origins and how exercise can assist with the prevention and management of various conditions. You will acquire proficiency in understanding and evaluating cardiorespiratory, metabolic, neuromuscular, and orthopaedic health across the lifespan, as well as performing clinical and functional exercise testing. Teaching combines theoretical knowledge with hands-on experience, preparing you for professional roles in health and fitness cogniscent of the scope of practice for Accredited Exercise Scientists.
learningOutcomes: Critically analyse the factors underpinning the development of chronic diseases
Identify appropriate assessments of physical performance for clients at risk of, or with known disease
Prioritise the requirement for collaborative partnerships in supporting clients with complex exercise needs
Evaluate the barriers to physical activity participation and develop methods to promote exercise in individuals with complex needs
Recognise the diversity of Indigenous Australians and integrate this knowledge into health, sport and exercise management

92554.title: Exercise Assessment, Prescription and Delivery
92554.description:
This subject is designed for students seeking hands-on experience in exercise science, in line with Exercise and Sports Science Australia (ESSA) standards. The subject has a practical focus in compliance with ESSA's practicum guidelines, and the opportunity to work in both on-campus and off-site settings.

Distinctive features include the UTS Telepractice Clinic and Project Based Learning placements whereby theoretical knowledge is applied into real-world settings. You will gain a minimum of 50 of the 60 hours of practical skills in exercise assessment, prescription, and delivery, catering to apparently healthy populations. Learning involves a combination of practical shifts, workshops, and formative assessments, fostering professional growth within the scope of practice for ESSA Accredited Exercise Scientists (AES). Detailed assessments document student progress and the achievement of AES graduate attributes.
learningOutcomes: Integrate knowledge and skills from exercise science sub-disciplines to deliver a broad range of services
Design, deliver, and manage physical activity and exercise-based interventions for health, fitness, well-being, or performance improvement
Use various modalities to communicate with clients, stakeholders, and maintain appropriate service documentation
Identify and apply risk management strategies in exercise science practice
Practice ethically, collaboratively, and innovatively, including making referrals and adhering to the ESSA Code of Professional Conduct and Ethical Practice

92555.title: Motor Learning and Control
92555.description: This subject is designed to gain a foundational yet practical insight into motor control and learning processes. You will develop expertise in the motor control system's structure, movement control processes, muscle and nerve function assessment, as well as posture, balance, and coordination. Your learning will be facilitated through a blend of pre-class activities, online engagement, and hands-on laboratory work, focused on applying theory to real-world scenarios.
learningOutcomes: Classify and measure motor skill performance and assess motor function in sport and exercise contexts
Discuss current theories of human motor control and identify central processes contributing to skilled motor behavior
Apply knowledge from biomechanics, anatomy, physiology, and sports psychology to motor control practice
Describe the neuromuscular systems involved in motor learning and how neuromuscular function changes with learning in various sport and exercise contexts
Promote critical thinking by understanding the limitations and strengths of motor control research and theories.

92562.title: Exercise Medicine and Rehabilitation
92562.description: This subject is designed for studying professionals with a background in functional anatomy and exercise prescription, aiming to develop their skills in exercise medicine and rehabilitation for a range of injuries and chronic conditions. You will deepen your understanding of the physiological, biomechanical, and psycho-social aspects of injuries and chronic conditions, and learn to tailor exercise programs for various client groups. You will gain proficiency in creating effective, individualized exercise interventions, preparing you for a career in exercise rehabilitation, physiology, or strength and conditioning. Real-world case studies and practical sessions will help you apply theoretical knowledge to practice. Interactive learning, with a focus on practical application, inter-disciplinary collaboration and critical evaluation, will bridge the gap between science and practice.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate the physiological, bio-mechanical and psychological risk factors, mechanisms and associated limitations of chronic conditions and injuries in sport, exercise and the workplace

Critically appraise methods of assessment, treatment and management of injuries and chronic conditions in sport, exercise and the workplace to inform evidence based exercise medicine and rehabilitation strategies
Prescribe, deliver, monitor and revise therapeutic exercise programs using an inter-disciplinary approach to optimise return-to-task capabilities
Communicate the role of exercise as a therapeutic adjunct in the amelioration of chronic conditions or injury resulting from sport, exercise, disease and the workplace

92618.title: Health Care Research Methodology
92618.description: This subject provides an understanding and appreciation of the multiple ways through which knowledge is generated in specific relationship to the disciplines of health. Students are exposed to the breadth of research methodologies that can be employed for such knowledge generation. Emphasis is placed on relationships between research question/problem, methodology and method. Basic descriptive research methods are used as exemplars of knowledge generation. Completion of the subject enables students to critically appraise an appropriate methodology and method for their chosen area of research inquiry. In addition, the subject explores how to situate an area of inquiry within existing knowledge, writing, as well as ethical and practical issues of conducting research in health.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate the ethical principles in relation to health research
Compose a research or review question
Attribute appropriate research methodology to answer different research questions
Justify an appropriate literature review and/or research methodology to answer a research or review question
Devise knowledge translation plan for translating findings from research evidence into practice

92667.title: Midwifery Practice 1: Preparation for Practice
92667.description: This subject introduces you to the foundational skills and professional behaviours required for midwifery practice. You will develop beginning-level competencies in performing physical assessments of women and newborns, communicating effectively with women, families, and healthcare teams, and applying principles of culturally safe, woman-centred care. Core clinical skills are developed and practised through simulation and professional placement, where you will provide midwifery care under direct supervision. You will engage with the Midwifery Professional Experience Practice Portfolio (MPEPP), develop reflective capabilities, and build an understanding of the professional and regulatory frameworks that guide midwifery practice in Australia.
learningOutcomes: Perform physical assessments of childbearing women experiencing normal pregnancies, identify deviations from normal, and communicate findings using appropriate clinical documentation.
Assess healthy newborns after birth, interpret findings in relation to expected parameters, and communicate results to parents and healthcare professionals.
Apply principles of safe medication practice in midwifery, including accurate dosage calculations and appropriate administration protocols.
Demonstrate effective, respectful, and culturally safe communication when interacting with women, families, and the interprofessional team.
Deliver beginning-level midwifery care under supervision that reflects professional standards, cultural safety, and reflective practice.

92668.title: Foundation of Midwifery Practice
92668.description: This subject provides a foundation for understanding midwifery as a distinct profession grounded in partnership, cultural safety, and woman-centred care. You will examine the historical, philosophical, and professional contexts that shape contemporary midwifery in Australia, including its regulatory, ethical, and legal frameworks. Through the lens of the International Definition of the Midwife and the concept of ‘being with woman’, you will begin to explore the midwife’s role across the childbearing continuum. The subject also introduces models of midwifery care, interdisciplinary collaboration, and the physical, emotional, and sociocultural changes experienced during preconception, pregnancy, labour, birth and the postnatal period. This foundational knowledge will support you to begin developing critical thinking, communication, and reflective practice skills essential to midwifery.
learningOutcomes: Describe the historical, philosophical and professional foundations of midwifery and the role of the midwife within the Australian health care system.
Explain the legal, ethical, and professional responsibilities of midwives and their application to culturally safe, woman-centred practice.

Apply foundational knowledge of maternal and fetal anatomy and physiology to beginning level midwifery practice across the childbearing continuum.
Identify the physical, emotional, and sociocultural changes experienced during childbearing and apply this knowledge to support women’s health and wellbeing.

93202.title: Preparation for Clinical Practice
93202.description:
This subject prepares you as the student nurse for the clinical placement environment. It will introduce you to both practical and interpersonal nursing skills, necessary for patient safety. You will develop an understanding of the nurse’s role within an interprofessional team, undertaking patient health assessments, promoting and maintaining health by encouraging and reinforcing positive health practices and preventing health breakdown through early detection and intervention.

You will develop your understanding of how the nurse supports patients to be active participants in managing their health, facilitating health literacy through the provision of health information and education. By providing person-centred care you will recognise how nurses empower patients to achieve their optimum health outcomes. Interactive learning in the clinical laboratories is at the core of this subject, with clinical scenarios and patient stories linking theoretical knowledge to real-world nursing.

The content and clinical scenarios in this subject is aligned to the subjects 93201 Foundations of Nursing Practice 1A and 93203 Healthcare Communication.
learningOutcomes: Discuss person-centred care principles and their application in health assessment and therapeutic communication (RN Standards for Practice 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1,5, 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.5, 2.7, 3.1, 3.2, 3.7, 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 5.2, 7.1)

Demonstrate an understanding of Workplace Health & Safety regulations, including hand hygiene and the use of Personal Protective Equipment (RN Standards for Practice 1.1, 1.4, 1.6, 3.7, 4.3, 5.1, 5.3, 5.5, 6.1, 6.2, 6.5, 6.6)

93203.description:
This foundational subject focuses on developing safe, effective and person-centred communication which is a vital skill for all healthcare professionals. You will learn the importance of employing evidence-based communication strategies for developing the nurse-patient relationship and providing safe care to a culturally diverse Australian population.

You'll explore the concept of lifestyle diseases and develop critical thinking through engaging clinical scenarios and patient stories. You will build skills in assessment, diagnosis, planning, implementation, and evaluation of nursing care, including safe and effective medication practices. Teaching methods include case studies and exposure to current nursing research, ensuring an engaging, practical learning experience.

This subject is designed to build on your foundational knowledge and skills in the care of the older person across various healthcare environments. You will deepen your understanding of the ageing process and learn to manage complex health conditions in older persons, focusing on delivering high-quality, person-centred care. 93212.title: Indigenous Health and Well-Being
93212.description:
Nurses have a major role to play in improving the health of Australian Indigenous peoples. To be effective however, nurses require both clinical skills and to be able to deliver culturally safe care. This subject focuses on improving your knowledge of Australian Indigenous people to foster respect and understanding. In this subject you will explore how your own attitudes, beliefs and understandings contribute to your ability to deliver evidence-based care in a culturally safe way.

This subject uses open discussions and personal reflections to explore: truth telling in historical and contemporary Australian Indigenous context and the ongoing effects of colonisation for Indigenous people nationally and internationally; intergenerational loss and trauma; acknowledging Indigenous people as experts in their own health; comprehending the social and cultural implications of engaging with the health care system for Indigenous people; and fostering humility in safe, appreciative, collaborative spaces.
learningOutcomes: Analyse the impact of colonisation on Indigenous people's health outcomes.
Examine the role of cultural respect in providing culturally safe healthcare to Indigenous populations.
Develop an awareness of and respect for Australian Indigenous perspectives on health and wellbeing.
Discuss the legal, ethical, social and cultural implications that arise in the nursing care of Australian Indigenous peoples through the life span.
Reflect on the roles and contributions of Australian Indigenous health professionals, including Aboriginal Liaison Officers, within the healthcare system.

93213.title: Fundamentals of Mental Health Nursing
93213.description:
This subject introduces you to the spectrum of mental health from flourishing to crisis. You will build foundational knowledge and practical skills in assessing and providing care for people experiencing mental health challenges. The subject will deepen your understanding of therapeutic communication and reflective practice. The contemporary mental health approach known as recovery-oriented practice is core to this subject. Stories and vignettes from people with lived experience of mental health challenges, and their carers, are presented. You will acquire an understanding of mental health challenges that are prevalent in Australia and around the world.

Learning will be facilitated through presentations, groupwork, readings and critical thinking exercises, fostering respect for evidence-based practice in mental healthcare. Interactive tutorials, case studies, and group discussions will enable you to emerge with the competence and confidence to contribute effectively to mental health care in both specialty and general health settings. You will have the opportunity to apply these skills under supervision during a 2 week (80 hours) clinical placement to consolidate your learning.
learningOutcomes: Develop an understanding of the way that social, environmental and genetic factors influence an individual’s mental health.
Understand the importance and implementation of nursing skills to foster therapeutic relationships in mental health care.
Apply assessment tools and documentation effectively in mental health nursing.
Demonstrate an understanding of mental health practice and care delivery.
Understand mental health challenges within specific Australian populations and ethical considerations in practice.

93218.title: Empathy and Compassion for Nursing Practice
93218.description:
Empathy is a required attribute for all healthcare professionals; it is fundamental to therapeutic communication and integral to safe and effective nursing care. In this subject, you will build on your empathy skills and understandings developed throughout your previous BN studies.

This subject incorporates immersive and experiential learning approaches informed by health care consumers’ lived experiences of diverse health issues and health care.

Your learning will include workshops in large collaborative spaces and standard tutorials. You will enhance your therapeutic communication skills needed for empathic and compassionate nursing practice and have opportunities via live simulation to therapeutically engage with consumers who are experts by lived experiences.
learningOutcomes: Discuss the significance of empathy in nursing leadership and its application in person-centred care.
Demonstrate an understanding and application of empathetic communication in nursing practice.
Demonstrate an understanding of the significance of the lived and learnt experiences of people to inform care.
Recognise the importance of self-compassion and resilience in the nursing profession.

93219.title: Transition to Professional Practice
93219.description:
This is the capstone subject for the Bachelor of Nursing. In this subject you will integrate and apply the knowledge, concepts and skills associated with your learning in the BN course. Transition to the role of registered nurse, clinical competence and safety and quality in health care are the primary focus of this subject. You will explore the challenges and opportunities associated with transitioning to the role of registered nurse through innovative teaching and learning strategies. In addition, there is also an emphasis on developing resilience and self-care and planning for ongoing professional development.

You will advance your critical thinking, clinical skills and your ability to deliver optimal evidence-based care across diverse health settings through interactive learning in clinical laboratories and simulations. An extended clinical placement of 6 weeks (240 hours), provides practical experience, culminating in an assessment of your readiness to practice competently as a newly qualified nurse.
learningOutcomes: Reflect on professional development needs and develop strategies to facilitate the transition from student nurse to registered nurse.
Communicate and collaborate effectively within healthcare teams.
Use critical thinking and clinical reasoning to provide comprehensive and evidence-based person-centred care.
Communicate effectively with patients and families when providing person-centred care.
Adhere to safety standards and regulatory nursing competencies.

93220.title: Leading, Teaching and Mentoring
93220.description: This subject introduces you to the concepts of leading, teaching, mentoring and preceptorship within contemporary nursing practice. You will explore the principles of nursing leadership, the different leadership styles and their application in the nursing workplace. You will develop a beginning understanding of the principles of adult learning, adult learning theories, clinical teaching, assessment, and how to apply these in the clinical setting through the use of in class group work and case studies. You will also explore the roles of the nurse preceptor and the preceptor's role in supporting and managing transition shock among new graduate nurses. Finally, you will examine what mentorship and clinical supervision are, the role and responsibilities of a mentor and its application in nursing practice.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate understanding of the nurse's leadership attributes and role in the Australian health care context.
Examine nurses' responsibility for learning and teaching for ongoing professional education.
Explain how adult learning theories enhance clinical teaching and mentorship in nursing.
Define and discuss the roles, characteristics, and purpose of mentors, preceptors, and clinical supervisors in nursing.

93224.title: Foundations of Nursing Practice 2B
93224.description:
This subject builds on the content covered in 93200 Foundations of Nursing Practice 2A. With an integration of patient stories you will gain an understanding of the nursing care related to 3 of the National health priorities: cardiovascular, cerebrovascular and respiratory health. This subject aligns with the subject 93225 Clinical Practice 2B.

You will acquire skills in preventative, acute, chronic, and rehabilitative care, with a focus on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health, evidence-based practice, and legal and ethical principles. The subject employs interactive scenarios and evidence-based frameworks for an immersive learning experience.
learningOutcomes: Utilise clinical reasoning and critical thinking skills in assessing, planning, implementing and evaluating nursing care for people diagnosed with selected cardiovascular, cerebrovascular and respiratory diseases, for example asthma, heart failure and stroke. RN Standards of Practice 1,4,5,7.
Demonstrate an understanding of quantitative research and how this informs evidence-based practice. RN Standards of Practice 1,5,6.

Explain and debate the ethical concepts of autonomy, beneficence and non-maleficence in relation to selected cardiovascular, cerebrovascular and respiratory diseases, for example asthma, heart failure and stroke. RN Standards of Practice 2,5,7.

Demonstrate an understanding of the preventative, acute and chronic care management of patients with selected cardiovascular, cerebrovascular and respiratory disease. RN Standards of Practice 1,4,5,7.
Consider the impact of chronic conditions on a person's independence, dignity, physical and psychosocial wellbeing. RN Standards of Practice 2.

requisite.text: Admission into C10122 Bachelor of Nursing

93225.title: Clinical Practice 2B
93225.description:
In this subject you will further develop your critical thinking and clinical reasoning skills for effective health assessment, planning, implementation, and evaluation of nursing care for persons across the lifespan.

The clinical scenarios and patient stories in this subject will focus on respiratory, cardiovascular and neurological conditions, all of which carry a significant burden of mortality and morbidity in Australia. The content in this subject aligns with the subject 93224 Foundations of Nursing Practice 2B.

You will learn to manage care of deteriorating patients, ensuring safety and cultural sensitivity, and improve therapeutic and interprofessional communication and safe medication practices. You will have the opportunity to apply these skills under supervision during a 2 week (80 hours) clinical placement to consolidate your learning.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate a comprehensive and person-centred approach to patient assessment and management, integrating physiological, pathophysiological and psychosocial factors (RN Standards for Practice 4 & 5).

Demonstrate clinical reasoning and critical thinking skills for people diagnosed with selected cardiovascular, cerebrovascular and respiratory diseases, for example asthma, heart failure and stroke (RN Standards for Practice 1, 6, 7).
Demonstrate a practical understanding of the administration and management of oxygen therapy and oxygen devices (RN Standards for Practice 1, 5, 6).
Practice quality use of medicines including administration of inhaler medication (RN Standards for Practice 1, 5, 6).

Demonstrate safe and appropriate communication, teamwork and nursing practice in accordance with the Registered Nurse Standards for Practice (2016) in the clinical environment ( (RN Standards for Practice 1, 2,3, 4, 5, 6 & 7).

93228.title: Foundations of Nursing Practice 3A
93228.description:
This subject is designed to assist you in the transition from student to new graduate nurse by increasing your understanding of patient safety and professional and legal issues related to nursing practice. Content in this subject aligns with the subject 93229 Clinical Practice 3A.

Your understanding of professional accountability and responsibility as a Registered Nurse will be explored through an ethico-legal framework with reference to the professional standards and codes and issues from the Royal Commission into Aged Care Quality and Safety.

The injury-focused clinical scenarios and patient studies based on Australia’s National Health Priority Areas and the impact of this health breakdown on morbidity and mortality will be used to help you develop critical and analytical abilities. This includes case studies related to sepsis, and safe blood administration and are focused on the identification and management of deteriorating patients across the lifespan.
learningOutcomes: Discuss the key ethical and legal dimensions of professional practice: direct dealings with patients, collaboration with colleagues, institutional issues and policy matters (RN Standards of Practice 1.4, 1.5, 2.1, 2.5)
Demonstrate an understanding of the concept of moral courage in nursing and how this relates to the legal and ethical dimensions of practice (RN Standards of Practice 1.5, 2.1, 2.2, 2.5, 2.7)
Identify and demonstrate best practice in the early detection and management of sepsis (RN Standards of Practice 1.1, 1.4, 1.5, 3.4, 6.1, 6.2. 7.1, 7.2)
Demonstrate an ability to access and evaluate literature to inform practice (RN Standards of Practice 1.1, 2.7, 3.3)
Demonstrate an understanding of the knowledge and skills required to safely administer blood and blood products to patients (RN Standards of Practice 1.1, 1.4, 1.5, 3.4, 6.1, 6.2, 7.1, 7.2)

94657.title: Futuring for Innovation with Impact
94657.description: In this subject, you will think beyond the world as it stands today and consider the different futures that may impact your personal innovation practice towards sustainability. You will learn critical research skills and futuring methods to identify trends that shape future worlds. You will explore your own innovative area of interest and assess how possible futures may impact or inform your innovation. This futuring process will leverage qualitative data to identify barriers and enablers to change, to support the design your innovations to have an impact and make a difference towards sustainable development. This subject is hands-on and will broaden your horizon.
learningOutcomes: Analyse real-world innovation contexts and cases in order to discern connections and patterns that are supportive of emergence of ideas, innovation and change.
Identify issues of interest or concern, and apply a range of disciplinary and professional practice approaches to examine the potential for action.
Analyse trends observed in real-world contexts and creatively combine futuring methods to speculate about future developments.
Apply appropriate methods to conduct enquiry into real-world challenges to identify their constitutive elements and connections situated in specific contexts.
Evaluate the alternatives and articulate a compelling argument for a proposed direction for innovation in response to a real-world challenge.

94658.title: Funding Innovative Initiatives
94658.description: Innovation costs money – whether it is a new product, service, or social initiative. In this subject, students go on an innovation funding journey with industry stakeholders to understand where money for innovative initiatives comes from, and what the advantages and disadvantages of different funding sources are. Students develop their own funding proposal for an innovative idea or project and learn how to pitch it to potential funders. This subject equips students with practical skills and knowledge to obtain funding for a diverse range of innovative initiatives.
learningOutcomes: Utilise quantitative and qualitative data analysis to identify opportunities and to support decisions for expanding an innovative initiative.
Develop skills and techniques to professionally engage and collaborate with key stakeholders in an innovation funding ecosystem.
Critically evaluate social and ethical elements and considerations within an innovation funding ecosystem.
Identify opportunities for innovation and develop strategies to persuade and support people to innovate.
Communicate the mission and value proposition of an emerging initiative by engaging with different audiences.

94662.title: Creating and Commercialising Ideas
94662.description: There is a lot we can learn from inventors, innovators and entrepreneurs who create change in the world. This subject takes you on a journey from developing ideas to tangible innovation. You'll start with generating ideas to solve a problem and learn a range of practical tools to refine and test your ideas – including rapid prototyping, user research and value proposition design. You'll also get a deep understanding of how to bring your idea to the market. This hands-on and dynamic subject inspires your entrepreneurial thinking.
learningOutcomes: Develop strategies towards realising an innovative initiative in consideration of ethical responsibilities related to social, legal and regulatory practices.
Explore and consider values and needs when engaging with diverse stakeholders and communities in the pursuit of developing an innovative initiative.
Utilise a range of strategies and methods to identify, articulate and iterate meaningful opportunities for innovative entrepreneurial initatives.
Develop, experiment with and validate innovative ideas that are appropriate for a chosen complex problem space.
Communicate the mission and value proposition of an emerging initiative by engaging with different audiences.

94663.title: Navigating Innovation Networks
94663.description: This subject explores the contexts around organisations and initiatives, usually defined by industry and geography, focusing on engagement with entrepreneurial support organisations like incubators, accelerators, and funders. You'll work in teams to explore a chosen context, potentially aligned with your career aspirations. Based on your investigations, you'll craft a proposal for a new, inclusive initiative that benefits the ecosystem. Interactions with key stakeholders will help you build professional networks, equipping you with practical skills to leverage these networks for initiating change.
learningOutcomes: Collaborate to explain and visualise entrepreneurial ecosystems.
Identify elements and gaps in the entrepreneurial ecosystem and envision levers to influence the ecosystem.
Responsibly engage with others in the entrepreneurial ecosystem with a view to develop longer-term professional relationships.
Develop a proposal to launch within the ecosystem, and a strategy for it to enhance the system.
Evaluate the impact that your proposed initiative within the ecosystem might have from practical as well as ethical considerations.

94665.title: Designing and Evaluating Sustainable Innovations
94665.description: In this subject, you will have the opportunity to work on real-world sustainability issues and the latest innovations in technology and society. You will explore how complexity and systems thinking can help you understand the potential for more sustainable innovations. This subject introduces you to a range of practical techniques and methods – such as Life Cycle Impact Assessment, Life Cycle Costing and other standards that professionals use to evaluate the sustainability of products and systems. You will learn how to apply these techniques in the context of a designing and evaluating a sustainable innovation and thereby contribute to positive change for sustainable futures.
learningOutcomes: Analyse and map complex systems, organisations and/or individuals using language, principles and tools of complexity.
Draw from different perspectives, schools of thought and philosophical positions to explore problems identified in a system in its entirety.
Compare and contrast judgements and assumptions that are intentionally and unintentionally applied when framing issues of sustainability.

Identify and choose appropriate tools, processes and/or frameworks to generate creative interventions in a complex system to enable sustainable futures, including Life Cycle Assessment, Life Cycle Impact Assessment and Life Cycle Costing.
Develop proposals that are suitable and compelling for key stakeholders.

94689.title: Special Subject 1 (FTDI)
94689.description:
This subject is intended for students in the Master of Data Science and Innovation (C04372) who are in their final stage of the course and have 2 credit points remaining to complete the course with 96 credit points. The study load of this subject is about 3-4 hours per week, or about 35 hours in total, for one assignment. It can be taken as an online self-study course or as a small project. In either case, the topic should be related to data science. Example of project: sentiment analysis of political autobiographies. Example of online self-study: data wrangling with pandas.

For the small project, an academic advisor needs to be organised by the student. Any UTS faculty, or a suitably qualified external professional can be the advisor. At the beginning of the semester, students write a one-page proposal including the assessment task, for which the academic advisor has agreed to supervise and assess the work. For the online self-study course, it should include assessment tasks with a certificate of completion.

94690.title: Special Subject 2 (FTDI)
94690.description: This subject allows students who have taken a 6 credit point substitution for BCII to make up the 8 credit points required to replace a BCII summer or winter school. Students are required to co-design an assessment with the subject coordinator in a way that enhances learning already undertaken and intersects productively with the Subject Learning Objectives of the school they missed.

94691.title: Deep Learning
94691.description: This subject provides a comprehensive understanding of deep learning through research paper analysis, coding exercises, and practical assignments. You'll grasp deep learning neural networks' principles, familiarize with prevalent architectures, and their uses. By the end, you'll be adept at constructing, evaluating, and deploying deep learning models with industry-standard software.
learningOutcomes: Gain a solid understanding of the fundamentals, underlying mathematical concepts, and applications of neural networks.
Design and enhance diverse deep learning frameworks.
Convey the processes of deep learning models effectively in business context.

Synthesise and interpret academic papers and diverse sources of knowledge on deep learning to construct a model encompassing current advancements, future prospects, commercial applications, and ethical considerations.
Explore and elucidate insights derived from intricate deep learning models.

94692.title: Data Science Practice
94692.description: This subject offers a detailed exploration of programming languages for data analysis purpose, hands-on learning in Python, collaborative version control with Git, data management with SQL, and practical skills in UNIX systems and Docker containers for building efficient and reliable data products and services.
learningOutcomes: Participate in the development of data related projects using popular programming languages including Python, SQL and R.
Articulate the strengths, weaknesses and use-cases of common code control workflows, and demonstrate ability to work collaboratively using these tools.
Interact with databases and query data sources using SQL.
Work confidently in a Unix environment, including the use of Docker and Bash via a Command Line Interface.
Understanding basic programming concepts.

94693.title: Big Data Engineering
94693.description: This subject equips you to harness Big Data, transcending traditional analytics with distributed systems, the Hadoop ecosystem, stream processing, and large-scale computation. As a data scientist, your ability to extract value from data aligns with your company's architecture and infrastructure; knowledge of Big Data Engineering enhances this capability. This elective gives you a competitive advantage, preparing you to meet the growing demand for data scientists skilled in Big Data Engineering.
learningOutcomes: Participate in the development of data engineering projects using popular tools (Snowflake, Databricks, PostgreSQL, Spark, Airflow, Kafka etc..) and languages including Python and SQL.
Build simple data pipelines or ETLs in order to load, transform and prepare raw data into modern data warehousing solutions.
Interact with and query data from modern data warehousing and data lake technologies.
Understand basic data engineering concepts including data modelling, big data, distributed data processing and data streaming.

94699.title: Innovation Lab: Internship Project
94699.description:
This subject provides a 140 to 160-hour Data Science internship, allowing you to apply your data science knowledge within a real-world business project. You'll work within a professional team, under a host organisation's supervision, on projects ranging from research to data analysis or consultancy, either solo or collaboratively. A learning contract detailing tasks, goals, and timelines will be crafted between you and your host supervisor and approved by the subject coordinator. Your assessment includes reporting on the internship's outcomes and reflecting on your internship's experience, enhancing your understanding of Data Science in practice. Enrolment is contingent on securing an internship and obtaining approval via e-request on CareerHub.

To help you prepare for exciting opportunities such as internships, consulting competitions, or industry placements, you are encouraged (though NOT mandatory) to join and complete the WIL to Work program: uts.ac/wiltowork.
This program is a valuable way to develop the skills needed to succeed in work-integrated learning (WIL) experiences in Australia and to carry those skills forward into your future career.
learningOutcomes: Apply data science knowledge and skills effectively in a workplace
Contribute productively and analytically to data science and innovation projects in organisations
Engage respectfully and ethically and communicate professionally with organisational practices and stakeholders in real-world contexts
Demonstrate appropriate professional attitudes, behaviour and performance in a business environment
Reflect on experiences critically and communicate outcomes of the internship effectively

94911.title: Person-Centred Care and Self-Management
94911.description:
In this subject, you will understand the principles of person-centred care that underpin clinical exercise physiology practice, including trauma-informed care, strength-based models, collaborative care, and recovery-oriented practices. You will examine the social determinants of health and health disparities, including cultural, historical, and social factors that underpin health inequities among priority populations, and you will learn about culturally sensitive practice, with a focus on Indigenous Australians.

As an aspiring allied health professional, you will learn how to develop and maintain strong therapeutic relationships with clinical clients, with a particular focus on self-management. Effective clinical communication skills to support a therapeutic alliance with clients will be emphasised. You will develop skills in motivational interviewing and behaviour change counselling to empower clients to take ownership of their own health. Ultimately, you will examine strategies that clinical exercise physiologists can adopt to optimise the implementation of person-centred care, including the integration of knowledge, skills, evidence-informed practice, ethical behaviour, and professional attributes necessary to function as an effective allied health care practitioner using a person-centred approach.
learningOutcomes: Understand and examine behavioural, cognitive, and social determinants of health.
Develop and demonstrate techniques in health behaviour change, motivational interviewing, and professional leadership in clinical exercise physiology practice.
Effectively and respectfully communicate with clients to facilitate shared decision-making.
Display safe, respectful, inclusive, person-centred care that is responsive to people of diverse backgrounds and populations including Indigenous Australians.

Engage with critical reflection on Indigenous Australian contexts to work effectively with and for, Indigenous Australians within culturally safe professional settings as it pertains to clinical exercise physiology practice.

requisite.text: Admission into C04449 Master of Clinical Exercise Physiology

94912.title: Clinical Exercise Medicine: Principles and Practices
94912.description:
In this subject, you will consolidate and advance your anatomical, physiological, mechanical, and behavioural sciences knowledge and skills to conduct accurate, valid, reliable, and appropriate clinical assessments and exercise prescriptions (including for older adults, as well as paediatric and adolescent clients). You will also expand your theoretical and practical skills in objective and subjective clinical assessment, including client interviews, goal setting, clinical needs assessment, client capacity versus capability, test preparation, test selection, test order, test timing, and knowledge of clinically important differences. You will also learn about the importance of clinical discussions and the provision of appropriate feedback to clinical clients.

You will develop proficiency in exercise planning and preparation, exercise selection, exercise demonstration, exercise education and support, exercise prescription principles, exercise delivery, progression, autoregulation, periodisation, monitoring, and case management for clinical clients. You will also learn how to adapt subjective and objective clinical assessments as well as adapt exercise prescription and programming for specific populations including paediatrics, adolescents, and older adults. You will engage in interactive sessions, practical exercises, and case studies to ensure you acquire the necessary skills to excel as a proficient and ethical healthcare practitioner committed to evidence-informed practice.
learningOutcomes: Apply, integrate, and adapt knowledge and skills for prescribing exercise to optimise health outcomes for clients including for older adults and special populations, including paediatric and adolescent populations.

Apply appropriate screening, risk management strategies, and behaviour change principles to safely create, prescribe, implement, and evaluate effective interventions for older adults and special populations, including paediatric and adolescent clients, to optimise health outcomes.
Apply evidence-informed practice and professional decision-making to optimise person-centred care for older adults and special populations, including paediatric and adolescent clients.
Effectively and respectively communicate with clients, including older adults and special populations, such as paediatric and adolescent clients

requisite.text: Admission into C04449 Master of Clinical Exercise Physiology

94913.title: Musculoskeletal and Occupational Conditions
94913.description:
In this subject, you will consolidate and advance your knowledge of gross and functional anatomy, physiology, and pathophysiology, as well as biomechanics and pathomechanics of the musculoskeletal system. You will also develop your clinical knowledge of systemic, axial, and appendicular (upper- and lower-body) musculoskeletal conditions across the lifespan, while expanding practical skills in clinical assessment, exercise selection, prescription, delivery, progression, monitoring, and case management, through adopting evidenced-informed practice and applying scientific knowledge.

You will also extend your clinical and musculoskeletal knowledge into the occupational setting, focusing on the prevention, management, and rehabilitation of workplace injury towards effective return-to-work, including ergonomic assessment, work-specific task analysis, functional capacity evaluation, work conditioning, and return-to-work planning and programming. Additionally, you will start practicing your communication techniques, clinical skills, and professional practices with real clinical clients through an internal clinical placement under clinical supervision.
learningOutcomes: Apply, integrate, and adapt knowledge and skills of normal and pathologic anatomy, physiology, and biomechanics of the musculoskeletal system as it relates to acute, sub-acute, or chronic disease management, as well as ergonomics, posture, task-appraisal, and functional capacity within the occupational setting.

Apply appropriate screening, risk management strategies, and behaviour change principles to safely create, prescribe, implement, and evaluate effective interventions for people with musculoskeletal or occupational conditions to optimise health outcomes or return-to-work outcomes within relevant legislative frameworks.
Apply evidence-informed practice and professional decision-making to optimise person-centred care across musculoskeletal and occupational conditions.

Effectively and respectively communicate with clients and other relevant professionals that results in shared decision-making through collaborative and interprofessional musculoskeletal and occupational practice.
Engage with ongoing personal and professional self-development and reflective practice as it pertains to musculoskeletal and occupational conditions.

requisite.text: Admission into C04449 Master of Clinical Exercise Physiology

94914.title: Neurological and Mental Health Conditions
94914.description:
In this subject, you will consolidate and advance your knowledge of the underlying anatomy and pathophysiology of the neurological and neuromuscular systems. Specifically, you will develop clinical knowledge of sudden, developmental, or degenerative neurologic conditions across the lifespan (such as spinal cord injury, dementia, stroke, and Huntington’s disease), as well as mental health conditions (such as stress, anxiety, depression, schizophrenia, bipolar affective disorder, and addiction) commonly seen in clinical exercise physiology practice.

To support people with these conditions, you will develop an understanding of common treatment practices and the role of the multidisciplinary care team. You will also expand your practical skills in clinical assessment and interpretation, exercise selection, prescription, delivery, progression, monitoring, and case management, by adopting evidenced-based practice and applying scientific knowledge as it relates to these clinical conditions. Lastly, you will gain an understanding of common barriers to exercise in these populations while developing evidence-based strategies to overcome these barriers.
learningOutcomes: Apply, integrate, and adapt knowledge and skills of normal and pathologic neuroanatomy, and neurophysiology together with neuroplasticity and healing processes of the neurological and neuromuscular system as it relates to management of sudden, developmental, or degenerative disease; as well as the clinical features, diagnostic procedures and treatments associated with mental health problems inclusive of severe mental illness and disorders.

Apply appropriate screening, risk management strategies, and behaviour change principles to safely create, prescribe, implement, and evaluate effective interventions for people with neurological and mental health conditions to optimise health outcomes.
Apply evidence-informed practice and professional decision-making to optimise person-centred care across neurological and mental health conditions.

Effectively and respectively communicate with clients and other relevant professionals that results in shared decision-making through collaborative and interprofessional neurological and mental health practice.
Engage with ongoing personal and professional self-development and reflective practice as it pertains to neurological and mental health conditions.

requisite.text: Admission into C04449 Master of Clinical Exercise Physiology

94921.title: Cardiopulmonary and Respiratory Conditions
94921.description:
In this subject you will consolidate and advance your knowledge of the anatomy and physiology of the cardiovascular, pulmonary, and respiratory systems. You will develop clinical, epidemiological, pathophysiological, and pathomechanical knowledge of cardiopulmonary and respiratory conditions (such as congestive heart failure, coronary and peripheral arterial disease, pulmonary and cystic fibrosis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), asthma, and emphysema) commonly seen in clinical exercise physiology practice.

You will also develop an understanding of common treatment practices and the role of the multidisciplinary team in managing these conditions. Additionally, you will expand your practical skills in clinical assessment, exercise selection, prescription, delivery, progression, monitoring, modification, and case management, by adopting evidence-informed practice and applying scientific knowledge as it relates to these conditions. Lastly, you will use critical thinking and develop clinical reasoning to deliver optimal outcomes for these clinical clients within a person-centred approach.
learningOutcomes: Apply, integrate, and adapt knowledge and skills of anatomy, pathophysiology, and pathomechanics of the cardio-vascular system, pulmonary system, and respiratory system.

Apply appropriate screening, risk management strategies, and behaviour change principles to safely create, prescribe, implement, and evaluate effective interventions for people with cardiopulmonary and respiratory conditions to optimise health outcomes.
Apply evidence-informed practice and professional decision-making to optimise person-centred care across cardiopulmonary and respiratory conditions.

Effectively and respectively communicate with clients and other relevant professionals that results in shared decision-making through collaborative and interprofessional cardiovascular, pulmonary, and respiratory health practice.
Engage with ongoing personal and professional self-development and reflective practice as it pertains to cardiopulmonary and respiratory conditions.

requisite.text: Admission into C04449 Master of Clinical Exercise Physiology

94922.title: Metabolic and Other Clinical Conditions
94922.description:
In this subject, you will consolidate and advance your knowledge of the anatomy and physiology of the endocrine and immune systems as well as normal and abnormal renal (kidney) and liver function. Here, you will also develop clinical, epidemiological, pathophysiological, and pathomechanical knowledge of metabolic, renal, and other clinical conditions (such as diabetes, obesity, metabolic syndrome, chronic kidney disease, and liver disease). You will also learn about gender-based conditions, autoimmune diseases, and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).

Importantly, you will expand your practical skills in clinical assessment, exercise selection, prescription, delivery, progression, monitoring, modification, and case management, by adopting evidenced-informed practice and applying scientific knowledge as it pertains to these diverse range of clinical conditions. You will also gain an understanding of common barriers to exercise in these populations while developing evidence-based strategies to overcome these barriers.
learningOutcomes:
Apply, integrate, and adapt knowledge and skills of anatomy, pathophysiology, and pathomechanics of metabolic
and other clinical conditions including the endocrine and immune systems, renal (kidney) function and liver
function, as well as human immunodeficiency virus and autoimmune diseases.

Apply appropriate screening, risk management strategies, and behaviour change principles to safely create,
prescribe, implement, and evaluate effective interventions for people with metabolic and other clinical conditions
to optimise health outcomes.

Apply evidence-informed practice and professional decision-making to optimise person-centred care across
metabolic and other clinical conditions.

Effectively and respectively communicate with clients and other relevant professionals that results in shared
decision-making through collaborative and interprofessional practice for people with metabolic and other clinical
conditions.

Engage with ongoing personal and professional self-development and reflective practice as it pertains to
metabolic and other clinical conditions.

requisite.text: Admission into C04449 Master of Clinical Exercise Physiology

94923.title: Oncology and Haematology Conditions
94923.description:
In this subject, you will develop, consolidate, and advance your knowledge of cancer biology, epidemiology, and pathophysiology of solid and non-solid tumours across oncology and haematology, from localised to the advanced and metastatic stages of disease across paediatric, adolescent, adult, and geriatric populations. You will also expand your clinical understanding of how cancer is medically treated (including surgery, radiotherapy, chemotherapy, and immunotherapy), and expand your clinical skills to support all people affected by cancer (including people with cancer as well as their informal caregivers) through-out the treatment and disease trajectories using exercise as medicine.

You will develop an understanding of clinical trials in oncology and haematology, and the interactions this may have with clinical exercise physiology practice among the multidisciplinary cancer care team. You will expand your practical skills in clinical assessment, exercise selection, prescription, delivery, progression, monitoring, and case management, through adopting evidenced-informed practice and applying scientific knowledge. Lastly, you will develop an understanding of the individual and system-level barriers and facilitators people affected by cancer may face to access clinical exercise physiology services and how to overcome these.
learningOutcomes: Apply, integrate, and adapt knowledge and skills of cancer biology, epidemiology, and pathophysiology as it relates to cancer stage and treatments among oncology and haematology conditions across the lifespan.

Apply appropriate screening, risk management strategies, and behaviour change principles to safely create, prescribe, implement, and evaluate effective interventions for people affected by oncology and haematology conditions (including people with cancer and their caregivers) to optimise health outcomes.
Apply evidence-informed practice and professional decision-making to optimise person-centred care across oncology and haematology conditions.

Effectively and respectively communicate with clients and other relevant professionals that results in shared decision-making through collaborative and interprofessional oncological and haematological health practice.
Engage with ongoing personal and professional self-development and reflective practice as it pertains to oncology and haematology conditions.

requisite.text: Admission into C04449 Master of Clinical Exercise Physiology

94924.title: Clinical Exercise Physiology Placement 1
94924.description:
In this subject, you will authentically participate in professional practice placements and work-integrated learning under the guidance of experienced clinical educators. You will undertake your supervised clinical exercise physiology practice across various exercise settings including public or private hospitals and health services, commercial clinic or community-based settings, or via tele-practice. Here, you will be immersed into professional practice settings to consolidate your anatomical, pathophysiological, pathomechanical, and behavioural sciences knowledge and skills across a range of clinical conditions (core, niche, and emerging areas of practice).

You will continue to develop clinical competency and progress towards independence and autonomy in professional practice. As a result, you will assess, prescribe, and deliver exercise to people across the full health spectrum to improve, maintain, or reduce the decline of health-related status and function under clinical supervision. Emphasis is placed on developing your abilities to integrate the knowledge, skills, principles of evidence-informed practice, clinical reasoning, ethical behaviours, and professional attributes that are necessary to function as an effective allied health care practitioner using a person-centred approach.

94931.title: Professional and Interprofessional Practice
94931.description:
In this subject, you will develop and consolidate knowledge and skills pertaining to effective professional and interprofessional practice, universal healthcare, and Australian health systems. You will learn how to navigate Australia's health system, including evolving health trends and priorities, as well as how healthcare is funded, organised, and delivered in the clinical exercise physiology context. You will also develop entrepreneurial skills, business acumen, and professional leadership in clinical exercise physiology. You will be exploring interprofessional, innovative, and collaborative practice, including role clarity, shared decision-making, and team functioning in the context of the multidisciplinary healthcare team.

Emphasis will be placed on developing your abilities to integrate professional knowledge, skills, principles of evidence-informed practice, ethical behaviours, and key professional attributes necessary to function as an effective allied health care practitioner using a person-centred approach, including the advancement of communication skills, understanding of legal frameworks, and consideration of work with vulnerable populations (such as people with disability or children). You will also demonstrate critical reflection on the provision of culturally safe professional settings for the Indigenous Australian context.
learningOutcomes: Develop and demonstrate entrepreneurial skills, business acumen, and professional leadership in clinical exercise physiology in the context of the Australian healthcare system.
Display interprofessional and collaborative clinical exercise physiology practice skills within the context of multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary healthcare teams.
Effectively and respectively communicate with other professionals to facilitate shared decision making.

Engage with critical reflection on Indigenous Australian contexts to work effectively with and for, Indigenous Australians within culturally safe professional settings as it pertains to clinical exercise physiology practice.

Emphasis will be placed on developing your ability to integrate the knowledge, skills, and principles of evidence-informed practice, as well as ethical behaviours, and professional attributes that are necessary to function as an effective allied health care practitioner adopting a person-centred approach.

You will also critically reflect on Indigenous Australian contexts to work effectively with and for Indigenous Australians within culturally safe professional settings. In this subject, you will apply your knowledge in an authentic clinical placement, consolidating and advancing your practical skills in the assessment, prescription, and delivery of exercise to clients with complex and multiple chronic conditions. This subject will prepare you for accreditation and professional practice using critical thinking and clinical reasoning to deliver optimal outcomes to Indigenous Australians, as well as clients with complex and multiple chronic conditions and co-morbidities.

This subject introduces students to ways of thinking differently about the ‘wicked’ problems we face when tackling big issues around sustainability. Students draw on a range of approaches from across our disciplines and professional domains to explore the complex social and environmental context in which every problem is situated and networked with other problems. Striving towards regenerative sustainable futures, these novel ways of thinking enable students to move away from conventional problem-solving approaches to discover new avenues for action. 95007.title: TD: Pathways to societal transitions
95007.description:
For help with deciding which Transdisciplinary Elective subject to study, do a web search for "UTS TD electives."

Artificial Intelligence seems to be everywhere – embedded in phones, homes, workplaces – but what are the physical infrastructures that make it possible, and how are they reshaping communities and our environment? This subject takes students beyond the screen to investigate the hidden, material side of AI. From data centres and fibre-optic cables to the vast demands for energy, water, and land, students will explore how rapidly expanding digital infrastructure is transforming communities and environments globally, and in their own backyard.

Students will hear from a diversity of industry experts working across sectors who are making digital infrastructure expansion possible, and learn how the challenges and opportunities this expansion presents affect sustainability efforts globally, and in Australia. In multidisciplinary teams, students will investigate how digital infrastructure expansion is unfolding in their local community and codesign future scenarios that balance environmental priorities with societal demand for AI. Through this process, they will use a range of ethnographic and creative research methods, including photography, video, and story-making, to learn from their local community and communicate possible futures. This process will be assisted through regular engagements with our industry partner, Lane Cove Council, who will provide first-hand insights into how digital infrastructure expansion is shaping their community.

Students participating in this subject will develop skills and confidence in understanding and responding to complex, real-world challenges in multidisciplinary teams, using effective systems approaches to change-making. It is relevant to students from all disciplines including (but not limited to) computer and data science, social sciences, fine arts, communications, science, law and medicine.
learningOutcomes: Integrate different perspectives to unpack and analyse complex challenges that the digital infrastructure industry is creating for local communities and environments.
Identify significant issues and emerging opportunities to create positive change in real-world contexts.
Apply transdisciplinary and creative research methods and collaboration in teams to generate responses to complex challenges.
Develop a cohesive rationale for proposals and communicate ideas persuasively to diverse audiences.
Synthesise your learning and research to generate insights about transdisciplinarity and your own role in imagining digital futures, and steps to bring about positive social change.

95009.title: TD: Change-making for social impact
95009.description:
For help with deciding which Transdisciplinary Elective subject to study, do a web search for "UTS TD electives."

How can we transform ourselves and the systems we live in? This subject invites students to explore the deep connection between personal transformation and systemic change. Through embodied, reflective, and collaborative learning, students engage with practices from mindfulness, complexity science, implementation science, decolonial thinking, and First Nations and other diverse knowledge systems. Across two integrated phases—self-transformation and systems evolution—students learn to sit with the discomfort of change within complex systems, understand the roots of suffering and injustice, and take ethical action in response to real-world challenges co-designed with our industry partner Stockland. Through creative, non-written assessments, students map their inner shifts, design micro-interventions within complex systems, and showcase ripple effects of their work through ritual, installation, and action pledges. Learning flows between immersive in-person sessions, interactive online sessions, and reflective practices, supporting students to build purposeful, relational, and sustainable approaches to social impact within the communities they care about.
learningOutcomes: Analyse and map systems, organisations and individuals utilising language, principles and tools of complexity to identify leverage points for change and impact
Articulate the current and future structures, processes, and practices that influence change and innovation across organisations, networks and systems
Develop strategies to mobilise and connect people and the organisations, networks and systems they work and live in to create and implement innovation
Design communication strategies to persuade organisational and community leaders to implement innovation in professional or social contexts to achieve impact

95728.title: Health Statistics
95728.description:
Understanding and using data correctly is crucial for planning and decision-making in public health. By taking this subject, you will gain the essential knowledge and skills needed to analyse and interpret health data, and critically evaluate the results of epidemiological studies. This subject will teach you key statistical concepts and tests used in public health. In this subject, you will focus on learning how to interpret statistical outputs and use the right analysis methods, rather than computing or programming skills. By the end of the subject, you will know how to select appropriate statistical analyses based on research questions and study designs. The skills and knowledge you gain will be directly applicable to real-world scenarios.

This subject uses a blended learning approach, combining online and on-campus activities. You will learn the theoretical aspects of health statistics through online lectures and materials. These online resources will also include activities to deepen your understanding and help you prepare for on-campus tutorials. During on-campus tutorials, you will apply what you have learned by using statistical software, giving you hands-on experience. An activity book will guide you throughout the subject. Expect to spend about 10–12 hours per week on all learning activities, including self-directed learning, on-campus sessions, and completing assessments.
learningOutcomes:
Construct and explain research questions to enable responsible and ethical decision making and research in
public health.
Compare and contrast different types of statistical analysis.
Perform and interpret basic statistical analyses using a statistical software package.
Communicate the results of statistical analyses

This subject equips you with a foundational understanding of pharmacy practice and the pharmacist's role in patient care, focusing on how regulations, professional standards, and ethics shape your future responsibilities.

You'll gain insight into the Australian healthcare system, including legal frameworks and policies for medicine supply and the National Strategy for Quality Use of Medicines. Key themes such as determinants of health and illness, health literacy, health promotion, and cultural capability are introduced and further developed in later subjects. Learning involves practical application and reflection on the patient experience throughout.

Advanced topics delve into the factors influencing drug efficacy, such as drug interactions and genetic variability. Practical applications include therapeutic drug monitoring, individualised treatment, and managing adverse drug reactions, all critical for optimising therapeutic outcomes. You will learn and apply these concepts through a blend of lectures, collaborative workshops, and a research-inspired group project.

96014.title: Molecule to Market
96014.description: This subject demystifies the drug development journey from lab to patient, a process marked by high risk and high cost, but also high potential reward. You'll learn that only one in 10,000 compounds typically reaches the market, starting with a five-year discovery phase assessing thousands of compounds. Following this, 250 enter pre-clinical studies over two years, with just five advancing to clinical trials lasting six years. The subject details the rigorous phases of efficacy and safety studies, leading to the potential creation of a regulatory dossier for submission to Australia's Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA). You'll understand the TGA's role in drug evaluation and the steps for a medicine to gain subsidised patient access through the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS), including TGA registration and PBAC pricing reimbursement. You will learn how to take a molecule from discovery to a registered product through collaborative workshop learning and a semester-long team project.

96027.title: Eye and Visual Systems
96027.description: This subject will equip you with essential functional anatomy and physiology for orthoptic practice, focusing on ocular structures, external adnexa, and support systems such as, vascular supply and tear film. You will also explore the visual pathway, from information transmission to visual processing, and neuroanatomy relevant to the eye and vision. Fundamental skills for the assessment of visual functions in clinical practice will be developed. Additionally, the optics of the eye and how this relates to refractive errors, and the optical principles of lenses and prisms will be explored. The foundational knowledge you gain in this subject is essential to further learning throughout the course.

96028.title: Binocular Vision and Ocular Motility 1
96028.description: This subject will explore foundational concepts related to binocular vision and ocular motility, including the anatomical and physiological basis for these functions. Development of binocular vision through the critical period, and the importance of neural plasticity for development of sensory adaptations in childhood, will be discussed. You will also study the role of accommodation and its synkinesis with convergence on ocular alignment. Through case-based learning, you will apply clinical reasoning and diagnostic thinking to conditions including, amblyopia, childhood strabismus, heterophoria and convergence insufficiency. You will learn about orthoptic therapies and how these are applied in practice, as well as essential clinical skills for the assessment of binocular vision, strabismus, and ocular motility.
learningOutcomes: Apply knowledge of normal binocular vision and ocular motility, including underlying anatomy and physiology to conditions that impact binocular development and function.

96029.title: Ocular Pathology 1
96029.description: Building on understanding of anatomy and physiology from 96027 Eye and Visual Systems, this subject adopts a practical approach to developing knowledge and skills necessary for work in ophthalmic practice. You will study pathological processes including, infection, inflammation, vascular disease and neoplastic growth, and how these may impact anatomical structures of the eye. The prevalence and causes of ocular pathologies will be explored, including ocular surface diseases and age-related conditions such as, cataract, macular degeneration and glaucoma. Therapeutic and diagnostic uses of ocular pharmaceuticals and their application to clinical management of various ophthalmic diseases will be discussed. Through a problem-based learning approach and clinical case studies, you will learn to plan diagnostic examination, interpret clinical findings and will develop an understanding of approaches to the management of common ophthalmic conditions. You will also learn essential clinical skills in ophthalmic assessment, as well as those needed for collaborative management, patient education and support.
learningOutcomes: Apply knowledge of ocular anatomy, function, and pathologies to the interpretation of presenting signs and symptoms, and the formulation of provisional diagnoses.
