96030.title: Introduction to Professional Practice
96030.description: This subject introduces you to the essentials of professional practice within eye care including, medical terminology and notation, medicolegal responsibilities and ethical practice. You will learn about social determinants of health, the structure of the healthcare system in Australia, and the roles of healthcare professionals working collaboratively in interdisciplinary teams to provide health services. Models of eye care provision will be discussed, including your role as an emerging orthoptist. You will be introduced to evidence-based practice and learn basic research and inquiry skills. Fundamental clinical skills, including medical history taking and visual acuity assessment in adults and children, will be developed. Important legislation governing the prescription and administration of medications, pharmacology of ocular medications, and how these may be applied in practice for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes, will be explored. You will develop knowledge and skills for culturally safe practice including, understanding the importance of strengths-based language, community-led healthcare and holistic approaches based on the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander model of health.
learningOutcomes: Assess and accurately record visual acuity in infants, children and adults, using standard clinical tests and adapting approaches as appropriate.
Use effective communication skills to accurately establish an ocular focused medical history and record using standard medical notation.
Apply skills in evidence-based practice, cultural safety, and an understanding of professional and ethical standards to orthoptic practice.
Apply knowledge of pharmacology to the use of ocular medications in diagnostic and therapeutic procedures, considering the safety, legal, and ethical implications.
Reflect on personal development as a student orthoptist, and the role of the orthoptist within interdisciplinary healthcare teams and the broader healthcare system.

args.text: Admission into C04299 Master of Orthoptics

96031.title: Clinical Management of Refractive Error
96031.description: Expanding on foundational knowledge of the optics of the eye and the physiological basis of refractive errors, this subject delves into the development and causes of refractive errors, and their clinical management. You are encouraged to critically evaluate methods for determining refractive error and ocular biometry, using current research. You will study the epidemiology of refractive errors across the lifespan and explore the impact of contemporary lifestyles on prevalence rates across the world. Through problem-based learning, you will develop an understanding of the advantages and limitations of various optical and surgical options for the correction of refractive error including, laser vision correction. Considered approaches according to life stage, ocular health, lifestyle, and occupation will be discussed. This will include novel management strategies for the prevention of myopic progression and effective implementation in clinical practice. Refractive pathologies including pathological myopia will be explored. By the end of this subject, you will have the clinical skills to assess refractive status, monitor refractive progression, educate on refractive correction options and prescribe spectacle lenses proficiently.
learningOutcomes: Integrate knowledge of optics and ocular anatomy to explain emmetropisation, refractive development and the impact of genetic and environmental risk factors.
Plan investigation and interpret clinical findings to diagnose and monitor progression of refractive errors and identify associated ocular pathologies.
Design person-centred, evidence-based management plans for refractive errors incorporating optical, surgical, medical, and lifestyle interventions, and evaluate treatment outcomes.
Accurately measure refraction using various methods, and use ocular medications as clinically indicated, to prescribe optical corrections in accordance with legislation.

Provide evidence-based education on the optical and surgical correction of refractive errors including, use and care of contact lenses, suitability for refractive laser surgery and treatments to reduce refractive error progression.

requisite.text: Admission into C04299 Master of Orthoptics

96032.title: Binocular Vision and Ocular Motility 2
96032.description: This subject extends your understanding of binocular sensory and motor functions from 96028 ‘Binocular Vision and Ocular Motility 1’, with a focus on more complex strabismus and ocular motility disorders. An in-depth exploration of binocular vision in the context of strabismus will include discussion of absent binocular vision, abnormal retinal correspondence, and eccentric fixation. Case-based learning will focus on acquired childhood and adult-onset strabismus and the impact of neural, myogenic, and orbital restrictive abnormalities on ocular motility. Evidence-based strabismus management including, treatment of diplopia, orthoptic therapies and surgical approaches, will be applied to clinical scenarios. You will also advance your orthoptic clinical skills for assessing and diagnosing binocular vision, strabismus and ocular motility disorders.
learningOutcomes: Interpret ocular motility findings in the context of extraocular muscle function and the laws of ocular motor control to differentiate between myogenic, neurogenic and restrictive conditions.
Analyse presenting signs and symptoms, and clinical data to diagnose concomitant and incomitant strabismus, as well as complex binocular vision and ocular motility disorders.
Develop person-centred, evidence-based, interdisciplinary management plans for strabismus and ocular motility disorders, incorporating orthoptic therapy, optical, medical and surgical interventions.
Perform and interpret advanced orthoptic investigative and therapeutic procedures, adapting approaches as required in response to clinical findings and individual patient needs.

Deliver respectful, inclusive and person-centred education on strabismus, binocular vision, and ocular motility disorders, including orthoptic therapies and other management approaches.

.

args.text: Admission into C04299 Master of Orthoptics

96033.title: Ocular Pathology 2
96033.description: This subject deepens your understanding of ophthalmic diseases and their occurrence across the lifespan. You will study complex ophthalmic conditions, extending learning from 96029 Ocular Pathology 1 to explore the impact of systemic pathologies such as, diabetes and hypertension on eye health. There is an emphasis on developing detailed understanding of retinal and corneal pathologies, along with their medical and surgical management. You will also further your skill in interpretation of ocular biometry and topography, and intraocular lens selection for targeted refractive outcomes post-cataract surgery. Advanced diagnostic and imaging approaches will be developed, including specialised imaging of the retina, measurement of intraocular pressure, and A-scan and B-scan techniques. You will extend your skills in interpretation of clinical data, with a focus on implementation of treatment, monitoring of disease progression and evaluating the effectiveness of treatment strategies. You will also develop skills in assisting with minor ophthalmic surgical procedures enabling you to maintain a sterile field, select appropriate ophthalmic surgical instruments and provide pre-, peri- and post-operative care.
learningOutcomes: Apply clinical reasoning to develop investigative plans that inform the diagnosis and management ophthalmic pathologies across the lifespan.
Perform and interpret advanced ophthalmic investigations, including ocular imaging and ultrasound of anterior and posterior structures, to detect and monitor pathology.

Interpret clinical data to plan, adjust and evaluate collaborative person-centred management of ophthalmic conditions, including the selection of intraocular lenses, use of ocular medications, and surgical interventions.
Demonstrate safe clinical practice by applying correct aseptic techniques to establish a sterile environment and prepare for in-room and in-theatre surgical procedures.

Effectively educate patients on ophthalmic conditions and management options to obtain informed consent for procedures, support adherence to therapies, and facilitate appropriate pre- and post-operative care.

args.text: Admission into C04299 Master of Orthoptics

96034.title: Professional Practice 1
96034.description: In this subject, you will have the opportunity to develop your clinical knowledge and skills within diverse clinical and community settings. Preparation for learning within the clinical environment will focus on professional and ethical behaviour, person-centred approaches to eye health delivery and cultural safety. Through clinical placement, you will be supported by experienced practitioners to refine your communication, clinical skills and clinical reasoning as a novice practitioner. You will develop your critical reflection ability as you explore reflective journalling, utilise feedback to refine skills and apply your knowledge of ocular conditions in a real-world setting.
learningOutcomes: Perform basic orthoptic and ophthalmic clinical skills accurately, ethically, and safely under supervision and guidance from experienced practitioners.
Reflect on personal development of orthoptic skills, professional behaviour and communication to support effective, culturally safe patient care.
Draw on clinical reasoning to analyse patient signs and symptoms, formulate provisional diagnoses and plan investigation.
Develop evidence-based and person-centred management plans for common eye conditions.
Communicate effectively and contribute to disciplinary and interdisciplinary health care teams within the clinical environment.

args.text: Admission into C04299 Master of Orthoptics

96035.title: Research Project 1
96035.description: This subject builds on the skills of research and inquiry and principles of evidence-based medicine introduced in 96030 Introduction to Professional Practice. It equips you with the skills to critically evaluate scientific evidence for informed clinical decision-making as a health professional. You will gain a deeper understanding of the research process, focusing on epidemiological and clinical research, including research design and methodology, analysis and ethical considerations for conducting health research. You will apply this knowledge to critically assess scientific literature, construct scholarly arguments, identify gaps to formulate research questions, and design a project to address these questions. Emphasising active participation in orthoptic and ophthalmic research, the subject uses problem-based learning to foster critical thinking for lifelong learning.
learningOutcomes: Critically appraise scholarly literature to determine limitations in methodology, quality of evidence, clinical significance of findings and relevance to orthoptic practice.
Apply the principles of human research ethics and ethical conduct as a health professional to research project design, including when working with and for Indigenous Australians.
Identify statistical methods appropriate for data analysis, considering study design, the nature of study variables and research questions to be answered.
Systematically review and synthesise scholarly evidence to identify gaps within a research area and apply this to the formulation and justification of research questions.
Design a qualitative or quantitative research project that addresses a specific research question, uses appropriate research methodology and statistical approaches, is ethical and feasible.

args.text: Admission into C04299 Master of Orthoptics

96036.title: Neurological Ocular Disorders
96036.description: Through the study of authentic clinical cases, you will explore complex neuro-ophthalmic conditions caused by stroke, traumatic brain injury, neurodegenerative diseases, and other pathologies. You will learn essential neuroanatomy and physiology, providing the foundation to develop high-level diagnostic skills and the ability to localise pathology within the central nervous system. You will study the major sensory and motor pathways, including those specific to ocular functions such as the visual, pupil and ocular motor pathways. The cranial nerves, saccades, pursuits, and vestibulo-ocular reflex pathways will be explored in detail and applied to the diagnosis of ocular motility disorders. You will refine your understanding of orthoptic and ophthalmic examinations, adapting procedures for patients with cognitive, physical, and communication impairments due to brain injury. A person-centred and evidence-based approach is taken to considering therapeutic management for visual rehabilitation and the role of the orthoptist in interdisciplinary and collaborative teams in this area of practice.
learningOutcomes: Localise pathology based on knowledge of neuroanatomy and physiology, ocular signs and symptoms and other functional impacts of acquired brain injury
Diagnose vision impairment, strabismus, ocular motility dysfunction and other neuro-ocular conditions caused by disruption of the visual, pupillary and ocular motor pathways
Design person-centred and evidence-based plans for investigation and management of vision impairment and ocular motility dysfunction caused by acquired brain injury and other neurological conditions
Use advanced orthoptic and ophthalmic skills, adaptive communication and modified ocular assessment, to accurately examine patients with neurological conditions

Discuss interdisciplinary practice within acute care and rehabilitation settings, including the role of the orthoptist in visual rehabilitation and in supporting other health professionals to understand the impact of vision and ocular motility deficits on recovery

args.text: Admission into C04299 Master of Orthoptics

96037.title: Therapy, Management and Rehabilitation
96037.description: This subject delves into specialised orthoptic practice in the area of low vision and explores approaches to supporting rehabilitation, assisting with activities of daily living, providing environmental modification and optimising use of vision through optical aides and other technologies. You will study the epidemiology of low vision in Australia and abroad, and the prevalence of visual impairment caused by different pathologies. The impact of low vision will be discussed from both an individual quality of life perspective and, from a health care system and economic perspective. Clinical approaches to the assessment of functional vision, application of electrophysiology and prescription of aides and devices will be a focus of your practical learning. Application of orthoptic skills to advanced contexts including, management of paediatric visual impairment, classification of visual impairment in paralympic athletes, brain injury and driver rehabilitation will be explored. You will have the opportunity to engage directly with clients with low vision, developing empathy and understanding that can be applied to person-centred management in this area of practice.
learningOutcomes: Integrate knowledge of ocular and neurological causes of vision impairment with psychosocial impacts of vision loss to guide empathetic and compassionate delivery of eye care.
Assess functional vision using standard and adapted examination procedures to classify vision impairment, determine impact on activities of daily living and inform therapeutic approaches.

Plan person-centred rehabilitation in collaboration with the interdisciplinary care team that includes optical treatment, therapies, environmental modification, visual aids and other strategies to optimise visual function.
Provide education on vision impairment, the impact of vision loss and rehabilitation approaches to individuals of all ages, families, health professionals, organisations and communities.
Advocate for clients/ patients to receive best-practice care, support for education and employment, and access to resources and services such as, Government grants and allowances.

args.text: Admission into C04299 Master of Orthoptics

96038.title: Professional Practice 2
96038.description: This subject allows you to enhance your clinical knowledge and practice across hospital, private, and community settings. You will refine your clinical competencies, continue developing clinical reasoning and gain further insight into the orthoptist's role within interdisciplinary, multidisciplinary and collaborative care teams, managing eye care for diverse patients. Person-centred eye care delivery is emphasised through strong communication, holistic approaches to management, and patient education and support. You will have the opportunity to learn through participating in orthoptic practice with support and feedback from experienced practitioners. Self-reflection is an important skill for professional practice that will be further developed throughout this subject.
learningOutcomes: Practice orthoptic and ophthalmic clinical skills accurately, efficiently and safely at a level expected of a training orthoptist.
Act professionally and ethically in the clinical environment when interacting with patients/ clients, healthcare professionals and others.
Demonstrate sound knowledge and clinical reasoning when planning investigation and management, drawing on person-centred and evidence-based approaches to care.
Critically reflect on practice as a training orthoptist to further personal and professional development, to enhance care delivery, patient experience and outcomes.
Collaborate effectively within the interdisciplinary eye-care team across a variety of clinical contexts.

96039.title: Research Project 2
96039.description: This subject enables you to apply the research skills learned in 96035 Research Project 1 as you undertake a supervised research project relevant to orthoptic practice. With approval, you may complete an individual project under academic staff supervision. You will identify necessary background information by reviewing scientific literature related to your research question and discuss the required data and methodology. Understanding of ethical research principles are deepened through discussion of ethical issues related to the project. You will collect data under supervision, employ current approaches to statistical analysis, and interpret findings. You will also learn about the peer review process, a system used to assess the quality of a paper before its published. The subject hones your scientific writing skills, culminating in an independently written dissertation that presents your results within the context of your research question and literature review, formatted as a research publication.
learningOutcomes: Critically analyse and synthesise research literature to justify research questions and discuss project findings in the context of current evidence.
Apply the principles of human research ethics to the conduct of a research project, including data collection and management.
Interpret statistical analyses, present research findings in appropriate scientific formats, identify study limitations and draw sound conclusions.
Write a thesis, dissertation or manuscript using appropriate scientific language and presentation for scholarly dissemination.
Reflect on the importance of integrating emerging evidence into professional practice and the need for lifelong learning as a health care professional.

args.text: Admission into C04299 Master of Orthoptics

96040.title: Advanced Professional Practice
96040.description: This subject brings together knowledge and skills from across the Master of Orthoptics course to prepare students for professional practice as a graduate. Orthoptist-led screening, triaging, monitoring and management will be explored, considering development of appropriate protocols, and approaches to auditing practice to ensure best-practice care provision. You will learn about service delivery models across various settings including, relevant legislative and regulatory requirements for designing safe and efficient clinical services. Funding streams to support health delivery such as, Medicare, private health insurance, the National Disability Insurance Scheme, Worker’s Compensation and the Department of Veteran's Affairs, will be discussed. Approaches to complex and challenging circumstances including, the presence of a functional vision disorder, malingering and factitious disorders will be included. You will refine your communication skills to ensure you are able to provide accurate and accessible information to other health professionals, facilitating collaborative care arrangements. Health promotion and advocacy will be examined, and you will learn techniques to increase health literacy of patients, supporting adherence to orthoptic and ophthalmic therapies. You will explore the development of health partnerships that prioritise person-centred and culturally safe approaches, alongside the vital role of community-led initiatives to promote eye health for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and communities.
learningOutcomes: Audit clinical data and draw on best-practice evidence to evaluate clinical services and propose business solutions to increase efficiency and optimise outcomes for patients and organisations.
Design innovative models of eye service delivery that are aligned with clinical guidelines, regulation, legislation and funding schemes.
Reflect on the impact of advanced orthoptic practice across diverse healthcare settings, and its contribution to improved outcomes for patients and communities.
Communicate eye health information effectively and accurately using culturally safe, respectful, and inclusive approaches that promote health literacy and education.
Advocate for equity in eye health care through health promotion informed by shared decision-making, community-led approaches, and partnerships that empower individuals and communities.

96043.title: Introduction to Clinical Practice Skills
96043.description: This subject equips you with essential clinical psychology skills, focusing on patient assessment, diagnosis, treatment, and ethical decision-making. You'll learn to address diverse patient issues effectively while adhering to professional ethical standards. Interactive learning methods, including case studies and role-playing, facilitate practical skill development in real-world contexts.
learningOutcomes: Locate, evaluate and communicate academic research as it applies to formulation, treatment planning and intervention within a diverse range of clinical contexts.
Develop an understanding of the appropriate diagnostic frameworks from a range of evidence-based clinical diagnosis, assessment and intervention models.
Effectively apply core therapy skills to establish and maintain positive therapeutic relationships, communicate the therapeutic framework, and collaboratively set clear goals for therapy.
Apply knowledge of historical and contemporary Indigenous experience to professional practice.

Identify and adhere to the relevant ethical, legal and professional requirements relevant to the practice of clinical psychology and demonstrate a good understanding of the ethical decision-making principles in professional practice.

args.text: Admission into C04300 Master of Clinical Psychology

96044.title: Child and Adolescent Clinical Psychology
96044.description: This subject merges current research and clinical theory to consider child and adolescent mental health, and family relational and behavioural functioning. Thus, it adheres to the scientist-practitioner model of evidence-based practice. You'll gain insights into the relation between developmental experience and child social, emotional, behavioural, and cognitive, functioning, and you'll develop skills in assessment, diagnosis, clinical formulation, and treatment. The subject views development through a number of theoretical and treatment lenses and is orientated toward clinical work with children and their families/carers. Mastery of this subject is a prerequisite for advancing to the second year of the Master of Clinical Psychology.
learningOutcomes: Source, evaluate, communicate and apply relevant research.
Demonstrate appropriate skills for evaluating and undertaking evidence-based clinical diagnosis and intervention.
Conduct evidence-based assessment, including risk assessment, and respond appropriately.
Communicate effectively in written and verbal forms within the course.
Demonstrate a strengths-based understanding of Indigenous experience and the importance of self-determination and cultural safety with culturally diverse clients.

96045.description: This subject adopts a scientist-practitioner approach to adult psychological disorders, covering assessment, diagnosis, and evidence-based treatments. Completion is essential for advancing to the second year of the Master of Clinical Psychology.

Prepare for a research project by selecting an appropriate design and methodology and completing an ethics application.

96057.description:
This introductory subject to Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) focuses on the fundamentals of manufacturing in industry.

It outlines the essential aspects of GMP which include risk management, risk assessment, decision making and compliance in Quality Assurance which all play a critical role in the manufacturing industry.

There are workshops incorporated into this subject which will allow you to apply key concepts or examples that you would experience in the outside world.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate manufacturing operations for therapeutic products in a GMP setting to ensure product quality, patient safety, and regulatory requirements are met.
Apply quality risk management in GMP manufacturing operations to assess and control risks to product quality, patient safety, and regulatory compliance.

Understanding cleanroom principles such as cleanroom behavior and gowning procedures will prepare you for operating in highly controlled cleanroom environments, while recognising bioburden risks and ensuring proficiency in environmental monitoring and various sterilisation techniques that are essential for maintaining product quality. Through real-world scenarios, you'll apply these skills, mastering the implementation of aseptic practices and sterilisation in diverse pharmaceutical settings.

96066.title: Clinical Trials Quality Assurance Management
96066.description: This subject introduces you to the Good Clinical Practice (GCP) regulations and protocols governing clinical trials that are essential for assessing medical treatments' safety and efficacy. You'll learn about trial design, project management, and the development of new products, gaining a solid understanding of everything from protocol development to participant recruitment, study initiation, data collection, and management. It also covers monitoring and auditing requirements for ensuring GCP-compliant clinical studies in accordance with the protocols, and are aligned with regulatory bodies such as Australia's TGA, the US FDA, and Europe's EMA.

Apply appropriate regulatory frameworks to design compliant pharmaceutical product clinical trials.

Critically evaluate and address challenges in the design, management, and execution of complex clinical trials.

96067.title: Supply Chain Management
96067.description: This subject explores the complex supply chains of therapeutic goods and global regulatory and logistical challenges. You will learn how to manage supply chain partners to ensure compliance and supply, covering key roles from raw material suppliers to distribution. Focusing on patient safety and supply reliability, the subject provides essential knowledge of laws, regulations, and inspection guidelines. You will learn to identify and mitigate risks, ensuring traceability and integrity from production to delivery. Through real-world scenarios, you will apply new skills and knowledge to solve practical supply chain problems. By the end, you will be equipped to design and manage quality systems for the safe and reliable delivery of medicines in a complex regulatory environment.

Evaluate risks and recommend mitigations in the supply chain.
Evaluate industry trends and regulatory initiatives to maintain supply chain integrity.
Evaluate vendor appropriateness using a risk-based approach to ensure product quality, patient safety, and regulatory requirements are met.
Evaluate therapeutic goods wholesaling and distribution practices in intended markets to ensure product quality, patient safety, and regulatory requirements are met.

96074.description: Building on 96052 Advanced Clinical Skills 1, this will subject enhance your knowledge and application of evidence-based therapeutic approaches in clinical psychology beyond CBT. Emphasizing contemporary methods, it covers their empirical support, theoretical foundations, and practical application. The subject also provides insights into the registrar program, employment opportunities post-graduation, and the integration of e-mental health into practice. 96075.title: Professional Practice 3
96075.description: As the capstone subject for the Master of Orthoptics, this final clinical placement consolidates your learning from the entire course through experience in diverse settings, including an out-of-Sydney placement in a rural, regional, interstate or international location. You will refine your clinical reasoning for diagnosing and managing ocular conditions, ensuring your knowledge and skills meet professional standards for work as an orthoptist. Learning emphasises the importance of reflective, person-centred and evidence-based practice for work as a healthcare professional and professional capabilities to work with and for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples. You will also reflect on your professional development, readiness for practice, and ability to collaborate within a healthcare team. Your clinical competency will be assessed against the Australian Orthoptic Board's registration standards to ensure requirements are met for practice.

96079.title: Inclusive Practice in Speech Pathology
96079.description: In this subject, you will learn and apply the theory, design, and implementation of inclusive practice in speech pathology. You will focus on engagement with online communities, working with multilingual populations and about cultural and linguistic diversity. You will work with and for Indigenous Australians, improving professional practices in speech pathology to meet their needs. Through case-based and clinical scenarios, you will become familiar with a range of strategies that acknowledge, embrace, and respect diversity to reduce inequity and restore justice. You will know about the impacts of racism and colonization on populations with communication or swallowing disability and their families and communities. This subject will prepare you for including all people in a culturally safe and responsive professional practice.
learningOutcomes: Engage with and show respect for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, their local communities, and multilingual populations in relation to speech pathology practice.
Identify and respond to a wide variety of personal and environmental factors that impact on speech pathology assessment or intervention and affect communication or swallowing.

96080.description: You will master the clinical assessment and treatment planning for physiotherapy management of musculoskeletal and neurological conditions, using inquiry-based learning to critically evaluate assessment techniques and evidence-based practice. Anatomy revision in practical workshops will enhance your diagnostic palpation skills and inform surface anatomy and impairment testing. The ICF is used to strengthen your clinical reasoning for differential diagnosis and treatment planning. You will also learn to set goals and make treatment decisions collaboratively with clients and families.

Your clinical reasoning will evolve to make collaborative treatment decisions, considering condition pathophysiology, patient preferences, and current evidence. Authentic cases will help you apply research and develop reasoning in a practical context.

96083.title: Pain Neuroscience and Management
96083.description: You will learn the contemporary neuroscience that underpins the experience of pain. By investigating case studies of people challenged by acute and chronic pain conditions, you will integrate knowledge of biological, psychological, and social factors into clinical assessments and treatments. You will understand a physiotherapist's role within an interdisciplinary pain management team. You will use evidence-based practice principles to identify interventions targeting pain neurobiology and maladaptive beliefs, including educational and learning strategies. You will also explore historical, current, and emerging approaches to treating and managing pain. Then you will apply your knowledge and skills to consider special populations such as stroke, paediatrics, aged care, dystonia, multiple sclerosis, rheumatoid arthritis, and cancer.

You will critique research and apply evidence-based rehabilitation, expanding your assessment skills to include functional and non-standardized tests. Rehabilitation skills emphasize motor learning for improved mobility and upper limb function, incorporating part-task and whole-task practice. You will explore the use of technology in rehabilitation and develop an ability to enhance client-centered care through self-management, goal setting and collaborative discharge planning.

You will understand the physiotherapy needs of acute care patients and apply research evidence for cardiopulmonary management in line with evidence-based guidelines. The focus is on person-centred care from an interprofessional perspective, including the physiotherapist's role in multidisciplinary teams. You will learn about the intensive care unit (ICU) environment, assessment and practical treatment skills for acute and ICU patients, as well as strategies for managing your own health, resolving conflicts, and working within teams in acute settings. This subject builds on previous learning in clinical assessment, professional practice, and core physiotherapy skills.

96089.description: This subject focuses on the prevention, wellness, and management of chronic diseases in community settings, emphasising exercise therapy and self-management to enhance health and daily life participation. You will explore exercise and lifestyle strategies for disease prevention, psychological well-being, and healthy ageing, including falls prevention. Critically assess evidence for varying exercise intensities including aquatic therapy for managing chronic cardiopulmonary conditions. You will study behavioural interventions like motivational interviewing and strategies to improve exercise adherence and self-efficacy for conditions such as amputation. The subject also covers community-based physiotherapy, vestibular disorders, Concussion, cancer and palliative care, and the use of telerehabilitation to increase social participation. It reinforces client-centred care, shared decision-making, and the physiotherapist's role as an educator.

96093.description: You will learn to synthesise your academic, clinical, and research knowledge to prepare you for the workplace as a physiotherapist. You will explore practice contexts, development, medico-legal issues, quality improvement, and leadership within the evolving healthcare landscape. You will refine your professional communication skills; verbal, non-verbal, and written. You will also develop job application expertise, including CV writing, interviewing, and business strategies. You will develop and refine advanced clinical reasoning skills to navigate complex case simulations involving musculoskeletal, neurological, and cardiorespiratory conditions. You will reflect on your placement performance and develop strategies to be able to measure your competence, and future performance, in line with the PPTAANZ's seven practice thresholds. You will set short and long term goals in light of placements, working as a new graduate physiotherapist, and beyond.

You will engage in weekly reflective practice blending theory with clinical experience and maintain your e-portfolio to critically assess your progress. Your assessments will mirror professional certification tasks, ensuring you are well-prepared for HGSA certification after graduation.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate and maintain effective client-counsellor relationships in genetic counselling practice.
Facilitate informed decision-making with clients and their families.
Educate and communicate effectively to enhance understanding of genomics and empowerment of clients, their families and healthcare professionals in the genomic healthcare setting.
Practice genetic counselling inclusively and adapt to diverse client needs.
Adhere to professional standards in genetic counselling and manage responsibilities effectively.

args.text: Admission into C04374 Master of Genetic Counselling

96102.title: Research Methods in Genetic Counselling
96102.description:
This subject lays the foundation for understanding and appreciating research methods crucial for healthcare practice, including critical appraisal and application of research findings. You will explore the philosophy, principles and practice of research.

This subject will introduce you to both qualitative and quantitative methodologies, as well as mixed method theories and systematic literature reviews. The skills acquired here support your future research projects and ethical considerations in genetic counselling. Instruction is provided by experienced researchers, ensuring a comprehensive learning experience that emphasises reflection, ethics and integrity in research practice.
learningOutcomes: Identify and discuss the underlying principles of research
Critically appraise selected research to assess its trustworthiness, value and relevance for clinical practice
Discuss the ethical implications of research and construct an ethics application
Identify and analyse the values expressed in different decisions made during the research process
Articulate ethical justifications for methodological decisions

args.text: Admission into C04374 Master of Genetic Counselling

96103.title: Medical Genetics and Genomics in Practice
96103.description: This subject equips you with the medical literacy needed to effectively convey complex genetic information, a vital skill for genetic counsellors. You'll gain a solid grasp of genetic concepts, inheritance patterns, genomics, and variant interpretation, alongside human development and genetic conditions. Through case studies, you'll learn to navigate medical assessments and diagnostic tools essential for genetic counselling. Additionally, you'll explore biomedical ethics and the delivery of genetic services, laying the groundwork for your clinical placement.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate client comprehension and facilitate their understanding of genetic concepts in genetic counselling practice.
Use relevant databases and the genetics/genomics literature to inform practice.
Interpret genetic information and pathology reports for use in genetic risk assessment and genetic counselling practice.
Identify and apply ethical considerations in genetic counselling.

args.text: Admission into C04374 Master of Genetic Counselling

96104.title: Communication and Counselling
96104.description: This subject lays the groundwork for your career in genetic counselling, focusing on essential counselling and communication skills within a supportive setting. You'll learn the theories that inform genetic counselling and develop culturally safe practices, particularly for Indigenous Australians, New Zealand Maori, Pacific Islanders, and other communities. Emphasising reflective practice, you'll engage in role-play exercises to hone your skills and foster professional self-awareness. This foundational module is a critical component of the Master of Genetic Counselling programme, setting the stage for your future practice.
learningOutcomes: Critique and apply psychological counselling theories in genetic counselling practice.
Develop and demonstrate effective communication and counselling skills in a clinical setting.
Engage in reflective practice to enhance genetic counselling skills and client outcomes.
Apply knowledge of historical and contemporary Indigenous experience to genetic counselling practice.

args.text: Admission into C04374 Master of Genetic Counselling

96105.title: Clinical and Community Placement 1
96105.description:
This subject is designed for future genetic counsellors seeking practical exposure to the field. Students will gain firsthand experience to understand the diverse nature of genetic counselling through clinical observations. Its unique feature is the blend of community engagement and expert interactions, fostering a comprehensive learning environment.

You will acquire skills in client interaction, cultural competence, and reflective practice, essential for professional development. Learning occurs through direct observation, community participation, expert meetings, supervised reflection, and e-portfolio documentation, ensuring a well-rounded educational experience.
learningOutcomes: Uphold professional and ethical standards in genetic counselling.
Enhance genetic counselling practice through reflective practice, skill development and ongoing learning.
Apply knowledge of historical and contemporary Indigenous experience to genetic counselling practice.

args.text: Admission into C04374 Master of Genetic Counselling

96106.title: Application of Genetics and Genomics
96106.description: This subject deepens your understanding of genetic concepts and genomic technologies, building on prior knowledge to enhance your genetic counselling practice. You'll explore case studies across various specialties, such as rare diseases and familial cancer, to understand cytogenetic and molecular genetics laboratory techniques and their result interpretations. Topics include human reproductive technology, risk calculation, and the societal and ethical impacts of genetic technologies. This knowledge is crucial for your progression and will be expanded upon in the subsequent module, Genetics and Genomics in Society.
learningOutcomes: Utilise genetic and genomic information and resources effectively in genetic counselling practice.
Communicate the implications of genetic/genomic testing and screening to clients and facilitate understanding of hereditary inheritance patterns.
Understand and interpret and communicate genetic and genomic test results.
Explain the impact of population, ancestry and ethnicity on genomic health care.
Describe laboratory techniques in the context of genetic counselling practice.

args.text: Admission into C04374 Master of Genetic Counselling

96107.title: Advanced Communication and Counselling
96107.description: This subject hones your counselling and communication skills, essential for supporting individuals and families navigating inherited conditions. Continuing to develop your understanding of counselling and communication theory, you'll delve into decision-making, crisis intervention, grief, family dynamics, and mental health assessment, while continuing to cultivate cultural sensitivity. Through case studies, skills-based learning and role-play, you'll demonstrate skill advancement and apply theoretical knowledge through reflective exercises. This training is integral to your preparation for second-year clinical placements, ensuring you're well-equipped to handle the complexities of genetic counselling.
learningOutcomes: Critique and integrate psychological and psychotherapeutic theories to genetic counselling practice.
Demonstrate effective client-counsellor relationships.
Elicit and assess clients' beliefs, values, mental wellbeing and capacity for decision making.
Facilitate adaptive responses and coping strategies for clients and their families.
Reflect on the use of counselling skills to enhance practice and improve client outcomes.

args.text: Admission into C04374 Master of Genetic Counselling

96108.title: Research Project 1
96108.description: In this advanced research-focused subject, you'll build on prior learning to conduct a research project, which could range from a systematic review to an original study. You'll set clear research goals with your supervisors, outline, plan and organise the project, and engage in a process of reflection to align expectations. Your main tasks include developing the study and gathering data, while maintaining a research journal to track progress, decisions, and their justifications. This journal not only keeps your research on course but also informs supervision meetings, tutorial needs, and reflections for the subsequent module, Research Project 2.
learningOutcomes: Identify and analyse the underlying principles and values of the research process.
Evaluate research critically to determine its credibility and applicability to genetic counselling practice.
Design and execute a research project.
Uphold ethical standards and academic integrity throughout the research process.

args.text: Admission into C04374 Master of Genetic Counselling

96109.title: Research Issues in Genetic Counselling
96109.description: Expanding on 96102 Research Methods in Genetic Counselling, this subject focuses on applying research principles within the context of evidence-based genetic counselling practice. It emphasises ethical research conduct, critical engagement with research processes, and the integration of research into healthcare and interdisciplinary settings. You'll develop skills in interpreting and evaluating research decisions, reflect on your role as practitioner researchers, and communicate research in ways that are appropriate to diverse audiences. The subject explores ethical review processes and the genetic counsellor's contribution within interdisciplinary research teams, alongside broader professional research development.
learningOutcomes: Critically appraise, evaluate and apply research findings to genetic counselling practice.
Discuss and demonstrate ethical considerations and integrity in the research process.
Choose appropriate modes of communication for target audience.

Apply knowledge from a strengths-based perspective and aligned to the Aboriginal Health and Medical Research Council (AHMRC) ethical guidelines for the conduct of genetic counselling research with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples

args.text: Admission into C04374 Master of Genetic Counselling

96110.title: Genetic Counselling
96110.description: Genetic counsellors support individuals in comprehending their family history, make informed decisions about genetic testing, understand and manage the results. In this subject, you'll practice key skills such as structuring counselling sessions, recording family histories, and discussing the impact of inherited conditions through case studies. You'll apply genetic counselling theories to these cases, integrating this knowledge with 96099 Genetic Counselling Clinical Placement 2 to prepare for clinical placement experiences.
learningOutcomes: Critically analyse and apply psychological, psychotherapeutic and counselling theories to genetic counselling practice.
Develop and demonstrate effective counselling skills.
Elicit and address client concerns and expectations in genetic counselling practice and obtain informed consent from clients and their families.
Communicate effectively in written form to diverse audiences and document client interactions.
Collect and utilise client personal and family history in genetic counselling practice.

args.text: Admission into C04374 Master of Genetic Counselling

96111.title: Genetics and Genomics in Society
96111.description: As media focus on genetics and genomics grows, it shapes public discourse and impacts genetic counsellors' work. You'll examine this interaction, considering the rise of genomic testing in various specialties, direct-to-consumer offerings like wellness genomics, and genomics in forensics. Through media articles and case studies, you'll assess the implications for individuals, healthcare professionals, policy, and society, both in Australasia and worldwide. The subject also explores health behaviour theories and the application of brief health interventions in genetic counselling.
learningOutcomes: Adapt genetic counseling practices to incorporate new information, technologies and changes to the genomic healthcare setting.
Educate clients, families, and healthcare professionals about genetic/genomic testing and screening including their risks and benefits.
Apply knowledge of historical and contemporary Indigenous experience to genetic counselling practice.
Interpret and communicate complex genetic and genomic test results effectively.
Apply knowledge of historical and contemporary mis-use of genetic information to genetic counselling practice.

args.text: Admission into C04374 Master of Genetic Counselling

96112.title: Advanced Professional Practice
96112.description: This subject facilitates your professional identity as a genetic counsellor, aligning with the Australasian Society of Genetic Counsellors' 'Scope of Practice' and 'Code of Ethics'. You'll prepare for the workplace and potential leadership roles by applying knowledge of health literacy, education, and advocacy to genetic counselling. The curriculum emphasises the importance of interprofessional collaboration, workload management, continuous professional development, and reflective practice supervision. You'll also learn about the Human Genetics Society of Australasia (HGSA) certification process and engage with international peers to understand global professional roles and standards, shaping your perspective on the profession's future.
learningOutcomes: Apply relevant genetic counselling theories in practice.
Evaluate client needs and advocate for clients and their families.
Communicate and collaborate professionally in healthcare settings.
Maintain professional practice in accordance with current standards relevant to genetic counselling and adapt to emerging changes in the genomic healthcare environment.
Manage workload and personal well-being while pursuing continuous genetic counselling professional development.

args.text: Admission into C04374 Master of Genetic Counselling

96113.title: Advanced Genetic Counselling
96113.description:
This final genetic counselling subject equips you with the core competencies for supporting individuals and families living with psychosocial impact of genetic conditions.

You will integrate your learning to prepare for graduation as entry-level genetic counsellors.

You will engage in case-based learning to enhance development of communication skills across a range of contexts in which genetic counsellors practice. You will focus on increasing cultural safety and working with diverse communities to demonstrate your readiness to join the genetic counselling profession.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate advanced client-centered communication and counseling skills for genetic counselling practice.
Apply reflective and inclusive practices in genetic counselling.
Adapt to changes in genomic healthcare field and identify professional development needs.
Collaborate effectively within multi-disciplinary teams.
Advocate for clients and their families and address ethical considerations in genetic counselling practice.

args.text: Admission into C04374 Master of Genetic Counselling

96114.title: Research Project 2
96114.description: You will advance your research project, building on the foundations laid in prior subjects on research methods and issues in genetic counselling. Through ongoing supervision and focused tutorials, you'll address learning needs and develop your research skills. You'll reflect on your project's impact on genetic counselling and the research process using your Research ePortfolio. The subject fosters your abilities in data analysis, writing, and sharing research findings, essential for professional development in the field.
learningOutcomes: Understand and articulate the foundational principles, values and ethical considerations of research.
Evaluate research critically to determine its credibility and applicability to genetic counselling practice.
Apply selected research findings to genetic counselling practice.
Execute an independent research project and communicate findings, ensuring academic integrity and adherence to ethical standards.
Collaborate effectively within a multidisciplinary team.

args.text: Admission into C04374 Master of Genetic Counselling

96115.title: Evidence-based Practice in Speech Pathology
96115.description: This subject equips you with the core principles of evidence-based practice for speech pathology. It will enhance your ability to apply research and ethical guidelines in diverse clinical settings. You'll gain proficiency in critical skills including interpreting speech pathology terminology, utilising the bio-psycho-social models of health and disability. You will know how to integrate various evidence forms to inform clinical decision-making. Emphasis is placed on developing cultural competence when engaging with Indigenous Australians and those with diverse linguistic and cultural heritage. Your learning journey involves practical exercises that also underpin all subjects in the Master of Speech Pathology. This subject ensures a solid foundation for your professional development and lifelong learning as an evidence-based speech pathologist.
learningOutcomes: Explain and apply principles of evidence-based practice and professional practice guidelines and standards.
Explain interprofessional collaboration and ethical practice.
Identify foundational clinical skills for assessment, treatment, and client-centered care.
Understand and apply principles of cultural safety and responsiveness with Indigenous, Multilingual, and diverse populations in Australia.
Implement effective communication and counseling techniques.

args.text: Admission into C04386 Master of Speech Pathology

96116.title: Fundamentals in Speech Pathology
96116.description: This subject provides a foundational understanding of speech pathology, crucial for evaluating and treating communication and swallowing disorders in children and adults. You will learn about anatomy and physiology relevant to communication and swallowing. You’ll also develop practical skills in clinical linguistics and phonetics and explore hearing as it relates to clinical practice. Through a blend of lectures and practical activities, you will apply theoretical knowledge to simulated cases, honing the essential skills required for the Master of Speech Pathology. This hands-on approach ensures you are well-prepared for advanced study and professional practice.
learningOutcomes: Apply suitable evidence-based speech pathology assessment procedures to collect and analyse resulting data.
Apply foundational knowledge of body structures and functions, genetics, anatomy, and neuroanatomy, to diagnose and manage communication and swallowing disorders.
Identify and accommodate cultural aspects of deafness and hearing impairment in speech pathology practice.
Seek appropriate feedback and guidance in the management of communication and/or swallowing disabilities.
Explain and enact appropriate infection control practices.

args.text: Admission into C04386 Master of Speech Pathology

96117.title: Speech Sound Disorders in Children
96117.description: This subject equips you with an understanding of speech sound disorders in children. It will highlight the effects of speech sound disorders on children’s communication, literacy, and social inclusion. You will gain practical skills in assessment, analysis, and intervention. You will learn to critically evaluate evidence-based practices through hands-on activities and simulations. You'll explore the relationship between phonological awareness and literacy, preparing you for clinical practice in the Master of Speech Pathology. Learning combines theoretical study with research application to foster a comprehensive skill set.
learningOutcomes: Diagnose communication disorders and effectively communicate the findings.
Develop, communicate, and implement evidence-based intervention plans.
Conduct and interpret common statistical operations on data in speech pathology research and standardized tests.
Integrate and apply knowledge of the relevant body structures and functions involved in or impacting on communication.
Advocate for client needs and inclusion in society in relation to speech pathology and other services.

args.text: Admission into C04386 Master of Speech Pathology

96118.title: Language Disorders in Children
96118.description: This subject prepares you to understand and address language disorders in infants, young children, adolescents, and youth. You will learn about language skills in listening, speaking, reading, and writing. You'll learn to apply theoretical frameworks and research to assess, diagnose, and design and deliver interventions for children with language disorders. You will know about the prevalence of language disorders and the impacts on social and educational participation. Through practical activities and simulations, you'll refine your clinical decision-making skills, laying a foundation for clinical practice in the Master of Speech Pathology.
learningOutcomes: Determine the client’s communication diagnosis and effectively communicate the findings.
Develop, communicate, and implement evidence-based intervention plans.
Conduct and interpret common statistical operations on data in speech pathology research and standardized tests.
Integrate and apply knowledge of the relevant body structures and functions involved in or impacting on communication.
Advocate for client needs and inclusion in society in relation to speech pathology and other services.

args.text: Admission into C04386 Master of Speech Pathology

96119.title: Research Design in Speech Pathology
96119.description:
You will learn about diverse research paradigms and designs used in the field of speech pathology. This includes qualitative, quantitative, mixed methods, and Indigenous approaches. You will develop skills in critiquing clinical research methods and results as well as designing ethical and rigorous studies.

This subject also covers implementation science and knowledge translation. It will prepare you for your future literature reviews, clinical practice, and ongoing professional growth in speech pathology.
learningOutcomes: Explain both qualitative and quantitative paradigms of research using examples from the field of speech pathology.
Source, appraise and report on selected research in terms of rigour and confidence in the study results.
Appropriately resolve problems relating to the ethical conduct of human research.
Conduct and interpret statistical analyses in speech pathology research.

args.text: Admission into C04386 Master of Speech Pathology

96120.title: Augmentative and Alternative Communication
96120.description: You will learn to design and implement both aided and unaided augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) systems for children, adolescents, and adults. You will focus on assessing communication needs and methods, overcoming barriers to communication access in an evidence-based approach. Through case-based inquiry, you'll explore a range of communication methods, emphasising a collaborative, strengths-based and user-centred approach. This subject complements your clinical placements and enhances your knowledge of a wide range of communication methods and technologies.
learningOutcomes: Integrate and apply foundational knowledge of body structures and functions with knowledge of communication disabilities to determine appropriate evidence-based interventions.
Communicate effectively with clients with communication disability and relevant stakeholders in speech pathology.
Critically evaluate and apply evidence-based practices in speech pathology.
Identify appropriate areas for professional development and advocacy and design relevant training materials.
Demonstrate proficiency in information literacy and communication technologies for clinical and professional purposes.

args.text: Admission into C04386 Master of Speech Pathology

96121.title: Motor Speech Disorders
96121.description: You will examine stuttering across all ages, focusing on assessment, intervention, and management in children and adults. You will also understand and apply knowledge of the psychosocial impacts of stuttering. You'll learn to evaluate stuttering severity, the experience of stuttering, speech naturalness, and associated anxiety in various age groups. You will also learn assessment and treatment principles for motor speech disorders including dyspraxia and dysarthria in adults. Through case-based inquiry and simulations, you'll be well-prepared for future clinical placements and practice in speech pathology.
learningOutcomes: Integrate and apply knowledge of body structures and functions with knowledge of communication disabilities to determine appropriate evidence-based interventions.
Identify and respond to environmental factors and life-course transitions that impact on communication and its assessment and intervention.
Appropriately refer clients to applicable services for the management of conditions that are outside the speech pathology scope of practice.
Demonstrate effective communication and counselling techniques in professional practice.
Demonstrate proficiency in information literacy and communication technologies for clinical and professional purposes.

args.text: Admission into C04386 Master of Speech Pathology

96122.title: Speech Pathology Clinical Practice 1
96122.description: This subject equips you with practical experience in working with children and adults, and their families in clinical teams. It will enhance your theoretical knowledge with hands-on application of knowledge and skills. You'll develop key skills in speech pathology management for children and adults through supervised clinical practice and in-class simulations, guided by experienced professionals. Your learning is captured in a portfolio, showcasing the development of your reflective practice and clinical skills.
learningOutcomes: Develop clinical competency in identifying, appraising, selecting, implementing, and documenting appropriate assessment, diagnosis, intervention, and management plans.
Effectively communicate assessment findings, intervention plans, and outcomes using respectful, inclusive, and person-centred approaches.
Collaborate respectfully with individuals, communities, and professionals in all areas of professional and clinical practice.
Develop awareness and skills in cultural safety, ethical practice, and evidence-based practice.
Demonstrate growth in clinical competency and recognise the importance of lifelong learning and professional development.

args.text: Admission into C04386 Master of Speech Pathology

96123.title: Literature Review in Speech Pathology
96123.description: This subject enhances your ability to search, find, and critically evaluate literature as essential skills for speech pathologists. You'll learn to formulate clinical questions, design inclusion and exclusion criteria, and efficiently locate and analyse relevant studies from scientific databases. Through data extraction and quality appraisal, you'll synthesise findings to answer clinical questions. You’ll write an impactful literature review, which also identifies research gaps. This training lays the foundation for your future evidence-based practice and knowledge translation in clinical settings.
learningOutcomes: Critically appraise, reflect, and report on research to improve practice in speech pathology.
Explain qualitative and quantitative paradigms of research using examples from the field of speech pathology.
Use relevant technologies and sources to identify research and related literature relevant to the field of speech pathology.
Contribute to the field of speech pathology through conducting and participating in research synthesis.
Promote effective use of speech pathology interventions and strategies by clients and their family members and community members.

args.text: Admission into C04386 Master of Speech Pathology

96124.title: Swallowing Disorders
96124.description: In this subject, you'll learn about the assessment and management of swallowing disorders in infants, children, and adults. This includes eating, drinking, oral health, and saliva control. You'll apply theoretical knowledge in clinical cases to diagnose swallowing disorders and create management plans. You will understand the expected pattern of swallowing, signs and symptoms of swallowing disorders, and related health and quality of life impacts. Practical activities with simulated clients will help you integrate your knowledge with case-based learning. You will also learn to apply ethical frameworks to guide your decision-making. This subject prepares you for your future clinical placements and managing complexity related to swallowing disability.
learningOutcomes: Apply foundational knowledge of body structures and functions, genetics, anatomy, and neuroanatomy, to diagnose and manage communication and swallowing disorders.
Develop and evaluate clinical plans and interventions based on evidence and theoretical frameworks.
Identify and respond to environmental factors and life-course transitions that impact on a person’s communication and swallowing disorders and that influence assessment and management.
Explain the principles and practices relevant to speech pathology, including ethical decision-making, clinical risk, and infection control.
Identify advanced practice areas in speech pathology that require further training.

args.text: Admission into C04386 Master of Speech Pathology

96125.title: Acquired Communication Disability in Adults
96125.description: You will learn to assess and treat adults with acquired communication disabilities, focusing on language, and cognitive-communication impairments. You will integrate theoretical frameworks, research evidence, and client perspectives, to create effective communication interventions. You will learn about engaging communication partners in both individual and group therapy settings. This subject prepares you for your clinical placements, for future lifelong learning, and integrated practice in the field.
learningOutcomes: Assess, diagnose, and manage clients’ needs and concerns, integrating appropriate foundational knowledge of body structures and functions with biopsychosocial models of health and disability.
Develop evidence-based intervention plans for communication disorders.
Explain clinical risk and governance involved in managing communication disorders.
Design and deliver training to communication partners of people with communication support needs including family, health professionals and support workers.
Promote inclusive practices for people with communication needs and advocate for client access to services and society.

96126.description: This subject offers you hands-on experience in speech pathology through clinical placements working with children and adults. Your placements will be complemented by practical workshops. You'll apply theoretical knowledge and skills in real clinic settings under the guidance of experienced speech pathologists. Your learning will be practice-based, focusing on enhancing speech pathology management for both children and adults. You'll also compile a portfolio to document your learning journey, reflective practice, and growth in clinical skills.
learningOutcomes: Develop clinical competency in identifying, appraising, selecting, implementing, and documenting appropriate assessment, diagnosis, intervention, and management plans.
Effectively communicate assessment findings, intervention plans, and outcomes using respectful, inclusive, and person-centred approaches.
Collaborate respectfully with individuals, communities, and professionals in all areas of professional and clinical practice.
Develop awareness and skills in cultural safety, ethical practice, and evidence-based practice.
Demonstrate growth in clinical competency and recognise the importance of lifelong learning and professional development.

args.text: Admission into C04386 Master of Speech Pathology

96128.title: Voice Disorders
96128.description: In this subject you will learn about voice anatomy and physiology, assess vocal quality and disorders, and develop interventions for voice improvement. Your skills will include evaluating voice in children and adults, and addressing environmental, social, and psychological influences on vocal health. You will apply your knowledge in clinical cases and explore areas of advanced practice including head and neck cancer, upper airways voice disorders, and gender affirming voice training. The subject involves practical analysis and intervention design, enhancing both theoretical knowledge and clinical application.
learningOutcomes: Diagnose communication disorders and effectively communicate the findings.
Develop, communicate, and implement evidence-based intervention plans.
Identify the many factors influencing communication and its assessment across the lifespan.
Integrate and apply foundational knowledge of body structures and functions related to communication disorders, as well as prevalence, clinical risk, and protective factors.
Apply appropriate interpersonal techniques and reflective practices in speech pathology.

args.text: Admission into C04386 Master of Speech Pathology

96129.title: Integrated Practice in Speech Pathology
96129.description: You will gain proficiency in evaluating and treating communication and swallowing disorders across multiple populations. You will consider the complex intersections and interactions of mental health, cultural competence, and socioeconomic factors. You'll learn to apply speech pathology principles in private practice, focusing on service design, legal and ethical compliance, and business management. This subject readies you for professional speech pathology practice, integrating multifaceted clinical knowledge with real-world application.
learningOutcomes: Adapt practice approaches and service planning according to principles of cultural safety, engaging with and demonstrating respect for all people including those with disability and of diverse backgrounds.
Apply improvement processes to guide improvements to clinical practice safety and quality, with reference to the Speech Pathology Australia Code of Ethics, Professional Standards, and legislation.

Plan speech pathology services addressing identified goals, removing barriers, and enhancing facilitators for improved access to evidence-based interventions, innovative approaches, and collaborative practice.

Acquire, critique, and integrate knowledge from a range of sources to develop and inform practice and support the development of the profession.

96130.title: Speech Pathology Clinical Practice 3
96130.description: This subject marks the culmination of your practice education, with placements that involve working with children and adults in a variety of settings. You'll apply theories and skills from your Master of Speech Pathology through supervised practice under the guidance of experienced speech pathologists and refine your clinical management with diverse populations. You will create a portfolio that documents your experiences and skill development, aligning these with course objectives and professional standards. By the end of this subject, you'll showcase your competencies in readiness to enter the profession and in line with the Professional Standards of Speech Pathology Australia.
learningOutcomes: Develop clinical competency in identifying, appraising, selecting, implementing, and documenting appropriate assessment, diagnosis, intervention, and management plans.

96134.title: Validation Principles and Practices
96134.description: In this subject you'll learn the importance of validation in pharmaceutical manufacturing to ensure a consistent and robust process. You'll explore the skills and requirements to perform various qualification activities, process validation, and cleaning validation, ensuring products meet required standards for safety, efficacy, and quality, thus safeguarding the patient. Additionally, you'll learn how to maintain a validated state of control throughout the entire validation lifecycle, ensuring continued compliance and product quality. Through real-world scenarios, you'll apply these skills, gaining the ability to implement effective validation strategies in pharmaceutical manufacturing.
learningOutcomes: Apply validation requirements and strategies in various regulatory environments.
Apply all stages of the V-model to new facilities and equipment within the pharmaceutical industry.
Devise validation plans and protocols for equipment, facilities, and manufacturing processes to meet regulatory requirements.
Critically reflect on the impact of teamwork experience on future professional practice.

96135.title: Biotech Manufacturing
96135.description: In this subject you will be learning about Biotech Manufacturing. Biotech Manufacturing varies from traditional pharmaceutical manufacturing. This subject focuses on the use of upstream and downstream processes in manufacturing stages. These processes include environmental monitoring in a clean room environment as well as gowning procedures. You will learn about the use of single-use and multi-use equipment. The concept of master cell banks and working cell banks this will also include lyophilization and terminal sterilization. You will apply applicable concepts to scenarios provided to you in class which will allow you to obtain real life experience out in the industry.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate comprehensive knowledge and skills in cleanroom operations and assess the importance of the clean room environment.
Devise appropriate sampling plans and procedures for the cleanroom and water systems in a pharmaceutical facility.
Explain the different steps required to perform biotech manufacturing, identifying their differences to traditional pharmaceutical manufacturing.
Outline the differences between single-use and multi-use technology with respect to aseptic processing of biotech products.
Apply knowledge of biological materials and equipment to ensure compliance with regulatory standards in the pharmaceutical industry.

96136.title: Advanced Clinical Skills 1
96136.description: In this subject you will build the clinical knowledge and skills needed to manage acute conditions and deliver preventive health services. You will learn to conduct patient assessments, interpret pathology results, and apply clinical reasoning to diagnose and treat common acute presentations, while identifying risk factors and referral criteria to other healthcare professionals. You will also develop the ability to provide preventive services such as contraception counselling, smoking cessation and weight management in a clinically and culturally safe and effective way. Learning will be online, combining self-directed study, interactive workshops and case-based activities to support application of knowledge to practice.
learningOutcomes: Perform structured patient assessments, including history-taking, physical examination and clinical measurements.
Request and interpret common pathology results relevant to acute and preventive care.
Apply clinical reasoning to assess and manage common acute conditions.
Provide preventive health services, including contraception counselling, smoking cessation and weight management, in a clinically and culturally safe and effective manner.
Apply evidence-based guidelines to support timely and appropriate decision-making, including the identification of risk factors and referrals when appropriate.

args.text: Admission into C11386 Graduate Certificate in Pharmacist Prescribing

96137.title: Advanced Clinical Skills 2
96137.description: In this subject you will focus on managing chronic disease and complex patient care. You will learn to integrate advanced assessment and diagnostic skills, initiate and adjust long-term pharmacotherapy, and optimise therapy for patients with multimorbidity and polypharmacy. You will also develop skills in the safe administration of medicines by injection and critically evaluate clinical practice through emerging evidence and case-based review. Learning will be online, with self-directed activities, interactive workshops and applied case-based learning to build confidence in managing chronic and complex care.
learningOutcomes: Integrate advanced assessment and diagnostic skills, including pathology requests and interpretation, into chronic disease management.
Initiate and adjust long-term pharmacotherapy for chronic conditions such as diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidaemia, COPD and asthma.
Optimise therapy for patients with multimorbidity and polypharmacy, balancing efficacy, safety and patient preferences.
Administer medicines by injection safely and in accordance with professional standards.
Critically evaluate practice using emerging evidence and case-based review of complex scenarios.

args.text: Admission into C11386 Graduate Certificate in Pharmacist Prescribing

96138.title: Prescribing Skills 1
96138.description: In this subject you will develop the foundations of safe and responsible prescribing within your scope of practice, learning how to apply legal and ethical frameworks (including the AHPRA prescribing framework) and consulting effectively with patients. You will build practical skills in gathering, interpreting and communicating clinical information, and collaborating with patients and health professionals on treatment planning, monitoring and adverse event management. Learning will take place online through self-directed modules, interactive workshops involving pharmacists and other prescribers, and practice-based exercises designed to help you apply prescribing concepts in realistic scenarios.
learningOutcomes: Apply legal, ethical and professional standards to ensure safe, accountable and person-centred prescribing practice.
Use the National Prescribing Competencies Framework to guide safe and evidence-based prescribing decisions, including the appropriate use of technology and digital decision-support tools.
Conduct effective patient consultations that gather and interpret clinical and contextual information to inform prescribing and monitoring decisions.
Collaborate and communicate effectively with patients and other health professionals to develop, document and review individualised treatment and follow-up plans.
Demonstrate culturally safe and responsive prescribing practice when working with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and diverse communities.
