013460.title: Science Teaching Methods 2
013460.description: This subject builds on the foundations established in Science Teaching Methods 1 and focuses on the design, implementation and evaluation of teaching and learning in senior secondary science education. Pre-service teachers develop advanced pedagogical content knowledge through engagement with the NSW Stage 6 Science syllabuses and associated curriculum requirements. Particular emphasis is placed on curriculum interpretation, content organisation, lesson sequencing, teaching strategies, assessment design, reporting practices and the development of coherent teaching programs that support student learning and achievement. Pre-service teachers complete the subject within one of four disciplinary pathways: Biology, Chemistry, Physics, or Earth and Environmental Science. While the subject is organised around a shared pedagogical framework focused on curriculum interpretation, lesson sequencing, assessment design, reporting and program evaluation, teaching is structured through pathway-specific disciplinary streams. Biology and Earth and Environmental Science pre-service teachers participate in a common disciplinary stream, while Chemistry and Physics pre-service teachers participate in a separate disciplinary stream. This structure enables pre-service teachers to engage with shared pedagogical challenges associated with senior secondary science teaching while maintaining strong engagement with the disciplinary concepts, inquiry traditions, representations, practical investigations, assessment practices and curriculum requirements associated with their chosen science specialisation. Drawing on examples from Biology, Chemistry, Physics and Earth and Environmental Science, pre-service teachers examine the distinctive disciplinary concepts, inquiry traditions, literacy practices, representational forms and pedagogical approaches associated with senior secondary science education. They explore how scientific knowledge is organised within Stage 6 curricula and how teachers design learning experiences that support conceptual understanding, scientific reasoning, practical investigation and preparation for external assessment. The subject develops pre-service teachers' capacity to design and evaluate lessons, assessment tasks and learning sequences that align curriculum outcomes, teaching strategies and evidence of learning. Particular attention is given to formative and summative assessment, standards-referenced reporting, feedback practices and the use of assessment evidence to improve teaching and learning. Pre-service teachers critically evaluate teaching resources, practical investigations, representations, digital technologies and assessment approaches used in senior secondary science classrooms. They learn to make evidence-informed pedagogical decisions that support student engagement, conceptual development and disciplinary understanding across diverse science contexts. The subject prepares pre-service teachers to design, implement and evaluate Stage 6 science programs and to teach effectively within their chosen disciplinary pathway. Particular attention is given to the distinctive curriculum structures, inquiry traditions, representations, practical investigations and assessment practices associated with Biology, Chemistry, Physics and Earth and Environmental Science. Learning developed in this subject provides an essential foundation for Science Teaching Methods 3 and for professional experience placements in senior secondary science classrooms.
learningOutcomes: Interpret and apply the objectives, outcomes, content and assessment requirements of the NSW Stage 6 Science syllabuses within their chosen disciplinary pathway (Biology, Chemistry, Physics, or Earth and Environmental Science).
Organise science content into coherent and effective sequences of learning using knowledge of curriculum structure, student learning and evidence-informed pedagogical approaches.
Design lessons and learning sequences that support diverse learners through the use of appropriate teaching strategies, practical investigations, representations, resources and digital technologies.

Analyse the role of social determinants of health, including socioeconomic status, culture, and geography, in influencing disparities in SRH access and outcomes across different population groups.

Evaluate the unique SRH needs of priority populations, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, culturally and linguistically diverse (CALD) communities, gender-diverse individuals and people with disability, and propose appropriate strategies to improve SRH outcomes.

Critically reflect on changes in public discourse, healthcare policies, and access to SRH services, focusing on their impact on health equity and the ongoing need for advocacy to maintain equitable access to care.

requisite.text: Admission into C04447 Master of Women's and Children's Health

090008.title: An introduction to Reproductive Health
090008.description:
This subject equips students with a comprehensive understanding of reproductive health, vital for supporting individuals on their fertility journey. Students gain insights into the anatomy, physiology, and hormonal mechanisms that inform fertility treatments, including assisted reproductive technology (ART). They also acquire the skills to educate and assist clients through fertility processes and collaborate effectively within a healthcare team. Learning involves tracing a typical fertility treatment trajectory, from initial consultation to potential outcomes, ensuring they can guide clients with empathy and expertise.

Students' skills in critical thinking and understanding are honed through interactive online resources, stimulating multimedia materials, and problem-solving tasks. Learning is reinforced with real-world case studies and immediate feedback, fostering reflective and analytical competencies in a guided, yet self-directed environment.
learningOutcomes: Critically analyse normal and abnormal reproductive anatomy and physiology and hormone values in males and females
Interpret and discuss the prognostic value of current diagnostic tools employed in fertility investigations including pre-conception screening
Critically examine and justify the standard ART treatment pathways using physiology and pharmacology, to identify appropriate interventions, as well as risks, complications and outcomes
Critically reflect on the emotional impact of infertility on individuals and couples

requisite.text: Admission into C04447 Master of Women's and Children's Health

090040.title: Assisted Reproduction
090040.description:
Over 76,000 assisted reproductive technology treatments cycles are reported in Australia each year. This subject aims to expand on students' understanding of the fertility pathway and build on the complexity of the concepts inherent in the fertility pathway to further develop their capacity to undertake or expand their career in the Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) sector. Through knowledge of anatomy, physiology, endocrinology and pharmacological theory, the students explore third-party reproduction, pre-implantation genetic diagnosis, reporting obligations and outcomes of treatment. A case study approach is used to consider risk management, genetics, and complex pre-implantation genetic diagnosis scenarios.

Student skills in critical thinking and understanding will be honed through interactive online resources, stimulating multimedia materials, and problem-solving tasks. Learning is reinforced with real-world case studies and immediate feedback, fostering reflective and analytical competencies in a guided, yet self-directed environment.
learningOutcomes: Analyse complexities in trajectories of assisted reproduction including issues associated with third party reproduction
Identify, plan, implement and evaluate collaborative healthcare for consumers undergoing assisted reproduction
Recognise the diversity of consumers and families undergoing assisted reproduction and integrate this knowledge into planning and implementing effective healthcare
Interpret and discuss genetics as it relates to fertility investigations, interventions and birth outcomes

010048.title: Professional Learning
010048.description: This foundational subject introduces you to the teaching profession, the process of teaching, and ongoing professional development, including a 20-day practicum for students. You'll prepare for classroom engagement by examining school settings, learning to plan lessons using the UTS template, and researching effective teaching strategies. Through workshops and online resources, you'll link theory with practice, develop key teaching skills, and reflect on what enhances student learning. The course emphasises context-aware, collaborative, and evidence-based approaches to teacher learning through immersive in-school professional learning. You will learn how to reflect on these learning opportunities to develop your teaching. All tasks are aligned with the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers: Graduate, setting the stage for your professional growth.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the role of the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers in identifying professional learning needs. (6.1.1)
Understand the relevant and appropriate sources of professional learning for teachers. (6.2.1)
Demonstrate an understanding of the role of the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers in identifying professional learning needs (6.3.1)
Explain the rationale for continued professional learning and the implications for improved student learning (6.4.1)
Communicate appropriately to a range of audiences

010049.title: Understanding and Engaging Adolescent Learners
010049.description: This subject prepares you to effectively connect with adolescent learners in Australian schools, blending psychological insights on learning and motivation with sociological understanding of youth. You'll learn to navigate and analyse the complexities of secondary education environments, applying diverse theories to foster engaging and adaptive teaching practices. By examining real-world scenarios from schools, families, and communities, you'll consider the practical implications of these theories. Your professional placement experiences and personal educational philosophy will enrich the subject's content, equipping you with a comprehensive and respectful approach to help future students thrive in high school.
learningOutcomes: Analyse how students learn and change, and how student motivation develops.
Analyse complex teaching and learning scenarios that affect adolescents.
Develop theoretically sound strategies for creating supportive teaching and learning environments for adolescents in diverse and complex contexts.
Describe and scrutinise challenging issues facing young Australians and their teachers in schools, drawing on relevant theoretical concepts, research and policy.
Develop teaching and learning strategies for dealing with authentic challenging scenarios that affect adolescents in modern day classrooms.
Identify how teachers can draw on their understanding of adolescent development to support the students they teach in schools.

010047.title: Literacy and Numeracy Across the Curriculum
010047.description: This subject hones your ability to address the literacy and numeracy needs of learners, especially those for whom English is an Additional Language/Dialect (EAL/D). You'll gain insights into linguistic and mathematical concepts, the interplay between language and thought, and learning from psychological and sociological viewpoints. You'll become aware of how literacy and numeracy are uniquely embedded within different subjects and learn to craft lessons that bolster students' English and maths skills in specific content areas. By enhancing your ability to teach these core skills across the curriculum, you contribute to your learners' academic success and societal engagement.
learningOutcomes: Identify the key issues in developing literacy and numeracy competency across the curriculum
Know and understand literacy and numeracy teaching strategies and their application in teaching areas (GTS 2.5)
Communicate appropriately to a range of audiences.

013241.description: This subject centres on student wellbeing and classroom management, featuring a 30-day school placement where you'll experience the role of a teacher firsthand. Successful completion of this supervised placement is essential. You'll develop classroom management skills, learn about effective instructional planning and delivery, and foster relationships to enhance student engagement in learning, all while adhering to pertinent policies, legislation, and guidelines for student wellbeing.

Appropriately identify and apply practical approaches to manage challenging behaviour in the classroom and the whole-school context (GTS 4.3)

013242.title: Professional Experience Teaching Practice 2
013242.description: During a six-week placement, you will gain practical experience as a pre-service teacher, receiving feedback on your teaching from both your university supervisor and the classroom teacher. The coursework is designed to consolidate your knowledge and teaching practices, enabling you to complete the Teacher Performance Assessment (TPA). In the TPA, you will evaluate your planning, teaching and assessment whilst on placement and consider their alignment with the Assessment for Graduate Teaching (AfGT) standards. The subject concludes with you curating and annotating a portfolio reflecting demonstration of the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers (APSTs). The subject and placement allow you to apply your learning in a real-world educational setting, with continuous feedback on your teaching practice and progress towards teaching domain standards.
learningOutcomes: Compile, analyse and evaluate evidence of own teaching practice for NESA Graduate Teacher Standards through the TPA during the teaching placement in schools (GTS 1 – 5; 6.3)
Plan for, and implement, effective teaching and learning (GTS 3.1, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5)

Develop professional practice and compile evidence and undertake reflection on the requirements of the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers (APST)/GTS from NESA.

024411.title: Literary Narrative from Sendak to Shakespeare
024411.description: This subject introduces you to the concept of literature as a continuum and the place of literature in the primary school curriculum. Your study will involve children’s fairytales, excerpts from the novels of the Brontë sisters, picture books and excerpts from the plays of William Shakespeare. You will develop theoretical understandings of literary concepts, narrative, and character patterns and archetypes. You will read and discuss a wide range of children's books and other literary texts, with particular reference to the prescribed readings and texts. In this subject you are expected to develop and demonstrate an understanding of a range of literary concepts and an understanding of how to apply them appropriately in the primary classroom.
learningOutcomes: Identify, explain and evaluate key features of texts relevant for the primary classroom, including key literary and language features.
Identify, explain and evaluate a range of literary and theoretical concepts.
Apply skills to create digital resources.
Skilfully communicate ideas in oral, written and visual modes.
Explain and apply knowledge of the NSW English K–10 syllabus.

028004.title: Ceramics and Claymation
028004.description: This interdisciplinary subject provides you with a comprehensive foundation of theory and practice by investigating the art-making practices of ceramics (making objects by shaping inorganic, nonmetallic material such as clay) and the more recent art practice of claymation (clay/plasticine/plastilina stop-motion animation). In this subject you will explore the history, current practices and trends in ceramics, claymation and animation to develop your understanding of artistic expression and teaching possibilities for the primary classroom. Through an exploration of ceramics as art-making and the work of early claymation and animation pioneers through to contemporary creators, you will learn how to utilise and integrate these practices into your teaching to foster the critical and creative capacities of primary school students. This subject addresses the unique challenges and opportunities of using ceramics, claymation and animation as engaging teaching tools, equipping you to infuse traditional, as well as technology-enhanced creativity into your teaching practices to enrich the educational and art-making experiences of young learners.
learningOutcomes: Identify and apply ceramics, claymation and/or animation art-making practices.
Apply knowledge of how students learn from artmaking and animation.
Plan integrated lesson plans and units.

Embed and make explicit the teaching of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander histories and
cultures through visual arts and animation.
Create and maintain an inclusive and safe learning environment that encourages artistic excellence.

028255.title: Reading, Writing and Spelling
028255.description: You will examine evidence-based literacy instruction tailored to meet the diverse abilities of students across the full range of abilities in inclusive primary classrooms. You will study cognitive processes involved in learning to read and write, emphasising phonemic awareness, phonological knowledge, decoding strategies, vocabulary development, fluency, and comprehension. And you will be taught to use assessment strategies to identify instructional priorities. The subject highlights explicit, systematic approaches to teaching literacy, equipping you with practical strategies to support primary school learners who are not meeting expected literacy outcomes.
learningOutcomes: Analyse the cognitive processes involved in learning to read, spell and write and strategies to support learning.
Develop strategies to support learners who are not achieving vocabulary, fluency, and comprehension outcomes.
Design and implement formal and informal assessment techniques to identify instructional priorities for learners not achieving expected literacy outcomes.
Apply explicit, systematic approaches to literacy teaching that address the needs of students who are not meeting expected literacy outcomes.
Collaborate with peers to evaluate existing programs and create and share inclusive literacy teaching resources and strategies.

010082.title: Advancing Academic Practice
010082.description: In this subject, you can build on the work that you completed in the previous subjects Teaching for Learning and Feedback and Assessment, or you can identify new priorities for your teaching practice. Through structured engagement with peers and teaching staff, as well as engagement with key theoretical frameworks for tertiary teaching and learning, you can review and revise the Draft Action Plans developed in those earlier subjects or, if more appropriate for your goals, create a new Action Plan. You will deepen your understanding of the iterative nature of tertiary teaching design, as well as explore practical strategies for creating communities of professional practice, peer mentoring, and giving and receiving constructive feedback in tertiary teaching.
learningOutcomes: Apply strategies such as reflective practice, professional communities of practice, and peer review to enhance an iterative teaching design process
Engage in a range of professional practices to collect, offer and critically evaluate feedback on teaching practice
Reflect on feedback in order to analyse the ways in which teaching practice contributes to a discipline and to the strategic priorities of the university

010085.title: Practising Inclusion
010085.school: Institute for Interactive Media and Learning
010085.description: This subject introduces students to concepts, principles and practices of diversity and inclusion in various areas of higher education. Students critique approaches to inclusion in relation to various groups and explore underlying reasons for exclusion and discrimination. Through reflecting on their practices, students identify areas of improvement and change in their professional role in a higher education institution. Students also learn to integrate principles of inclusion into their own practice and take action to ensure greater inclusion and wider participation of all students and staff.
learningOutcomes: Reflect critically and creatively on the assumptions, consequences, and possibilities of being an inclusive practitioner
Apply foundational knowledge of Solomon Islands and other Indigenous cultures and histories to support inclusive teaching and learning in a range of settings.
Identify opportunities to be an ally for social change
Apply critical analysis of complex issues related to discrimination, equity and social justice to the maintenance and improvement of inclusive practices in higher education

requisite.text: Admission into C11383 Graduate Certificate in Higher Education Teaching and Learning

010081.title: Feedback and Assessment
010081.description: In this subject, you will study theoretical concepts and practical strategies to support the design of a feedback and assessment strategy to enhance student learning within your personal teaching context. Beginning with the purpose and types of assessment, you will investigate how your current feedback and assessment strategies align with a range of evidence-based principles and consider opportunities for improvement. You will learn to apply the elements of an effective feedback and assessment strategy and be able to articulate the rationale underpinning your feedback and assessment strategies to your students.
learningOutcomes: Analyse and evaluate the impact of feedback and assessment practices in terms of their ability to support student learning relevant to the teaching context
Design a feedback and assessment strategy that facilitates student learning and engagement with feedback
Identify opportunities for designing assessment and feedback practices that engage with the diversity of Solomon Islander cultures
Communicate the rationale and design of feedback and assessment strategies to a variety of audiences using different channels

requisite.text: Admission into C11383 Graduate Certificate in Higher Education Teaching and Learning

010087.title: Evidencing Academic Practice
010087.school: Institute for Interactive Media and Learning
010087.description: In this capstone subject, students reflect on their learning goals in relation to the learning experiences completed for each subject in the course. Students complete a course portfolio to demonstrate their development of capabilities against a set of criteria (e.g. the Graduate Certificate course- intended learning outcomes and their own professional practice goals). At the end of the subject, students renew their learning goals as they relate to their own academic career, and present what they’ve learned to colleagues, supervisors and learning and teaching leaders.
learningOutcomes: Apply relevant knowledge to justify curriculum, learning, assessment and evaluation choices in the higher education context
Reflexively assess complex issues related to curriculum, assessment and pedagogy, and generate effective scholarly and creative solutions
Demonstrate support and facilitation of inclusive practices that foster respectful engagement with diverse learners and perspectives at a local and global level
Engage respectfully with Solomon Islands peoples’ cultures, knowledges, histories, policies, and priorities, and discuss the implications for Higher Education
Articulate your contribution to the culture and climate of the University, and to the sector/discipline more broadly on matters of concern for higher education teaching and learning
Produce a coherent narrative on teaching and learning impact to a selected audience in a chosen mode

requisite.text: Admission into C11383 Graduate Certificate in Higher Education Teaching and Learning

010086.title: Course Design
010086.description: In this subject, you will study higher education curriculum models, theories and principles of course design, and apply these models to courses that are taught at your university. Through practical applications of key theories and concepts from this subject, you will develop your ability to design courses that provide integrated, coherent and engaging learning experiences that both fulfil the needs of your students and meet university and national requirements. You will examine the courses you teach and suggest opportunities for changes that enhance your students’ experience and align courses with university and national strategic goals.
learningOutcomes: Reflect on key principles of course design and the identify the impact these principles have on the student experience
Critically evaluate course or curriculum models and course design processes
Identify opportunities to enhance a course design and communicate the rationale for course design decisions

requisite.text: Admission into C11383 Graduate Certificate in Higher Education Teaching and Learning

010083.title: Student Agency and Teamwork
010083.school: Institute for Interactive Media and Learning
010083.description: In this subject, students explore how they can enable active and collaborative learning that fosters university degree student independence, initiative and teamwork. Students devise teaching and learning practices that promote university degree student independence and teamwork opportunities.
learningOutcomes: Examine agency as a social cultural concept
Critique teamwork practices to identify fundamental elements that enhance collaborative teamwork

requisite.text: Admission into C11383 Graduate Certificate in Higher Education Teaching and Learning

010080.title: Teaching for Learning
010080.description: This core subject introduces you to learning and teaching in higher education, with a particular focus on key theoretical frameworks and practical strategies related to constructive alignment, student-centred learning, and active learning. It provides an opportunity to reflect on the comparative context of higher education in Australia and Pacific Island nations, with particular attention to the experience of Indigenous students in tertiary education.  It builds on your own experiences of learning and teaching and enables you to contextualise your experience with reference to key scholarship, and to explore models for learning that enhance your understanding of tertiary student experience.
learningOutcomes: Reflect on your prior experiences of tertiary teaching to identify key learning priorities for developing your teaching skills
Analyse how learning design, constructive alignment in curriculum, and feedback and assessment optimise student learning

Reflect on key principles supporting inclusive teaching practices, and analyse the cultural, historic, and contemporary contexts that influence the lives of Indigenous peoples in the Solomon Islands and Australia
Identify and describe key educational principles that underpin strategic priorities in relation to your teaching
Communicate about teaching skills effectively in a range of contexts

requisite.text: Admission into C11383 Graduate Certificate in Higher Education Teaching and Learning

010084.title: Technology-Enhanced Learning
010084.school: Institute for Interactive Media and Learning
010084.description: In this subject, students explore the opportunities for learning and teaching afforded by online, blended and hybrid models of learning delivery. Students examine theories and strategies that consider time and place for student engagement and teacher presence and investigate ideas for online and blended learning in their own context and discipline. Students learn collaboratively and are encouraged to share ideas and provide peer feedback on ideas and issues related to synchronous and asynchronous settings in technology-enhanced learning.
learningOutcomes: Critically evaluate current models and frameworks for the use of technology in learning
Assess opportunities and affordances of technology-enhanced learning to facilitate inclusive practice and engage diverse learners

requisite.text: Admission into C11383 Graduate Certificate in Higher Education Teaching and Learning

023821.title: Inclusive Education: Behaviour
023821.description: This subject develops an understanding of the underlying causes of behaviour in children and adolescents. It examines the intervention strategies that can be applied by teachers to prevent, support and minimise behaviours. Students learn how to identify the function of behaviours and develop intervention programs to support students.
learningOutcomes: Identify the causes and function/s of student behaviour through Functional Behaviour Assessment and Risk Assessment
Understand the contextual nature of behaviour and examine environmental triggers
Understand the role of multitiered systems of support including Positive Behaviour Support (PBL).
Select appropriate antecedent/consequence interventions to prevent/decrease inappropriate behaviours
Identify and safely manage escalating aggressive behaviour chains
Develop as critical readers of literature in the field of behaviour management which will carry through later professional practice

013246.title: Technological and Applied Studies Teaching Methods: Technology (Mandatory)
013246.description: This subject prepares you to effectively organise and deliver Technology Mandatory 7-8, blending theory with practice for a comprehensive understanding of the four context areas in Stage 4. You'll gain insight into the structure of Technology Mandatory and its alignment with the Australian Curriculum. The subject introduces lesson planning with collaborative, student-centred, and project-based methods. Additionally, you'll acquire practical skills in creating teaching resources with timber and basic hand tools, applicable across various Technology Mandatory contexts.

Plan and implement a range of teaching strategies for Technology Mandatory
Locate and deploy knowledge of a range of resources, including ICT, that engage Technology Mandatory students in their learning
